# Part XXII — Unit 322F001: the HP carbamate ejector

The circulator of the HP synthesis loop, and the only thing that moves liquid round it. Liquid
ammonia from the 321P002 A/B triplex pumps drives the nozzle, entrains the 322E003 scrubber's
carbamate overflow, and delivers the mixture to 322E002. It has no moving parts, which is why
it is there: the loop runs at 144 bar a, and a mechanical pump with a seal at that pressure on
a carbamate stream would be a maintenance item measured in weeks. What it costs instead is
that the loop's circulation is hostage to the ammonia feed.

## XXII.1 The design duty, and where each number comes from

| quantity | value | source |
|---|---|---|
| motive ammonia | 42 762.05 kg/h | PFD, re-pinned; `unit_321` owns it |
| motive composition | 99.67 % NH3 + CH4 / H2 / N2 / H2O | PFD stream 116, liquid row, mass % |
| motive temperature | 28.934 C | derived from the pump-thermal path at the design drum state |
| entrained carbamate | 57 561.32 kg/h | the reconciled 322E003 overflow, PFD 206 |
| suction temperature | 178.8 C | PFD 206, heat of mixing lumped in |
| suction / discharge pressure | 140.0 / 144.2 bar a | PFD; the lift is 4.2 bar |
| discharge | 100 323.37 kg/h at 107.57 C | computed, TT-322012 |
| entrainment ratio $\mu$ | 1.34608 | computed |

**The motive is not pure ammonia, and that is load bearing.** The plant ammonia's trace
methane and hydrogen are the ONLY source of the CH4 and H2 that leave in the 322E003 vent —
PFD 204 puts them at 3.84 and 2.03 kmol/h, and this row delivers 4.00 and 2.12, closing the
inert balance to within 4 %. With a pure motive the reactor recycle tear had to create them
out of nothing.

**The motive temperature is reconstructed, not entered.** The number the 322E002 heat balance
needs is the temperature the RUNNING loop feeds, and an earlier version of V1 used 170 C here,
which moves the condenser's mixed feed by tens of degrees and takes its UA back-calculation
with it. Ammonia arrives at the battery limit at 25 C and the pumps add about 4 K across 152
bar. `data/unit_322f001.py` repeats the arithmetic of
`units.feed.station.pump_discharge_temperature_c` because `data` sits below `units` and cannot
import it; the equivalence suite asserts the two agree to the bit.

## XXII.2 Anchoring — the ratio of the closure to itself

$$ \text{capacity} = \dot m_{suc,des}\cdot
   \frac{\dot m_s^{\,live}(\dot m_p,\,p_s,\,p_d,\,A_t(\theta))}
        {\dot m_s^{\,des}(\dot m_{p,des},\,p_{s,des},\,p_{d,des},\,A_{t,des})} $$

so the design duty is reproduced BIT-EXACTLY, which an absolute form would not be: the
back-solved geometry does not multiply back through to the original float, and the boot pin
asserts the design point to the last bit.

The reference is the licensor's design PAIR, which is the same pair the geometry is
back-solved from, so the anchor and the geometry cannot disagree. It is deliberately not the
settled motive flow that V1's retired $\phi_m$ normalised on: the settled loop runs 0.078 %
under the PFD motive, and this closure amplifies that about tenfold for the reason XXII.4 is
about. Anchoring on a settled value would move that offset onto the FIRST tick from a fresh
state, which is exactly where the boot pin and every unit test measure the design point.

## XXII.3 HV-322602 acts on the nozzle, and therefore runs backwards

$$ A_t(\theta) = A_{t,des}\cdot\frac{40 + 0.6\,\theta}{40 + 0.6\,\theta_{des}},
   \qquad \theta_{des} = 74\ \% $$

The 322F001 DDS states the nozzle free area directly — variable over 40-100 % on a linear
instrument map — so this is a primary source for exactly the quantity the model needs, and it
is used unchanged. Below 10 % of travel the stroke is held, because extrapolating a datasheet
map past its own stated range would be inventing data.

**CLOSING the spindle RAISES entrainment.** At constant motive mass a smaller area raises the
jet momentum $\dot m_p^2/(\rho_p A_t)$ and therefore the head the pump can develop, and more
head available at the same lift means more entrainment. The motive comes from
positive-displacement pumps, so the valve cannot change the mass flow — only the velocity it
leaves at. V1's superseded law asserted this direction; here it is derived. An operator who
treats HV-322602 as a throttle gets the opposite of what they intend.

**FINDING: the range is about 38:1, not 2.15:1.** Measured at the design motive:

| opening | 10 % | 25 % | 50 % | 74 % | 90 % | 100 % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| capacity, fraction of design | 3.682 | 2.899 | 1.851 | **1.000** | 0.454 | 0.098 |

V1's retired `EJ_SPINDLE_R = 2.1517` was itself back-solved from this same free-area map, but
through the linear-ish capacity relation the old model assumed — and that assumed relation is
precisely what the momentum balance replaces. The derived range is an order of magnitude
wider, for the same reason as XXII.4: this machine runs close to its own shutoff head, where
capacity is a steep function of jet momentum.

## XXII.4 FINDING: the machine stalls at 91 % motive

*Signed off 2026-10-16 (decision 122, handoff B-12 closed, §LXXI.3): kept as V1, as ported.*

The jet develops $C_0 = 5.106$ bar at zero entrainment against a design lift of 4.2 bar, and
the shutoff head scales with the square of the motive mass flow, so

$$ \phi_{m,stall} = \sqrt{\frac{p_d - p_s}{C_{0,des}}} = \sqrt{\frac{4.2}{5.106}} = 0.907 $$

Measured, with the spindle at design:

| motive fraction | 1.000 | 0.950 | 0.920 | 0.910 | 0.9069 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| entrainment, fraction of design | 1.000 | 0.530 | 0.181 | 0.044 | **0 — stalled** |

**Why it matters.** 322F001 is the only thing that circulates the HP loop, so if the model is
right, a 5 % ammonia-feed shortfall halves the loop's circulation and a 9 % shortfall stops
it. That makes the feed ratio a far more critical handle than a trainee would expect, and the
321 pumps a single point of failure for the whole synthesis section.

**Why it is the better-founded number.** V1's retired law put the knee at a motive fraction of
0.20 with a quadratic recovery to 0.35 — three fitted constants producing a plausible-looking
collapse, with nothing deriving them. This comes from the momentum balance through the
back-solved geometry. The uncertainty is not in the balance, which is algebra, but in the four
loss coefficients of XXI.5: a more efficient diffuser or a lower throat friction raises $C_0$
and moves the stall point down. The design duty is unaffected either way. The MARGIN is not,
and it is recorded as handoff **B-12** rather than presented as settled.

## XXII.5 The suction head and the choked throat

$$ \dot m_{suc} = \text{capacity}\cdot
   \min\!\big(\max(L/L_{NLL},\,0),\; 1.25\big)
   \cdot \mathbb{1}[\text{XV-322903 open}] $$

The 322E003 sump's own gravity head helps the suction, and the closure does not model it, so
it enters as a ratio to its own design. At design the level is at normal, the multiplier is a
literal 1.0, and the entrainment is the capacity to the bit.

The 1.25 is the throat-choke ceiling: above a finite suction head the throat reaches its
maximum mass capacity and entrainment stops rising. Being above 1.0 it never engages at
design. What it prevents is a 322E003 flood self-amplifying — the raw multiplier wants 2.0 at
a 100 % level against a 50 % normal level, and without the ceiling the un-pumpable excess
would be recirculated through 322E002 into the reactor, where the conversion self-loop
re-amplifies it. With the ceiling the excess backs up in the sump, which is what a choked
throat actually does.

XV-322903 is a block valve, not a throttle: shut, the suction carries nothing whatever the
spindle and the sump head are doing, and the discharge is pure motive ammonia. The JET is
still healthy in that state, so `stalled` stays false — the line is isolated, not the machine.

## XXII.6 The discharge heat balance, and the step at the bottom

$$ T_d = \frac{\dot m_{mot}\,c_{p,N}\,T_{mot} + \dot m_{suc}\,c_{p,C}\,T_{suc}}
               {\dot m_d\,c_{p,D}} $$

cp-weighted on BOTH sides. The literal mass-only denominator $(\dot m_{mot} + \dot m_{suc})$
is dimensionally an enthalpy rather than a temperature and breaks the design pin, so the
dimensionally correct form is carried and $c_{p,D} = 3.50$ kJ/kg.K is the one number
back-solved — to hold the design TT-322012 exactly. The CAPPED suction drives it, so a choked
throat shows up in the temperature as well as in the flow.

**A separate branch at zero motive.** A dead jet pump does not read 0 C. The thermowell sits
in the stagnant 322E003 carbamate backed up into it, so TT-322012 RISES to 178.8 C on a
complete motive trip, because the cold ammonia that was holding the blend down has gone. That
is the useful lesson and it is the opposite of intuition.

**FINDING: the two branches do not meet.** Approaching zero motive from above, the discharge
is pure cold ammonia at $T_{mot}c_{p,N}/c_{p,D} = 39.18$ C. At a motive of $10^{-6}$ kg/h and
below, the no-flow branch hands back 178.8 C. Both are right for their own situation; the
threshold between them is a microgram per hour, so the transition is a step of 140 C rather
than a rundown. On the plant it is a thermowell losing its flowing film and coming to
equilibrium over the tag's own 120 s thermal constant — and that lag is not ported, because
this model is stateless and has nowhere to keep it. The finding and the missing lag are the
same gap, recorded as handoff **B-11**.

## XXII.7 Design closure

All thirteen published fields and all nineteen design constants agree with V1 to the bit,
including the two that are the output of a 200-step bisection over a fixed-point inner solve.
The spindle factor is a literal 1.0 at the design opening and the entrainment is the design
suction exactly, not to a tolerance.

Both halves of this unit are proven by EXECUTION: `backend/jet_pump.py` imports cleanly and is
compared function by function, and `ejector_322f001` comes through the AST lifter. There is no
transcription anywhere in it.

---

# Part XXIII — Unit 322E002: the HP carbamate condenser

Where urea synthesis begins, and the largest LP-steam source on the plant. The stripper's top
gas and the ejector's carbamate discharge meet in the top channel of a vertical falling-film
condenser and run down it together; NH3 and CO2 condense into the film and react to ammonium
carbamate; a two-phase product leaves for the reactor. On the shell, 322D001 boiler feed
water boils and raises 4.4 bar a steam.

The carbamate reaction releases about 160 kJ per mole of CO2 absorbed, and that is not waste
heat. At design it is **62.0 MW of a 62.6 MW duty — 99.1 %** — with the sensible cooling of
the gas contributing the other 0.6 MW. This unit is a reactor with a cooling jacket, not an
exchanger with a reaction in it, and that is worth having in front of anyone reading a duty
excursion: the duty follows the loop's COMPOSITION, not its temperature.

## XXIII.1 The calibration, and the three layers on top of it

$$ \dot n_i^{\,gas} = \dot n_i^{\,feed}\,\phi_i, \qquad
   \dot n_i^{\,liq} = \dot n_i^{\,feed}(1 - \phi_i) $$

The licensor balance shows urea unchanged across 322E002, so at the calibration point the
unit is a pure component phase split with the carbamate reaction implicit in the measured
numbers:

| | CO2 | NH3 | H2O | N2 | O2 / CH4 / H2 | Urea / Biuret |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $\phi_{i,des}$ | 0.2036 | 0.2977 | 0.0450 | 0.982 | 1.0 | 0.0 |

Four of the nine are structurally non-distributing: a component calibrated at exactly 1 never
condenses and one at exactly 0 never boils. They stay out of the flash and come back
untouched.

Frozen, that vector makes the condenser thermodynamically **inert**: raising the LP-steam
pressure would change the shell duty and the outlet temperature but not one mole of
condensate, and a synthesis-pressure excursion would move nothing at all. Three layers fix
that, and each is a departure FROM the calibration rather than a replacement for it.

## XXIII.2 Layer one — the anchored isothermal flash

$$
\begin{aligned}
\psi_{des} &= \sum_i z_i\,\phi_{i,des} \\
K_{i,des}  &= \frac{\phi_{i,des}(1 - \psi_{des})}{\psi_{des}(1 - \phi_{i,des})} \\
K_i(T,P)   &= K_{i,des}\;
              \exp\!\left[\frac{\Delta H_i}{R}\left(\frac1{T_{des}} - \frac1{T}\right)\right]
              \cdot \frac{P_{des}}{P}
\end{aligned}
$$

solved by Rachford-Rice,

$$ g(\psi) = \sum_i \frac{z_i(K_i - 1)}{1 + \psi(K_i - 1)} = 0,
   \qquad \phi_i = \frac{K_i\,\psi}{1 + \psi(K_i - 1)} $$

**The calibration is not discarded — it is the anchor.** $K_{i,des}$ is back-solved from the
measured split against the LIVE feed composition every tick, so the activity coefficients of
this strongly non-ideal electrolyte melt stay baked into the K-values exactly as measured.
Only the DEPARTURE is model-driven.

**Where the slopes come from.** NH3/CO2 "condensation" here is not physical condensation; it
is the carbamate equilibrium

$$ \mathrm{NH_2COONH_4\,(l)} \;\rightleftharpoons\; 2\,\mathrm{NH_3\,(g)} + \mathrm{CO_2\,(g)},
   \qquad K_p = p_{NH_3}^2\,p_{CO_2} $$

whose dissociation enthalpy is about 160 kJ/mol — the same number as the exotherm. Because
$K_p$ is a THIRD-order product, the temperature coefficient of the dissociation PRESSURE is
one third of the reaction enthalpy, 53 333 J/mol (Bennett 1953; Ramachandran 1998). With
$y_{NH_3} \approx 2 y_{CO_2}$ each partner's gas mole fraction scales as $K_p^{1/3}/P$, which
is the form above. H2O is ordinary Raoult condensation on its own latent heat, 36 900 J/mol;
N2 is a permanent gas on Henry's law, no temperature slope, still $1/P$.

**Bisection, not Newton, and a fixed count.** $g$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,1]$, so 60
sweeps is exact to $2^{-60}$ with BOUNDED cost and no possible convergence failure. An OTS
tick must never miss its deadline; that is worth more here than the iterations Newton saves.

**Finding A-15, and what it now measures.** There used to be a branch returning the design
vector whenever the pressure ratio was exactly 1 and the temperature exactly $T_{des}$. It was
deleted, so at the calibration point the routine runs the same solve it runs everywhere else
and lands on the design split by CONVERGING to it. Measured, the residual is $7\times10^{-16}$
on CO2 and $8\times10^{-16}$ on NH3 — a few ulps. The point of the deletion was to make that
number visible, and the rewrite asserts the convergence rather than the branch.

**Two guards remain, and neither is a short-circuit.** Each protects a division on the very
next line — by the distributing feed total, and by $\psi(1-\phi)$. With no distributing feed,
or a feed already single phase, there is no flash to solve, so returning the design vector is
a degenerate-input answer rather than a bypass of the maths at design.

## XXIII.3 Layer two — the film relaxation, and why equilibrium alone is unusable

$$ \phi_i^{\,film} = \phi_i^{\,prev} + a\,(\phi_i^{\,eq} - \phi_i^{\,prev}),
   \qquad a = \mathrm{clamp}\!\left(\frac{\Delta t}{\tau_{fill}},\,0,\,1\right),
   \qquad \tau_{fill} = 360\ \text{s} $$

**A pure equilibrium split is far too stiff for this vessel.** The distributing K-values are
tightly clustered, so a common factor moves the whole mixture together. Measured at the
design feed:

| $T$ | 155 C | 170 C | 190 C |
|---|---|---|---|
| $\phi_{CO_2}^{\,eq}$ | < 0.02 | 0.2036 | > 0.99 |

A 35 C band takes the condenser from almost total condensation to none. That is not how a
falling-film condenser behaves. `References/HPCC description.md` §5.2-5.3 is explicit that
322E002 is INTERFACIAL MASS-TRANSFER limited: the gas must diffuse to the film, cross the
interface and react, so the achievable split LAGS equilibrium by the film's own residence
time. The flash is the equilibrium TARGET; the split relaxes toward it.

This makes the split a genuine DYNAMIC STATE rather than an instantaneous algebraic map, and
it is the audit's "missing equation" for this tag — the condenser had no composition dynamics
at all. $\tau_{fill}$ is the same 6 min that sets the liquid level's fill time, deliberately:
both are how long liquid stays in this vessel.

$\Delta t = 0$ gives $a = 0$ and holds the split exactly, which is what the boot pass and the
conductance back-calculation need.

## XXIII.4 Layer three — the exotherm spike and the NTU quench

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot n_{CO_2}^{\,abs} &= \max(\dot n_{CO_2}^{\,strip} - \dot n_{CO_2}^{\,gas},\, 0) \\
Q_{carb} &= \dot n_{CO_2}^{\,abs}\,\Delta H_{carb} \\
Q_{sens} &= \dot m_{gas}\,c_{p,gas}\max(T_{top} - T_{prod,des},\,0) \\
T_{feed}^{\,mix} &= \frac{\dot m_{gas}^{\,in}T_{top} + \dot m_{liq}^{\,in}T_{ej}}
                          {\dot m_{gas}^{\,in} + \dot m_{liq}^{\,in}} \\
T_{adb} &= T_{feed}^{\,mix} + \frac{Q_{carb}}{\dot m\,c_p} \\
T_{prod}^{\,live} &= T_{shell} + (T_{adb} - T_{shell})\,e^{-UA/(\dot m\,c_p)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The mixed feed is COLD — 155.2 C at design, because the ejector discharge is only 107.6 C —
and the carbamate exotherm lifts it to an adiabatic 600.5 C; the shell then quenches it back
to 170.0 C.

**The spike is INTENSIVE, and that is what keeps the asymptotes physical.** Both $Q_{carb}$
and $\dot m$ scale with throughput, so $T_{adb}$ is constant against flow to within a
rounding error — measured across a 16-fold throughput range it moves by less than
$10^{-6}$ C. The NTU term is then the only thing that changes:

| throughput | 0.02x | 0.5x | 1.0x | 2.0x | 100x |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $T_{prod}$ | 151.94 C | 152.66 C | **170.00 C** | 241.95 C | 586.30 C |

Zero flow gives an infinite NTU and full quench to the shell saturation, 151.94 C; infinite
flow gives no NTU and the full adiabatic temperature. Both limits are reached, monotonically.

**$UA$ is back-calculated, and it is the only number in this unit that is.** Inverting the
quench at the design throughput:

$$ UA = -\dot m\,c_p \ln\!\left[\frac{T_{prod,des} - T_{shell}}{T_{adb} - T_{shell}}\right]
   = 1{,}610{,}148.5\ \text{kJ/h.K} $$

so the outlet lands on the licensor's 170.0 C exactly. Both inputs are FEED properties,
independent of $UA$ and of the gate, so the inversion resolves in one pass. V1 reaches the
same line inside a routine that first settles the plant for 18 000 ticks, but its own comment
is explicit that the settle is not what the expression uses — a SYNTHETIC single call at the
reconciled design feed is, because the settled attractor has drifted off the reconciled N/C
and H/C and pinning on it would land the design quench high.

**The shell saturation is thermodynamic, not the licensor's rounded indicator.** 151.94 C
from the shared IAPWS-IF97 Region 4 boundary at 5.01325 bar a, where the PFD prints 146.3 C.
The rounded figure is kept beside it as provenance so the difference cannot be mistaken for a
port error.

## XXIII.5 What the shell actually raises

$$ Q_{steam} = \max\!\left[Q_{duty} - \dot m\,c_p\,(T_{prod} - T_{prod,des}),\; 0\right] $$

The LP steam RAISED is the process duty minus the extra sensible heat the product carries out
above the design pin. At design the two are bit-identical, and it is precisely that identity
which makes the shell a stable back-pressure on the LP header: any rise in the outlet is heat
the product takes away instead of boiling, and the header feels it at once. Floored at zero,
which is the full-quench limit rather than a numerical guard.

**An intended emergent behaviour, and not a defect.** The CO2 absorbed is MINIMISED at the
design N/C, because the CO2 recycle is smallest at the balanced operating point and moving off
it either way sheds more CO2 into the loop. That minimum propagates through the steam header
as a positive-feedback V-trough in TT-322010: less exotherm, less LP steam, more MP-to-LP
letdown, a lower MP header, a cooler stripper, a cooler feed back here. The vertex is sharp
but CONTINUOUS: V1's own fine N/C probe records 180.9, 167.0 and 211.4 C at 2.00, 2.023 and
2.05, where a coarse 0.05-step sweep makes it look like a 30 C discontinuity. That appearance
is a sampling artefact of a sharp minimum amplified by the NTU exponential. (Those three
figures are V1's measurement, carried with its comment; reproducing them needs the reactor
and the steam header, so they are not yet re-measured here.) Do not smooth this in the
chemistry; the legitimate lever is the steam-header feedback gain.

## XXIII.6 The disturbance gate, and what it costs

$$ \phi_i = \phi_{i,des} + g\,(\phi_i^{\,film} - \phi_{i,des}), \qquad
   T_{prod} = T_{prod,des} + g\,(T_{prod}^{\,live} - T_{prod,des}) $$

Two of this unit's couplings have loop gain above 1 around the design point, so a fresh seed —
which is the design SEED, not the dynamic fixed point — self-excites a thermal runaway with no
operator action: V1 measured a 220 C shell and a 253 C reactor node. The gate multiplies both
coupling deltas by a factor computed from the EXOGENOUS operator and feed handles, zero within
0.2 % of design and ramping to one over the next 1 %.

At $g = 0$ the design balance is bit-exact and there is no self-excitation. At $g = 1$ the
full live response is back. Between them it interpolates linearly.

**And at the published operating point $g$ is 0**, which means the flash, the film dynamics
and the NTU quench are all inert there and the condenser does not respond to its own shell —
V1's own boot comment says the outlet holds 170.0 C for ANY value of $UA$ in that state. That
is a deliberate and defensible fix for a real instability, and it is also a fidelity statement
that has never been signed off. It is recorded as handoff **B-13**, and the gate itself is not
ported here: it reads the whole plant's handle vector, so it is an engine object, and it
arrives as an argument. **Decided 2026-10-09 (B-13 closed, §LXIV.8): $g = 1$ permanently** —
the plant passes 1.0 (`condenser_holdup`), as V1's own ``step_sim`` does (``g_dist = 1.0``,
``main.py`` 7692-7701; its ``_disturbance_gate`` is defined and never called), so the paragraph
above describes a V1 state its own code had already left.

## XXIII.7 PI-322E002, the melt bubble pressure

$$ P_{bub} = P_{des}\,
   \exp\!\left[\frac{\Delta H_{vap}}{R}\left(\frac1{T_{des}} - \frac1{T}\right)\right]
   \max(f_N, 0)\,\max(f_W, 0) $$

$$ f_N = 1 + 0.18\,(N/C - N/C_{anchor}), \qquad f_W = 1 - 0.25\,(H/C - H/C_{des}) $$

Telemetry only: the operator reads it beside the measured loop pressure, and the gap between
the two says whether the loop is holding the melt down or the melt is holding the loop up. It
does not enter the pressure target, so it adds no loop. Monotone the right way in all three —
hotter and NH3-richer raise it, wetter lowers it — and evaluated at the LIVE melt temperature,
because a bubble pressure taken at a fixed temperature is not a bubble pressure.

**The N/C anchor is the design MELT, not the reactor feed.** All the fresh ammonia enters as
ejector motive and passes through here first, so the melt is NH3-richer than the feed the
reactor is controlled on. V1 captures the settled melt figure at boot, about 3.12324, and
falls back to the reactor-feed 3.07296 until it does. At the synthetic design feed the melt is
**3.0786**, so with the fallback anchor the indication reads 144.35 bar a against the 144.2
the constant carries — a 0.1 % offset, pinned by a test rather than left to be discovered.
The 1.4 % gap between 3.0786 and the settled 3.12324 is an independent measurement of the
attractor drift recorded as handoff B-3.

**Both ratios are clamped** to half and twice their design values. They are NH3/CO2 and
H2O/CO2, so a CO2-feed cut drives them to infinity for arithmetic reasons rather than physical
ones — unclamped, the indication impulses to about 330 bar a for one tick on the way through.
The design melt sits well inside the band, so the design point is untouched.

## XXIII.8 Design closure

All 26 published fields and all 17 constants agree with V1 to the bit. The outlet is 170.0 C
exactly; the duty is 62 581.75 kW and is raised entirely as steam, 106 271 kg/h; the carbamate
make to the reactor is 189 258 kg/h against 61 381 kg/h of gas; and the unit conserves mass
component by component, because no reaction extent is tracked here — the reaction is in the
measured split.


# Part XXIV — Unit 322R001: the HP urea reactor

## XXIV.1 What the vessel is, and why it is all geometry

A 2.95 m bore, 25 m tall column at 144.9 bar a with eleven sieve trays, no heating, no cooling
and no moving parts. Two-phase carbamate from 322E002 enters at the bottom nozzle N1; liquid
melt leaves over an internal funnel at +19.3 m and goes to 322E001; uncondensed gas leaves the
top separately and goes to 322E003.

Everything the reactor does, it does with time. At the design 228.5 m3/h the liquid takes
**44.9 minutes** to cross the span, and the vessel holds **136 tonnes** of melt. Those two
numbers are behind every complaint that the reactor is slow to answer a ratio change, and in
this port they are geometry — bore, height, level — rather than a fitted time constant.

The model divides the column at the four thermowell elevations, because those are the only
places the plant can tell you what is happening inside:

| node | tag | elevation | zeta | wetted volume at NLL | residence time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | TT-322008 | 1 000 mm | 0.040 | 6.83 m3 | 1.80 min |
| 2 | TT-322007 | 7 900 mm | 0.316 | 47.16 m3 | 12.39 min |
| 3 | TT-322006 | 14 800 mm | 0.592 | 47.16 m3 | 12.39 min |
| 4 | TT-322005 | 21 700 mm | 0.868 | 35.54 m3 | 12.39 min |

A node spans from the thermowell below it, so node 4 runs from zeta 0.592 upward and dries out
when the level falls below that, not below 0.868. The wetted volume is truncated at the live
level, which is what makes a level drop cost conversion continuously rather than in steps.

## XXIV.2 The mechanism, and which equilibrium constrains it

Two steps, the second rate-controlling (Stamicarbon / Inoue):

```
(1)  2 NH3 + CO2  <-> NH2COONH4          fast, equilibrium-limited, dH = -117 kJ/mol
(2)  NH2COONH4    <-> NH2CONH2 + H2O     rate-controlling, dH = +15.5 kJ/mol
```

Step 1 is taken to completion in the liquid — the standard assumption at 140 bar a and N/C
around 3 — so essentially all the CO2 in the melt is carbamate, and the axial march that
carries CO2 is carrying the carbamate inventory.

**Which equilibrium limits the conversion was got wrong once in V1, and the mistake is worth
recording because the wrong answer is dangerous in a training simulator.** The rate-controlling
step is dehydration, which is ENDOTHERMIC, so its own equilibrium constant rises with
temperature; constraining the march with that alone gave X = 0.92 at 200 C and X = 1.00 at
230 C, which teaches that a hotter reactor converts more. The conversion is limited by the
OVERALL reaction,

```
2 NH3 + CO2 <-> NH2CONH2 + H2O ,   dH = -117 + 15.5 = -101.5 kJ/mol
```

which is exothermic, so its attainable conversion FALLS as the column heats. That, against a
rate constant that rises, is what produces the optimum. No fitted parabola is needed and none
is used — V1's superseded correlation had one, with a fitted curvature and a fitted optimum
band, and both are retired.

Measured on the ported model, held isothermal at the design feed:

| T | k2 [1/h] | Kov [m3/kmol] | extent [kmol/h] |
|---|---|---|---|
| 183 C | 1.98 | 0.698 | 1503 |
| 201 C | — | — | **1908 (peak)** |
| 220 C | 16.67 | 0.094 | 1706 |
| 250 C | — | — | 1248 |

The optimum is interior and it is at 201 C. Past it the reactor loses conversion, which is the
behaviour an operator pushing temperature has to be taught.

## XXIV.3 The rate laws, and where they live

```
r2      = k2(T) . ( C_carb - C_urea . C_H2O / ( Kov(T) . C_NH3^2 ) )      kmol/(m3.h)
k2(T)   = A2 . exp( -Ea_dehyd / R T )                                     Arrhenius
Kov(T)  = Kov_ref . exp( -dH_overall / R . (1/T - 1/T_ref) )              van 't Hoff
```

`Ea_dehyd` is DERIVED, not asserted. Inoue & Otsuka (1973) Eq. (6) gives the REVERSE step —
urea hydrolysis — as `ln k = 21.8 - 11100/T`, so its activation energy is `11 100 . R`. For one
elementary step run both ways the two barriers differ by the step enthalpy, so

```
Ea_dehyd = 11 100 . R + 15 500 = 107 785.4 J/mol
```

with R the ROUNDED 8.314 the correlation was fitted against. The CODATA constant would move it
5.1 J/mol and the rate constant 0.13 %, which is why the two gas constants are kept apart under
names that say why.

All of that is chemistry, and it lives in `thermo/kinetics.py` beside the hydrolysis constant
it is derived from. V1 wrote the two enthalpies out three times in three units of measure —
`reactor.DH_CARB_JMOL`, `main.STRIP_DH_HYD_JMOL` (the same dehydration heat, negated, for the
stripper sump) and `main.R328_HYD_DH_KJMOL` (the same overall heat, negated, for the
hydrolyser) — and 328C003 will want them a fourth time.

The three rate-law functions take their back-solved pre-exponentials as ARGUMENTS rather than
reading module globals. That is not a physics change: it is what keeps the chemistry layer free
of plant knowledge, and it makes an uncalibrated call impossible to write rather than merely
discouraged. V1's `A2_PRE = None` sentinel exists precisely because the call was possible.

## XXIV.4 The march, and why the node integral is exact

Within a node the rate is linear in its own driving force, so the approach is first order and
has a closed form:

```
dxi/dt = k2 . (xi_eq - xi)    ->    dxi = xi_eq . ( 1 - exp(-k2 . tau_n) )
```

and that closed form is what the march uses. Multiplying the rate by the node volume instead
lets a large pre-exponential overshoot the equilibrium inside one node and reverse in the next,
which makes the total extent non-monotone in A2 and leaves the design back-solve with nothing
to converge on. The point is numerical rather than physical, but it decides whether the
calibration exists at all.

`xi_eq` is the signed extent at which the overall reaction is at equilibrium for that node's
composition, found by bisection on the bracket the stoichiometry allows — forward to
`min(CO2, NH3/2)`, reverse to `-min(Urea, H2O)`, both pulled in by one part in 1e12. Eighty
halvings, fixed, no convergence test, for the reason every solver in this engine has one.

Two early returns, and neither is an approximation: if the residual is already non-positive at
the lower bracket the stream is past equilibrium beyond what the products can supply, and if it
is still positive at the upper bracket the stoichiometry binds before equilibrium does. The
bisection is entered only when a root is genuinely enclosed.

**Activity basis, stated rather than hidden.** The march uses CONCENTRATIONS. The Extended
UNIQUAC service refuses the HP loop and is right to — finding G-VLE-3 measured the 322E003
feed at 869 mol per kg of water against a 16.0 top node on the loading grid — so an activity
coefficient at 183 C and 140 bar a would be a clamped edge lookup wearing a thermodynamic name.
This is the right place for an HP activity package when one exists.

## XXIV.5 The column exotherm as energy, and where the heat is released

```
Q_n = xi_carb,n . 117 000  -  xi_dehyd,n . 15 500        [kJ/h]
```

The two terms OPPOSE and that is the physics: carbamate formation heats the column, urea
dehydration cools it. At design the carbamate term is **9 481 kW**, the dehydration term takes
**5 607 kW** back, and what reaches the liquid is **3 874 kW** — into 226 t/h of melt at
4.741 kJ/(kg.K), which is the PFD's 13.0 C rise by construction.

The per-node heat at design is 212 / 1 226 / 1 275 / 1 111 kW, bottom to top: the release is
distributed up the whole column, not loaded at the bottom.

**That distribution is the licensor's own mechanism, not a fit.** `References/322R001
Description.md` section 4: a controlled amount of uncondensed NH3 and CO2 from the HPCC is
allowed to enter the reactor, and as the endothermic reaction cools the liquid it induces
further physical absorption and condensation of those gases from the bubbles, maintaining a
steady, slightly rising profile. For a bubbling column the interfacial area per unit liquid
volume is uniform, so the absorption is taken proportional to each node's liquid volume — which
introduces no fitted shape parameter at all, where the superseded Damkohler form needed one.

`xi_carb` is a STREAM BALANCE and not a second kinetic prediction: the free CO2 322E002 hands
over as gas, minus the CO2 that leaves in the off-gas, is by definition what formed carbamate
in this vessel. Taking it from the streams keeps it consistent with the off-gas split instead
of letting two mechanisms disagree about one quantity.

**Against the plant's own trend.** The 1921-sample means in
`References/Urea_NormalOp_29-06-2025_Trends.md`, against the ported profile:

| thermowell | TT-322008 | TT-322007 | TT-322006 | TT-322005 | RMS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| plant (measured) | 171.134 | 174.303 | 179.697 | 183.084 | — |
| this model | 170.721 | 174.893 | 179.228 | 183.000 | **0.43 C** |
| V1's retired Damkohler shape | 172.613 | 180.791 | 182.530 | 182.900 | 3.66 C |

The fitted shape was 6.5 C wrong at TT-322007: it put nearly the whole rise below the second
thermowell, where the real profile is very nearly linear. V1's own comment quotes 0.78 C for
the volume-distributed form and a profile of 170.77 / 173.60 / 178.20 / 183.00 — those figures
predate the joint solve of XXIV.6 and the code no longer produces them. Re-measured here
against the same trend and pinned by a test.

## XXIV.6 The two back-solves, and why the second is joint

No vendor kinetics exist for this reactor. The licensor sells a converged design, so two
numbers have to come from the plant — the same treatment the Phase 2 valve coefficients got,
and bounded the same way: **one design point determines one parameter.**

```
Kov_ref  <-  the conversion CEILING X_INF.  At the ceiling the overall reaction is at
             equilibrium by definition, so the quotient is evaluated directly at the
             composition that ceiling implies.  No iteration.
A2       <-  the design urea EXTENT, 1302.27 kmol/h.  Geometric bisection over thirty
             decades; the march is monotone in A2, so there is no wrong root to find.
biuret A <-  the design biuret EXTENT, 2.414 kmol/h.  Linear in its own pre-exponential
             and it does not deplete what it feeds on, so it divides straight out.
```

**The second is solved JOINTLY with the temperature profile, and has to be.** Closing the
energy balance means the reactor temperature is no longer imposed: node temperatures set the
extents, the extents set the heat, the heat sets the node temperatures. A pre-exponential
back-solved at a guessed profile is a pre-exponential at the wrong temperatures, and V1
measured exactly that when it first closed the loop — 1236 kmol/h against 1302.27, with the
column settling at 184.42 C rather than 183.0.

Two plant anchors, two unknowns, one fixed point:

```
T_overflow == 183.0 C         (PFD)   ->  the axial profile
xi_urea    == 1302.27 kmol/h  (PFD)   ->  A2
```

400 damped sweeps, 50 % on the profile and a 0.7 exponent on the pre-exponential correction,
because the loop is stiff — an Arrhenius rate on top of an equilibrium approach — and an
undamped step oscillates. It runs once at import and takes milliseconds; settling the whole
plant for each trial value takes a quarter of an hour, which is why the calibration lives in
the unit and not in the engine's boot.

Solved on the PFD design vectors, deliberately not on a live capture. V1 tried both live
references and both are the wrong operating point: the warm-up settle sits on an attractor
whose carbamate balance reads 253 kmol/h against the 279 the runtime produces, and a post-reset
capture is one tick off the seed, which is the seed.

**The one back-solved constant in the energy balance is the melt heat capacity**, 4.741
kJ/(kg.K), fixed by the PFD column rise. The repository has no heat capacity for a 140 bar a
ammoniacal carbamate/urea melt; `urea_soln_cp` is anchored on an aqueous value from the
evaporation section and gives 3.6096 here, which lands the rise at 15.30 C against 13.0.
Fixing c_p is the right choice of the available ones: it is a genuine physical property, it is
the one the repository is missing, and 4.7 is entirely ordinary for a melt about 29 % ammonia
by mass — liquid NH3 alone runs above 5 at these conditions. Fixing a wall-loss coefficient
instead would have implied 18 W/(m2.K) on an insulated HP shell, which is not credible. And it
is not a free parameter fighting the other anchors: once A2 is calibrated the duty is fully
determined by the two anchored extents, so `c_p = Q/(m.dT)` closes on itself and the joint
solve converges straight back to it.

**Two things the calibration leaves undone, both recorded as handoff items.**

* The **biuret** pre-exponential is solved at the SEED profile and never re-solved, while the
  dehydration one is. The final profile is 2.75 C colder on the node mean, which at 85 kJ/mol
  is a factor of 1.15, so the design biuret extent comes out **2.0737 against the PFD's 2.414,
  14.1 % low** — on the plant's principal product-quality specification. Handoff **B-14**.
* Two design **throughputs** on two density bases, 0.42 % apart: the calibration divides by the
  PFD's constant 990 kg/m3, the boot anchor by the melt density at the column's own bulk
  temperature, 994.19. Residence time is throughput, so that is 0.28 % of extent. Handoff
  **B-15**.

V1 covers both by re-running the whole calibration at boot against a settled plant. Nothing at
import can do that, in V1 or here.

## XXIV.7 The vapour disengagement, and a fixed point worth checking

The licensor's split vector is derived from the two published product vectors, so the design
point is bit-exact by construction:

```
theta_i = offgas_des,i / ( overflow_des,i + offgas_des,i )
```

Frozen, it has a derivative of exactly zero — the reactor could run 20 C hot or 10 bar low and
not one mole would move between the melt and the off-gas, which is the wrong answer for a
vessel whose whole job is holding NH3 and CO2 in the liquid. So it is re-flashed live by
`anchored_split`: back-solve the design K-values from the calibrated split against the LIVE
feed, multiply them by the K-value ratio, and RE-SOLVE Rachford-Rice so the phase ratio moves
and the species are coupled through the overall balance.

**Urea, biuret and the four inerts never distribute, and that falls out of the arithmetic
rather than an exception list.** Urea and biuret have zero off-gas so their theta is exactly 0;
N2, O2, CH4 and H2 have zero overflow so theirs is exactly 1; and the flash only ever touches
species strictly between. A reactor that dissolved its own nitrogen would be a new claim, and
there is no datum for one.

**One thing had to be measured rather than assumed.** At a unit ratio the K-values are the
back-solved ones, but that does NOT algebraically guarantee the re-solve returns the
calibrated vector: the phase ratio the splits imply, `psi_des = sum_i z_i theta_i`, need not be
the Rachford-Rice root of the K-values they back-solve to. At the design vector it is, to
7e-16 — three distributing species, psi_des = 0.112846, and the residual at that psi is
1.8e-16. That is what lets the published overflow survive a live re-flash, and it is now a test
rather than a comment.

## XXIV.8 The two conservative composition shifts

Both exist so an analyser can respond to something it must respond to, and both move species
BETWEEN the two product streams rather than creating any.

**AT-322701, the excess-ammonia partition.** With the recycle pinned, the reactor-to-stripper
N/C is atom-locked: an operator can move the feed ratio and the analyser will not move. The
shift moves ammonia only, so total nitrogen and total carbon are both held:

```
d_NH3 = 0.5 . (L_feed/L_ref - 1) . NH3_overflow,des . s
```

bounded by 90 % of the off-gas ammonia one way and half the overflow ammonia the other.

**The conversion-deficit slip.** When the reactor converts less than its design reference, the
ammonia and CO2 it failed to convert leave as gas rather than as melt:

```
delta_X = max(1 - X_conv/X_ref, 0)
shift_k = min(delta_X . offgas_k, overflow_k)      for k in NH3, CO2
```

One-sided and floored at zero, so a reactor at or above design shifts nothing. It replaces an
earlier amplifier that multiplied the off-gas by `1 + g`, which CREATED mass, and the loop it
fed drifted.

Both are written on deviations, so both are identically zero at the pinned design state — and
both references are boot pins for that reason. `L_ref` in particular: the reactor's design feed
N/C is **3.078581** against the live-probed `L0_DES` of 3.072961, a 0.18 % gap that would
otherwise move 3.66 kmol/h of ammonia at the design point. See handoff **B-3**.

## XXIV.9 The inventory, the funnel and HV-322605

Level is a state of the conserved holdup MASS, not a pass-through of the inlet flow:

```
rho(T)  = rho_ref . [ 1 - beta . (T - T_ref) ]        beta = 7e-4 /K, rho_ref = 990 at 183 C
level   = m_liquid / ( rho(T_bulk) . A_cs )
```

Cooling raises the density, so a fixed mass reads a LOWER level. A reactor that loses its
exotherm loses indicated level without losing an ounce of inventory, and keeps losing it as it
cools even with the discharge shut.

The liquid leaves over an internal funnel, 1 044 mm mouth, lip at +19.3 m — **0.7 m below the
design surface** — down a 305 mm downcomer to N5 and through HV-322605. The discharge is
whichever of two restrictions passes less:

```
m_valve = m_des . Kv(theta) / Kv(theta_des)                     funnel flooded: the valve sets it
m_weir  = rho(T_bulk) . C_w . max(L - L_lip, 0)^1.5             funnel free: its lip sets it
m_out   = min(m_valve, m_weir)
```

At design the Kv ratio is exactly 1.0 and the weir, with 0.7 m of head over a 3.3 m
circumference, passes more than fifty times the production — so the `min` selects the valve and
the design pin is bit-exact. Below the lip the weir term is exactly zero, so **the vessel
cannot drain through N5 below the funnel**: a feed trip parks the level at the lip and only
cooling contraction takes it lower. That is a real safety-relevant behaviour and it is
structural, not a clamp.

**Why the valve sees its design differential pressure.** While the funnel is flooded the
reactor's clear-liquid head does not reach the valve. The stripper gas enters 322R001 at the
bottom nozzle, so the stripper back-pressure carries the same reactor column the downcomer
does, and the two cancel:

```
dP_valve = (rho_L - rho_mix) g z_lip + rho_L g (z_R - z_S) - dP_gas-path
```

The departures from that — gas-path losses and live liquid density — need the loop pressure
network (finding A-1) and the piping elevations, and stay open.

HV-322605's characteristic is the vendor CONVAL table (DN 200 angle valve, parabolic
single-seat plug, linear trim, Kvs 600), linear between points. The shut end is the class-IV
seat, `(0 %, 0)`, not the trim line's 12 m3/h intercept — interpolating that line to zero
stroke would leave the reactor draining at 2 % of full flow with the valve closed.

## XXIV.10 The node energy balance, and the wall loss that is off at design

```
dT_n/dt = [ (T_{n-1} - T_n) + Q_n/(m_dot . c_p) ] / tau_n
          - (1 - flow_frac) . (T_n - T_amb) / tau_loss
```

The first term is the lumped node balance divided through by `m_dot . c_p`. The second is the
shell's heat loss to a 40 C ambient over a six-hour time constant, GATED on flow.

The gate is exactly zero at design flow, so the as-built profile is bit-exact — the exotherm
anchor already nets out the design-flow loss and counting it twice would cool the column below
the PFD. It opens to full strength as flow collapses, so a stagnant reactor, whose flow term
has gone to zero with it, relaxes toward ambient instead of freezing at whatever temperature it
stopped at. A trainee who trips the feed and walks away should come back to a cold reactor.

The gate is written `min(max(1 - flow_frac, 0), 1)` rather than through the engine's `clamp`,
and the difference is not cosmetic: the two disagree on NaN. V1's form propagates it; `clamp`
would return 1.0 and silently apply full wall loss to a broken temperature.

## XXIV.11 What was not ported

V1's `reactor.py` still carries the whole superseded Inoue-Kanai separable correlation —
`inoue_kanai_X`, `conversion_factor`, `t_opt_c`, `f_T_parabola`, `react_couple`, `X_DES_RAW`
and the four coefficients they were fitted with (a = 3.6180, b = 0.85, k = 0.0015 /C2, an
N/C-dependent optimum clipped to [185, 195] C). Not one has a live call site left in `main.py`;
the three remaining mentions are comments. Neither do `node_heat_weights`, `node_tau_s` or
`holdup_dmdt_kgph`, which `step_sim` inlines, nor `TANK_AREA_M2`, a default cross-section V1
labels ILLUSTRATIVE and which is wrong — 5.31 m2 against the real 6.835 — but never reached,
because every call passes the true area.

Two things survive the retired correlation and are carried as constants: **X_INF = 0.9140**,
the thermodynamic ceiling the overall equilibrium constant is anchored on, and **X_DES =
0.543**, the published per-pass conversion, used as the deficit-slip reference before the
engine pins a live one.

The engine wiring stays for Phase 5, as the ejector's instrument lag does: the recycle
inventory lag on the feed ratios, the Euler integration of the four node temperatures and the
holdup, the forward-carbamate pulse from the ejector, the flood carryover to 322E003 and the
LT-322504 narrow-band display. Every right-hand side those need is in `reactor_hydraulics.py`,
so Phase 5 wires rather than derives. V1 divides it the same way.

## XXIV.12 Design closure

All 24 published fields and all 60 named constants agree with V1 to the bit, over sixteen
operating points. The axial profile is 170.721 / 174.893 / 179.228 / 183.000 C, rising
monotonically and landing on the PFD overflow temperature exactly; the urea extent is
1302.27 kmol/h, a per-pass
conversion of 0.5418; the holdup is 135 904 kg at 994.19 kg/m3; and with the four boot pins
supplied the overflow and off-gas CO2 and H2O come back as the published stream table exactly,
with nitrogen closing to the biuret shortfall of B-14.

Turndown raises per-pass conversion — 0.660 at 70 % load against 0.542 at design and 0.510 at
110 % — because the wetted volume is geometry and the residence time scales inversely with
flow. V1 measured the opposite sign before its throughput scaling was added, and that is what
the scaling is for.

**One thing V1 needs a correction pass for and this port does not.** V1 derives the bulk melt
temperature, density and holdup against the import-time seed profile, because the holdup has to
exist before the energy balance can be solved; it then replaces the profile twice and never
re-solves them, so its seeded holdup and its seeded profile are two design points 0.9 C apart.
V1's `_rederive_react_bulk_anchors()` traces the consequence in its own docstring: a 0.156 %
level step on the first tick, straight into the conversion, into the one-sided conversion
deficit that cannot average out, and from there into TIC-329005's load term and the CCW
condensation gate. Here the three are simply derived after the fixed point, which needs no
pass; the equivalence test asserts against V1's post-re-derive values.


# Part XXV — Unit 322E003: the HP scrubber

## XXV.1 What the vessel is, and the number that pays for it

A vertical falling-film reactive absorber at the top of the synthesis loop. Inert-rich
off-gas from the reactor rises through the tubes; cold weak carbamate from the 323 section
falls down the tube walls. Ammonia and carbon dioxide cross into the film and react there,

    2 NH3(aq) + CO2(aq) <-> NH2COONH4(l)        dH ~ -160 kJ/mol

practically instantaneously, so the liquid-phase concentrations of both stay near zero and
the transfer is gas-film controlled. Tempered cooling water on the shell carries the exotherm
away; if the film is allowed to heat up, Le Chatelier shifts the equilibrium back and
absorption stops. That single sentence is why the shell-side model is as much of this unit as
the mass balance.

The synthesis loop is not closed. Inerts arrive dissolved in the CO2 feed and with the
passivation air, and if they are not purged they blanket the carbamate condenser and the
reactor top. But the only gas available to purge them in is saturated with ammonia. The
measured design numbers:

| | kmol/h | kg/h |
|---|---|---|
| ammonia entering the tubes | 1329.23 | 22 637 |
| ammonia leaving with the vent | 5.351 | 91.1 |
| ammonia in the reactor off-gas alone | 665.73 | 11 338 |

**99.60 % recovery.** Without this vessel the plant would throw away 11.3 t/h of ammonia in
order to get rid of 58 kmol/h of nitrogen, oxygen, methane and hydrogen. The vent it produces
instead is 1708 kg/h and **89.26 mol % inert**, and that inert fraction is the cleanest single
indicator that the wash is working.

## XXV.2 The vent is solved and the overflow is a difference — finding A-2

This is the structural decision the whole unit rests on, and it is worth stating why the
obvious alternative fails.

The obvious way round is to pin the overflow on its published row and let the vent absorb
whatever the balance leaves over. V1 did exactly that, and it does not work, because the
loop's design flows do not close to better than a couple of tonnes an hour while the vent is
the smallest stream in the section. The reconciled vent came out at **214.8 kmol/h and
44 mol % ammonia — 5901 kg/h against the published 1708** — a three-and-a-half-fold error on
the one stream whose entire purpose is to be small. A modelled plant that vents four tonnes an
hour of ammonia it does not vent will teach the wrong lesson about every purge decision an
operator makes.

Solving the vent from its own physics and taking the overflow by difference inverts the
dependency:

    vent_j    = feed_j                                        j over the inerts
    vent_c    = n_inert . y_c / (1 - sum_c y_c)               c over NH3, CO2, H2O
    overflow  = feed - vent

The unit then **closes per species by construction**. The residual it publishes is a
diagnostic that reads exactly 0.0, never a correction injected anywhere, and the test suite
asserts that at seven states including a flood with the cooling lost.

What comes out at the design feed, against the published stream rows:

| | model | PFD 204 / 206 |
|---|---|---|
| vent, kmol/h | 64.787 | 64.78 |
| vent, kg/h | 1708.32 | 1708 |
| vent average molar weight | 26.368 | 26.36 |
| overflow, kmol/h | 2517.49 | 2517.69 |
| overflow, kg/h | 57 561.3 | 57 564 |

Nothing was fitted to land there. The inerts are whatever the reactor sent, and the
condensables are the published saturation.

## XXV.3 The saturated-inert closure, and where it now lives

The relation is the simplified Colburn-Hougen closure for condensation in the presence of a
non-condensable. The inerts fix the gas RATE, because every kmol that enters has to leave;
the saturation fixes its COMPOSITION; and the `1/(1 - sum y_c)` factor is the inert-basis
conversion between them. It is what makes the ammonia loss rise faster than linearly as the
top warms, and it is the same closure the 324 vacuum condensers use, so it is not a 322E003
relation and does not belong in a 322E003 module.

It went into **`thermo/splits.py`**, a module created in this session, beside the two split
primitives that were already ported:

| function | the phase ratio is | the equipment |
|---|---|---|
| `ratio_shift_frac` | FIXED by something else | a stripping column, an absorber |
| `anchored_split` | FREE, and re-solved | a flash, a reactor top |
| `saturated_inert_vent` | irrelevant — the gas rate is fixed by the inerts | a wash top, a vacuum condenser vent |

Which one a unit uses is a statement about the equipment rather than a modelling preference,
and picking the wrong one invents physics. The three were in `thermo/kvalues.py`, whose own
scope is K-values and bubble and dew points; they import nothing from it and it imports
nothing from them, so the extraction was textual and the module now imports nothing at all.
`kvalues.py` went from 636 to 499 lines and `splits.py` is 254. Every consumer reaches them
through `thermo.service`, which is the only edit the move required.

Two limits are part of the closure and neither is a tuning limiter:

* **`y_max = 0.95`.** As the condensables approach filling the gas the inert-basis factor
  diverges — the closure is being asked about a gas with no inerts in it, which is a
  condition it does not describe. The saturation is scaled back proportionally, so the
  measured RELATIVE saturation between the three condensables survives and only the
  divergence is removed. It is four times the design sum of 0.1074 and never binds in normal
  operation.
* **The feed cap.** A condensable cannot leave faster than it arrives. Handed an
  ammonia-starved feed the closure vents the 0.4 kmol/h it has and no more.

## XXV.4 The wash, and the reason a surplus of it does nothing

The wash is PFD stream 308: 36 915 kg/h at 38.49 % CO2, 30.83 % H2O, 30.61 % NH3 and 0.07 %
urea by mass, which is 1618.5 kmol/h at 22.81 kg/kmol. The liquid rows of the PFD stream table
are mass per cent and the gas rows are mole per cent; both readings were confirmed against the
published average molar weights, which the correct basis reproduces and the other does not.

Measured, over a 0.8 / 1.0 / 1.2 sweep of the delivered wash:

* the overflow grows by 7383 kg/h for each 20 % of extra wash, as it must;
* **the vent does not move by one bit** — the same float at all three;
* **the CO2 absorbed does not move either** — 196.25 kmol/h at all three.

That is A-2's claim made measurable. What the cold top can hold is set by the saturation and
the inert rate, not by how much liquid is running past it. The surplus-wash absorption gain
this replaced — 0.15 kmol of CO2 per kmol of extra wash — was asserting the opposite.

The engine passes what 323P001 A/B actually delivered; a unit-level caller that omits it gets
the CO2 throughput ratio instead. Before that distinction existed, a 787 kg/h sag in the wash
during a LIC-323502 cascade transient left the loop boundary short while the scrubber went on
condensing a design wash the pump was not sending.

## XXV.5 The shell side — one back-solve, two pinned temperatures

The cooling water is a closed tempered loop, not once-through: 306 t/h at 80 C in and 95 C out
(PFD streams 1111 and 1112), circulated by 329P006 A/B, with FIC-329409 on the rate and
TIC-329005 on the supply temperature. It is tempered because the scrubber must not be cooled
too hard either — carbamate crystallises at about 60 C, and a solidified overflow line is
worse than a warm one.

    Q_des      = m_ccw . cp . dT = 5329.5 kW
    C_ccw,des  = m_ccw . cp / 3600 = 355.3 kW/K
    UA_eff,des = Q_des / (T_overflow,des - T_ccw,in,des) = 53.942 kW/K
    eps_des    = UA_eff,des / C_ccw,des = 0.15182
    UA         = -C_ccw,des . ln(1 - eps_des) = 58.505 kW/K

and the running form inverts it:

    eps        = 1 - exp(-UA / C_ccw)
    T_cond     = min(T_ccw,in + Q / max(eps . C_ccw, 1e-6), T_proc)
    T_ccw,out  = T_ccw,in + (T_cond - T_ccw,in) . eps

The conductance is constant and the EFFECTIVENESS floats with the water rate. That is what
makes the unit behave when FIC-329409 is throttled — measured at 200 t/h the process side is
183.05 C and the return 102.95; by 100 t/h both are against the ceiling; at zero flow the
effectiveness is exactly 1 and both sit at 185.0 rather than at the 1e9 the raw
duty-over-flow form produced. The cooling-water rise TDY-329125 goes the other way, 15.0 K at
design to 105.0 K at no flow, because the same duty is being carried by less water.

One number pins two. Anchoring the water's gradient on the LIVE condensing temperature rather
than on the ceiling is what preserves the 95.0 C return pin; against the raw ceiling it drifts
to 95.9.

**The condensation ceiling is a frequently active rail, not a rare guard.** Design sits 6.2 C
below it, and the measured thresholds that reach it acting alone are +7 % throughput, a purge
valve below 24 % open, a 35 % stronger ejector spindle, or cooling water at half the design
rate. Those are ordinary excursions. Above the rail the model reports 185.0 and stops
distinguishing a bad state from a worse one, which is worth knowing before TT-322002 goes on a
screen — and the margin is narrow partly because the design pin itself is 13 C high (XXV.7).

## XXV.6 The three duty derates, and the one that reads backwards

The base duty is `Q_des . s . nu`: throughput, and the synthesis-vent load ratio, because in a
closed loop a rise in reactor-top pressure lifts the uncondensed vent load into this vessel
and the exotherm rises with it. Three multipliers sit on top, and each is exactly 1.0 at its
design position, so the published temperatures stay pinned by the arithmetic.

**The ejector-spindle coupling**, `chi_sp = 1 + 0.25 (1 - 1/phi_sp)`. The motive jet sets how
hard the off-gas is drawn down through the bottom condensation zone, so closing HV-322602
condenses more per unit time. Measured 4758 kW at phi 0.7, 5330 at design, 5637 at 1.3. It is
driven off the same `(1 - 1/phi)` term as the reactor's forward-carbamate coupling, so the two
cannot disagree about which way that handwheel pushes.

**The flooded-surface choke**, linear from 1.0 at normal level to 0.30 at a full sump. Liquid
rising above normal level floods the condensation surface from the bottom. The signature is
the counter-intuitive one and it is worth teaching:

| LT-329501 | duty, kW | TDY-329125, K |
|---|---|---|
| 50 % (normal) | 5329.5 | 15.00 |
| 75 % | 3464.2 | 9.75 |
| 100 % | 1598.9 | 4.50 |

**The cooling-water return gets colder as the sump floods.** An operator watching the rise
fall away could read it as the duty easing off; it is the duty dying. The floor is 0.30 rather
than zero because the upper tubes stay wetted and keep condensing.

**The cooling-limited condensation gate** is the third and it acts on the streams rather than
on the duty — see XXV.9.

## XXV.7 The two published thermowells, and what they actually are

Both are correlations: a design pin plus deviation terms that are exactly zero at design.

    TT-322011 = clamp( 114.0 + 120 (AT-322701 - N/C_des) + 20 theta_dev, T_ccw,in, T_proc )
    TT-322002 = clamp( T_cond - 12 theta_dev,                            T_ccw,in, T_proc )

with `theta_dev = HIC-322604 / 50 - 1`. The two vent-opening gains have OPPOSITE signs, and
that matters: one operator action must not move two published temperatures the same way.
Measured across the full stroke, TT-322011 rises 94.0 -> 134.0 C as the valve opens, because
more uncondensed vapour goes over the top, while TT-322002 falls 185.0 -> 166.8 C, because
relieving the vessel cools the bottom carbamate.

The ammonia-slip gain is the physics of a CO2-limited loop: at high feed N/C the excess
ammonia has no carbon to form carbamate with, slips through unabsorbed, and its vapour load
lifts the vent top. 120 C per unit of N/C, so 0.2 of analyser movement is 24 C.

The analyser reference is the REACTOR overflow's N/C, not this vessel's, because AT-322701
sits on the reactor product line; it measures 2.99975 on an atom basis. Writing the
correlation as a deviation from it is what makes the 114.0 C pin exact.

Both rails are physical rather than range checks: neither published temperature can fall below
the water that is cooling it or rise above the condensation ceiling. That is the right pair of
rails precisely because the gains are fitted — pushed hard enough, an unrailed correlation
would publish a vent hotter than the reactor.

## XXV.8 FINDING: TT-322002's design pin is a pseudo-temperature (handoff B-16)

The design overflow temperature is pinned at **178.8 C**. Both of its sources say otherwise:

* **PFD stream 206** gives 165 C, and V1's own comment elsewhere quotes stream 206 at 165 C
  when it is reading the density off the same row.
* **The plant** reads TT-322002 at a mean of **165.696 C** over the 1921-sample normal
  operation trend, with a range of 164.1 to 167.1.

Two independent sources, 13.1 C below the pin, and they agree with each other to 0.7 C.

Where the number comes from is traceable. V1 sets `SCRUB_OVERFLOW_T_C = EJ_T_SUCTION_C`, and
`EJ_T_SUCTION_C` is the 322F001 ejector's suction temperature, whose own comment says the
carbamate heat of mixing is *lumped into it* so the ejector's discharge enthalpy comes out
right without a separate mixing term. That is a legitimate enthalpy-carrying pseudo-temperature
for the ejector. It is not a thermowell reading, and publishing it as one is the defect.

It is ported exactly, because directive 5.2 makes the anchoring part of the equation and the
shell-side conductance is back-solved against this number: with 165 C the conductance would be
62.7 rather than 53.94 kW/K, a 16 % change in the unit's off-design temperature gain. The
95.0 C cooling-water pin is NOT affected, because the design rise is the duty over the
heat-capacity rate and is independent of the approach.

The consequences are two, and they are recorded rather than fixed:

* a trainee comparing the simulator's TT-322002 with the plant's sees 13 C;
* the condensation ceiling's headroom above design is 6.2 C instead of about 20, which is why
  ordinary excursions reach the rail (XXV.5).

## XXV.9 FINDING: the vent-top correlation overshoots the plant's own trend (handoff B-17)

Driven at the plant's own normal-operation means — HIC-322604 at 78.188 %, AY-322701 at 3.236,
TIC-329005 at 84.459 C and PT-329201 at 139.603 bar a — the TT-322011 correlation predicts
**153.6 C against a measured 130.316 C**. It overshoots by 23.3 C, in the direction its gains
drive: the ammonia-slip term alone contributes +28.3 C and the vent-opening term +11.3 C,
against a total measured departure from the 114.0 C pin of +16.3 C.

Both gains are calibrated rather than sourced and V1 says so. No trend in `References/` moves
either of them in isolation, so this one steady record cannot separate the two, and the
reference N/C is itself in question through B-3 — at the settled melt ratio of 3.12324 the
prediction falls to 138.8 C, still 8.5 C high. What is needed is a trend that steps
HIC-322604 at a held analyser reading. The measurement is pinned by a test so that the
question is not re-opened from memory.

TT-322002 at the same operating point comes out at 175.7 C against the measured 165.7, and
what is left of that gap after the vent term has pulled 3 C off it is B-16's anchor.

## XXV.10 Losing the cooling, and why a mass balance cannot see it

Carbamate formation is strongly exothermic, so the rate at which the shell can put NH3 and CO2
into the liquid is limited by the rate at which the water can carry the exotherm away. The
capacity ratio is

    f_th = (T_cond(P) - T_ccw,in) / (T_cond,des - T_ccw,in,des)
    rho  = (m_ccw / m_ccw,des) . pump_frac . max(f_th, 0) / s

and there are **three independent ways to lose it**, which is what makes the scenario
teachable: throttle the water, lose the temper, or stop the pumps. Each reads exactly 1.0 at
design so the product does too, and the gate is inert there.

The pump fraction is deliberately separate from the flow term. The flow term reads the
FT-329409 transmitter, which carries a 25 s lag; the circulation itself stops with the pumps,
immediately, because their discharge check valves shut. Reading the capacity off the lagged
indication alone left 0.33 % of design condensation alive long after both machines had been
stopped.

Below full capacity the fraction `(1 - rho)` of what would have condensed stays as vapour and
is moved from the overflow back to the off-gas, per species. Only the CONDENSED part can flash
back: the wash arrived as liquid and stays liquid however hot the shell gets. Measured:

| capacity | vent, kg/h | vent NH3, kmol/h |
|---|---|---|
| 1.00 | 1708 | 5.4 |
| 0.50 | 12 032 | 335.5 |
| 0.00 | 22 355 | 665.7 |

**Thirteen times the design vent, carrying the whole of the reactor off-gas ammonia.** And
nothing has crossed the loop boundary while it happens: 322E003 sits INSIDE the synthesis
loop, so a boundary mass balance reads unchanged and is blind to the event. What changes is
the specific volume of the retained mass — a kilogram held as vapour at 140.7 bar occupies
1/111 m3 instead of 1/1133 — and in an isochoric loop that frustrated expansion is pressure.

The gate carries a dead band of 1e-6, and it is not a tolerance on the physics. The capacity
is built from live controller process variables, and TIC-329005 settles on 80.00000005 C
rather than a bit-exact 80.0, which leaves the ratio at 1 - 5.3e-10. A deficit four orders
below any instrument resolution is the supply-temperature loop's own residual; treating it as
real would make the uncondensed mass non-zero at design and carry the level swell and the
loop-pressure phase term with it.

The condensing temperature rides the loop pressure through Clausius-Clapeyron on the carbamate
exotherm, `1/T_cond = 1/T_des - (R/dH) ln(P/P_des)`, measured at **0.0754 K/bar**. The slope is
small; the SIGN is the point. V1's earlier form held the condensing temperature fixed and
divided the capacity by the pressure ratio instead, which asserts that a higher loop pressure
makes a condenser weaker. With the sign wrong the loop fed back on itself — capacity fell,
vapour was retained, the pressure rose, capacity fell further — and six of the eight
design-seed inertness gaps in the cooling-water chain were that one loop.

## XXV.11 The sump, and the transmitter that lies

The sump holdup is a true state: `dM/dt = m_condensate - m_entrained`. At design the
condensate the scrubber makes and the mass the 322F001 ejector pulls are the same number, so
the derivative is exactly zero and the level sits at its 50 % normal value independently of
the inventory scale. Stall the ejector and the entrainment collapses while the condensation
continues, and the sump fills.

The inventory scale is a 4-minute residence time at design throughput, 3837 kg at normal level
and 7675 kg full. It is back-solved rather than measured — no datasheet in `References/` gives
this vessel's sump volume — and it only sets how fast the level moves, never where it settles.

**LT-329501 does not read the level.** It is a differential-pressure cell, and a DP cell reads
the hydrostatic head of whatever column stands between its taps. Stop condensing and the sump
boils: the mixture density collapses with the void fraction and the column swells upward to
hold the same mass. Over a fast transient the swell beats the density loss, so the cell reads
HIGH while the vessel is actually draining — and it is draining, because the drain to 322F001
keeps pulling after the condensate make has stopped.

Measured: a sump actually holding **40 %** is displayed at **58 %** with condensation lost, and
the reading hunts across roughly 56 to 60 % as the 17 s slug period and the 7.3 s bubble period
beat against each other. The periods are driven off the simulation clock rather than a random
number generator, because an instructor must be able to replay the same excursion the same way.

Both terms scale with the condensation deficit, so at design they are identically zero and the
indication IS the level, to the bit, at any point on the clock.

The trainee is meant to reach past the level they can see to the evidence that is telling the
truth — the cooling-water rise, which is collapsing. The integration itself is the engine's, as
the reactor's node temperatures are; every right-hand side Phase 5 needs is in this module.

## XXV.12 What moved, and what was not ported

Three things moved to their producer, and none is a physics change.

* **PFD stream 206** left `data/unit_322f001.py`, where it had been a literal while the
  scrubber was unported, and is now derived in `data/unit_322e003.py` from the reactor off-gas,
  the wash and the vent. The derived vector reproduces the literal **to the bit**, so nothing
  about the ejector's design point moved when the two were joined.
* **The loop design pressure**, 140.7 bar a, left `data/unit_320.py` for the same reason: the
  tag is PT-329201 and it sits on this vessel's overflow line. `unit_320` re-exports it under
  V1's own alias `SYN_P_DES_BARA` — V1 writes precisely the same assignment — so every
  existing call site is untouched and the CO2 tie-in differential stays a bit-exact
  subtraction of one float.
* **The three split primitives** left `thermo/kvalues.py` for `thermo/splits.py` (XXV.3).

`react_nc_ratio` became `core/stream.py` `atom_ratio`, taking its atom maps and its span as
arguments so the core layer holds no plant data. The span exists because the denominator can
reach zero: cut the CO2 feed and the loop's carbon drains away against an ammonia inventory
that does not, and V1 measured a raw ratio of 6.1e9 on a tripped loop. A real analyser has a
span and pegs at it.

Four V1 constants in this block have no reader anywhere in V1 and are recorded rather than
ported, per the reachable-only rule: `SCRUB_OFFGAS_MOL_DES` (the published 64.78 kmol/h,
superseded by the derived vent total), `SCRUB_CARB_KMOLH_DES_REF` (a frozen copy of the wash
kept as a deviation datum), and `SCRUB_CARB_T_C` / `SCRUB_CARB_P_BARA` (the wash inlet state,
PFD 308 at 74 C and 140.7 bar a). The FV-329409 and TV-329005 design openings and the two CCW
controller tunings are V1's too, but they belong to the 329 tempered-water loop rather than to
this vessel and they land when that loop does.

HV-322604 is the next unit, not this one. This module publishes the off-gas at the scrubber
nozzle; the valve decides how much of it actually passes, and the difference matters precisely
in the loss-of-cooling scenario, where the vessel offers thirteen times what a DN-24 trim was
sized for.

## XXV.13 Design closure

All 23 published fields, all 40 named scalar constants and all 7 design vectors agree with V1
to the bit, over twenty-seven operating points spanning load turndown and overload, the loop
pressure from 128 to 151 bar a, hot and cold cooling water, the water halved and shut, the
purge valve at both stops, the analyser either side of its reference, a flooding and a full
sump, both spindle directions, the condensation capacity at 1, 0.5 and 0, a short and a
surplus wash, a reactor flood, and one case with all of them at once.

The design self-call reproduces PFD 204 and PFD 206 exactly, TT-322011 at 114.0 C, the
cooling-water return at exactly 95.0 C and TDY-329125 at exactly 15.0 K, with every optional
argument at its default — which is the statement that none of the deviation terms is doing any
work at the design state. TT-322002 comes back as 178.799999999999955, one bit off the literal
178.8 out of the effectiveness-NTU inversion, and V1 produces the same float.

The published absorption duty is 8722 kW against the 5330 kW the water removes. The two are
separately anchored rather than solved together — one is the full reaction enthalpy on the CO2
the gas lost, the other is the PFD's cooling-water balance — and the 64 % gap is what that
costs. It is a diagnostic; the shell-side balance is what sets the temperatures.
