# Part XXXII — 323E011 and 323D011: the flash condenser and the LP flash gas node

## XXXII.1 What the unit is

323E011 is the cooling-water condenser on unit 323's LP flash gas: the 323F004 flash vapour
(PFD 701), the 328D001 reflux-drum vent (786) and the 323D001 vent of the LP carbamate condenser
(321), with an ammonia-water wash from 328D003 (791) that absorbs them. Its condensate falls by
gravity through the DN 100 N2 nozzle into 323D011 directly beneath it, and 323P008 pumps it out as
lean carbamate, PFD 718: 718B to 323E003 on FIC-323418, 718A to 328D001 as the unmetered remainder
of LIC-323503's draw. What does not condense leaves through PV-323203 to 323C005, PFD 702. The PFD
closes the condenser exactly, 701 + 786 + 321 + 791 = 7563 = 718 (7123) + 702 (440) kg/h; the 3.39
kg/h its rounding carries beyond the four modelled inlets is charged at 701's temperature and kept
in every tick's inlet.

There is no valve between 323F004 and 323E011, nor between 323E011 and 323D011: the drum, the
vapour line, the condenser shell and the tank are ONE gas space at one pressure, and PV-323203 is
the only element on it. The envelope integrated here is the condenser shell less its 382-tube
bundle plus the tank — 4.375 m3, 3.14 m3 of it vapour at design. Everything is in
`units/recirc/flash_condenser.py`, with the design basis in `data/unit_323e011.py`.

## XXXII.2 The node: how the stroke, the condensation and the pressure are related

The node integrates its moles on the free volume (report A-6, `core.node.vessel_dpdt`):

$$
\frac{dP}{dt} = \frac{R\,T}{V_v}\left(\frac{\dot m_{gen}}{M_{702}} - \frac{\dot m_{702}}{M_{702}}\right)
+ \frac{P}{T}\frac{dT}{dt} - \frac{P}{V_v}\frac{dV_v}{dt},\qquad P \ge 0.1\ \mathrm{bar\,a}
$$

with $M_{702}$ = 17.395 kg/kmol (PFD 702, 89 wt% ammonia), the thermal term on the temperature
change of the tick before (a tear, zero at the seed), and $V_v$ shrinking as the tank fills. The
two rates are the condenser's and the valve's:

$$
\dot m_{gen} = \max(G - C,\ 0),\qquad G = \dot m_{701}' + \dot m_{786} + \dot m_{321} + 3.39,\qquad C = 5589\ \mathrm{kg/h}
$$

$$
\dot m_{702} = 440\,\frac{h}{25}\sqrt{\frac{\max(P - 1.0,\ 0.001)}{0.13}}
$$

where $\dot m_{701}'$ is PFD 701 less what LV-323505 blows through to 323F010 plus what LV-323501
blows through from 323C003, and $h$ is PV-323203's stroke. **The condensing rate is a constant.**
$C$ is the design gas load less the design vent; it does not depend on the node pressure,
TT-323011 or the cooling water. So wherever the gas exceeds it the node settles where the valve
passes the excess,

$$
P^* = 1.0 + 0.13\left(\frac{25\,(G - C)}{440\,h}\right)^2,\qquad
h^* = \frac{25\,(G - C)}{440}\ \ \text{to hold}\ P^* = 1.13,
$$

and 1.13 bar a is simply $h$ = 25 % against $G - C$ = 440 kg/h. Measured on the unit alone:

| state | $G - C$ | stroke | node |
|---|---|---|---|
| design | 440 kg/h | 25 % (AUTO) | 1.1300 bar a |
| PV-323203 in MAN | 440 | 10 % | 1.8125 |
| PV-323203 in MAN | 440 | 50 % | 1.0325 |
| PFD 701 up 10 % | 883 | 25 % (MAN) | 1.5231 = 1 + 0.13 (883 / 440)$^2$ |
| PV-323203 shut | 440 | 0 % | no steady state: 7.1 bar a at 100 s, 25.0 at 400 s (24.9 on the vendor valves, §XL.3) |
| PFD 701 down 10 % | 0 | any | no steady state: the 0.1 bar a floor (§XXXII.3) |

The node is fast. At design it holds 2.07 kg of vapour per bar and the vent passes 1692 kg/h more
per bar, a time constant of 4.4 s; a 10 % rise in PFD 701 with the stroke held takes it from 1.13
to 1.31 bar a in 4.4 s and 1.42 in 10 s.

## XXXII.3 FINDING: what holds the node is 323F004's flash, not the condenser (handoff B-30)

*Decided 2026-10-15 (decision 114): the port's 323E011 condenses on its dew point and its vent never
runs backwards, §LXIX.1; what follows is V1's, which the harnesses keep.*

With the condenser's capacity constant, the node's restoring force has to come from elsewhere,
and in the coupled plant it does: 323F004 takes the node's pressure as its own one tick later
(Part XXIX), so a lower node lowers the drum's bubble point and flashes more PFD 701, which raises
$G$. At design that is about 2800 kg/h of flash per bar — more than the vent's 1700. Measured with
the ported 323F004 on the ported condenser, both bit-exact with V1:

| upset | alone | coupled to 323F004 |
|---|---|---|
| 10 % less gas: PFD 701 alone, the column bottoms coupled | the 0.1 bar a floor, 178 s (MAN) or 182 s (AUTO) after | 1.043 bar a, 4230 kg/h of flash, 243 kg/h still vented |
| PV-323203 shut | 25 bar a at 400 s and rising | 1.287 bar a: the flash has fallen to 3984 kg/h, exactly the capacity |

Alone, below the capacity, nothing is generated and the vent empties the node; its differential
is floored at 0.001 bar, so PV-323203 keeps passing 38 kg/h at 25 % out of a node below the
1.0 bar a absorber it discharges to, and walks it to the 0.1 bar a floor. Coupled, the floor is
reached whenever the flash cannot make up the gap — a stripper trip, which stops the flash, does
it in 180 s on V1's gain (§XXXII.7; on the gain decided since, §XXXII.11, the vent shuts first). A
physical condenser's capacity rises with its dew point; V1's own 323E003 carries that form
(Part XXXIII).

## XXXII.4 PIC-323203 (handoff B-32, decided 2026-09-27)

DIRECT acting, Ti 100 s, derivative off, set point 0.5 to 2.0 bar a. The DCS table gives Kc 0.60,
and V1 applies it in engineering units, %/bar. A DCS gain is per cent of output per per cent of
span; PT-323203 is calibrated 0 to 1 bar g (Uhde loop summary UD-MR-323-EC-0001, loop P 323203 —
the transmitter sits on 323F004), so the loop V1 runs is 100 times weaker than the DCS's. On V1's
gain, measured on the unit alone: PFD 701 up 10 % takes the node to 1.51 bar a within a minute and
the loop has it back to 1.34 an hour later; a set point of 1.30 reaches 1.14 in ten minutes and
1.17 in an hour, the stroke at 21.8 % of the 16.5 % it needs. In V1 the node is set by the stroke
and 323F004, and PIC-323203 trims it over hours. The process engineer decided the rescale: the
port runs 60 %/bar (§XXXII.11).

## XXXII.5 323D011 and the 718 draw

$$
\frac{dM}{dt} = G + 3.39 + \dot m_{791} - \dot m_{702} - \dot m_{718A} - \dot m_{718B},\qquad M \ge 1\ \mathrm{kg}
$$

Everything not vented lands in the tank. LT-323503 reads $M / 1187.2 \cdot 50$ %: the design holdup
is ten minutes of the design draw, at the OEM's 50 %. **LIC-323503** (Kc 1.8, Ti 120 s, the DCS pair
unscaled, its PV being already in per cent) sets the total draw demand, $7123 \cdot op / 50$ kg/h.
**FIC-323418** meters 718B by volume — `FlowLoop` with a 45 s transmitter, Kc 1.00 read per cent
of FT-323418's 0-10 m3/h span, 10 %/(m3/h) (decided 2026-09-30, handoff B-41, Part XXXVII; V1 runs
$1.0 \cdot 1065$), Ti 100 s — and 718A is the demand less 718B's SET POINT, not its measured flow: chasing the lagged flow
coupled the two legs into a two-tick limit cycle in V1. In MAN the stroke is the operator's and the
flow itself is used. 718A reaches 328D001 through a first-order line lag whose time constant is the
line's 44.5 kg over the live flow (report D-8), capped at 3600 s. V1's comments place the 734 flush
into 323D011; its code does not, and the PFD's closure agrees with the code — ported as the code.

## XXXII.6 TT-323011: the energy balance (handoff B-31)

*Decided 2026-10-16 (decision 118, handoff B-31): the port charges these inlets at their producers' live temperatures as departures from the producers' designs, §LXX.2; what follows is V1's, which ``live_inlets=False`` keeps.*

$$
M c_p\frac{dT}{dt} = \sum \dot m_{in}c_p(T_{in} - T) + \dot m_{cond}\,\lambda - UA\,(T - 35),\qquad
\dot m_{cond} = \max(G + 3.39 - \dot m_{702},\ 0)
$$

$c_p$ = 3.0, V1's unsourced lean-carbamate value; UA = 344 kW/K from the datasheet's 3440 kW across
10 K to the 35 C mean of its 30 / 40 C water; $\lambda$ = 2038.7 kJ/kg back-solved so the design
holds. The step is semi-implicit in the inlets and the water, as every LP stage is. The inlets are
charged at their design temperatures — 701 at 106 C, 786 at 61, 321 at 74, 791 at 56 — whatever
their sources do (B-31). And the energy balance condenses $G + 3.39 - \dot m_{702}$ where the
pressure balance condenses $\min(G, C)$: the two agree only in steady state (B-30). The flash lost
from design cools TT-323011 to 37.8 C in four hours.

## XXXII.7 FINDING: V1's FIC-323418 pumps an empty tank (handoff B-33, decided 2026-09-27)

In V1 718B is held at its set point whatever the tank holds, and LIC-323503 can cut only 718A.
With the 323F004 flash lost — a stripper trip — 3136 kg/h still arrives and 3561.5 is drawn: the
node reaches its floor 180 s later, the tank its 1 kg floor 31 minutes after the trip, and the
floor then makes up what the pump takes, 2.78 t in four hours. The process engineer decided the
heel cap already decided for 323D002 (§XXXI.9); it is §XXXII.11.

## XXXII.8 323E003 / 323D001: the other LP gas node

V1's LPCC closes the node PT-323201 rides through the column's friction head, condenses on its
dew point, and vents into THIS node through PV-323202 on the live differential — so a 323E011
node at its floor raises PFD 321 by 22 %. Surveyed here in session 20 and ported in session 21:
Part XXXIII, with the survey's measurements.

## XXXII.9 Structure, and what is not here

`FlashCondenser` holds the tank holdup, TT-323011, the temperature of the tick before, the node
pressure and the 718A lag; `step` takes PIC-323203, LIC-323503, FIC-323418 (a `FlowLoop`), 323F004's
flash and both blow-throughs, and the 786, 321 and 791 flows, and returns a frozen
`FlashCondenserResult`. The order is V1's: the controllers act on the state at the top of the tick;
the vent, the generation and the draws follow; the pressure steps on the OLD holdup and on the
temperature change of the tick before; the temperature and the holdup advance last.

What it publishes crosses ticks: 323F004 and PV-323202 read the node at the start of the next tick
(a `State` read in the scheduler's terms), and 702, 718A and 718B reach 323C005, 328D001 and 323E003
one tick later (tears, V1's `R3232_702`, `R3232_718A`, `R3232_718B`). Not modelled, in V1 or here:
any composition — the node, the tank and PFD 718 carry none — the cooling-water circuit, and
SV32357, the envelope's one relief valve, on 323D011 nozzle N6 at 5.0 bar g (handoff B-30). Since
2026-09-27 the unit also holds the 718B flow delivered on a tick 323P008 lost suction, which
FT-323418 reads on the next.

## XXXII.10 Equivalence achieved

79 tests in `test_flash_condenser_equivalence.py` (76 at the port, session 20; the scenarios
below run PIC-323203 on V1's gain, and the tank-on-its-floor scenario is now the heel's
two-sided test, §XXXII.11): the design basis (39 constants, the capacity
and the vent split); V1's `e011_vent_generation_kgh` EXECUTED at ten gas loads through and around
the capacity, and its four refusals matched message for message; the state and all three
controllers seeded field by field, FIC-323418's flow element included; nine scenarios TICK BY TICK
on the unit alone — design hold, PFD 701 up 10 % and down 10 % (to the floor), 786 doubled, 321 up
30 %, 791 halved, each blow-through, and the flash gone — and eight more: PV-323203 held at 10, 50
and 0 %, PIC-323203 on 1.30 bar a, FIC-323418 on a new set point and in MAN, LIC-323503 in MAN, and
the tank on its floor; four runs of V1's 323F004 into V1's condenser against the ported pair, the
drum riding the node — the column bottoms cut, raised and 3 C colder, and PV-323203 held open; and
one run of V1's stages 1 to 4 and 9 against the ported five through a stripper feed cut, both
blow-throughs wired to the condenser. Every tick compares every published field, the node, the
tank, both lags and all three controllers with `==`. Two mutations — the pressure step without its
thermal term, and a vent that passes nothing below 1.0 bar a — are caught at the 11th and 18th tick.
11 behaviour tests pin the pressure relationship, the floors, the coupled restoring force,
PIC-323203's pace and the empty tank.

## XXXII.11 The decided divergences (handoffs B-32, B-33), 2026-09-27

**B-32, PIC-323203 on its transmitter's span.** The table's gain is per cent of output per per
cent of PT-323203's 0-1 bar g span:

$$
K_{c,EU} = K_{c,table}\cdot\frac{100}{S} = 0.60\cdot\frac{100}{1\ \mathrm{bar}} = 60\ \%/\mathrm{bar},\qquad T_i = 100\ \mathrm{s}
$$

With the node on its set point the error is zero whatever the gain, so the design point is
bit-exact on both (600 ticks compared). Off it:

| on the unit alone | V1, 0.60 %/bar | the port, 60 %/bar |
|---|---|---|
| PFD 701 up 10 %, after a minute | 1.510 bar a | 1.252 bar a |
| the same, after an hour | 1.338 bar a, stroke 31.1 % | 1.130 bar a, stroke 50.15 % (the stroke that passes the doubled excess) |
| set point 1.30, after ten minutes / an hour | 1.136 / 1.171 bar a | 1.296 / 1.300 bar a, stroke 16.46 % |
| PFD 701 down 10 %, below the capacity | the vent walks the node to 0.1 bar a in 182 s | the vent shut within two minutes; the node stands at 0.880 bar a |
| coupled to 323F004: the column bottoms cut 10 % | 1.043 bar a, 243 kg/h vented | the vent shut; 1.129 bar a, where the flash equals the capacity |

The rescale does not give the node an equilibrium below the capacity (B-30): it stops the vent
from walking it to the floor.

**B-33, 323P008's heel.** The 718A + 718B draw is capped at the liquid above a 1 kg heel plus what
arrives on the tick, the net of the inlet and the vent:

$$
\dot m_{718A} + \dot m_{718B} \le \frac{\max(M - 1\ \mathrm{kg},\ 0)}{\Delta t}\,3600 + (\dot m_{in} - \dot m_{702})
$$

718B, the metered leg, is served first; 718A takes what is left and its line lag is reset to
what was delivered. When the cap binds the result flags `suction_lost`, and FT-323418 reads the
delivered flow on the next tick (`FlowLoop.step(flow_cap=...)`, register row 106), so FIC-323418
sees the shortfall and opens. The vent, which V1 books against the tank, is not capped (B-30).

| the flash and the 791 wash stopped on 200 kg, 1 s step, V1's PIC gain | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|
| until the heel, in the 359th second | bit-exact | bit-exact |
| 718B at the floor | 3561.5 kg/h, FIC-323418's set point | what arrives, about 1570 kg/h |
| liquor made in the next nine minutes | 299.6 kg | none (below 1e-9 kg a tick) |
| FT-323418 / FV-323418 | 3561.5 kg/h / 50 % | the delivered flow / 100 % |

The flash lost from design (the behaviour test, on the decided gain): the vent shuts 70 s after
the trip and the node stands at 0.634 bar a; the tank reaches its heel at 1967 s (1992 s on the vendor valves, §XL.3) and 323P008 then
delivers the 3136 kg/h that arrives; nothing is made in four hours, where V1 made 2.78 t.

Proof: `test_the_decided_gain_is_inert_on_the_set_point`, the two-scenario
`test_pic_323203_on_its_transmitter_span_decided_divergence` (the controllers part on the first
tick PIC-323203 sees the node off its set point, the 11th after a load step, and both sides are
asserted an hour on) and `test_the_tank_pumped_to_its_floor_decided_divergence` (both sides on
every tick after the heel). The behaviour tests were re-measured on the decided gain and heel.

# Part XXXIII — 323E003, 323D001 and 323P001: the LP carbamate condenser

## XXXIII.1 What the unit is

323E003 condenses the 323C003 overhead, PFD 305 (119 C, 24 563 kg/h), into lean carbamate from
323D011 (718B, 3561.5 kg/h) and 328D001 (776, 8275.5 kg/h), with the inert-laden 797 recycle
(1758 kg/h, 46 C), against a closed tempered-water circuit — PFD 1102 in at 55 C, 1103 out at
65 C, 14 000 kW. The liquid collects in 323D001 (11.10 m3, 74 C, 3.2 bar a) and 323P001 A/B,
three-plunger pumps on a Voith scoop-tube drive, return it to the HP synthesis as PFD 308,
36 835 kg/h. What does not condense leaves through PV-323202 to the 323E011 node, PFD 321,
1323 kg/h.

    PIC-323202 (323D001 pressure)       ->  PV-323202 (vent 321 to 323E011)
    LIC-323502 (323D001 level)          ->  SIC-323901 (323P001A speed)  ->  PFD 308
    TIC-323013 (tempered-water supply)  ->  TV-323013A / TV-323013B (split range)

Source: V1 `main.py` step_sim stage 8 (9513-9578), the constant block (1733-1828), the seeds in
`State.__init__` (6887-6948). The design data are in `data/unit_323e003.py`; 776 is a boundary
at its design value until unit 328 is ported, written as V1 builds it from 328C002 and 328D001.

## XXXIII.2 The node: the dew point holds it, PIC-323202 trims it

Stream 305 has no valve, so 323C003's vapour space, the 323E003 shell and 323D001 are one gas
inventory at one pressure. V1 integrates it on the tank's volume alone, the documented lower bound,
at the PFD stream-332 gas density: $C = 11.10 \cdot 2.99 / 3.2 = 10.37$ kg/bar.

$$
\frac{dP}{dt} = \frac{\dot m_{env,in} - \dot m_{env,cond} - \dot m_{321}}{3600\,C},\qquad P \ge 0.1\ \mathrm{bar\,a}
$$

$$
\dot m_{env,in} = \dot m_{301} + \dot m_{302} + 1758 + \dot m_{blow,322501} - \dot m_{blow,323501}
$$

$$
\dot m_{env,cond} = 24\,998\,\frac{\max(T_{dew} - \bar T_{tw},\ 0)}{74 - 60},\qquad
T_{dew} = 74 + T_{sat}(P) - T_{sat}(3.2)
$$

$$
\dot m_{321} = 1323\,\frac{h}{25}\sqrt{\frac{\max(P - P_{E011},\ 0)}{3.2 - 1.13}}
$$

$\bar T_{tw}$ is the mean of the live supply and return. The dew point takes water's saturation
slope on a frozen offset, the idiom of the bubble points of unit 323. Unlike 323E011's constant
capacity (§XXXII.3), it gives this node a restoring force: about 19 300 kg/h per bar at design,
against PV-323202's 320. So the condenser and the water set this node, and the vent trims it.
V1 capped the capacity at the gas that arrives; the cap is removed by decision (§XXXIII.3).
Measured, PFD 305 up 10 % with PV-323202 held at 25 %: the node settles at 3.372 bar a, where the
higher dew point condenses 97.8 % of the extra gas; the vent passes 54 kg/h more. PV-323202 vents
against the 323E011 node of the start of the tick, a `State` read (323E011 steps after this unit),
so 323E011's pressure moves PFD 321: a 323E011 at its floor raises it 22 %.

## XXXIII.3 The capacity uncapped (handoff B-34), decided 2026-09-27

V1 capped the capacity at the gas that arrives, $\min(\text{capacity},\ \dot m_{env,in})$ —
"cannot condense what is not there". While the cap bound, the node's balance was minus the vent
alone; PIC-323202 shut the vent, and the node then stood wherever it was. A real condenser with
surplus cooling keeps drawing the pressure down, from the gas the envelope holds, until its dew
point has closed on the water far enough for the capacity to meet the load. The process engineer
decided to remove the cap; the port condenses the whole capacity (the equation of §XXXIII.2).

It is inert at design: the capacity, 24 998 kg/h, is below the 26 321 kg/h that arrives. Measured,
V1 against the port — bit-exact until V1's capacity first outruns the gas, and then:

| upset | V1, the cap | the port |
|---|---|---|
| TIC-323013 set to 45 C (V1's PIC-323202 tuning) | the cap binds at 636 s, the vent shuts at 640 s; frozen at 2.725 bar a with 6119 kg/h of capacity unused an hour on | the vent shuts at 640 s; the node follows the water down to 2.458 bar a, the capacity on the load |
| TIC-323013 set to 45 C (the decided tuning) | — | the capacity passes the gas at 440 s, the vent shuts at 445 s; 2.746 bar a at 600 s, 2.458 at the hour (V1's cap: frozen at 2.840) |
| PFD 305 cut 30 % | the node falls on the vent alone; frozen, then creeping back as the water warms | the node falls on the capacity; both meet at 2.797 bar a within half a minute |
| the 305 overhead gone (a stripper trip) | falls on the vent to 1.864, stands, then creeps back as the water warms | the vent shuts at 23 s (decided tuning); the node falls to 1.867 bar a, where the dew point condenses just the 797 recycle |

So the cap matters where the cooling, not the load, moves: with TIC-323013 driven down, V1's node
stood 0.27 bar above where the condenser holds it. With PV-323202 shut, PIC-323202 has no lever
left — the split range that would give it the cooling is not built (§XXXIII.5) — and the node
stays below its set point until TIC-323013 is put back.

The energy balance meanwhile condenses $\dot m_{305} + 1758 - \dot m_{321}$ and the pressure
balance the capacity; the two agree only in steady state, as on 323E011 (B-30). The gas the
capacity draws from the envelope's own inventory, at most $C = 10.37$ kg per bar the node falls,
is not credited to the tank.

## XXXIII.4 The tempered water and the energy balance (handoff B-31)

*Decided 2026-10-16 (decision 118, handoff B-31): the port charges these inlets at their producers' live temperatures as departures from the producers' designs, §LXX.2; what follows is V1's, which ``live_inlets=False`` keeps.*

TV-323013A admits cold make-up and TV-323013B bypasses hot return, one stroke and its opposite.
V1 maps last tick's stroke onto a steady-state supply, lags it 25 s, and closes the duty on the
live water mean with last tick's return — the tear that breaks the loop between the duty and the
return it sets:

$$
T_{sup,ss} = \mathrm{clamp}\!\left(65 - 10\,\frac{h_A}{50},\ 20,\ 65\right),\qquad
T_{sup} = \mathrm{lag}(T_{sup,ss},\ 25\ \mathrm{s})
$$

$$
Q = 1000\,\bigl(T - \tfrac12 (T_{sup} + T_{ret,prev})\bigr),\qquad T_{ret} = T_{sup} + 10\,\frac{Q}{14\,000}
$$

TIC-323013's PV is the supply, not the shell. The 20 C floor cannot bind: the stroke spans 45 to
65 C. The first-order lag initialises on its first call to its target, as V1's does, so a stroke
set before the first tick reaches the supply without the 25 s.

$$
M c_p\frac{dT}{dt} = \sum \dot m_{in}c_p(T_{in} - T) + \dot m_{cond}\,\lambda - Q,\qquad
\dot m_{cond} = \dot m_{305} + 1758 - \dot m_{321}
$$

$c_p$ = 3.0 kJ/(kg K), the LP carbamate value shared with 323E011; UA = 1000 kW/K on the design 14 K
to the water mean; $\lambda$ = 1914.7 kJ/kg back-solved on the 704.4 kW of design sensible heat so
the design holds. Semi-implicit in the inlets and the water. The inlets are charged at design —
305 at 119 C, 718B at 45, 776 at 61, 797 at 46 — whatever their sources do (B-31).

## XXXIII.5 PIC-323202 drives one vent, as in V1 (handoff B-36), decided 2026-09-27

The functional diagram (UD-MR-323-FF-0002, the PIC-323202 sheet, REVACT = 0) gives the
controller two characterised outputs: PV-323202A opening from 30 to 100 % of the output, and
PV-323202B closing from 100 to 0 % over the whole range. The tuning table's only row for the loop
is "PIC-323202B | 329058,WC", on the tempered-water supply line. V1 models one vent, PV-323202, on
the whole output, and runs TIC-323013 on its own set point, in CAS with no master. The sources
disagree on what PV-323202B drives (vendor archive and `References/`, 2026-09-27):

| source | the gas vent on 100-GCB4-323204 (DN 80, FO) | the tempered-water valves at cooler 329E002 |
|---|---|---|
| P&ID 103/1 and 109 (rev 0, 2003) | tagged TV-323013, on TIC-323013's signal | tagged PV-323202A (outlet, FC) and PV-323202B (bypass, FO), on PIC-323202's signal |
| loop summary P 323202 (rev 1, 2007) | PV-323202, driven by output "PV-323202A": 600 / 1200 / 4000 Nm3/h, 3.2 to 1.3 bar a | — |
| loop summary T 323013 (rev 1, 2007) | — | TV-323013A (DN 300 butterfly, FC, 917.8 m3/h) and TV-323013B (DN 250, FO), driven by TIC-323013 on 400-WC2-329058 |
| `References/323E003 323D001 323P001 Datasheets.md` | "the vent valve (TV323013)" for coarse control | fine control by moving TIC-323013's set point |

The process engineer kept V1's structure — one vent on the whole output, TIC-323013 on its own set
point — since the P&IDs do not carry the functional diagram's split range. So PIC-323202's only
lever is the vent; under surplus cooling it shuts it and the node stays below its set point
(§XXXIII.3). PT-323202's loop summary gives 3.9 bar a as normal; the datasheet, the PFD and V1 all
have 3.2, and the port anchors on 3.2.

## XXXIII.6 323D001 and 323P001; the heel (handoff B-35), decided 2026-09-27

$$
\frac{dM}{dt} = \dot m_{305} + \dot m_{718B} + \dot m_{776} + 1758 - \dot m_{321} - \dot m_{308},\qquad
\dot m_{308} = 36\,835\,\frac{n}{59.93}
$$

LI-323502 reads $M / 6759.9 \cdot 50$ % (the telemetry $M / 13\,519.8 \cdot 100$). **LIC-323502**
(Kc 1.5, Ti 300 s, V1's own — the table has no row) sets **SIC-323901**'s speed in CAS (Kc 1.1,
Ti 30 s, the table's, in rpm); the speed PV is the last output through a 3 s lag. The functional
diagram scales LIC-323502's output onto SIC-323901's range, $SP = OUTP \cdot MAX / 100$, with
ST-323901 calibrated 0 to 145 rpm (loop S 323901), and limits the speed demand at 130 rpm (82 %
of the output). V1 carries both outputs as speeds in rpm and clamps them at 100 rpm. 323P001 is a
plunger pump, so the flow is the speed's whatever the discharge pressure: 0.5046 m3/h per rpm —
three 130 mm plungers on a 220 mm stroke at 96 % volumetric efficiency — at 1218 kg/m3, so 59.93
rpm at design (V1's comment says 62.99; its expression gives 59.93). The vendor datasheet
(UD-AU-323-EC-0014, sheets 7 and 8) gives 41 m3/h at the rated 81 rpm, 32 at the normal 64 and
9.6 at the minimum 19: 0.500 to 0.506 m3/h per rpm. 718B is last tick's, V1's `R3232_718B` tear.
308 feeds the HP scrubber on the next tick.

V1 guarded the pump only once the tank was ON its 1 kg floor, capping it at what arrives. On the
tick the tank reached the floor the draw was not capped, and the floor made up that tick's
overdraw once: SIC-323901 held at 100 rpm empties the tank at 989 s and V1 makes 6.2 kg at the 1 s
step (at most 0.7 kg at the engine's 0.1 s). The process engineer decided the heel cap already
decided for 323D002, 323F010 and 323D011 (`project.md` decision 11):

$$
\dot m_{308} \le \max\!\left(\frac{(M - 1)\cdot 3600}{\Delta t} + \dot m_{in} - \dot m_{321},\ 0\right)
$$

with the loss of suction flagged (`suction_lost`). Inert above the heel. Measured, V1 against the
port: bit-exact to the 989th second; on it V1 draws its full 61 460 kg/h and makes 6.16 kg, the
port delivers the 39 271 kg/h above the heel and makes nothing; from then on both hold the pump at
what arrives, 36 835 kg/h. The vent, which V1 books against the tank, is not capped.

## XXXIII.7 The decided tuning (handoff B-32), 2026-09-27

The process engineer decided that the DCS tuning table's gains are rescaled by their
transmitters' spans on PIC-323203 and on both LPCC loops. **PIC-323202:** V1 runs 5.0 %/bar and
40 s, which no source gives; the table's row for the loop, "PIC-323202B", gives 1.00 and 100 s,
and PT-323202 is calibrated 0 to 5 bar g (UD-MR-323-EC-0001, loop P 323202). The port runs

$$
K_c = 1.00\cdot\frac{100}{5\ \mathrm{bar}} = 20\ \%/\mathrm{bar},\qquad T_i = 100\ \mathrm{s}
$$

— four times V1's proportional action and 1.6 times its integral. **TIC-323013:** the table's
1.00 and 100 s on TT-323013's 0 to 100 C (loop T 323013) is 1.0 %/K — V1's own number, so nothing
changes. **SIC-323901:** ST-323901 is calibrated 0 to 145 rpm (loop S 323901, found 2026-09-27);
V1 carries both its measured speed and its output in rpm, so on that span the table's per cent per
per cent is the same number in rpm per rpm — 1.10, V1's. LIC-323502 has no table row and runs as
V1; the pump's own documents (the technical specification and the Voith function scheme) carry no
DCS tuning.

With the node on its set point nothing moves (600 ticks compared). PFD 305 up 10 %: the
controllers part on the 11th tick after the step; an hour on V1's node is at 3.234 bar a and the
port's at 3.215 with PV-323202 at 68 %. Because the dew point, not the vent, sets this node, the
retune changes the node by hundredths of a bar — and, under V1's cap, the frozen node of
§XXXIII.3 by 0.1 bar.

## XXXIII.8 Structure, and what is not here

`LpCarbamateCondenser` holds the holdup, TT-323006, the node, the return of the tick before and
the two lags; `step` takes PIC-323202, LIC-323502, SIC-323901, TIC-323013, the column's overhead
and its two sources, both blow-throughs, 718B, 776 and the 323E011 node, and returns a frozen
`LpCarbamateCondenserResult`. The order is V1's: the controllers act on the state at the top of
the tick; the vent, the draw and the water follow; the duty closes on the water mean with last
tick's return; the node steps on the condensation; the temperature and the holdup advance last,
the draw capped at the heel. It publishes the node, which 323C003 reads at the start of the next tick; 321 for 323E011
on the tick; 308 for the HP section on the next.

Not here: any composition (V1 carries none); SIC-323902, the standby pump's speed loop, which
V1 seeds in MAN at 0 and never steps; the 744 wash, which is unit 328's; PV-323202B, not built
by decision (§XXXIII.5).

## XXXIII.9 Equivalence achieved

82 tests in `test_lp_carbamate_condenser_equivalence.py`: the design basis (34 constants, 776
twice); PV-323202's law at eight states, the tempered-water supply at seven strokes, the dew point
and the capacity at six pressures, each against V1's expressions; the state and all four
controllers seeded field by field; ten scenarios TICK BY TICK on the unit alone — design hold, the
gas up 10 %, down 30 % (the capacity outrunning the gas) and gone, 718B halved, 776 up 20 %, each
blow-through, the 323E011 node raised and raised above this one — and eight more: TIC-323013 set
to 45 and 65 C and in MAN, PV-323202 in MAN, PIC-323202 on 3.5 bar a, LIC-323502 in MAN, and the
pump onto the tank's heel; V1's 323C003 into V1's LPCC against the ported pair, the column riding
the node, through a stripper feed cut; V1's LPCC into V1's 323E011 against the ported pair, 321
on the tick and 718B on the next; and V1's stages 1 to 4, 8 and 9 against the ported seven. Every
tick compares every published field, the node, the tank, the water, both lags and all four
controllers with `==`. The transcription carries the two decided lines, B-34's and B-35's, as a
switch, so these scenarios compare the rest of V1's stage 8 wherever the limits are reached. The
decisions are asserted from both sides on V1's own lines: the tuning (inert on the set point,
then the gas up 10 %), the uncapped capacity three ways (TIC-323013 at 45 C, the gas down 30 % and
gone) and the heel once. Mutations caught: the return tear off by one part in ten million, at the
first tick of the design hold; the cap restored, and the loss of suction never flagged, each
caught by the scenarios and the behaviour tests. 7 behaviour tests pin the design point, the dew
point's hold, PIC-323202's decided tuning, the tempered water both ways, the gas gone, and the
pump at the heel.

# Part XXXIV — 323C005: the atmospheric absorber, the first unit of `desorption/`

## XXXIV.1 What the unit is

323C005 is a packed column at 1.00 bar a (Uhde DDS UD-AU-323-EC-0003: ID 1180 mm, on a
1150 mm skirt). The gas that reaches atmospheric pressure rises through the packing — PFD 702,
440 kg/h at 45 C, 89.4 mol% NH3, the LP flash gas node's vent through PV-323203, and PFD 708,
462 kg/h at 121 C, the vacuum train's vapour — against the lean solvent PFD 756, 33 358 kg/h at
43 C. The inert gas leaves the top as PFD 341, 80 kg/h at 43 C, to 328V001's stack. The liquor
drains from the dished bottom head through N4 into 328V001, whose overflow seal passes it to
328D003's compartment II as PFD 343, 34 180 kg/h. 756 + 702 + 708 = 343 + 341 exactly. No
controller acts on it.

Source: V1 `main.py` step_sim, stage 1 of the "LP recirculation and desorption" block
(8847-8881), the constant block and the sump relations (1831-1937), the vent anchor of report
D-11 (3908-3930), the seeds in `State.__init__` (6877-6878). The design data are in
`data/unit_323c005.py`.

## XXXIV.2 The vent: the saturated-gas law (report D-11)

PFD 341 is the inert gas of 702 and 708 leaving saturated at the absorber top, in equilibrium with
the lean solvent that enters there: its 2.490 kmol/h of N2 + O2 are the 2.486 that 702 and 708
bring, and its water partial pressure, 0.0821 bar, is psat(43 C) = 0.0865 at a water activity of
0.95. V1 therefore takes the vent from the same law as a condenser's cold end, ported as
`thermo/saturated_vent.py`:

$$
y_c(T, P) = Y_{des}\,\frac{P_{des}}{P}\,\frac{p^{sat}_w(T)}{p^{sat}_w(T_{des})},\qquad
n_{vent,c} = n_{inert}\,\frac{y_c}{1 - y_c},\qquad
n_{vent,k} = \min(n_{vent,c}\,s_k,\ n_{in,k})
$$

with $Y_{des}$ = 0.1443 and the split $s_k$ of the 341 row, NH3 and CO2 riding water's
saturation line; every inert leaves, $y_c$ is held below $1 - 10^{-9}$. The inerts are 702's with
its flow and 708's with the inerts 324E002 vents (708 is part of that condenser's vent), and the
condensables available are all that 702 and 708 bring:

$$
\dot m_{341} = \min\!\left(80\,\frac{\mathrm{model}(\dot m_{702}/440,\ n_{706}/n_{706,des},\ T_{solvent})}
{\mathrm{model}(1,\ 1,\ 43)},\ \dot m_{702} + \dot m_{708}\right)
$$

exactly 80 kg/h at design. $T_{solvent}$ is 322C001's live liquor temperature, the solvent's.
Measured: an NH3 surge that triples 702 vents 146 kg/h; 702 gone, 47; 324E002's inerts doubled,
127; the solvent at 55 C, 89. Half the solvent leaves the vent at 80 kg/h — the top still meets
fresh solvent at 43 C — and warms the liquor to 66.4 C.

## XXXIV.3 The liquor, and the boiling point that stops the absorption

*Decided 2026-10-16 (decision 118, handoff B-31): the port charges these inlets at their producers' live temperatures as departures from the producers' designs, §LXX.2; what follows is V1's, which ``live_inlets=False`` keeps.*

$$
M c_p\frac{dT}{dt} = \sum \dot m_{in}c_p(T_{in} - T) + \dot m_{abs}\,\lambda,\qquad
\dot m_{abs} = \dot m_{702} + \dot m_{708} - \dot m_{341}
$$

semi-implicit in the three inlets, charged at 43, 45 and 121 C whatever their sources do (B-31);
$c_p$ = 3.0 kJ/(kg K); $\lambda$ = 1365.7 kJ/kg, back-solved on the design's -311.8 kW of
sensible heat and 822 kg/h absorbed so the design holds at V1's 55 C (PFD 343 prints 56). The
liquor cannot absorb past water's boiling point at 1.00 bar a, 99.61 C: when a tick would carry it
past, the absorption is cut to what takes the liquor exactly there, and the rest vents. With the
solvent cut, the few kilograms left reach it 1.4 s later; from then on 31 kg/h is absorbed and
871 of the 902 kg/h of gas goes to the stack. The port publishes the cut as `boil_limited` (V1
raises no flag).

## XXXIV.4 The sump (report A-16)

The bottoms fall from N4 (DN 150, 168.3 x 5.6 mm) about 10 m to 328V001, whose N1 overflow holds
its pool; both gas spaces are atmospheric, so the sump drains freely and holds only the head that
pushes the bottoms into the pipe — the smaller of a Francis weir over the pipe rim and a
sharp-edged orifice on its bore:

$$
Q(h) = \min\!\left(1.84\,\pi d\,h^{1.5},\ 0.61\,\frac{\pi d^2}{4}\sqrt{2 g h}\right),\qquad
\dot m_{343} = 34\,180\,\frac{Q(h(M))}{Q(h(M_{des}))}
$$

on a 2:1 ellipsoidal head (V1's reading; the head type is not on the DDS). At the design
34.9 m3/h the weir governs at 49 mm, 8.07 kg in the head. The step is backward Euler — the drain's
time constant falls as $h^{1.5}$ toward an empty sump — solved by bisection on the depth, and the
bottoms returned are the flow that closes the mass balance exactly; measured, the balance closes
to 3e-11 kg/h on every tick of every upset. With every inlet stopped the sump is empty within a
minute. V1 once held 2848 kg here, 2.5 m deep, over the gas inlets and into the packing (A-16).

## XXXIV.5 The boundaries, and why every one is a tear

V1 steps this unit FIRST in its LP recirculation and desorption block — before 328D003, the
desorbers, 328D001, 322C001, the LPCC and 323E011 — so everything it takes is read as it stood
at the end of the tick before:

| input | from | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|---|
| PFD 702 | 323E011 (`FlashCondenserResult.m_702_kgh`) | tear `R3232_702`, written at the end of V1's block | the same tear |
| PFD 756 | 322C001's circuit | tear `R322_756` | a boundary at design until 322C001 is ported |
| PFD 708, 324E002's vent inerts | unit 324 | tears `R324_708`, `R324_706_INERT` | boundaries at design until unit 324 is ported |
| the solvent's temperature | 322C001 | a State read at the top of the tick | the same |

The one-tick delay on 702 is V1's own; the port reproduces it and adds none. The coupled test
steps V1's absorber and 323E011 in V1's order with V1's tear write, against the ported pair in
the same order, for 3000 ticks with PFD 701 up 10 %, and they agree on every tick.

PFD 776 and 786 do not enter 323C005: they are 328D001's, to 323E003 and 323E011. V1 computes
both in its stage 6 and the two condensers take them in stages 8 and 9 of the same tick — no
tear. Until 328D001 is ported the two condensers hold them at design; when it is, the engine
must step 328D001 before them to keep that.

343 leaves on the same tick: V1 steps 328D003 immediately after this unit, and the tank takes
this tick's bottoms (§XXXV.6).

## XXXIV.6 Structure

`AtmosphericAbsorber` holds the sump and the liquor temperature; `step` takes 702, 756, 708,
324E002's vent inerts, the solvent's temperature and the tick, and returns a frozen
`AtmosphericAbsorberResult`: the gas, the vent, the absorption and its cut, 343, the state and
the sump's head. The order is V1's: the vent on the gas that arrives, the absorption and its
heat, the boiling-point cut, the sump, the temperature. The saturated-gas law lives in `thermo/`,
where it knows no plant; 324's vacuum condensers will extend it with their back-pressure branch.

Not here: 328V001 as a vessel (V1 carries it as the temperature at which 343 reaches compartment
II, `A328_D003_V001_T`, which is 328D003's); LT-323011 on the sump (V1 publishes the head, and no
loop acts on it); the 9 bar steam injected after PV-323203 to keep carbamate from depositing
(`References/323C005 328V001 Datasheets.md`), which V1 does not model.

## XXXIV.7 Equivalence achieved

96 tests in `test_atmospheric_absorber_equivalence.py`: the design basis (22 constants, 702
against both of V1's names) and the four vapour rows; the vent spec, the sump's design holdup and N4 anchor, the
boiling point, and the design state exact (80 kg/h, 34 180 kg/h); the saturated-gas law against
V1's `vacuum_condenser` executed — `moles_from_mole_pct` on five rows, `saturated_gas_spec` on
four, `vent_moles` and `vent_mass_kgh` at ten states; the sump at nine heads, nine masses and ten
steps and the vent at nine states against V1's functions executed; eleven scenarios TICK BY
TICK; and the coupled run through the `R3232_702` tear. Every tick compares every published
field and the state with `==`. Three mutations — the vent not topped up when the boiling point
cuts the absorption, 708's inerts frozen, the sump fed one part in ten million high — are caught
at once. 13 behaviour tests in `tests/units/desorption/test_atmospheric_absorber.py` pin the
design, the vent's four answers, the half solvent, the boiling cut, the empty sump and the weir,
and 3 in `tests/thermo/test_saturated_vent.py` pin the law's design row, its direction and its
two bounds.

# Part XXXV — 328D003: the ammonia water tank

## XXXV.1 What the unit is

328D003 is the atmospheric tank that collects the plant's ammonia water: 490 m3 of liquid in
three bays whose baffles have openings, so the three levels stand together. The capacities are
the owner-approved liquid capacities, 18, 43 and 429 m3 (`References/323D003 Datasheets.md`, its
approved correction of 2026-07-27, which supersedes that file's 561 m3 geometric envelope and its
50/30/20 split); at V1's 992 kg/m3 they hold 17 856, 42 656 and 425 568 kg, half of each at
design.

| bay | in | out |
|---|---|---|
| I, 18 m3 | the vacuum train's condensates: 719 (324E002, 26 768 kg/h, 45 C), 720 (324E005, 2758, 40 C), 721 (324E006, 1763, 41 C), 759 (324E007, 190, 55 C) | 744 to 322P002 and the LP absorber, 31 478 kg/h, FIC-328402, while 322P002 A or B runs |
| II, 43 m3 | 343 from 323C005 through 328V001, 34 180 kg/h; 741, the process-condensate recycle, normally closed (FIC-328406) | on 328P003's header: 735 to 328E007 and the desorbers, 31 114 kg/h; 734, 1534 (FIC-323401); 791 to 323E011, 1534 (FIC-323402); the spare 793, 0 (FIC-328405) |
| III, 429 m3 | none: the surge volume the other two level into | none |

## XXXV.2 The two active bays

Each advances on its own streams first. With $\dot m_c = \dot m_{719} + \dot m_{720} +
\dot m_{721} + \dot m_{759}$:

$$
\frac{dM_I}{dt} = \dot m_c - 1 - \dot m_{744},\qquad
\frac{dM_{II}}{dt} = \dot m_{343} + \dot m_{741} + 2 - (\dot m_{735} + \dot m_{734} + \dot m_{791} + \dot m_{793})
$$

$$
M_I c_{p,I}\frac{dT_I}{dt} = c_{p,I}\sum_k \dot m_k (T_k - T_I) + \dot m_c\,\lambda_I,\qquad
M_{II} c_{p,II}\frac{dT_{II}}{dt} = c_{p,II}\left[\dot m_{343}(56 - T_{II}) + \dot m_{741}(40 - T_{II})\right]
$$

both stepped semi-implicitly in their inflows' heat-capacity rates, and each holdup floored at
1 kg. $c_p$ is `aqueous_cp` on V1's 4.0 at each bay's design temperature, 44 and 56 C. The
$-1$ and $+2$ kg/h are the PFD's rounding, which V1 books so each bay closes at design (31 479 in
against 31 478 out; 34 180 against 34 182).

$\lambda_I$ is back-solved so compartment I holds PFD 744's 44 C. V1 names it the
carbamate-formation exotherm, but the four condensates arrive at 44.40 C on average — 719, at
45 C, dominates — so the back-solve is a sink: $\lambda_I = -1.593$ kJ/kg, 13.9 kW at design. It is
ported as V1's anchor.

No controller sets 735: it is drawn in proportion to compartment II's holdup,
$\dot m_{735} = 31\,114\, M_{II}/M_{II,des}$, so it rises with the level and does the tank's level
regulation — at 100 % it is twice its design.

734 is booked out of the tank and delivered to no unit, as in V1 (handoff B-37). 741 arrives as
328C004 sent it on the tick before (a tear): since B-50 (decided 2026-09-30, §XLII.5) FIC-328406 is
stepped with the column and draws 741 from its bottoms ahead of LV-328505. V1 steps FIC-328406
here and holds 741 to the 328C004 bottoms of the tick before,
$\dot m_{741} = \min(\dot m_{741,FIC},\ \dot m_{739})$; the tank's transcription keeps V1's lines
and hands the port's tank V1's 741.

## XXXV.3 The openings

*Decided 2026-10-16 (decision 118, handoff B-31): the port charges these inlets at their producers' live temperatures as departures from the producers' designs, §LXX.2; what follows is V1's, which ``live_inlets=False`` keeps.*

With no opening areas or elevations in the sources, V1 levels the three bays after the streams —
the communicating-vessel limit — with every transfer crossing compartment III at the donor's
temperature:

$$
L = \frac{\sum M_i}{\sum M_{i,full}},\qquad M_i' = L\,M_{i,full}
$$

The donors among I and II give their excess to III first; the receivers then take what they lack
from III's mix, which stops an almost empty III exporting more liquid at its old temperature than
it held. Neither mass nor sensible energy is created, and 429/490 of any net disturbance settles
in compartment III: with the condensates up 30 % for an hour, III's share of the rise is 0.87551,
429/490 to 1e-12. Compartment III starts at the holdup-weighted mean of I and II, 52.46 C, so it
brings no heat anchor of its own.

The inlets are charged at design temperatures — 343 at 56 C, 328V001's, whatever 323C005's liquor
does, the condensates at 45, 40, 41 and 55 C, and 741 at 40 C (handoff B-31).

## XXXV.4 The five flow loops

All five are volumetric `FlowLoop`s on a 5 s transmitter, stepped in V1's order (FIC-328406 with
328C004 since B-50, §XLII.5), each gain the
DCS table's number read per cent of its transmitter's span (decision 10; B-38 and B-41, decided):

| loop | leg | design | density | span | Kc, the port | V1's Kc | Ti |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FIC-323401 | 734 | 1534 kg/h at 50 % | 992.4 | 0-4 m3/h | 2.5 %/(m3/h) | 0.10 x 992.4 | 7 s |
| FIC-323402 | 791 | 1534 kg/h at 50 % | 992.4 | 0-3.3 m3/h | 3.03 %/(m3/h) | 0.10 x 992.4 | 7 s |
| FIC-328405 | 793 | shut; 1534 kg/h at 100 % | 992.4 | 0-2.3 m3/h | 8.70 %/(m3/h) | 0.20 x 992.4 | 15 s |
| FIC-328406 (328C004's) | 741 | MAN, shut; 77 169 kg/h wide open (B-44) | 992.42 | 0-60 m3/h | 1.25 %/(m3/h) | 0.75 x 992.42 | 80 s |
| FIC-328402 | 744 | 31 478 kg/h at 50 % | 1002.48 | 0-70 m3/h | 1.071 %/(m3/h) | 0.06 x 1002.48 | 60 s |

744's density is back-solved from the PFD's own 31 478 kg/h at 31.4 m3/h (the row prints 1002).
V1 applies each table number per kg/h, times the density; on FIC-328406, 744 %/(m3/h), the loop
cannot hold a set point in AUTO. FIC-328402's decision is §XXXV.9, the other four's Part XXXVII;
V1 had cut FIC-328402's 0.75 per kg/h to 0.06 on a stability estimate (its AUDIT G16). Uhde's loop summary puts FIC-328402 on 328P003's discharge — 735, not 744 (handoff
B-39); the loop stays on V1's structure until Phase 7. **Superseded 2026-10-09** (decision 81,
§LXIV.3): the loop meters 735 at its 990.9 kg/m3, FV-328402 at 58.40 % on it, and 744 is 322P002's
delivery.

## XXXV.5 The decided divergence: the heel and the overflow, 2026-09-27

V1's tank has both boundary flaws the process engineer ruled out for 323D002 and 323D001
(decision 11): its pumps draw their full flow whatever the tank holds, the 1 kg floors making up
the difference, and it has no overflow, so the bays level above their capacity without limit.
At the process engineer's instruction the same rule is applied here, found and decided in the
same session. Both changes are inert between the heel and full.

**Neither pump draws below the tank's heel.** Because the bays level together, the heel is one
level: the level at which compartment I, the smallest bay, holds V1's 1 kg floor,
$L_h = 1/17\,856 = 5.6\times10^{-5}$. Each active bay's heel is its share, $h_I = 1$ kg and
$h_{II} = 1 \cdot 43/18 = 2.389$ kg, and each bay's draws are capped at the liquid above its heel
plus what arrives on the tick:

$$
\dot m_{744} \le \frac{\max(M_I - h_I,\ 0)}{\Delta t} + \dot m_c - 1,\qquad
\dot m_{735} + \dot m_{734} + \dot m_{791} + \dot m_{793} \le \frac{\max(M_{II} - h_{II},\ 0)}{\Delta t} + \dot m_{343} + \dot m_{741} + 2
$$

328P003's four legs lose their share of the suction alike (pro rata). A binding cap raises
`suction_lost_i` or `suction_lost_ii`, and each capped leg's transmitter reads the flow
delivered on the next tick (`FlowLoop.step(flow_cap=...)`, register row 106), so the controller
sees the shortfall and opens. With every bay held at or above its heel, the levelled total never
falls below $L_h$ times the tank, 27.22 kg, so the levelled bays never fall below their floors
either. A 1 kg heel per bay is not enough: the levelling carries the bays back below 1 kg into
compartment III, and V1's floor restores them every tick — measured at 3040 kg/h, which
328P003's legs then pump out.

| nothing arriving, from 300 kg levelled, 0.1 s step | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|
| until 322P002 reaches the heel, 26.1 s | bit-exact | bit-exact |
| 328P003 at the heel | draws on, its floor making the liquid | capped from 31.6 s |
| 744 / 734 / 791 then | 31 478 / 1534 / 1534 kg/h | 0 / 1.0 / 1.0 kg/h |
| the tank then holds | about 25 kg | 27.22 kg, the heel level |
| liquid made in the hour | 34 273 kg | 0.99 kg |
| FT-328402 | the valve's flow | the delivered flow, to 1e-19 |

The one liquid the port still makes is V1's own rounding: at the heel with nothing arriving,
compartment I's $-1$ kg/h is restored by the floor, 1 kg/h, and compartment II's $+2$ kg/h is
what 328P003 then delivers.

**A full tank overflows.** Above the 490 m3 of approved liquid capacity — the approved capacities
are liquid capacities, the envelope's remainder being roof and headspace — the excess at the
common level leaves at each bay's temperature, published as `m_overflow_kgh` at
`t_overflow_c`:

$$
\dot m_{over}\,\Delta t = \sum_i \max(L\,M_{i,full} - M_{i,full},\ 0),\qquad M_i' = M_{i,full}
$$

Its destination is outside this model, so it leaves the plant. The P&ID UD-VT-328-FB-0003 rev 02
(sheet 104) shows a high shell connection on 328D003 running through the loop seal Z2801Z and a
DN200 line to the drain system "30"; it is unlabelled and its elevation is not sourced (Open data
gaps).

| 741 at all of 328C004's design bottoms, 33 724 kg/h, from 99.95 %, 0.5 s step | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|
| until the first tick above full, 333.5 s | bit-exact | bit-exact |
| that tick | kept above full | the same excess overflowed, to 1e-9 |
| after two hours | 100.9 %, 735 at 62 793 kg/h | 100 %, 735 at 62 228, 2610 kg/h over the top at 51.77 C |

V1's 735 regulates slowly, so these limits are hours away from design: with 741 wide open V1's
tank passes full after about 20 hours and settles at 104.2 %; with 322P002 stopped as well it
passes full in 5.1 hours and settles at 155 %.

## XXXV.6 The boundaries, and which are same-tick

V1 steps 328D003 second in its LP recirculation and desorption block, immediately after 323C005,
and the tank's draws go forward on the same tick:

| stream | from / to | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|---|
| 343 | 323C005 (`AtmosphericAbsorberResult.m_343_kgh`) | this tick's `bot_c005` | a same-tick `Result`, not a tear |
| 719, 720, 721, 759 | unit 324 | tears `R324_719` ... `R324_759` | boundaries at design until unit 324 is ported |
| 739 | 328C004 | tear `R328_739` | a boundary at design until 328C004 is ported |
| 322P002 running | the operator | `s.aux_pumps` | an argument |
| 791 | to 323E011 | this tick's `m_402`, stage 9 | `AmmoniaWaterTankResult.m_791_kgh`, same tick |
| 735, compartment II's temperature | to 328E007 | this tick's | same tick |
| 793 | to 328D001 | this tick's | same tick |
| 744 (755) | to 322C001's circuit | this tick's | same tick |

The scheduler draft (§3.6 of `project.md`) carries this as a `Result` source: a same-tick output
of an EARLIER step, which the start-up validation refuses unless the producer runs first. Three
tests hold it. The flowsheet 323C005 -> 328D003 -> 323E011 -> (702) -> 323C005 is refused as a
cycle until 702 is declared a tear, and then orders exactly as V1 steps: 323C005, 328D003,
323E011. The coupled run steps V1's stages 1, 2 and 9 with V1's tear write against the ported
absorber, tank and condenser in the same order for 3000 ticks, 323C005's solvent halved and
FIC-323402 moved, and agrees on every tick. The control run feeds the tank the absorber's bottoms
one tick late, as a tear would, and it leaves V1 on the tick the bottoms first move.

## XXXV.7 Structure

`AmmoniaWaterTank` holds the three bays' holdups and temperatures and the four transmitter caps;
`step` takes the five loops (`TankLoops`), 343, the four condensates, 739, whether 322P002 runs
and the tick, and returns a frozen `AmmoniaWaterTankResult`: the six draws, each bay's streams,
the two suction flags, the overflow and its temperature, and the state with the three levels
unrounded (V1's telemetry rounds them to 0.1 %, and the publication layer will). The order is
V1's: the loops, the draws and the caps, compartment I, compartment II, the openings, the
overflow. The openings are ported with V1's refusals: anything but three bays, a non-finite input,
a negative mass, a non-positive capacity.

Not here: 328E007, the feed/effluent interchanger V1 steps after the tank (Part XXXVI);
LT-328507 and LT-328508, which V1 publishes open loop on bays I and II; 328V001 as a vessel.

## XXXV.8 Equivalence achieved

76 tests in `test_ammonia_water_tank_equivalence.py`: the design basis (43 constants, and 756
against V1's second name); the four loops' seeds and tuning field by field (FIC-328402's gain the
decided one; FIC-328406 is 328C004's, B-50); the openings at nine states and their five refusals against V1's function executed;
eleven scenarios TICK BY TICK, V1 verbatim; the heel and the full tank each run twice — the port against the switched
transcription through the limit, and V1 verbatim against the port, bit-exact to the limit and
then each side's behaviour asserted; the flowsheet order, the coupled run and its one-tick-late
control. Every tick compares every published field, the three bays, the telemetry's rounded
levels, the four loops and their transmitters with `==`. Seven mutations — 735 on compartment
I's holdup, compartment II's rounding dropped, a 1 kg heel per bay, the overflow not removed, 735
kept out of the header's share, 343 charged at compartment I's temperature, and, before B-50
moved FIC-328406 to 328C004, 741 not held to 739 — are each caught. 10 behaviour tests in `tests/units/desorption/test_ammonia_water_tank.py` pin
the design, the one level and III's 429/490, 322P002 stopped and restarted, 343 gone, 741 back
into compartment II, FIC-328402 on the table's gain, the heel, the overflow with its books closed to 1e-6 kg, and
the heel's level. FIC-328402's decided divergence has 5 tests of its own (§XXXV.9).

## XXXV.9 The decided divergence on FIC-328402 (handoff B-38), 2026-09-27

Two changes to the loop on 744, decided by the process engineer.

**The gain, per cent of span.** Decision 10 read on FT-328402's calibrated range, 0 to 70 m3/h
(Uhde loop summary UD-MR-328-EC-0001 rev 1, loop F 328402, sheet 1/2, line D07, read from the
scanned page):

$$
K_{c,EU} = K_{c,table}\cdot\frac{100}{S} = 0.75\cdot\frac{100}{70\ \mathrm{m^3/h}} = 1.0714\ \%/(\mathrm{m^3/h}),\qquad T_i = 60\ \mathrm{s}
$$

where V1 runs $0.06 \cdot 1002.48 = 60.15$ %/(m3/h), 56.1 times stronger. On the pure-gain valve
and the 5 s transmitter the closed loop's dominant time constant goes from about 61 s to about
145 s; both are monotone at the engine's 0.1 s step. With the loop on its set point the error is
zero whatever the gain, so every scenario that does not move FIC-328402 is V1's to the bit.

**The transmitter reads what 322P002 delivers.** V1 gates 744 on 322P002 after the loop, so with
both pumps stopped the flow is zero and FT-328402 goes on lagging the valve's flow — 31.4 m3/h,
and the controller holds. Here, as for the heel caps (decision 11), the transmitter reads the flow
delivered on the previous tick: nothing while 322P002 is stopped.

| at 0.1 s | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|
| set point 31.4 to 25 m3/h: within 1 % | 199.5 s | 476.9 s (414.7 s on FV-328402's vendor trim, §XL.3) |
| 322P002 stopped two minutes: FT-328402 / FV-328402 | 31 478 kg/h / 50 % | nothing from the next tick / 100 % after 34.3 s |
| the tank through the stop | — | bit-exact with V1 on every tick (744 is zero either way) |
| 322P002 restarted | 744 at design at once | 62 956 kg/h, twice design, on the open valve; within 1 % after 449.8 s, from above (3.44 times design and 295.7 s on the vendor trim, §XL.3) |

The restart surge is what a wound-up flow loop does when its pump returns; V1's frozen reading
hid it. On V1's wall clock the old gain was not safe either: at the 0.5 s step of the tank's

cycle, FV-328402 alternating 0 and 100 % every tick (discrete loop gain 3.43; 0.74 at 0.1 s).

Proof: `test_ammonia_water_tank_fic328402_equivalence.py` — the gain against V1's seed; the port
against its switched transcription through a stop and restart and through the set-point move; and
both divergences V1 verbatim against the port, bit-exact to the tick each departure acts (tick 10
for the move, tick 11 for the stop), then each side's behaviour asserted. Two mutations — the
transmitter cap on the stop removed, V1's gain restored — are each caught.

# Part XXXVI — 328E007: the desorber heat exchanger

## XXXVI.1 What the unit is

328E007 is the plate exchanger that preheats the desorbers' feed on the purified condensate
leaving them. Its cold side takes PFD 735, the ammonia water 328P003 draws from 328D003's
compartment II, 31 114 kg/h at 56 C, and sends it to 328C002 as 738 at 114 C. Its hot side takes
739, 328C004's bottoms through LV-328505, 33 724 kg/h at 143 C, and sends it on as 740 at 89 C to
328P007, the battery limit (742) and the recycle 741. No stream is split or mixed: 738 is 735 and
740 is 739.

    735 (56 C) --cold--> 328E007 --> 738 (114 C) --> 328C002
    739 (143 C) --hot--> 328E007 --> 740 (89 C) --> 742 / 741

Source: V1 `main.py` step_sim, "328E007 feed/effluent interchanger (AUDIT C10)" (8952-8963) and
`m_738 = m_735` (8967); the constants 2007-2021 and `R328_C004_T` (1380). The design data are in
`data/unit_328e007.py`, the unit in `units/desorption/feed_effluent_interchanger.py`.

The datasheet case (UD-AU-328-EC-0007: 10.58 m2 on 25 plates, 2649 kW, 44 252 kg/h from 60.4 to
111.3 C against 45 479 kg/h from 143.0 to 93.5 C, U = 7727 W/m2K) is the exchanger's rating case,
not the 1750 MTPD point; V1 anchors on the PFD, and so does the port. V1's `R328_E007_EPS = 0.6667`
is dead in V1 and is not ported.

## XXXVI.2 The exchange law

V1 uses the two-part idiom 328E021 also uses: a temperature effectiveness on the cold side,
back-solved from the design temperatures, and the energy balance, not a second effectiveness, on
the hot side:

$$
T_{738} = T_{735} + \varepsilon_T\,(T_{739} - T_{735}),\qquad
\varepsilon_T = \frac{114 - 56}{143 - 56} = \frac{58}{87}
$$

$$
T_{740,raw} = T_{739} - \frac{\dot m_{735}\,(T_{738} - T_{735}) + L}{\max(\dot m_{739},\ 10^{-6})},\qquad
L = 33\,724 \cdot 54 - 31\,114 \cdot 58 = 16\,484\ \mathrm{kg\,K/h}
$$

$$
T_{740} = \mathrm{clamp}\big(T_{740,raw},\ \min(T_{735}, T_{739}),\ \max(T_{735}, T_{739})\big)
$$

cp cancels between the sides (V1's one aqueous cp, 4.0 kJ/kg K); $L$ is the shell loss the design
state leaves between the hot duty and the cold duty, 18.32 kW (V1 books a literal 18.3 kW in unit
328's energy diagnostic). At design both outlets are the PFD's to the bit: 114.0 and 89.0 C, the
feed taking 2005.1 kW. The cold inlet is compartment II's temperature, which 735 leaves at.

## XXXVI.3 The boundaries, and the thermal loops

| stream | from / to | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|---|
| 735, compartment II's temperature | 328D003 (`AmmoniaWaterTankResult.m_735_kgh`, `.t_ii_c`) | this tick's, after the tank | a same-tick `Result` |
| 739, 328C004's temperature | 328C004 | tears `R328_739`, `s.a328_c004_T` | arguments, at design until 328C004 is ported |
| 738 and its temperature | to 328C002 | this tick's `m_738`, `T_738` | `DesorberHeatExchangerResult`, same tick |
| 740 and its temperature | TT-328006, unit 328's energy diagnostic | this tick's | same tick |

V1 steps the exchanger immediately after the tank and before 328C002, which takes 738; 328C004 is
stepped after 328C002, so its bottoms and temperature come back a tick late. The flowsheet 323C005
-> 328D003 -> 328E007 -> 328C002 -> 328C003 -> 328C004, with 739 back to 328E007 and 750 back to
328C002, is refused as cyclic until 739 and 750 are declared tears, and then orders exactly as V1
steps.

No thermal loop closes within a tick. The feed's heat returns to the exchanger only through the
three columns, a tick later, through 328C004's temperature. The condensate return 740 -> 328E001
-> 741 -> 328D003 is open: 741 enters compartment II at a design 40 C (handoff B-31), standing for
328E001, the recycle cooler, which is not modelled, so 740's temperature reaches nothing
downstream. Charging 741 live would close a loop — compartment II, 735, the exchanger, 740,
328E001, 741 — that needs 328E001 and a tear.

## XXXVI.4 The decided divergence: the pinched exchanger, 2026-09-27

V1's cold outlet does not look at the hot flow. When 739 cannot give the feed its $\varepsilon_T$
share of the approach down to the pinch, the clamp holds 740 at the feed's temperature and the
feed is heated all the same, so the exchanger makes the heat 739 did not give. At design
temperatures the clamp binds

$$
\dot m_{739} < \frac{58\,\dot m_{735} + L}{87} = 20\,932\ \mathrm{kg/h}\ (62\ \%),\qquad
\dot m_{735} > \frac{87\,\dot m_{739} - L}{58} = 50\,302\ \mathrm{kg/h}\ (162\ \%)
$$

— the second whenever 328D003 stands above 80.8 %, since 735 follows compartment II's holdup.
Raised as handoff B-40 and decided by the process engineer the same session (decision 14), so no
handoff item stood: where the clamp binds and a feed flows, the feed takes only what 739 gave, less
the shell loss, bounded between no change and V1's share:

$$
Q_{share} = \dot m_{735}\,\varepsilon_T\,(T_{739} - T_{735}),\qquad
Q_{given} = \dot m_{739}\,(T_{739} - T_{740}) - L
$$

$$
T_{738} = T_{735} + \frac{\mathrm{clamp}\big(Q_{given},\ \min(Q_{share}, 0),\ \max(Q_{share}, 0)\big)}{\dot m_{735}}
$$

The bound matters at a trickle: the design loss charged to 100 kg/h of feed would cool it 165 K.
A loss the hot side cannot pay is not charged to the feed, so the balance closes on the loss
actually paid, between 0 and $L$. With no feed the outlets are V1's. The cap is inert while the
clamp does not bind.

| at design temperatures | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|
| 328C004's bottoms stopped | 738 at 114 C, 740 at 56 C; 2023.44 kW made | 738 at 56.0 C — the feed passes through; no loss paid |
| 328C004's bottoms halved | 114 C; 393.45 kW made | 102.6192 C; the design loss paid |
| 735 doubled (the tank full) | 114 C; 768.58 kW made | 102.8841 C; the design loss paid |

The published flag `hot_outlet_clamped` marks a pinched tick.

## XXXVI.5 Structure

`interchanger_outlets` is the law, with its constants as arguments, so 328E021 can take it when
the hydrolyser is ported; `desorber_heat_exchanger` applies it to 328E007 and returns a frozen
`DesorberHeatExchangerResult`: 738 and its temperature, 740 and its temperature, and the flag. The
unit holds no state.

## XXXVI.6 Equivalence achieved

14 tests in `test_feed_effluent_interchanger_equivalence.py`: the design basis (six constants
against V1's, executed); the design point; 81 inlet sets crossing every branch of the clamp — the
hot side hotter and colder than the feed, each flow at design, zero and far off it — with the port
equal to its switched transcription on each, to V1 verbatim wherever the clamp does not bind or
no feed flows, and, where it binds on a feed, V1's made heat and the port's closed balance both
asserted; the three pinched cases both ways; the two thresholds; the flowsheet order; and 3000
ticks coupled to V1's stages 1 and 2 in V1's order — 323C005's solvent halved, 741 opened,
328C004's temperature and bottoms stepped — equal on every tick with `==`. 16 behaviour tests in
`tests/units/desorption/test_feed_effluent_interchanger.py`. Nine mutations: the shell loss
dropped, the clamp dropped, the floor moved, the flag stuck, the cap dropped, the cap's loss
dropped, the cap unbounded, the cap bounded one side only are caught; the cap's balance written
on the feed's inlet temperature instead of the clamped outlet survives, and is equivalent — every
pinched tick has 740 at the feed's temperature or the feed at its V1 share.

# Part XXXVIII — 328C002: desorber I, and the desorption train's species layer

## XXXVIII.1 What the unit is

328C002 is the upper section of the desorption tower: fifteen sieve trays over its own sump,
1250 mm across, stacked on 328C004 on a common skirt (Uhde UD-AU-328-EC-0001 rev 01). Four streams
enter — the feed 738, which 328E007 has heated to 114 C; the reflux 775 from 328D001 at 61 C; and
the two hot overheads of the sections below it, 748 from the hydrolyser at 188 C and 750 from
328C004 at 140 C, which condense in it and are its stripping vapour. What they strip leaves
overhead as 737 at 117 C to 328E004 and 328D001; the stripped liquor leaves the sump at 139 C as
743 through 328P006 and LV-328503 to 328E021 and the hydrolyser.

    738 + 775 + 748 + 750 = 737 + 743:    31 114 + 1675 + 812 + 6833 = 6665 + 33 769 kg/h

Source: V1 `main.py` step_sim, "Stage 3 : 328C002 Desorber-I" (8965-9060), with the aqueous cp
(8828) and the tear reads (8838-8840); the 328C002 constant block (1309-1337), the tray geometry
(1412-1462), the column pressure (2022-2062), LV-328503 (2081-2105), and the F-8 species layer
(2925-3280). The design data are in `data/desorption_train.py` (what the three columns share) and
`data/unit_328c002.py`; the physics in `thermo/ammonia_water.py`, `units/desorption/desorber_stage.py`
and `units/desorption/first_desorber.py`.

## XXXVIII.2 The species layer

**Vapour rows are mole %.** PFD-22 tabulates liquids in mass % and vapours in mole %: read as mass %,
carbon is not conserved across 328C002 (1658 kg/h of CO2 in, 858 out). Stream 737 read as mole %
gives the PFD's own 20.81 kg/kmol; read as mass %, 18.94 (V1 AUDIT F-8).

**The design back-solve over N feeds.** Each stage's vapour is what its feeds bring, plus what
hydrolysis makes, less its liquid, water closing the balance; the vapour against the liquid is the
lumped volatility:

$$
v_i = \sum_f \dot m_f w_{f,i} + \nu_i \xi - \dot m_L w_i \ (\ge 0),\qquad
v_{H_2O} = \dot m_V - \sum_{i\ne H_2O} v_i,\qquad
\alpha_i = \frac{y_i/w_i}{y_{H_2O}/w_{H_2O}}
$$

The anchors chain, in V1's order: 328C003's (4.2734 kmol/h of urea hydrolysed) and 328C004's
first, then 328C002's on the vapours those two deliver — anchoring on the PFD's 748 and 750 rows
instead made the design state a slow leak in V1. 328C002's feed rows bring 0.337 kg/h less urea than
743 carries, inside their rounding; the negative vapour is clipped and reported. Its back-solved
overhead sits within 2.3e-4 of PFD 737. The back-solve's hydrolysis coefficients write CO2 at its
molar mass and lose 6e-4 kg/kmol — 0.0026 kg/h at the design extent, which the overhead's water
carries; the runtime's write CO2 as the closer and conserve it. Both are V1's.

**The live volatility.** A lumped alpha makes one well-mixed stage strip what the trays strip at
design. Off design it moves with the Kremser single-stage equivalent of the column's real stage
count, 13.98 / 22 x 15 = 9.532 theoretical stages:

$$
S_i = K_\infty\,\frac{\alpha_{i,model}(T,P)}{\alpha_{i,model}(des)}\,\frac{V}{L},\qquad
r = \frac{S-1}{S^{N+1}-1},\qquad k = \frac{L}{V}\,\frac{1-r}{r},\qquad
\alpha_i = \alpha_{i,des}\,\frac{k(S_i)}{k(S_{des})}
$$

with $K_\infty$ = 9.5 (V1's AI-328701 derivation at 143 C), V the two hot overheads and L the
bottoms. At design S = 2.1507, r = 3.617e-4, k = 12 206. The model ratio is
`thermo.service.k_ratio` on the stage's live liquid, T held inside 80.05-209.95 C: six degrees
hotter at 4.2 bar a, NH3's relative volatility falls 4.2 % and CO2's rises 16.3 %. Half the design
stripping vapour takes S below 1 and the lumped NH3 and CO2 volatilities to 1.03 % of design.

**The implicit step.** With the summation's denominator lagged one step the vapour is linear in
each species holdup, and the step closes in one line, cannot go negative and is exactly
stationary where source equals sink:

$$
m_{i}^{+} = \frac{M w_i + (\sum_f \dot m_f w_{f,i} + \nu_i\xi)\,h}{1 + (\dot m_V c_i + \dot m_L)\,h / M},\qquad
c_i = \frac{\alpha_i}{\sum_j \alpha_j w_j},\qquad h = \frac{\Delta t}{3600}
$$

M is the stage's new holdup from its own mass balance, so the layer cannot move the heat and
material balance.

**The liquor's vapour pressure at a valve** is its gamma-phi bubble pressure
(`thermo.service.bubble_p`): 743's 0.63 % NH3 lifts it from water's 3.51 to 3.93 bar a at 139 C,
and from 12.55 to 14.97 at 190 C; beyond 209.95 C it is carried on the water line from the edge,
and off the fitted surface it is water's.

## XXXVIII.3 The column

One node: one holdup, one pressure, one temperature, one species vector.

$$
q = \frac{c_p}{3600}\Big[\dot m_{738}(T_{738}-T) + \dot m_{775}(61-T) + \dot m_{748}(188-T) + \dot m_{750}(140-T)\Big]
+ \frac{\dot m_{748}}{3600}\,2000 + \frac{\dot m_{750}}{3600}\,2100
$$

$$
\mathrm{gen} = \dot m_{737,des}\,\frac{q}{Q_{des}},\qquad Q_{des} = 3479.38\ \mathrm{kW}\ (\approx 1879\ \mathrm{kJ/kg\ of\ 737})
$$

with $c_p$ water's at the live temperature (`aqueous_cp` on 4.0 at 139 C). 737 is what the overhead
line passes, not the boil-up: IEC 60534's compressible law anchored on 6665 kg/h, stroke 1, from the
live column pressure to 328D001's, at the live bottoms less the design 22 K, on the live molar mass
of last tick's vapour against the design 20.81. The pressure integrates the imbalance on the free
volume of the 12.85 m3 shell (V1 report A-6):

$$
\frac{dP}{dt} = \frac{RT}{V_v}\,\frac{\mathrm{gen} - \dot m_{737}}{M_{737}} + \frac{P}{T}\frac{dT}{dt} - \frac{P}{V_v}\frac{dV_v}{dt},\qquad P \ge 0.1\ \mathrm{bar\,a}
$$

and the temperature is water's bubble point at the bottom node, $T = T_{sat,water}(P + \Delta P_{col})$,
with $\Delta P_{col} = P_{sat}(139) - 3.5$ = +0.0139 bar on IAPWS-IF97 (V1's comment gives -0.0104, a
value of its retired Antoine curve; the expression is what runs). The round trip returns 139 C to
6e-14 K. The holdup is liquid and overhead lumped, $dM/dt = \sum \dot m_{in} - \dot m_{737} - \dot m_{743}$,
and LI-328503 reads $M / 1588.2 \cdot 50$ %, the design inventory being fifteen aerated trays and the
sump at 1.150 m.

LIC-328503 (DIRECT, 1.50, 180 s — the table's, the PV already in per cent) strokes LV-328503 on
IEC 60534's liquid law: its inlet 328P006's discharge, $P + \rho g (h + 11.728)/10^5 + 19.7$ bar with
the live sump depth and the fixed drop to the pump back-solved so the design suction reads the
datasheet's 4.7 bar a; its outlet the hydrolyser's live pressure; linear trim; its choke the
liquor's bubble pressure (§XXXVIII.6, B-43).

## XXXVIII.4 The overhead and the reflux: what is live and what is assumed

*Decided 2026-10-16 (decision 118, handoff B-31): the port charges these inlets at their producers' live temperatures as departures from the producers' designs, §LXX.2; what follows is V1's, which ``live_inlets=False`` keeps.*

| term | in V1, and the port |
|---|---|
| 737's flow | live: the column's and 328D001's pressures, the live molar mass |
| 737's composition | live: the Kremser volatility on the column's liquid, rigorous T/P derivative |
| 737's temperature | the live bottoms less a fixed 22 K (TT-328008) |
| the boil-up | energy-limited on the live duty, with CONSTANT latent heats (2000, 2100 kJ/kg) |
| the bottoms temperature | water's bubble point at the column pressure plus a lumped offset — not the liquor's |
| 738's temperature | live, 328E007's outlet this tick |
| 775's temperature | the drum's DESIGN 61 C, not 328D001's live temperature (handoff B-31) |
| 748's and 750's temperatures | the PFD's 188 and 140 C, not the live 328C003 and 328C004 (B-31) |
| 738's and 775's compositions | the PFD rows: 328D003 and 328D001 carry no species |
| 748's and 750's compositions | live, the vapours the two sections below delivered last tick |
| 775's flow | live, one tick late |

The overhead's condensing is 328D001's, not 328C002's: in V1 328E004's duty is a stroke-proportional
$Q_{des}\cdot op/50$ on TIC-328002, not a UA on the live cooling water, and the drum's energy balance
condenses 737 at a back-solved 2163.55 kJ/kg where 328C002 boils it at an implied 1879 kJ/kg — a
526 kW gap V1's AUDIT C4 ascribes to carbamate formation. Both are 328D001's (Part XLIII).

## XXXVIII.5 The boundaries, and the loops

| stream | from / to | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|---|
| 738, its temperature | 328E007 | this tick's | `DesorberHeatExchangerResult`, same tick |
| 748 + its vapour, 750 + its vapour, 775 | 328C003, 328C004, 328D001 | tears `R328_748`, `R328_750`, `R328_775`, `y_328_748`, `y_328_750` | arguments, one tick late |
| the hydrolyser's pressure, 328D001's | 328C003, 328D001 | their states at the top of the tick | arguments |
| 743, 737 + its vapour | to 328C003, 328D001 | this tick's | `FirstDesorberResult`, same tick |

V1 steps 328D003, 328E007, 328C002, 328C003, 328C004, 328D001. The flowsheet with 739, 748, 750 and
775 declared tears orders 328D003 -> 328E007 -> 328C002 -> 328C003 -> 328C004, with 328D001 anywhere
after 328C002; V1's order is one the same-tick edges allow. No loop closes within a tick: the
column's heat returns to 328E007 only through 328C004, and its overhead to it only through 328D001's
reflux, each a tick late.

## XXXVIII.6 The decided divergences

*Re-measured 2026-09-30 on decision 24's books (the liquid loses what boils, §XLI.5), which stand
on both sides of every test below; the figures moved in the third or fourth digit.*

**B-42, a negative duty condenses vapour — decided 2026-09-30.** V1 clamps the boil-up at zero.
With 748 and 750 lost the net duty goes negative, the overhead empties the vapour space to 328D001's
pressure, and V1's bottoms stay at water's bubble point there — 128.5 C, where the two liquid feeds
mix at 111.3 C: 622.5 kW made, every hour, and a 743 17 K too hot for 328E021. The port lets the
negative boil-up condense vapour: the pressure and its bubble point fall until the duty balances.
The overhead line passes nothing backwards, so 328D001 does not feed the column below its pressure.

| 748 and 750 stopped, 300 s on | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|
| boil-up | 0 (clamped) | condensing, back to 0 |
| net duty | -636.7 kW, discarded | 0.54 kW |
| pressure / bottoms | 2.599 bar a / 128.87 C | 1.482 bar a / 111.28 C (feeds mix at 111.29) |

**B-43, LV-328503's flash choke reads the liquor at the valve — decided 2026-09-30.** V1 reads the
liquor's bubble pressure at 328E021's cold OUTLET, 190 C (design Pv 14.97 bar a). Uhde's loop summary
UD-MR-328-EC-0001 rev 1, loop L 328503 sheet 2/2 (scanned, read from the page image), puts the valve
on line 100-AW7-328180 with its inlet at 24.0 bar a and 140 C, its outlet at 16.98 bar a, 37.2 m3/h,
design temperature 170 C: upstream of the exchanger. The port reads the bottoms, design Pv 3.93 bar a.

| 750 halved | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|
| the bottoms' NH3 | doubles in 30 s | rises to 5.4 % (half the stripping vapour) |
| LV-328503 | chokes: Pv at 190 C passes the pump's discharge; wide open, 14.4 t/h | 33.7 t/h at 52 % |
| LI-328503, 600 s on | 148 %, climbing to 613 % in an hour (19.5 t in a 12.85 m3 shell) | 50.0 % |

The two parted at 7.2 s; on a doubled reflux V1's choke binds after 100.6 s and carries a level 0.6
points higher. Where it does not bind, V1 and the port are the same float.

**Decision 11, applied as a standing rule.** 328P006 is capped at the liquid above a 1 kg heel plus
what arrives net of what boils, flagged; with LV-328503 wide open it reaches the heel at 169.7 s,
where V1's floor would make the liquid. A full shell overflows: V1's holdup has no ceiling, so with
LV-328503 held at 20 % the shell is full at 1881.6 s and V1 goes on filling past it; the port holds
11 988 kg — the cylindrical shell at 933 kg/m3, LI-328503 then reading 377 % — and 19.5 t/h leaves
as the overflow at the bottoms' state, the liquid a flooded column carries through its overhead
line to 328E004 and 328D001, which takes it (decision 30, §XLIII.4). The swell term sees the holdup the overflow leaves. The
boil-up is not capped: a column that boils more than arrives still reaches the floor.

## XXXVIII.7 Structure

`thermo/ammonia_water.py` (the liquor: the mole-% rows, the N-feed back-solve and `DesorberAnchor`,
Kremser's residual and its inverse, `DesorberStage` and its builder, the relative-volatility ratio,
the liquor's Pv); `units/desorption/desorber_stage.py` (`alpha_live`, `advance_species`, shared by
the three columns); `units/desorption/first_desorber.py` (`lic_328503`, `FirstDesorber`,
`FirstDesorberResult`); `data/desorption_train.py` (PFD-22's flows and compositions for the three
columns, 328D001's design temperature and pressure, the tower's trays, the Kremser stage counts, the
three anchors); `data/unit_328c002.py` (the vessel, holdup and shell, the pressure offset, the energy
anchor, LV-328503 and 328P006, LIC-328503, the stage). 328E021's effectiveness and the hydrolyser's
temperatures are not needed and not ported here: B-43 retires V1's one reading of them.

## XXXVIII.8 Equivalence achieved

108 tests in `test_first_desorber_equivalence.py`: the design basis (72 constants, 739 against the
tank's own float, the three anchors and the Kremser stage, B-43's choke anchor both ways); the
state and controller seeds; eleven scenarios TICK BY TICK against the switched transcription —
design hold, the stripping vapour lost and 750 up a fifth, the reflux doubled, the feed cut and
hotter, 328D001 lower, the hydrolyser higher and hotter, a richer 748, every inlet lost, the
hydrolyser depressured so LV-328503 flashes — and the seven no later departure reaches also on V1's
lines for all four, on decision 24's books; LIC-328503 in MAN at 20 % and on 60 %; each of the five
departures both ways (decision 24's with the books, §XLI.5), bit-exact to the tick
it first acts; the flowsheet order; and 3000 ticks coupled to V1's 328D003 and 328E007 in V1's
order, 738 and its temperature same-tick. Every comparison with `==`. 15 tests in
`tests/thermo/test_ammonia_water.py`, 6 in `tests/units/desorption/test_desorber_stage.py`, 8 in
`tests/units/desorption/test_first_desorber.py`. Ten mutations — the heel cap and the overflow
each dropped, the overflow left out of the swell term and of the species step, the boil-up clamp
restored, the volatility at the overhead pressure, the choke at a frozen temperature and at 190 C,
the heel's overhead term dropped, the top's 22 K dropped — are each caught.
