# Part XXXIX — Phase 4's scheduled items: the flash budget, the liquid-full line, B-2, the data hunt

## XXXIX.1 The flash budget, 60 sweeps (handoff A-9) — decided 2026-09-30

`thermo.service.flash` ran V1's 40 successive-substitution sweeps. A dilute, hot 328-type liquor
reaches a residual of 1.09e-7 against the 1e-7 tolerance at sweep 40 and converges at sweep 41, so
V1 flags a good solve unconverged. The process engineer decided the budget be 60
(`FLASH_OUTER_ITERS`). The handoff had said the change moved no ported number. It does: the 323
stages' rigorous vapour departure (`urea_liquor.model_alpha`, V1 `_sol_model_alpha`) REFUSES an
unconverged flash and sends the stage to its anchored vector, so every state whose solve needs 41
to 60 sweeps now takes the rigorous branch where V1 fell back. Raised again with that measured,
and decided the same way, 60 everywhere:

| at 60 sweeps, where V1's 40 refused | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|
| 323F004's liquor at 114 C | refused, the anchored vector | converged on sweep 41, the rigorous departure |
| 323F010, PV-329208 at 45 %, two hours on: superheat | 16.448 K | 19.901 K |
| 323F010, HV-323605 at 80 %: PT-323204 / level / superheat | 0.3828 bar a / 121.56 % / 2.966 K | 0.3825 / 121.51 % / 3.806 K |
| 323F010 on a sagging LP header (4.5 / 4.0 bar a) | 99.0414 / 98.8722 C | 99.0424 / 98.8643 C |
| 323C003 with PV-329202 shut: heater gas ratio / pressure / temperature | 0.0563 / 3.6181 bar a / 116.07 C | 0.0287 / 3.6056 / 115.55 C |

Every design state converges in 20 sweeps or fewer, so no design point moves. 323F004's liquor at
116 C still refuses at 60 sweeps (residual 5.4e-6). V1's `thermo_service` is seeded on the port's
budget in every harness that lifts V1 physics (`tests/equivalence/v1_loader.v1_service`, a proxy
whose `flash` defaults to 60 and clears V1's memo when the budget changes — V1's memo keys do not
carry it), so each comparison executes V1's own code on the decided budget; the budget itself is
asserted both ways in `test_service_equivalence.py` (the marginal state refused on 40, converged on
41 sweeps on 60, to V1's floats on V1's own 60) and `test_liquor_stage_equivalence.py` (three
liquors whose grids part).

## XXXIX.2 The liquid-full line (handoff B-21) — decided 2026-09-30

V1's product lines carried the flow rate in the packet with the temperature and composition, so a
line delayed its FLOW by the dead time and created or destroyed liquor on every flow change
(§XXIX.6). Decided by the process engineer: the line delivers the live departure flow at once and
delays only what the liquor IS. `core.transport.transport_process_properties` carries a
`property_packet` — temperature, composition and cp on a unit flow — through V1's own FIFO, the dead
time still the line's inventory over the LIVE flow; `units.recirc.liquor_line.receive_liquor`, the
arrival at 323C003, 323F004, 323F010 and 323D002, delivers the departure flow with the arrived
properties. A settled line hands back the original scalars, as before, so no design point moves.

| on the 323C003 -> 323F004 line, the drain changed at 5 s | V1 | the port |
|---|---|---|
| stops | 52 959 kg arrive that were never sent, over the 1800 s cap | nothing arrives from the stop |
| cut 25 %, 200 s | +157.4 kg made | 0 |
| up 20 %, 200 s | -78.9 kg lost | 0 |
| cut 25 %, then 140 C liquor at 10 s | — | the flow at once; the hotter liquor 21.31 s later, the slower line's residence |

The four stage transcriptions carry the switch ``line_decided`` (default the port's lines, V1's
own FIFO on the unit-flow packet), so every scenario compares the port with V1's code on the
decided line; ``test_flash_tank_equivalence.py::test_a_stopped_column_drain_decided_divergence``
runs V1 verbatim against the port — bit-exact to the stop, then V1's drum taking in 3.5 t in two
minutes that the column never sent, the port's nothing. `tests/core/test_transport.py` (3) and
`tests/units/recirc/test_liquor_line.py` pin the line's behaviour.

| 20 000 s, CO2 against design | per species | whole volatile sub-vector |
|---|---|---|
| design bottoms: 323C003 / 323F004 / 323F010 | +0.1 / -0.1 / +0.1 % | +0.1 / 0.0 / +0.3 % |

# Part XL — The chest anchors, the chest cascades on span, and the vendor valves

Three decisions of the process engineer, 2026-09-30, each a decided divergence asserted from both
sides: the 323E002 and 323E010 steam chests anchored on their datasheets (handoff Open data gaps
and B-23, closed); the two chest cascades on the DCS table's gains per cent of span (decision 10
extended); and every ported vendor valve on its own trim and rated capacity (handoff B-44,
closed).

## XL.1 The chest anchors

A chest's design pressure sets its conductance and its valve's design stroke, both back-solved on
it, so the design duty holds whatever the anchor; what moves is the approach the heater works
across, and so every off-design response.

| | 323E002 | 323E010 |
|---|---|---|
| V1's anchor | 3.96 bar a — 0.90 x a retired 4.4 bar a header (`main_backup.py` 854-855) | 1.76 bar a — a 40 % stroke on the same retired header (0.40 x 4.4) |
| the port's anchor | **3.9 bar a**, Tsat 142.70 C | **2.5 bar a**, Tsat 127.41 C |
| sources | DDS UD-AU-323-EC-0007 page 2 (3.900 bar a in and out, 145 C in, 142 C out); PFD 918 (3.9 bar a, 145 C); PT-329202's loop summary (UD-MR-329-EC-0001, loop P 329202, normal 3.9 bar a) | PFD 926 (2.5 bar a, 139 C, 1.35 kg/m3, 11 230 kg/h); DDS UD-AU-323-EC-0009 page 2 (2.5 bar a, 139 C, 1.29 kg/m3) |
| conductance UA [kW/K], V1 -> port | 710.01 -> 760.57 | 421.04 -> 255.13 |
| design stroke [%], V1 -> port | 78.99 -> 77.79 | 35.11 -> 49.87 |

**The superheat is the header's.** Both datasheets print "LP Steam - saturated" beside a
temperature above the saturation of their pressure: 145 C at 3.9 bar a, 139 C at 2.5 bar a. It is
the LP header steam, PFD 917, saturated at 4.4 bar a and 147 C, let down through PV-329202 and
PV-329208: the letdown is isenthalpic, and at 2742.4 kJ/kg IAPWS-IF97 puts it at 145.06 C at 3.9 bar
a and 139.28 C at 2.5 bar a — the two datasheets' figures. Both densities confirm the pressures
(2.03 and 1.29 kg/m3; saturated steam at 3.5 bar a would be 1.91). The chest
condenses at the saturation of its pressure, and the few kelvin of superheat are ignored, as V1's
chest law ignores them. One source disagrees: PT-329208's loop summary (UD-MR-329-EC-0001, loop P
329208, sheet 1/2, line D01) gives the normal as 3.5 bar a (2.5 bar g) — 139 C's own saturation
pressure. It is outvoted by the design basis and the heater's own datasheet.

**What the anchor changes, both sides** (`test_rectifying_column_equivalence.py`,
`test_a_sagging_header_saturates_v1s_steam_valve_and_not_the_ports`): the LP header sags to 4.6 bar
a. On V1's 3.96 bar a anchor PV-329202 needs more than its full stroke to hold the chest; it pins at
100 % inside 480 s and 323C003 settles 0.110 K low for good. On the datasheet's 3.9 the valve keeps
its margin (at most 99.35 %) and the column returns to 135 C.

The switch in the transcriptions, ``chest_decided``: V1's own ``R323_E00x_OP_DES`` and
``R323_E00x_UA_KW`` statements (``main.py`` 1055, 1098, 1171, 1182) re-executed by `lift` on the
decided anchor, so the stroke and conductance are V1's expressions on the sourced number.

## XL.2 The chest cascades on span

The functional diagrams (UD-MR-323-FF-0002, sheets 4 and 5) scale each temperature master's output
onto its chest slave's range, SP = OUTP / 100 . PIC:MAX. The ranges (loop summaries, line D07):
TT-323007 and TT-323012 0-160 C; PT-329202 and PT-329208 0-6 bar g. V1 applied the DCS table's
numbers in engineering units and multiplied each chest PIC by ``_chest_slave_kc_scale``, the ratio
of its retired PV's gain (P_header / 100 bar per %) to the physical chest's, to hold the loop gain
it had tuned against the retired PV.

| loop | table | V1 | the port, per cent of span |
|---|---|---|---|
| TIC-323007 | 2.00, 500 s | 2.0 bar/K | 2.00 x 6 / 160 = **0.075 bar/K** |
| PIC-329202 | 0.65, 30 s | 0.65 x 5.8716 = 3.817 %/bar | 0.65 x 100 / 6 = **10.83 %/bar**, no scale |
| TIC-323012 | no row | 3.6 bar/K, 1200 s (V1's retune, Appendix C) | TIC-323007's row on its own spans, **0.075 bar/K, 500 s** |
| PIC-329208 | 0.20, 60 s | 0.20 x 1.8594 = 0.372 %/bar | 0.20 x 100 / 6 = **3.33 %/bar**, no scale |

**The scale is dropped** (decided): the table's gain on span is the plant's own controller on the
plant's own chest, and V1's scale existed only to hold a loop gain set on the wrong unit basis.
`units.steam_chest.chest_slave_kc_scale` is deleted; 324E001 and 324E003's chest PICs take the same
rule at their ports.

**TIC-323012 runs its sibling's row** (decided). Its gain was V1's own retune, not the table's, so
not the unit-basis error — but it was stable only behind V1's slow PIC-329208 (a closed loop of about
6000 s). Behind the slave on span, V1's 3.6 bar/K and 1200 s limit-cycle after a -2 K set-point
step: +/- 0.5 K, a period of about 50 minutes, with the evaporation touching the B-24 cap at every
peak — and the cycle survives the cap removed (+/- 0.65 K), so it is the tuning, not the cap.
TIC-323007's row, the same cascade on the same unit, on TT-323012's span is stable. A stated tuning,
not a table value (handoff B-45).

Measured, the port against V1's gains on the port's anchors (4 h at 0.1 s):

| scenario | V1's gains | span, scale dropped (built) | span, scale kept |
|---|---|---|---|
| TIC-323007 +2 K: settled within 0.1 K | 1550 s | 3570 s | 3667 s |
| 323C003, LP header to 4.6 bar a: dip / recovered | -0.5 K / 203 s | -0.8 K / 1479 s | -0.2 K / 226 s |
| TIC-323012 -2 K (sibling row) | 3304 s (V1's retune) | 4435 s | 4633 s |
| TIC-323012 +2 K | 3573 s | 3173 s | 3241 s |
| 323F010, LP header to 4.6 bar a | -0.46 K / 1792 s | -0.38 K / 2218 s | -0.32 K / 1733 s |

**B-20's closed-loop limit cycle is gone.** On V1's gains the 323C003 cascade reaches for 135.000 C
faster than the composition cap lets the overhead follow, winds against the cap and cycles, 134.9896
to 135.0085 C with a 267-268 s period — on V1's anchor and on the port's alike (1191 of 5400
samples on the cap). On TIC-323007's table gain on span it settles: 135.00000 to 135.00002 C from
the second hour on, PV-329202 at 77.738 %, the overhead never on the cap. Asserted both ways in
`test_v1s_closed_loop_limit_cycle_and_the_ports_settled_column`. The open-loop fixed point's
offset, 135.0039 C, is B-20's and stays.

## XL.3 The vendor valves (handoff B-44)

**The trim.** Flowserve's calculation sheets (UD-MR-G00-DZ-0048-003, one page per position, PDF
pages 46-64) give each valve's Kvs and plug code and three sizing cases: pressures, temperature,
flow, density, the calculated Kv, the stroke, and FL (liquid) or xT (gas). The plug code's sixth
letter is the characteristic: G, Valtek's modified equal percentage, on fourteen valves; L, linear,
on two. The modified trim is fitted to its own 41 cases (44 with PV-328203's three, catalogued
with 328C003 in session 26 and reproduced within the same 0.50 %):

    Kv/Kvs = R^(h - 1)              h >= h0 = 1 / ln R          R = 20
    Kv/Kvs = h . e . ln R / R       h <  h0 = 0.334             (the tangent line through 0)

reproduces every printed stroke, 9 % to 91 %, to within 0.50 % — the sheets print it to a whole
per cent; the least-squares optimum, R = 19.9, is no better. The two pieces meet with equal value
and slope. The linear trims run 0.3 to 2.2 points of stroke below a pure line; the port's linear
law is the line. `control.valve.cv_fraction(h, "mod_equal_pct")`, `stroke_for_cv_fraction` its
inverse. CCI's PV-322203 (UD-MR-G00-DZ-0009-004, sheet 6) is a Drag 28-stage angle valve, equal
percentage, rated Cv 32; the sheet prints no rangeability, FL or xT, so it runs on the IEC 50:1 of
`EQUAL_PCT_RANGE` and `XT_GLOBE`, both stated.

**The design stroke** is where the rated capacity passes the design flow on the vendor's normal
case: phi = C_normal . (Q_des / Q_normal) / C_rated at the vendor's density, h_des its inverse
(`data.control_valves.design_stroke_pct`). A valve shut at design is anchored on its full-stroke
capacity on the normal case instead.

| valve | Kvs | trim | normal case: Q, Kv, stroke, FL / xT | the port's design stroke | V1's |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FV-323401 | 4 | mod. eq. % | 1.5 m3/h, 0.8488, 48 %, FL 0.9770 | 49.26 % | 50 %, linear |
| FV-323402 | 4 | mod. eq. % | 1.5 m3/h, 0.6101, 37 %, FL 0.9790 | 38.23 % | 50 %, linear |
| FV-323418 | 4 | mod. eq. % | 3.3 m3/h, 2.07, 78 %, FL 0.9722 | 78.45 % | 50 %, linear |
| LV-323503 | 25 | mod. eq. % | 8 m3/h, 7.19, 58 %, FL 0.9457 | 52.86 % (all of 718) | 50 %, linear |

## XL.4 What the sheets add that is not built

* **LV-323501 is sized flashing.** The vendor's cases give the column liquor at its bubble point,
  vapour pressure 4.1 bar a against 4.3 upstream: FL^2 (P1 - FF . Pv) = 0.50 bar against a 2.7 bar
  drop, so the normal case is choked. V1 passes the anchored law no vapour pressure at LV-323501 or
  LV-323505, so neither can choke and the drain always answers the downstream pressure. Decided
  2026-09-30 and built: every letdown flashes where its downstream condition warrants it (B-46,
  §XLIV.2).
* **The HP angle valves' CONVAL sets** (UD-MR-G00-DZ-0042-012 to -054: HV-322605, LV-322501,
  XV-322902, XV-322903) are Uhde's, not Flowserve's or CCI's, and are not read.
* LV-328503, LV-328504, PV-323202, PV-323203, PV-329202, PV-329208 and HV-323605 are in no vendor
  set found; V1's back-solves stand.

# Part XLI — 328C003 and 328E021: the hydrolyser; the liquid pays what boils; the relief devices

## XLI.1 What the unit is

328C003 destroys the urea the process condensate still carries, so the purified condensate meets
its 1 ppm guarantee:

$$
\mathrm{NH_2CONH_2 + H_2O \rightarrow 2\,NH_3 + CO_2}
$$

It is a liquid-filled trayed column, 1950 mm across and 20 850 mm of shell (62.27 m3), at 200 C and
16.8 bar a. The feed, 328C002's bottoms 743, reaches it as 746 through 328E021's cold side at 190 C;
MP steam 911 injected at the bottom carries the reaction's heat and strips the gas it makes, which
leaves overhead as 748 through PV-328203 to 328C002; the hydrolysed liquor leaves as 747 through
LV-328504 and 328E021's hot side (749, 148 C) to 328C004.

    746 + 911 = 748 + 747:    33 769 + 1105 = 812 + 34 062 kg/h

Source: V1 `main.py` step_sim, "Stage 4 : 328C003 Hydrolyser" (9062-9165), 328E021's hot outlet in
"Stage 5" (9181-9183), TIC-328012 (10080), the cp line (8829), `hydrolysis_x_328c003` (3328-3353);
the seeds in `State.__init__`; the telemetry (10767-10790). Data in `data/unit_328c003.py` and
`data/desorption_train.py`; physics in `units/desorption/hydrolyser.py`, with 328E021 on
`feed_effluent_interchanger.interchanger_outlets` and the species on `desorber_stage.advance_species`.

## XLI.2 The equations

**The conversion** — second-order plug flow on Inoue and Otsuka's rate constant
(`thermo.kinetics`), the residence scaling inversely with the live feed, $U_0$ and $H_0$ the feed's
urea and water in kmol/m3 at 908.5 kg/m3:

$$
\tau = \tau_{des}\frac{\dot m_{746,des}}{\dot m_{746}},\qquad
X = \frac{H_0(1-e)}{H_0 - U_0 e},\quad e = \exp\!\big(-k(T)(H_0-U_0)\tau\big),\qquad
\xi = \frac{\dot m_{746} w_{urea}}{M_{urea}} X
$$

($X = kU_0\tau/(1+kU_0\tau)$ where $H_0 = U_0$). At design, $\tau_{des}$ = 3600 s, $X$ = 0.999919,
$\xi$ = 4.273 kmol/h.

**The overhead generation** — the reaction's gas plus what the steam strips:

$$
g_{748} = \xi\,(2M_{NH_3} + M_{CO_2}) + g_{strip,des}\frac{\dot m_{911}}{\dot m_{911,des}}
\qquad (333.60 + 478.40 = 812\ \mathrm{kg/h})
$$

**The overhead** is what PV-328203 passes on the IEC 60534 compressible law, from the live column
to 328C002's live pressure, on the live molar mass of the tick before's vapour, anchored on the
design overhead; PIC-328203 strokes it on the column pressure.

**The pressure** integrates generation against overhead on the free volume (V1 report A-6):

$$
\frac{dP}{dt} = \frac{RT}{V_v}\,\frac{g_{748} - \dot m_{748}}{M_{748}} + \frac{P}{T}\frac{dT}{dt}
- \frac{P}{V_v}\frac{dV_v}{dt}
$$

on the old holdup and the tick before's temperature change.

**The heat balance**, semi-implicit in the 746 feed — with the liquid charged the latent heat of
everything that boils (decision 24):

$$
(Mc_p + \dot m_{746}c_p\,\Delta t)\frac{\Delta T}{\Delta t} = \dot m_{746}c_p(T_{746}-T)
+ \dot m_{911}\Delta H_{911} - g_{748}\lambda_{748} - \xi\,\Delta H_{hyd}
$$

$\Delta H_{911}$ = 2235 kJ/kg; $\Delta H_{hyd}$ = 101.5 kJ/mol, 120.48 kW at design. $\lambda_{748}$ is
back-solved so the design holds — 1377.97 kJ/kg — and V1 then takes the design endotherm out of it
(`main.py` 3373, an augmented assignment): 843.84 kJ/kg, the value the stage runs on.

**The holdup** — $dM/dt = \dot m_{746} + \dot m_{911} - g_{748} - \dot m_{747}$ (decision 24); the
level is $M/M_{des}\times 50$, 34 062 kg at 50 %.

**The letdown.** LIC-328504 strokes LV-328504 on the IEC 60534 liquid law, from the live column
plus its live head (1.118 bar at design) to 328C004's pressure of the tick before, linear, 50 % at
design; its choke on the liquor's bubble pressure at 328E021's hot outlet of the tick before — 5.06
bar a at 148 C, so it flashes at design (V1).

**328E021** heats 746 by a temperature effectiveness back-solved on the design temperatures,
$\varepsilon_T$ = 51/61, and cools 747 by the energy balance less the design shell loss, 49 005
kg.K/h (`interchanger_outlets`, 328E007's law). Its hot outlet, 749, goes to 328C004 and to
LV-328504's choke next tick.

**TIC-328012** reads $T - T_{746}$, 10 K at design, for its faceplate; its output drives nothing (V1).
The P&ID's cascade onto FIC-329402 is kept unwired by the process engineer's decision of
2026-09-30: on this PV, which rises with the column's temperature, the drawn direct action runs
away (handoff B-48, deferred to Phase 7; §XLII.7).

**The species** step implicitly on the design volatilities times the live ratio
(`des_rel_vol_ratio`), with no Kremser stage correction — a liquid-filled column — the hydrolysis
extent as a source.

## XLI.5 The liquid pays what boils — decided 2026-09-30 (decision 24)

V1 takes the overhead out of the liquid and charges its latent heat on what the overhead VALVE
passes, while the pressure integral fills the head space with what the column GENERATES. The
vapour a throttled valve holds back is therefore counted twice — once as liquid, once as head-space
vapour — and boiled for nothing. The process engineer decided the liquid pays for what boils: it
loses the generation, and on 328C003 pays its latent heat; the head space holds the difference,
which the pressure integral already carried. Decided on 328C003 and retro-fitted to 328C002, where
the boil-up is energy-limited and may be negative (decision 15): there the liquid gains the
condensate of a negative boil-up. Both are inert at design to rounding (1e-6 kg/h on 328C002's
second tick).

The books are kept on both sides — the liquid plus the head space's vapour, the moles read off the
pressure state by the gas law on the free volume and priced at the molar mass the tick ran on,
against what crossed the boundary:

| scenario | V1 makes | = V1's integral of generation less overhead | the port | temperature |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 328C003, PV-328203 at 20 %, 1 h | 505.10 kg | yes | < 0.05 kg | V1 203.09 C (3.1 K on latent heat never charged); the port 200.000 C, 40.63 bar a (V1 36.10) |
| 328C003, PV-328203 shut, 1 h | 812.04 kg | yes | < 0.05 kg | V1 205.11 C; the port 200.000 C, 53.07 bar a (V1 42.32) |
| 328C003, PIC-328203 to 17.5 bar a, 1 h | 14.43 kg | yes | < 0.05 kg | V1 200.08 C; the port 200.000 C |
| 328C002, 748 and 750 lost, 5 min | -16.23 kg (the condensate vanishes) | yes | < 0.01 kg | — |
| 328C002, 328D001 1 bar higher, 5 min | +4.52 kg | yes | < 0.01 kg | — |

Pricing the stored moles at the tick's molar mass is what makes the books close: re-priced at the
final composition, a head space whose vapour shifts from ammonia-rich to steam changes mass with no
flow (+10 kg on 328C002's lost-vapour case, on both sides alike) — the lumped node carries one
vapour composition, the equilibrium one, and that limit is V1's.

On 328C003 the throttled column now holds 200 C while its pressure rises faster — to 53 bar a with
the overhead shut, past the column's 28.5 bar a design and its relief valve's 24.01 bar a set
pressure (§XLI.6) — on V1's lines. Decided 2026-09-30 and built: SV32852 holds it between 24.01
and 21.71 bar a (B-47, §XLIV.3).

Pins moved on 328C002 (both sides of every test on the new books): B-42's port 1.482 bar a /
111.28 C and 0.54 kW; B-43's partings 7.2 s and 100.6 s, V1's LV-328503 14.4 t/h and 148 %; the heel
at 169.7 s; the full shell at 1881.6 s; the behaviour pins in the fifth digit.

# Part XLII — 328C004: desorber II, FFIC-329401 on the desorbers' feed, its ratio station and the 741 recycle

## XLII.1 What the unit is

328C004 is the lower section of the desorption tower: twenty-two sieve trays over its own sump,
1250 mm across and 13 030 mm of shell (15.99 m3), under 328C002 on a common skirt. 749 — the
hydrolyser's bottoms after 328E021's hot side — enters at the top at 148 C; LP steam 931 enters at
the bottom on FIC-329401. The steam and what it strips leave overhead as 750 to 328C002 through a
line with no valve; the purified condensate leaves the sump as 739 at 143 C through 328E007's hot
side and LV-328505 to the boundary — or, from ahead of LV-328505, through 328E001 and FV-328406 back
to 328D003 as 741 (§XLII.5).

    749 + 931 = 750 + 739:    34 062 + 6495 = 6833 + 33 724 kg/h;    739 = the export + 741

Source: V1 `main.py` step_sim, "Stage 5 : 328C004 Desorber-II" (9169-9253, less 328E021's hot
outlet 9181-9183, which is the hydrolyser's), the cp line (8830), the tear reads (8842, 8844) and
writes (9670, 9675-9676), AI-328701 (10330), the seeds and the telemetry (10796-10813). Data in
`data/unit_328c004.py`; physics in `units/desorption/second_desorber.py`, the species on
`desorber_stage`, AI-328701's inference in `thermo/ammonia_water.py`.

## XLII.2 The equations

**The boil-up** is what the net duty can boil, anchored on the design duty (4042.9 kW):

$$
q = \frac{\dot m_{749} c_p (T_{749}-T)}{3600} + \frac{\dot m_{931}\,\Delta H_{931}}{3600},\qquad
g = \dot m_{750,des}\,\frac{q}{Q_{des}}
$$

$\Delta H_{931}$ = 2136 kJ/kg (V1's literal); $c_p$ water's at the live temperature. Negative where
the duty condenses vapour (decision 15).

**The overhead** 750 is the IEC 60534 compressible law, stroke fixed at 1, from the live column to
328C002's live pressure at the live bottoms' temperature, on the live molar mass of last tick's
vapour (design 17.98 kg/kmol), anchored on 3.7 -> 3.5 bar a.

**The pressure** integrates boil-up against overhead on the free volume (V1 report A-6), on the old
holdup and the tick before's temperature change; **the temperature** is water's bubble point at the
bottom node, $T = T_{sat}(P + \Delta P_{col})$, $\Delta P_{col}$ = +0.2325 bar on IAPWS-IF97 (V1's
comment gives +0.204, a value of its retired Antoine curve). **The holdup** loses the boil-up
(decision 24); level $M/M_{des}\times 50$, 1436.5 kg at 50 %.

**The letdown.** LIC-328505 (1.45, 180 s, the table's) strokes LV-328505 on the IEC 60534 liquid
law from the live column plus its live head (0.1148 bar at design) to the 1.0 bar a boundary datum
— 328E007 between, its drop lumped on the valve (V1's stated choice) — or, while FIC-328406 is in
cascade, sets FIC-328406 with LV-328505 shut (§XLII.5).

**The steam.** FFIC-329401, a ratio station (§XLII.4), asks FIC-329401 for its ratio set point,
0.20685 t/m3, times the desorbers' feed in m3/h, in kg/h, and displays the measured ratio — last
tick's 931 in t/h over the feed; FIC-329401 strokes FV-329401 (linear from 50 %, a butterfly valve
with no sizing sheet) on FT-329401's reading lagged 5 s.

**The species** step implicitly on the stage's live Kremser volatility — 13.98 theoretical stages,
the LP steam the stripping agent, the bottoms the liquid — and **AI-328701** reads the slip as a
conductivity at 25 C (Kohlrausch; NH3 a weak base, Kb 1.8e-5; 5 % of the urea slip hydrolysed in
the hot line; CO2 left out as PFD 739 tabulates none): 6.93 uS/cm at design.

## XLII.3 FFIC-329401 on the desorbers' feed — decided 2026-09-30 (handoff B-39)

The P&ID (sheet 104, `References/Merged_Searchable_PIDs.pdf` page 7) draws FIC-328402 on the line
into 328E007's cold side — PFD 735, the desorbers' feed — and FFIC-329401 taking its signal from
FIC-328402 and FIC-329401 and setting FIC-329401's set point; the functional diagram
UD-MR-329-FF-0002 page 2 draws the same (FFY-329401 = FT-329401 / FT-328402). V1 takes the feed
from 744, the 323E003 wash leg, where it hangs FIC-328402. The process engineer decided the ratio
reads 735. It reads the tank's draw this tick (the tank steps first) at PFD 735's density,
31 114 / 31.4 = 990.9 kg/m3; the design ratio is V1's to 3e-16. FIC-328402 itself stays on 744
(B-39, kept until Phase 7) — until 2026-10-09, when it moved to 735 (decision 81, §LXIV.3).

| 735 cut a fifth | V1 (on 744) | the port (on 735, the station) |
|---|---|---|
| 931 at 30 s / 120 s / 600 s | 6495 / 6495 / 6495 (blind) | 6413 / 6170 / 5493, the ratio's 80 %, 5196, asked on the tick |

With 749 unchanged (the column alone) the cut steam strips less: an hour on 15 ppm of ammonia
reaches AI-328701, 32 uS/cm. (Before the station, on V1's PI, the port's steam was at 6085 / 5239 /
5196: §XLII.4.)

## XLII.4 FFIC-329401, a ratio station — decided 2026-09-30 (handoff B-49)

The functional diagram UD-MR-329-FF-0002 page 2 (vendor archive, scanned, read from the page image)
draws FFIC-329401 as a RATIOSTN block: its output OUTP is FIC-329401's external set point E1REF;
its inputs are the base flow MV (FT-328402, 735) and the measured ratio EXTRATIO (FFY-329401,
FT-329401 / FT-328402); SEQAUTO and SEQE1 come from FIC-329401's external-set-point status. V1
runs a PI on the measured ratio instead, on its own retune (8.0e5 kg/h per t/m3, 40 s; the tuning
table has no row). The process engineer decided the port builds the station as drawn (the "typo
rule": V1 missed the wiring the diagrams show).

$$
\mathrm{OUTP} = \mathrm{clamp}\!\left(R_{sp}\cdot\frac{\dot m_{735}}{\rho_{735}}\cdot 1000,\ 0,\ 12\,000\right)\ \mathrm{kg/h}
$$

$R_{sp}$ in t/m3 (0-0.5, V1's limits), the feed in m3/h at PFD 735's 990.9 kg/m3, 1000 kg/t; the
design is exact: $0.20685 \times 31.4 \times 1000 = 6495$ kg/h. Nothing integrates, so nothing

station's ratio set point follows the measured ratio, so the return to cascade hands FIC-329401 the
flow it already has. In MAN the operator sets OUTP. `control/ratio.py` `RatioStation`;
`data/unit_328c004.py` `FFIC_329401_FACTOR`.

# Part XLIII — 328D001 and 328E004: the reflux drum, where the desorbers' overhead returns

## XLIII.1 What the unit is

328C002's overhead, 737 — the ammonia, carbon dioxide and water the desorbers and the hydrolyser
strip from the process condensate — is condensed in 328E004, a vertical U-tube exchanger on
cooling water (4357 kW, 212 m2), absorbed into the lean carbamate 718A that 323P008 sends from
323D011 for the purpose, and falls into 328D001, the level tank (1684 mm inside, 1950 mm tangent
to tangent). What does not condense leaves the top as 786 through PV-328202 to 323E011, the LP
flash condenser; the liquid is pumped by 328P002 A/B (774) and split, 775 back to 328C002 as its
reflux on FIC-328404, 776 forward to 323E003, the LP carbamate condenser, on LV-328501.

    737 + 718A = 786 + 775 + 776:    6665 + 3561.5 = 276 + 1675 + 8275.5 kg/h

This is where the desorption train hands its recovered ammonia and carbon dioxide back to the LP
section — as vapour to 323E011, as liquid to 323E003 — and it closes unit 328.

Source: V1 `main.py` step_sim, "Stage 6 : 328D001 Desorber-I reflux drum" (9254-9347), the cp line
(8831), the tear reads (8840-8841) and write (9671), the seeds (6840-6847, 6993-7025, 7066-7081),
the telemetry (10815-10846), the constants (1571-1646, 2065-2068, 5974). Data in
`data/unit_328d001.py`; physics in `units/desorption/reflux_drum.py`.

## XLIII.2 The equations

**The condenser.** 328E004's duty is stroke-proportional on TV-328002 (V1), held above the cooling
water (decision 28, §XLIII.4):

$$
Q = \min\!\left(Q_{des}\,\frac{op}{50},\ \max\!\left(q_{sens} + \frac{\dot m_{737}\lambda_{737}}{3600} + (T - 30)\frac{C}{\Delta t},\ 0\right)\right)
$$

with C the temperature step's capacity below. The less it condenses, the more of 737 reaches the
drum as vapour:

$$
g = \dot m_{786,des}\,\frac{\dot m_{737}}{\dot m_{737,des}} \Big/ \max(Q/Q_{des},\ 0.1)
$$

**The vent.** PIC-328202 reads 328C002's pressure — its transmitter is on the column (Uhde's loop
summary, P 328202, line 100-AW4-328066; V1 AUDIT B5) — and strokes PV-328202, IEC 60534
compressible, from the live drum to 323E011's live pressure of the tick before (decision 29),
anchored on 2.6 -> 1.13 bar a at 61 C, on 786's molar mass, 17.154 kg/kmol (V1 report D-2).

**The pressure** integrates the uncondensed vapour against the vent on the free volume, on the old
holdup and the tick before's temperature change (V1 report A-6):

$$
\frac{dP}{dt} = \frac{RT}{V_v}\,\frac{g - \dot m_{786}}{M_{786}} + \frac{P}{T}\frac{dT}{dt} - \frac{P}{V_v}\frac{dV_v}{dt}
$$

**The temperature**, semi-implicit on the inlets' capacity (328E004's duty is a stroke, not a UA,
so it is not in it):

$$
T' = T + \frac{\Delta t\,\big[q_{sens} + \dot m_{737}\lambda_{737}/3600 - Q\big]}{M c_p + \Delta t\,c_p\,(\dot m_{737} + \dot m_{718A} + \dot m_{793} + \dot m_{over})/3600}
$$

$$
q_{sens} = \frac{c_p}{3600}\big[\dot m_{737}(T_{737} - T) + \dot m_{718A}(45 - T) + \dot m_{793}(T_{793} - T) + \dot m_{over}(T_{C002} - T)\big]
$$

$\lambda_{737}$ = 2163.57 kJ/kg, back-solved so the design duty closes the drum at 61 C; 328C002 boils
737 at an implied 1879. V1's AUDIT C4 ascribes the 526 kW between them to carbamate forming in the
drum — condensation plus formation, rightly larger than a boil-up latent — and it is ported as V1
anchors it (the "737 latent gap" the earlier sessions carried).

**The reflux.** TIC-328008 controls an inferential of 737's water content,
$100\,\varphi\,p_{sat,w}(T_{737})/P_{C002}$ with $\varphi$ = 0.8960 back-solved to the PFD's 46.21 mol%
on IAPWS-IF97 (V1's comment gives 0.898328, its retired Antoine curve's), on FIC-328404's set point
in kg/h. $T_{737}$ is 328C002's bottoms less a top offset that runs from 10 K without reflux to the
design 22 K with it, on the reflux lagged over 328C002's residence $M_{C002}/\dot m_{in,C002}$.

**The draw.** LIC-328501 strokes LV-328501, a pure gain on its linear trim:
$\dot m_{776} = \dot m_{776,des}\cdot op/op_{des}$.

**The holdup:** $dM/dt = \dot m_{737} + \dot m_{718A} + \dot m_{793} + \dot m_{over} - g - \dot m_{775} - \dot m_{776}$
(decision 24); level $M/M_{des}\times 50.5$ %, $M_{des}$ = 2401.7 kg, half the 4755.8 kg cylinder.

# Part XLIV — Phase 4 closed: the letdowns flash, the nodes relieve, 328D001 has heads

Three handoff items decided by the process engineer and built in session 29, each a decided
divergence asserted from both sides: B-53 (328D001's vessel and LT-328501's taps), B-46 (the
letdowns sized flashing) and B-47 (relief). The decisions are recorded as `project.md` decisions
31-33 and are now classes under §5 rule 7. The handoff items are deleted.

## XLIV.1 328D001's vessel and LT-328501's taps — decided 2026-09-30 (handoff B-53)

**Decision.** "A tank volume that ignores the heads is mathematically incorrect": the drum is the
vendor's 5500 l, heads included, and LI-328501 reads across LT-328501's 1510 mm tap span.

**Source.** Reuther's as-built assembly UD-AU-328-DZ-0006-003 rev 02 (the vendor archive, scanned,
read from the page image): nominal volume 5500 l with the heads; LT-328501 on N6A / N6B, 220 mm
inside each tangent line, 1510 mm apart (and Uhde's loop summary UD-MR-328-EC-0001, loop
L 328501).

**Equations** (`data/unit_328d001.py`, `units/desorption/reflux_drum.py` `lt_328501_pct`):

$$ V_{head} = \tfrac12\,(V_{vessel} - V_{cyl}) = \tfrac12\,(5.5 - 4.3432) = 0.5784\ \mathrm{m^3} $$

$$ h = \frac{\max(M/\rho - V_{head},\,0)}{A},\qquad
   LI_{328501} = 100\cdot\mathrm{clamp}\!\left(\frac{h - 0.220}{1.510},\,0,\,1\right) $$

with A = 2.2273 m2 and rho 1095 kg/m3. The full drum holds 5.5 x 1095 = 6022.5 kg, where V1's
cylinder held 4756 kg. The design holdup is the one at which the taps read V1's 50.5 %:
h = 0.98255 m, M = 3029.66 kg — `_design_holdup_kg` steps the seed by ulps until
`lt_328501_pct` returns exactly 50.5, so the design tick stays bit-exact.

**Both sides** (`test_reflux_drum_equivalence.py`, switch "B-53";
`test_reflux_drum_decided_equivalence.py`): V1's transcription on its cylinder reads M / M_des x
50.5; the port's on the taps. Re-pinned on the vessel: the 737 cut settles at 59.050 C,
2.6277 bar a, LI 48.316 %; the heel is reached at 548 s, the pinch at 84.0 s, the drum full at
1301.5 s (100 % on the taps from 793 s), 6022.5 kg.

## XLIV.2 The letdowns flash — decided 2026-09-30 (handoff B-46)

**Decision.** "All letdowns must use two-phase/flashing sizing (IEC 60534-2-1, choked flow /
flashing) if their downstream condition warrants it." V1 passes no vapour pressure to its
anchored liquid law, so no letdown can choke.

**The law** is V1's own `valve_liquid_anchored` (§XV.2), handed the liquor's live vapour pressure
and its design value:

$$ \Delta P_{eff} = \min\!\big(P_1 - P_2,\; F_L^2\,(P_1 - F_F P_v)\big),\qquad
   F_F = 0.96 - 0.28\sqrt{P_v/P_c} $$

$$ \dot m = \dot m_{des}\,\frac{f(h)}{f(h_{des})}\sqrt{\frac{\Delta P_{eff}\,\rho}
   {\Delta P_{eff,des}\,\rho_{des}}} $$

so it chokes exactly where its downstream condition warrants it, and where it does not — a
subcooled liquor, or a downstream pressure above the choke point — nothing changes.

**The liquid at the valve is at most saturated at the valve's inlet**:

$$ P_v = \min\!\big(P_{bub}(w, T),\; P_1\big) $$

A liquor whose bubble pressure exceeds the vessel's has boiled down to it in the vessel. The cap
is also the domain of the IEC liquid law: past P1 = FF . Pv its choked differential turns negative
and `_phi_liquid` falls back to the full differential (V1's behaviour, kept in the shared law). It
was found on the coupled liquor train: a stripper feed cut lets 323C003's temperature climb while
its pressure falls — the two relax on separate balances — carrying the liquor's bubble pressure 9 %
over the column's, and the uncapped law drained 307 626 kg/h, three times PFD 314. Capped, the
drain eases to 93 334 kg/h with the feed.

| valve | the liquor's Pv | design: choked / across | where it binds |
|---|---|---|---|
| LV-322501 | 1.0940 x the rigorous bubble pressure of the stripper's bottoms (`stripper_sump.bottoms_pv_bara`), 101.43 bar a at design | 52.88 / 136.7 bar | always at design |
| LV-323501 | 323C003's stage bubble pressure (`urea_liquor.stage_bubble_p`), 4.1 bar a | 0.278 / 2.97 bar | always at design |
| LV-323505 | 323F004's stage bubble pressure, 1.13 bar a | 0.054 / 0.67 bar | while 323F010 is below 1.076 bar a |
| LV-328505 | 740's, at 328E007's hot outlet (`liquor_pv_bara`), 0.68 bar a at 89 C | 2.85 / 2.81 bar | not at design; on a hot 740 |

* **LV-322501** (`units/synthesis/stripper_sump.py`). Uhde's CONVAL sizing, UD-MR-G00-DZ-0042-032
  (the vendor archive, scanned): urea solution at 173 C let down from 143.7 to 4.2 bar a,
  "Flashing!" on every operating point, pv1 99.0 bar a, FL^2 0.845 at the mean flow. The scale
  1.0940 is the vendor's 99.0 over the rigorous surface's 90.49 bar a for PFD 208 at 173 C: the
  level is the vendor's, the slope in temperature and composition the model's. The stripper's
  published bottoms (`bot_mass_pct`) are a new argument of `StripperSump.step`. Off the fitted
  domain (80.05-209.95 C) the bubble pressure rides water's saturation curve. Measured: 10 % more
  Pv, 5.6 % less drain; a loop 3 bar low, 2.4 % less (V1: 1.1 %); bottoms 8 C hotter, 7.5 % less;
  bottoms in the mushy band (134.7 C, Pv 40.2 bar a) relax the choke 1.31 times, so LIC-322501
  settles at 53.8 % at 136 C, not V1's 70 %, and wide open at 134 C passes 74 % of the bottoms
  (the sump still floods).
* **LV-323501** (`rectifying_column.py`): the drain answers the column's pressure and
  temperature, not 323F004's — the drum at 2.0 bar a moves nothing, where V1 loses 16 %.
* **LV-323505** (`flash_tank.py`): the vacuum reaches the drum only past the choke point,
  1.076 bar a. HIC-323605 pinched to 20 % lifts 323F010 to 0.94 bar a, and LIC-323505 holds its
  stroke (V1: answers); 323F010 at 1.10 bar a cuts the drain to 74.5 % and LIC-323505 wins it back
  at 77.56 % (V1, unchoked, at 0.90 bar a: 59 465 kg/h and 85.58 %).
* **LV-328505** (`second_desorber.py`): the valve stands on 740, after 328E007's hot side (P&ID
  sheet 104). `SecondDesorber.step` takes 328E007's hot outlet, `t_740_c`, as an argument.
  Flowserve lets 740 down from 3.54 to 3.0 bar a, far above its 0.68 bar a: on the vendor's
  conditions it never chokes. On the model's datum — the whole drop to 1.0 bar a lumped on the
  valve (V1) — it stands 0.031 bar short of its choke at design; it binds when 328E007 loses its
  cold side and 740 arrives at the column's 143 C, saturated: the drain falls to 30.6 % at once,
  LIC-328505 strokes fully open within a minute and the column fills, 107 % five minutes on. At
  120 C the choke costs 22 % and LIC-328505 wins it back at 98 % open. Unstripped bottoms (the LP
  steam lost) carry 0.9 % ammonia to the valve and flash there too.

LV-328503 and LV-328504 already carried their liquor's vapour pressure (B-43, §XLI).

**Both sides.** Each harness carries the switch — `flash_decided` on the recirc states, `flash` in
`v1_sump_step` and in 328C004's `decided` — that hands V1's own law the port's Pv:
`test_the_flashing_letdown_decided_divergence` (323C003, 322E001's sump),
`test_a_pinched_hic_323605_reaches_the_drum_only_unchoked` (323F004),
`test_a_hot_740_flashes_lv_328505_decided_divergence` (328C004). Every tick-by-tick scenario,
alone and coupled, runs the port against the switched transcription with `==`. The mass a letdown
passes is one number, taken from the upstream holdup and given to the downstream inflow; the
328C004 books close on both sides (`made` below 1e-6 kg).

## XLIV.3 Relief — decided 2026-09-30 (handoff B-47)

**Decision.** "When a node exceeds its set point, model the mass venting out of the system at the
relief capacity." V1 ports the API 520 capacity law (`hydraulics.py`, D-9) and connects it to no
node.

**The law** (`ureasim/core/relief.py`; the V1 capacity law moved there from `control/relief.py`,
verbatim, still proved `==` in `test_valve_equivalence.py`):

* **capacity** — API 520 Part I critical vapour flow, on an orifice back-solved from the vendor's
  certified capacity at its relieving pressure (set + 10 %) on its sizing fluid
  (`psv_area_from_rated_m2`), so Kd, Kb, Kc, k and the constant cancel and only P1, M, T and Z
  move:

$$ W = n\,K_d\,A\,P_1\sqrt{\frac{kM}{ZRT}\left(\frac{2}{k+1}\right)^{\frac{k+1}{k-1}}} $$

  with the node's head-space vapour as the ideal gas its pressure integral carries (Z = 1, its
  live molar mass and temperature). Every valve carried discharges to atmosphere or a low back
  pressure, below 0.4 of its inlet over its open band: critical throughout.
* **lift** — pop action: shut below the set pressure, fully lifted at it, reseating at
  P_set - blowdown . set (gauge): 10 % of the set pressure on every gas and steam valve, 20 % on
  every liquid one (Sempell's sheets; Series S manual UD-RL-G00-DZ-0001-003 §3.9). Sempell's gas
  valves reach full lift within 5 % above set; the lift is taken full at set.
* **the tick** — the valve reads the pressure at the top of the tick and vents at most the moles
  above its reseat pressure in the tick (`reseat_vent_kgh`, the inverse of `vessel_dpdt`'s molar
  term), so it reseats inside the tick where the pressure gets there, and never carries the node
  below. A liquid law, anchored likewise on the certified capacity, is in the module for the
  liquid-rated valves.

**The data** (`data/relief_devices.py` `RELIEF_SIZING`): Sempell's orifice selections for ten
valves — orifice, area, certified alpha_w, actual capacity, sizing fluid (molar mass, exponent,
compressibility, temperature, density), overpressure and blowdown — from UD-RL-G00-DZ-0001-001
(pages 89-92) and UD-RL-G00-DZ-0002-001 (pages 1-5).

**Applied** where a mass-balance node can reach the set pressure:

* **328C003, SV32852** (`hydrolyser.py`): set 23.0 bar g, 24.01 bar a, reseating at 21.71;
  orifice L, 24 897 kg/h of superheated steam at 330 C and 26.31 bar a, Z 0.9448 (IAPWS-IF97
  region 2); the sheet prints no exponent for steam, and the law's 1.30 is taken on both sides of
  the back-solve. PV-328203 shut: the column reaches 24.01 bar a at 459 s, the valve vents the
  head space at 27.1 t/h for 5 s down to 21.71 and reseats, and the cycle repeats every 165.5 s —
  19 lifts in the hour, 670 kg vented, what the column made and could not pass. V1, relieving
  nothing, stands at 53.07 bar a on the liquid's decided books (42.32 on its own). PV-328203 at
  20 %: first lift at 619.5 s, every 226 s, 454 kg in the hour.
* **328C002, SV32850 and SV32851** (`first_desorber.py`): set 5.0 bar g, 6.01 bar a, reseating at
  5.51; two alike, each orifice T lift-limited to 16.23 mm, 25 000 kg/h of M 18.0, k 1.310, Z 0.99
  gas at 159 C and 6.51 bar a. 328D001 at 7.0 bar a stops 737: the column reaches 6.01 bar a
  10.9 s later, both valves vent 52 t/h for three ticks and reseat, every 2.7 s — 218 lifts in ten
  minutes, 817 kg, the 4.96 t/h the column boils at 158.4 C. V1 stands at 7.14 bar a.

Each unit publishes `m_relief_kgh` (the vent, at the head space's vapour composition, to
atmosphere) and `relief_lifted`. The decision-24 books count the vent among what crosses the
boundary and close within 50 g over an hour of cycling.

**Not applied, and why** (handoff A-16):

* **323C003, SV32351/52** — its pressure is the two-source target law (§XXVIII), not a node with
  an inventory, and reaches 6.01 bar a only at 2.54 times the design flash gas; LV-322501 wide
  open on the bottoms gives 5.50 bar a. The valves' sizing case, HP gas blowing through a failed
  LV-322501, reaches the column when the flowsheet routes the sump's blow-through (Phase 5).
* **322R001, SV32251/52** — the synthesis loop's pressure is a flowsheet node (Phase 5); its data
  are in `RELIEF_SIZING`.
* **323D011, SV32357 and 328D001, SV32353** — liquid-rated valves ("not for flashing liquids")
  on vapour nodes, whose gas discharge coefficients are not on Sempell's sheets or in its Series S
  manual. **Applied 2026-10-01** on an assumed coefficient (§XLVI.1).

**Both sides.** `decided_relief.py` transcribes the lift, the blowdown and the tick on V1's own
`psv_area_from_rated_m2` and `psv_api520_choked_kgh`; the hydrolyser's and 328C002's harnesses
carry the switch "relief": `test_sv32852_relieves_the_shut_overhead_decided_divergence`,
`test_sv32850_relieves_a_blocked_overhead_decided_divergence` — parted on the tick the valve lifts,
bit-exact before it. 8 tests in `tests/core/test_relief.py`.

# Part XLV — The engine: the plant state's tears and the fixed-step simulator

Phase 5's first two modules (session 29), on the architecture of `project.md` §3.6.

## XLV.1 The recycle tears (`engine/state.py`, handoff A-10)

V1 reads its inter-section recycles as `s.tlag.get(key, design_default)` (`main.py` 8835-8845)
and writes them at the end of the tick (9666-9676). The port declares each:

$$ \text{tear}(k) = \text{producer}(k-1), \qquad \text{tear}(0) = \dot m_{des} $$

`TearState` is a frozen dataclass of the eight that cross units — 702, 756 and 708 into 323C005,
748 and 750 into 328C002, 718A into 328D001, 718B into 323E003, 739 into 328E007 — each seeded
with its producer's design flow. A consumer reads it during the tick; `PlantState.end_tick`
replaces it with the producers' writes when the tick is committed, so the one-tick delay is
structural and no write can reach a reader early; a write to a name that is not a tear is
refused. Of V1's eleven, 775 and 931 are read by their producers too (328D001's top lag,
FFIC-329401's PV) and are the producers' state, `RefluxDrum.m_775_prev_kgh` and
`SecondDesorber.m_931_prev_kgh`; 744 is retired by decision 25. 756 and 708 hold their seeds
until the schedule wires 322C001 (ported in session 30, Part XLVI) and unit 324. No tear is
iterated (decision 8).

`PlantClock` counts steps; plant time is the count times the step, exact — tick 36 000 is
3600.0 s to the bit, where a running sum of 0.1 is not.

**Equivalence** (`tests/equivalence/test_state_equivalence.py`): the ten seeds `==` V1's boot
defaults; and 328C002, 328C003 and 328C004 coupled in V1's order with 748 and 750 carried by
`PlantState.tears`, against V1's three stages coupled through `s.tlag` — every published field,
state and controller `==` for 3000 ticks through a feed cut and an MP steam step. 6 behaviour tests
in `tests/engine/test_state.py`.

## XLV.2 The fixed step (`engine/simulator.py`, handoff A-14)

$$ \text{owed} \mathrel{+}= \min(\Delta t_{wall},\,0.5\ \mathrm{s})\cdot \text{pacing}, \qquad
   n = \lfloor \text{owed}/0.1\ \mathrm{s}\rfloor, \qquad \text{owed} \mathrel{-}= n \cdot 0.1\ \mathrm{s} $$

in integer nanoseconds, so no step is lost or made by rounding; pacing 1 (SLOW) or 60 (FAST),
V1's `SIM_SPEED`; the per-pass cap V1's `min(now - last_t, 0.5)` (`data/engine.py`). Every step
is exactly 0.1 s: a late pass runs more steps, never a larger one. A step that raises freezes the
pass and drops what it owed, as V1 does, and the fault is held for the server. **The replay**:
328C003 with its overhead shut, SV32852 cycling, run SLOW on irregular passes and FAST on others —
the same 12 000 plant states to the bit. 7 tests in `tests/engine/test_simulator.py`. V1's
variable step (`sim_task`, sub-steps up to 0.25 s) is not reproduced: the Phase 7 driver runs V1
at the same fixed step (A-14).

# Part XLVI — Phase 4 re-opened: the liquid-rated valves relieve gas; 322C001, the LP absorber

Session 30. The process engineer (2026-10-01) chose A-16's option (b) for the two liquid-rated
valves, and re-opened Phase 4: 322C001, unit 324 and the steam system are ported before the
scheduler, because the schedule is built on the completed plant's data flow (project.md decisions
34, 35). 322C001 is ported here; it is the first unit of `units/absorption/`.

## XLVI.1 A liquid-rated valve relieving gas — decided 2026-10-01 (handoff A-16, option b)

A valve Sempell rated on liquid alone has no certified gas capacity to back-solve its orifice
from (§XLIV.3). Where one sits on a vapour node, the API 520 law runs on its orifice's own flow
area and on the series' full-lift gas coefficient:

$$ W = K_d\,A\,P_1\sqrt{\frac{kM}{RT}\left(\frac{2}{k+1}\right)^{\frac{k+1}{k-1}}}, \qquad
   K_d = 0.917,\ k = 1.30,\ Z = 1 $$

0.917 is alpha_w as certified on SV32351/52's orifice T (UD-RL-G00-DZ-0002-001 page 3), taken
for orifices F, K and M — an assumption, logged in handoff Open data gaps for Phase 7; k is the
law's default (no sheet prints one for these vapours). The valve relieves gas, so it reseats on
the gas blowdown, 10 % of set below (Series S manual §3.9), not its liquid sizing's 20 %.
`GasReliefValve` gained ``kd`` (0.975 for a back-solved orifice, where it cancels);
`data/relief_devices.py` `GAS_KD_ASSUMED`, `GAS_BLOWDOWN`, `gas_reseat_bara`.

* **323D011, SV32357** (`flash_condenser.py`): orifice F, 240.53 mm2; set 5.0 bar g on 1.010,
  6.01 bar a, reseating at 5.51. It passes 881.6 kg/h of the node's M 17.4 vapour at 57 C and
  6.61 bar a — twice the 440 kg/h the condenser cannot take. The relief, like the vent, is gas
  that does not land in the tank: booked against the tank, not condensed in the energy balance;
  its share of the tank's swell is left out of the pressure step so the reseat cap holds exactly
  (a thousandth of the molar term). PV-323203 shut: the first lift at 82.1 s, then every 19.1 s,
  17 lifts in 400 s, 39.8 kg vented, between 5.51 and 6.013 bar a (6.016 on the first approach);
  V1 has no ceiling (B-30): 24.912 bar a at 400 s. The tank's books close to 2e-13 kg.
* **328D001, SV32353** (`reflux_drum.py`): orifice K, 1462.20 mm2; 6.01 / 5.51 bar a; the head
  space alone (the liquid already paid for the vapour, decision 24). PV-328202 shut: the drum
  lifts at 75.5 s, every 12.5 s, 186 lifts in forty minutes, 178.2 kg vented, peaking at
  6.032 bar a on the half-second tick; V1 stands at 111.6 bar a.
* **322C001, SV32253** — the same class, on the unit ported below (§XLVI.4).

Both sides: the 323E011 and 328D001 harnesses carry the switch "relief"/``relief_decided``;
`decided_relief.Valve.orifice` writes a liquid-rated valve out on V1's own capacity law.

## XLVI.2 The back-pressure over ammonia water (`thermo/ammonia_backpressure.py`)

V1's `packed_absorber` back-pressure block, ported verbatim on the ported speciation, activity
model and Henry constants: only the free molecules exert a pressure,

$$ p_{NH_3} = H_{NH_3}(T)\,x_{NH_3(aq)}\,\gamma_{NH_3(aq)}, \qquad
   p_{CO_2} = H_{CO_2}(T)\,x_{CO_2(aq)}\,\gamma_{CO_2(aq)} $$

tabulated lazily on a grid geometric in both molalities (ratio 1.2, floors 0.01 and 0.001 mol/kg)
and 1 K in temperature, interpolated trilinearly on the logarithms; beyond the speciation's
10-100 C each pressure follows van 't Hoff at the edge's heat of absorption,
$\ln p = \ln p_e - (\Delta H/R)(1/T - 1/T_e)$; the slopes dp/dx by a 2 % difference; the heats
$\Delta H_i = -R\,d\ln p_i/d(1/T)$ at fixed composition, so CO2 carries its carbamate heat. Over
the design sump at 43 C: NH3 4815 Pa and CO2 829 Pa, 36.1 and 79.8 kJ/mol; continuous at 100 C to
2e-6. The water and nitrogen transport properties (`thermo/transport_properties.py`): Vogel,
IAPWS R1-76, Sutherland and Fuller-Schettler-Giddings, verbatim.

## XLVI.3 The packed beds (`units/absorption/packed_beds.py`)

Two beds counter-current to their washes (lower 1500 mm in the 922 mm part on 755 and the upper
bed's effluent; upper 1000 mm in the 576 mm part on clean 954; 25 mm Pall rings, a = 250 m2/m3):

$$ \frac{y_{out} - y^*_{in}}{y_{in} - y^*_{in}} = \frac{1-\lambda}{e^{NTU(1-\lambda)} - \lambda},
   \qquad \lambda = \frac{mG}{L}, \qquad NTU = c_i\,\frac{k_G a_w P Z}{G_m} $$

with Onda's wetted fraction and gas-film coefficient; y*_in over the wash, the slope m over the
live sump liquor; a liquid desorbs no more than it brings; the upper bed warms by its own heat of
absorption (iterated, 8 passes, 1e-6 K); the vent leaves the 954 saturated with water,
y_w = a_w psat(T_954)/P. The beds couple through the liquid: the unit passes once a tick and lags
the upper bed's uptake over its liquid residence (Billet-Schultes film holdup), 23.4 s at the
design 954. **Calibration**: c_NH3 0.8004 and c_CO2 0.8379 on Onda's k_G and a_w 0.8808, solved
on PFD 204 -> 797 (NH3 89.33, CO2 62.00 taken up, water 21.34 given). At design: transfer units
7.93 / 6.66 (lower NH3 / CO2), 2.54 / 2.13 (upper); the upper bed rises 3.50 K; 1.79 kg/h of NH3
slips. Twice the gas slips 7.39 kg/h; a 70 C sump 5.73; without 954, 13.28.

## XLVI.4 322C001 (`units/absorption/lp_absorber.py`, `data/unit_322c001.py`)

$$ \frac{dP}{dt} = \frac{RT}{V_v}\,\frac{\dot m_{gas} - \dot m_{abs} - \dot m_{797}}{M_{vent}}
   + \frac{P}{T}\frac{dT}{dt} - \frac{P}{V_v}\frac{dV_v}{dt}, \qquad
   \dot m_{797} = \dot m_{797,des}\,\frac{\phi(h)}{\phi(h_{des})} $$

$$ Mc_p\frac{dT}{dt} = \frac{c_p[\dot m_{755}(40 - T) + \dot m_{954}(46 - T)]}{3600}
   + Q_{gas} + Q_{res} + Q_{flood} $$

$$ Q_{gas} = \sum_i n_i\,[h_i(T_{gas}) - h_i(T)] + n_{NH_3}\Delta H_{NH_3} + n_{CO_2}\Delta H_{CO_2}
   + n_{H_2O}\,[h_v - h_l](T) $$

semi-implicit in the washes and the gas (1.05 kJ/kg K); M_vent the live vent's; the sump
dM/dt = m_755 + m_954 + m_abs - m_756, its species a plain multi-feed mix. **The design pin**
(`design_pin`, V1's boot pin, about 4 s once): 322E003's design vent through HV-322604 at its
design opening, PFD 204, 1708.3 kg/h let down to 94.8 C; the beds calibrated on it; the design
vent 1578.3 kg/h; the heat residual Q_res 1.330 kW (the PFD's rounded 40 / 43 / 46 C).

**The column's cooling — the process engineer's question (2026-10-01).** 322C001 has no cooling
water and no heat-transfer coefficient. The heat of absorption leaves in the liquor as the washes'
sensible heat, against 755 arriving at 322E006's 40 C outlet — a temperature V1 FIXES (an
infinite-capacity cooler, a fixed approach), whatever 322E006's load or cooling water. 322E006 is
not modelled; its datasheet gives a plate exchanger, 6.44 m2, 222 kW on 38.2 t/h from 45 to 40 C
against cooling water 30 to 40 C, U = 4781 W/m2 K on its LMTD. Measured: 755 lost, the liquor
runs to 68.9 C; an ammonia-rich purge (1.2 times, NH3 six times) to 52.1 C with 844 kg/h taken
up. Handoff B-54.

**Findings, ported as V1 and logged** — all three decided by the process engineer on 2026-10-01
and built in session 31 (Part XLVII): 322E006 ported (B-54), the flood in the vent line (B-55),
the letdown flashed onto the liquor it condenses (B-19).

* **XV-322915's flood** (B-55): trip 22.1 adds 500 kW to the liquor with no steam mass. The
  reference describes the steam flooding the gas discharge line, on TI-322015 at that line,
  where V1 trips on the liquor's temperature. Flooded, the liquor settles at 56.24 C — above
  the 55 C reset, so a latched trip holds itself in.
* **B-19 on the absorber**: a rich purge charged at the let-down solver's -36 C floor brings
  75.6 kW less than at 26 C; the liquor settles at 55.6 C against 57.6 — either side of trip
  22.1's 57 C.
* HV-322604 discharges to a fixed 4.0 bar a (decision 29's class): wired to 322C001's live
  pressure with the schedule (handoff A-17).
* V1's pre-pin branch runs only through its boot settles and is not reachable: not ported.

# Part XLVII — The absorber's three decisions: 322E006, the flood in the vent line, the letdown that condenses; unit 324 surveyed, its vacuum condensers ported

Session 31. The process engineer decided the three findings raised on 322C001 on 2026-10-01
(project.md decisions 36-38): B-54, port 322E006 on its datasheet UA and the 30 C cooling-water
supply; B-55, put XV-322915's 500 kW and the steam that carries it into the vent gas and trip on
the vent's temperature; B-19, replace the letdown solver's floor with the true isenthalpic flash
down to the actual downstream pressure. Each is a decided divergence, asserted from both sides.

## XLVII.1 322E006, the LP absorber feed cooler (`units/absorption/feed_cooler.py`, `data/unit_322e006.py`)

The datasheet, read from the scan (Uhde UD-AU-322-EC-0012 rev 00, page 2, operating case 1): a
bolted plate exchanger, 6.44 m2, 16 plates, 222 kW; ammonia water 38 200 kg/h from 45.00 to 40.00 C,
cp 1.003 kcal/(kg K); "cooling water return" 19 150 kg/h from 30.00 to 40.00 C, cp 0.998 / 0.996;
20 % excess area on each side; the heat-transfer coefficient line blank. Counter-current:

$$ \Delta T_{lm} = \frac{10 - 5}{\ln 2} = 7.2135\ \mathrm{K}, \qquad UA = \frac{222}{7.2135} = 30.776\ \mathrm{kW/K}
   \quad (U = 4779\ \mathrm{W/m^2K}) $$

$$ \varepsilon = \frac{1 - e^{-NTU(1-C_r)}}{1 - C_r e^{-NTU(1-C_r)}}, \quad NTU = \frac{UA}{C_{min}}, \quad
   Q = \varepsilon\,C_{min}\,(T_{744} - T_{cw}), \quad T_{755} = T_{744} - \frac{Q}{C_h} $$

($\varepsilon = NTU/(1+NTU)$ at $C_r = 1$; no flow on either side, no duty). On it the rating case
comes back at 40.015 C and 222.12 kW. **The design anchor.** At the PFD's 31 478 kg/h from 44 C,
the datasheet's 19 150 kg/h of water would bring 755 to 38.51 C, not 40. The one quantity no
document fixes at the design point is the water through the plates (no flow element is drawn on
it), so it is back-solved — bisected, then stepped one float at a time until 755 reads exactly
40.0: `E006_M_CW_DES_KGH` = 10 374.435 kg/h, 146.87 kW, returning at 42.21 C (Open data gaps,
Phase 7). The plates hold about 20 kg (590 kg filled, 570 dry), under 3 s of 744: steady each tick.

755 against the water: lost 44.0 C (744's own), a quarter 42.85, half 41.73, three quarters
40.76, half again 38.97. Compartment I at 50 C: 44.29; 744 at 60 %: 37.67; water supplied at
35 C: 41.43. `LpAbsorber.step` takes 755's temperature as an argument (the schedule hands it
328D003's `t_i_c` through 322E006, Phase 5).

**Both ways** (`test_755_from_322e006_decided_divergence`): the water lost 5 s on, bit-exact until

## XLVII.2 XV-322915's flood in the vent line (`units/absorption/vent_line.py`)

P&ID UD-VT-322-FB-0003, sheet 102 (`References/Merged_Searchable_PIDs.pdf` page 3, read from the
page image): line 150-GCB6-322254 runs from PV-322201 to atmosphere (VE100, to a safe location);
XV-322915 (fail open, DN100/DN50, FO-322457's DN15 bypass beside it) admits LP steam from
100-STLS4-329722 just downstream of PV-322201; TI-322015 (SAHH, AH) stands on the same line
further down and initiates I 22.1; HS-322915 OVERRIDE CLOSE acts on the valve.

**The gas leaving the beds.** V1 computes no vent temperature; it saturates the vent's water at
954's temperature, and PFD 797 leaves at 46 C, 954's. The upper bed is taken as a perfect
counter-current exchanger between the 954 and the gas from the lower bed (at the liquor's
temperature, where 322C001's balance brings it), the heat of absorption to the wash:

$$ T_{top} = \begin{cases} T_{954} & C_{gas} \le C_{954} \\
   T_{liq} - \dfrac{C_{954}}{C_{gas}}\,(T_{liq} - T_{954}) & C_{gas} > C_{954} \end{cases} $$

with the beds' own capacities (cp 4.18 and 1.05 kJ/kg K) and the gas into the upper bed rebuilt
from `BedsResult`. At design: 46.0 C, PFD 797 without an anchor. The liquor's own balance is V1's
(the vent's sensible heat at 46 against 43 C is inside V1's design residual).

**The flood.** The LP steam whose latent heat at the 5.013 bar a header (151.94 C) is V1's 500 kW:
$\dot m_s = 500/\lambda \cdot 3600 = 854.05$ kg/h. **TI-322015**: the line's adiabatic mix at
1.013 bar a, every species an ideal gas on H0, the steam entering saturated:

$$ \sum_i n_i\,h_i(T) + n_s\,h_w(T) = \sum_i n_i\,h_i(T_{top}) + n_s\,h_w(T_{sat}) $$

below its dew point the water condensing to $p_{w} = p_{sat}(T)$, the rest liquid at its latent
heat. On the design vent: 96.31 C; no vent, the steam's own 151.94; 3 t/h, 80.16; 10 t/h, 59.23;
20 t/h of a 3 % wet gas at 5 C condenses 267.7 kg/h and settles at 43.32. Shut, TI-322015 reads
the vent as it leaves the column. **Trip 22.1** (`trip_22_1`): V1's thresholds, 57 C latch and
55 C release (`TRIP_22_1_HIGH_C`, `TRIP_22_1_CLEAR_C`), on TI-322015.

**Both ways** (`test_the_flood_in_the_vent_line_decided_divergence`): XV-322915 open 5 s on; V1's
liquor settles at 56.244 C, above the reset; the port's stays at 43.0 and TI-322015 reads 96.31.

**What the move changes, measured.** 755 lost: the liquor runs to 68.9 C, but the polish still
holds the gas at 46.0 C, so TI-322015 does not trip (V1 tripped on the liquor). A total cooling
loss in 322E003: the gas outweighs the polish and TI-322015 reads 65.75 C — the trip fires.
**Finding B-56**: with the thermometer downstream of the injection as P&ID 102 draws it, a latched
flood holds TI-322015 at 96.3 C (103.7 with the top at 60), above the 55 C release, so the trip
holds itself in while the steam flows; only the steam shut off clears it — HS-322915's override,
which V1 builds as a one-tick toggle the latch re-opens. Decided 2026-10-01: I 22.1 as the DCS
executes it, HS-322915 a maintained keyswitch (§XLVIII.1).

**Declared.** PV-322201's own Joule-Thomson cooling (about 0.7 K on the nitrogen vent) is left
out; FO-322457, FO-329458 and FO-329459's continuous trace steam has no flow in the archive and is
not modelled; the vent line carries no carbamate chemistry.

## XLVII.3 The letdown that condenses (`thermo/condensing_letdown.py`, `purge_valve.py`)

A letdown is isenthalpic. While the purge stays above its dew point the outlet is V1's single-phase
SRK answer, kept verbatim; below it NH3, CO2 and water condense together as an ammonium-carbamate
liquor whose heat holds the outlet a few kelvin under the dew point. Vapour: SRK enthalpy
(`real_gas.h_molar`) and ideal-gas equilibrium, the beds' own basis; liquor: the Extended UNIQUAC
speciation and the Henry constants the beds stand on:

$$ y_{NH_3}P = p_{NH_3}(m_N, m_C, T), \quad y_{CO_2}P = p_{CO_2}(m_N, m_C, T), \quad
   y_{H_2O}P = a_{H_2O}(m_N, m_C, T)\,p_{sat}(T) $$

$$ n\,h_{SRK}(y, T_{in}, P_{in}) = V\,h_{SRK}(y_v, T, P_{out}) + \sum_i l_i\,h_i^{ig}(T)
   - l_{NH_3}\Delta H_{NH_3} - l_{CO_2}\Delta H_{CO_2} - l_{H_2O}\,\lambda(T) $$

the heats of absorption the back-pressure's van 't Hoff slope over the liquor (the heats 322C001
charges its beds at). **Method**: V1's single-phase answer T1; the dew test walked down from T_in
in 10 K steps (the incipient liquor matching the gas's NH3 and CO2 pressures stands only if it
holds its water back no harder than the gas carries it); dry to T1, T1 stands; otherwise Illinois
regula falsi between the last dry and first wet step, each evaluation an isothermal flash —
Newton on (ln m_N, ln m_C, ln W) from fixed starts and the nearest temperature's answer, solved
per mole of gas, so the outlet is a function of the composition alone.
**`liquid_state`** (`ammonia_backpressure`): a second lazy grid of V1's spacing carrying the two
pressures and the water activity from one speciation per node; it reads `back_pressure`'s
pressures to the bit; PFD 755 holds its water at a_w 0.952, a 150 / 60 molal liquor at 0.215.

| 322E003's cooling | V1's outlet | the port's | liquor condensed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100 % (design) | 94.8 C | 94.8 C, dry, `==` V1 | — |
| 95 % | 53.3 | 66.8 | 24.1 kg/h |
| 90 % | 26.0 | 71.7 | 120.4 |
| 80 % | -11.1 | 75.3 | 375.0 |
| 70 % | -36.0 (floor) | 76.5 | 696.2 |
| 50 % | -36.0 (floor) | 77.4 | 1 529.7 |
| 0 % | -36.0 (floor) | 77.9 | 4 342.3 |

The design purge from a 30 C vent: 34.8 C with 1.66 kmol/h of liquor, where V1 gives -6.4. At 70 %
the liquor is 162 mol NH3 and 66 mol CO2 per kg of water; every pressure balances to 1e-10 and the
enthalpy to 1e-12. **HV-322604** (`PurgeValveResult`): the purge through the seat as before, now
also its gas, its liquor and whether it condenses; L3-7's deposition flag also fires while a liquor
condenses (at 66-78 C the outlet no longer reaches V1's 20 C, and the liquor is the deposit the flag
warns of); the outlet pressure an argument (decision 29's class, handoff A-17): choked, the same
purge, the gas 94.5 C at 2.5 bar a and 95.2 C at 6.013. **322C001** takes the gas to its beds and
the liquor to its sump — its mass, species and sensible heat, semi-implicit with the washes.

**Both ways** (`test_the_purge_condensate_decided_divergence`), V1's dry purge against the port's
two-phase one on the same gas: at 90 % the liquor ends at 68.485 C (V1) against 68.464 — the
purge's enthalpy is the same either way — the slip 18.90 against 17.41 kg/h; at 70 %, where V1's
purge is its solver's floor, not a root of its own balance, 88.274 against 88.981, the slip 454.5
against 392.4. Every field of HV-322604 `==` V1's where the line is dry; where it condenses, V1's
outlet `==` the port's single-phase answer and the port's above it.

**Declared.** Solid ammonium carbamate is not a phase: its dissociation constant is in none of the
archives (Open data gaps). The speciation is regressed on dilute liquors at 10-100 C; the liquor
here is 110-230 mol NH3 per kg of water, extrapolated. The first flash in a new region tabulates
the grid nodes it crosses, a few seconds once; a warm flash costs 5-55 ms, and a repeated call (a
steady purge) is served from a cache.

## XLVII.4 Unit 324 surveyed: the vacuum ejectors (handoff B-57)

V1 does not hardcode the 324 vacuums: 324F001 (0.33 bar a) and 324F003 (0.131) are live states,
each a molar balance on its vapour space between the vacuum condenser's saturated vent and the
ejector's pull, stepped backward in pressure (`_backward_euler_p`) inside a pressure-temperature
fixed point (`main.py` 9759-9830, 9925-9966). But each ejector is a straight line anchored on the
PFD, not a performance curve:

$$ \dot m_{F002} = 72 \cdot \frac{\dot m_{motive}}{390} \cdot \frac{P}{0.33}, \qquad
   \dot m_{F004/F005} = 584 \cdot \frac{HIC_{329606}}{50} \cdot \frac{P}{0.131}\ \ \mathrm{kg/h} $$

— proportional to the motive (or its hand valve) and to the suction pressure, with no break
pressure, no discharge-pressure limit, no motive-pressure or molar-mass dependence and no stall.
323F010's vacuum boils on its design 0.46 bar a (B-22). V1 carries a 1-D compressible ejector
model (Huang 1999, `ejector_huang.py`) and a first-principles envelope (`gap_g9a_ejector_envelope.py`)
that it never wires. The archive: Körting's operating data for 324F002 (UD-AU-324-DZ-0007-006 p20:
motive 650 kg/h at 4.1 bar a, 144.5 C; suction 94 kg/h of 24.1 kg/kmol gas at 0.2 bar a, 45 C;
discharge 1.0 bar a — one point, the instructions' "characteristic curve" being this sheet); for
the 324F004/F005 unit (UD-AU-324-DZ-0009-005 p7: suction 27.4 air, 366 water, 155.3 NH3, 212.3 CO2
kg/h at 40 C and 122 mbar; intermediate 350 mbar, final 1050 mbar; diffuser throats 106.5 and
30.8 mm, motive nozzle orifices 24.7 and 14.5 mm; motive 3.1 bar g, 146 C) and Uhde's vacuum-unit
stream table (p20: 927 1061 kg/h and 929 366, against the PFD's 1220 and 180); Körting's generic
correction for the suction gas's molar mass and temperature (p42).
