## XLVII.6 The vacuum condensers — the first unit of `evaporation/` (`units/evaporation/vacuum_condenser.py`, `data/unit_324.py`)

324E002, 324E005, 324E006 and 324E007, V1's `vacuum_condenser.py` ported verbatim (its
saturated-gas branch already ported as `thermo/saturated_vent.py` for 323C005). **The vent** leaves
the cold end saturated: water on its own line, NH3 and CO2 on their back-pressure over the
condensate the exchanger is making (the condensate taken at the inlet's condensable composition),
each as a departure from design,

$$ p_w = Y_{des}s_wP_{des}\frac{p_{sat}(T_v)}{p_{sat}(T_{v,des})}, \quad
   p_k = Y_{des}s_kP_{des}\frac{p^*_k(w,T_v)}{p^*_k(w_{des},T_{v,des})}, \quad
   n_{vent,c} = n_{inert}\frac{y_c}{1-y_c} $$

with $y_c = \sum p/P$, held below 1 and no condensable vented past what arrives. **The cold end**
is the root of $Q_{bal}(T_v) - UA\cdot LMTD(T_{in}, T_v; T_{cw,in}, T_{cw,in} + Q/\dot m_{cw}c_p)$ by
Illinois regula falsi between the water and vapour inlets, $Q_{bal}$ the H0 enthalpy the vapour gives
up (each species' enthalpy off a lazily filled 0.05 K grid), the back-pressure read off one
log-linear bracket re-centred at most four times. **UA** is back-solved on the PFD rows at design
(324E002: 18 019 kW against the 18 460 its cooling water carries — the H0 tier's missing mixing and
carbamate heat — 478.4 kW/K), and the published vent is the PFD's times the model's against the
model's at design, so 72, 584, 41 and 31 kg/h hold to the bit. The four condensers' rows, ratings
and geometry: `data/unit_324.py` (`CondenserRating`, `VACUUM_CONDENSERS`, `PFD_324_MOL_PCT`,
`CONDENSER_ROWS`), built into specs once by `design_specs()`.

Measured on 324E002: the water halved, the cold end 48.35 C and the vent 87.0 kg/h; supplied at
35 C, 51.22 C and 111.6; lost, nothing condenses; the shell 20 % below its vacuum, 92.5 kg/h, 25 %
above, 61.9. **Equivalence**: `test_vacuum_condenser_equivalence.py` (394) executes V1's module
and lifts V1's ``VACUUM_CONDENSER_SPECS``: the ratings, rows and constants; every field of the four
design specs; `solve` and the anchored vents over 96 cases each (three shell pressures, four
water flows, loads and an ammonia-rich inlet, a re-centred bracket), warmer water and a fouled
surface; the bracket — all ``==``. Behaviour: 7 in `tests/units/evaporation/`. Not yet ported, with
the stages: V1's node wrapper (`vacuum_condenser_node`, which charges every inlet at its design
temperature — B-31's class), the train (`vacuum_train_324`) and the inlets
(`vacuum_inlet_kmolh`). The node and the inlets were ported in session 32 (§XLVIII.4).

# Part XLVIII — I 22.1 on the DCS's logic; unit 324: the ejector data exhausted, the melt's equilibrium checked and ported, the condenser nodes

Session 32. The process engineer decided B-56 and B-57 on 2026-10-01 and asked for the evaporation
stages' water boil-off and the melt's boiling-point elevation to be checked against the physical
properties of the concentrated melt. B-56 is built (project.md decision 39). B-57 could not be
built as decided: the vendor archive holds no performance curve (§XLVIII.2). The melt check found
the model's slopes too steep (B-58).

## XLVIII.1 I 22.1 as the DCS executes it (`units/absorption/vent_line.py`)

**The logic.** Uhde's application software for the urea plant's controller AC4,
UD-MR-G00-FF-0004 (scanned; PC22.5.1, PDF page 43, read from the page image at 300 dpi):

    OR(.1):  in 1 = AI1.29:29/TT-322015:VALUE>H2   (inverted input)
             in 2 = DI5.5/HS-322915
             out  -> DIC661:19/TRIP_22_1_FLAG1:CALC_VAL  and  DO1.4/XVY-322915

$$ XVY_{322915} = \lnot\,(TT_{322015} > H2)\ \lor\ HS_{322915}, \qquad
   XV_{322915}\ \mathrm{open} = \lnot\,XVY_{322915} $$

the valve fail open (loop summary X 322915, UD-MR-322-EC-0001: power failure position FO; its
solenoid XVY-322915 a 24 V binary output, its limit switch XVSH-322915). HS-322915 is a
control-room keyswitch (loop summary H 322915: "Keyswitch (controlroom)", binary input) — a
maintained switch. There is no latch, no reset and no operator open: the valve follows
TT-322015's high-high limit, and the keyswitch holds it shut whatever the limit says. The limit is
the analogue input's own H2 flag, with the input's limit hysteresis; neither its value nor its
hysteresis is in the archive (loop summary T 322015: range 0-200 C, AH, SAHH, normal 46 C), so the
thresholds stay V1's 57 / 55 C (Open data gaps).

**Built** (`xv_322915_open(h2_limit, hs_322915)`; `trip_22_1` the limit, a `HystereticInterlock`,
self-clearing, no operator reset). Measured on the design vent, each tick TI-322015 on the valve
the tick before left:

| tick | beds' top | HS-322915 | TI-322015 | H2 limit | XV-322915 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 60 C | off | 60.00 | set | opens |
| 2 | 60 C | off | 103.66 | set | open |
| 3 | 46 C | off | 96.31 | set | open — the flood holds itself in |
| 4 | 46 C | **on** | 96.31 | set | **shut** |
| 5 | 46 C | on | 46.00 | clears | shut |
| 6 | 46 C | off | 46.00 | clear | shut |
| 7 | 60 C | on | 60.00 | set | shut |
| 8 | 60 C | off | 60.00 | set | opens — released onto a live limit |

(TI-322015 on B-55's 854 kg/h; on the valve's rated 1000 kg/h, B-60, tick 2 reads 119.15 C and
ticks 3 and 4 112.35, §XLIX.2. The valve sequence is unchanged.)

**Both ways** (`test_i_22_1_on_the_dcs_logic_decided_divergence`): V1's lines transcribed (handoff
A-12): flooded, its liquor at 56.24 C (the B-55 test's end) holds the latch, and every operator
close is re-opened in the same step, six commands running; the port's keyswitch shuts the valve,
TI-322015 falls from 96.31 to 46.0 C and the limit clears. Behaviour:
`test_the_flood_holds_itself_in_until_hs_322915_ends_it_b56`,
`test_i_22_1_is_pc22_5_1s_or_on_a_fail_open_valve`.

**Raised.** V1's operator command opens XV-322915 when the trip is clear; PC22.5.1 has no input
that opens it (B-59, before the command layer). The loop summary X 322915 rates the valve at
1000 kg/h normal, 1200 maximum, of LP steam at 9.0 bar a and 175 C (line 100-STLS4-329722,
outlet 7.8 bar a), where the flood is V1's 500 kW, 854 kg/h at the 5.013 bar a header: 1000 kg/h
at 175 C is 564 kW latent and reads 112.35 C on TI-322015 over the design vent, against 96.31
(B-60).

## XLVIII.2 B-57: the vendor archive holds no ejector performance curve

The decision asked for the Körting performance curves and an interpolation of suction capacity
on suction and motive pressure. Every Körting and Uhde document for the three ejectors was read:

| document | content |
|---|---|
| UD-AU-324-EC-0007, -0009, -0010 (Uhde's technical specifications) | one duty point each: 324F004's suction 634 kg/h normal, 761 maximum, at 0.12 bar a and 40 C; motive 927 600 kg/h, 929 505 kg/h at 4.1 bar a, 146 C ("Manufacturer shall optimise the vacuum unit") |
| UD-AU-324-DZ-0007-006 (324F002's operating instructions) | "Operating data": one point, motive 650 kg/h at 4.1 bar a, 144.5 C; suction 94 kg/h of 24.1 kg/kmol gas at 0.2 bar a, 45 C; mixed flow 1.0 bar a. Pages 21-23: noise spectra |
| UD-AU-324-DZ-0009-005, -0010-005 (the 324F004 / F005 unit's instructions) | the suction composition, the stage pressures, the nozzle and diffuser throats, Uhde's stream table (§XLVII.4); Körting's generic "Trouble Sources" and "Performance Measurement" leaflets — the molar-mass and temperature correction (Figure 4), calibrated test nozzles; no curve |
| UD-AU-324-DZ-0007-004, -0009-004, -0010-004 (design calculations) and the References copies | AD 2000 wall-thickness calculations |
| UD-AU-324-DZ-0007-007, -0009-006 (fabrication and inspection) | material certificates, hydraulic test reports (body 3.0 bar g, steam chest 10.6 bar g), no performance test |

So there are no suction-against-motive-pressure points to interpolate: each ejector has one duty
point (V1's own audit of 2026-07-26 said the same of 324F002). Nothing was built. Measured for the
question (V1's unwired `ejector_huang.py`, ideal gas, gamma 1.33, loss-free): Körting's motive
nozzles choke **1085 and 374 kg/h** at 4.11 bar a and 146 C (Napier's rule: 1034 and 356) —
Uhde's vacuum-unit table, 1061 and 366, not the PFD's 1220 and 180 nor the specification's 600 and
505. On the nozzle and diffuser throats (area ratios 18.6 and 4.5), Huang's loss-free critical mode
gives entrainment 0.488 and 0.223 — 529 kg/h against Körting's 761 at 0.122 bar a for 324F004 —
and critical back pressures of 1.34 and 2.39 bar a, against 0.35 and 1.05 behind them. 324F002's
nozzle is not in the archive (a controllable spindle ejector).

## XLVIII.3 The melt's equilibrium (`thermo/urea_melt.py`) and its boiling-point elevation

*Signed off 2026-10-16 (decision 122, handoff B-1 closed, §LXXI.3): kept as V1, as ported.*

**Ported** verbatim: `equilibrium_urea_fraction` (V1 `evap_w_eq`), `melt_concentration_pct`
(`conc_infer_324`, the PY-324201 / AY-324701 soft sensor), `melt_diagnostics` (`evap_thermo_diag`):

$$ w_{eq}(T, P) = w_{des} + \big[\,w_{UQ}(T, P) - w_{UQ}(T_{des}, P_{des})\,\big] \in (10^{-9}, 1 - 10^{-9}) $$

$w_{UQ}$ the neutral H2O/urea UNIQUAC root (`extended_uniquac.solve_urea_mass_fraction_fast`), the
arguments held at the window's edge (99-200 C, 0.02-1.00 bar a), no root returning the design
strength. The stages' anchors in `data/unit_324.py`: 0.9431 at 130 C, 0.33 bar a; 0.9771 at 140 C,
0.131 bar a (PFD 401 and 402). **Equivalence** (`test_urea_melt_equivalence.py`, 9): V1's
functions lifted and executed on V1's own UNIQUAC module, both stages over 132 states across and
beyond the window, five non-finite arguments, the diagnostics — all ``==``.

**The melt's strength.** The PFD's melt is 97.71 wt% urea, 0.85 biuret, 1.39 water (402, mass per
cent for liquid rows), V1's "98.6 %" being urea and biuret together. The process engineer's 99.7 %
is in none of the plant's documents: it comes from the References' generic scenario notes (a
prilling plant at 0.03 bar a). Helwan's design is 98.6 % at 0.131 bar a.

**V1's boil-off.** Each stage's water is what takes the feed's urea to the equilibrium strength,
$\dot m_v = \dot m_{feed} - \dot m_{urea}/w_{eq}(T, P)$ in [0, feed], inside a P-T fixed point with
the separator's vapour balance (§XLVIII.5). There is no hard ceiling: V1's TD-016 removed the
fixed 94.31 % cap.

**Checked against the melt's physics** (B-58). The PFD's own rows fix the melt's water activity:
705 and 709 put the water at 96.77 and 87.58 mol % of the 0.33 and 0.131 bar a vapour, so

| stage | x_w (PFD melt) | p_w (bar a) | gamma_w PFD | gamma_w UNIQUAC | Margules (Voskov) | boils at, raw UNIQUAC | PFD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 324F001 | 0.1494 | 0.3193 | **0.791** | 0.517 | 0.983 | 144.0 C | 130 C |
| 324F003 | 0.0453 | 0.1147 | **0.701** | 0.485 | 0.924 | 152.8 C | 140 C |

The single-parameter Voskov-Voronin UNIQUAC (urea -> H2O, -211.96 K) overstates the melt's hold on
its water: raw, it boils the PFD melts 14 and 13 K hotter (BPE 73.5 and 104.2 K against the PFD's
59.5 and 91.5). Anchoring removes the offset at design, not the slope:

| stage | dw/dT, wt%/K | dw/dP, wt% per 0.01 bar |
|---|---|---|
| V1 (anchored UNIQUAC) | +0.249, +0.069 | -0.240, -0.176 |
| UNIQUAC refitted to the PFD (-85.3 K) | +0.175, +0.045 | -0.173, -0.119 |
| Fahmy-Nassar (plant correlation, `Urea-Water VLE Data Research.md`) | +0.167, +0.045 | -0.202, -0.144 |
| Margules (Voskov, a0 128, a1 521 J/mol) | +0.127, +0.035 | -0.129, -0.093 |

A one-parameter refit of the same UNIQUAC to Helwan's own rows (-71.6 K fits stage 1, -98.9
stage 2; -85.3 both within 4 %) lands on the independent plant correlation's temperature slopes
within 5 %; V1's are about half as steep again. Second, the strength is on a urea-only basis:
402 carries 0.90 wt% that is neither urea nor water, so its urea cannot pass 99.10 %, and the
anchored strength does at 140 C below 0.0523 bar a, at 150 C below 0.0700 (0.9936 at 150 C,
0.05 bar a) — a stage there would boil its biuret as water. Third, the solve takes the whole
vacuum as the water's pressure, where the PFD's vapour carries 3 and 12 % NH3, CO2 and air.
Behaviour: `tests/thermo/test_urea_melt.py` (6).

## XLVIII.4 The condensers as nodes (`units/evaporation/condenser_node.py`)

V1's `vacuum_inlet_kmolh` and `vacuum_condenser_node` ported verbatim. The inlet, the PFD row on
its air-free mass plus the live false air:

$$ r = \frac{m_{in} - m_{air}}{m_{in,des} - m_{air,des}}, \quad
   n_k = n_{k,des}\,r + y_{air,k}\frac{m_{air} - m_{air,des}}{M_{air}}
   + y_{air,k}\frac{m_{air,des}}{M_{air}}(1 - r) $$

a known part (LV-323505's blow-through gas in 324E002) replacing the same mass of the row's
condensable and carried species; the node, the anchored vent capped at the inlet while the duty is
positive (the whole inlet otherwise), the condensate the rest. V1's dictionary of lagged cold ends
is the caller's: `t_v_prev` in, `t_vent_c` out. **Equivalence**
(`test_condenser_node_equivalence.py`, 73): the inlet on both first-stage condensers over four
loads, three false-air rates and three blow-through cases; the node on all four over three shell
pressures, four cooling-water cases and two lagged cold ends; every field ``==``, V1's lagged cold
end the port's. Measured: twice and three times the design false air take 324E002's vent from 72
to 107.97 and 143.89 kg/h; its water lost, it vents its whole 26 840 kg/h. Behaviour: 5.

## XLVIII.5 The stages surveyed (`main.py` 2141-2340, 9680-10010)

Each stage: a TIC -> PIC chest cascade (TIC-324001 -> PIC-329203 on LP steam, chest 3.96 bar a;
TIC-324002 -> PIC-329212 on the 9-bar header, chest 8.1 bar a), the chest pressure solved
(`steam_chest_pressure`, ported), the duty $UA(T_{sat}(P_{chest}) - T)$; the boil-off to the
equilibrium strength (§XLVIII.3); the melt temperature semi-implicit,
$T' = T + P_{wr}\,dt/(M c_p + k_{cap} dt)$; the separator's vapour space a molar balance between
the condenser's anchored vent and the ejector's pull, stepped backward in pressure; T and P closed
together by Picard to 1e-12 in at most 20 iterations. The ejector's pull sits inside that fixed
point, so the stages wait on B-57. Stage 1 drains through the barometric leg,
$\dot m = \dot m_{des}\sqrt{M/M_{des}}$; stage 2 through LIC-324501 to LV-324501A, LV-324501B a
relief to 323D002 on PIC-335201; UF85 deferred with unit 335. The species layer, the transport
packet and the condensate traps are V1's 323 machinery.

**V1's design balance against the PFD.** V1 conserves urea (none in the vapour, no biuret
formed): its stage-1 melt is 78 676 kg/h against PFD 401's 78 042 (+0.8 %), its vapour 14 073
against 705's 14 799 (-4.9 %); stage 2, 75 938 against 402's 74 721 (+1.6 %), vapour 2 738 against
709's 3 342 (-18.1 %). The condensers see the PFD rows by departure (`inlet + (v - v_des)`), so
the design point holds; V1's F-11 records the PFD's 317 as not reachable from 319 by evaporation
alone.

# Part XLIX — Four decisions: XV-322915's keyswitch and rated steam, the melt on the PFD's own water activity, the ejectors' maps; the vacuums the maps hold (B-61); stage 1 of unit 324

Session 33. The process engineer decided B-57 (again), B-58, B-59 and B-60 on 2026-10-01, all as
the recommended options, and authorised the port of the 324 stages. The four are built and
asserted both ways (project.md decisions 40-43). Building B-57 exposed one consequence: the
vendor-anchored ejectors cannot hold the PFD's design vacuums (§XLIX.5, handoff B-61), so the
maps are built and not yet wired into the stages' pressure loops. Stage 1, 324E001 / 324F001, is
ported with the pull as an argument (§XLIX.7); stage 2 waits for its own port.

## XLIX.1 XV-322915 has no operator open (handoff B-59)

AC4's PC22.5.1 (§XLVIII.1) drives XVY-322915 from TT-322015's limit and HS-322915 only, and the
loop summaries list no other hand switch for the valve. V1's operator command ``322915`` opens it
whenever trip 22.1 is clear (``main.py`` 11494-11500), and the 328-2 overlay's valve symbol and its
EXT-OVR button both send it. Decided: the console carries the plant's controls only.

* The screen. `data/screen_layout.py` is generated; what an element does is changed only through
  the converter's `DECIDED_EDITS` table (`tools/convert_overlays.py`), each edit naming its
  decision and raising if its element is gone. XV-322915's symbol loses its command (a status
  display); the override button becomes HS-322915, command ``HS-322915``, its lamp lit while
  TT-322015 is over its limit. The coordinates are untouched.
* The command. `keyswitch_set` (`{"type": "keyswitch_set", "id": "HS-322915", "on": bool}`), an
  operator command (§4a rule 3: the keyswitch is a control-room switch), routed to unit 322 by its
  tag (`data/tags.py`). The engine's command layer, Phase 5, refuses an ``xv_toggle`` on 322915
  with the process reason (handoff, Phase 5 row).

**Both ways** (`test_xv_322915_has_no_operator_open_decided_divergence`): V1's transcribed command
opens the valve with 22.1 clear; the port's `xv_322915_open` has no input that can, the overlay
carries no command on XV-322915 and the keyswitch on HS-322915.

caller — the K-value service's neutral domain — runs V1's model bit-exact, with its own fast
grid per parameter). Fitted to Helwan's PFD rows, the melts 401 and 402 under their vapours 705
and 709 (water activity coefficients 0.7908 and 0.7010):

| 324F001 | 0.1494 | 0.7908 | -71.66 | 0.7594 (-4.0 %) | 0.5167 |

`MELT_A_UREA_WATER_K = -85.3` (`data/unit_324.py`), the two fits' mean to 0.1 K (-85.29). The
anchored departure is kept, so the PFD melts hold to the bit at design.

| stage | dw/dT [wt%/K]: refit, F-N, V1 | dw/dP [wt% per 0.01 bar]: refit, F-N, V1 |
|---|---|---|
| 324F001 | **+0.1745**, +0.1670, +0.2489 | -0.1732, -0.2024, -0.2400 |
| 324F003 | **+0.0451**, +0.0446, +0.0692 | -0.1190, -0.1440, -0.1765 |

The temperature slopes, TIC-324001's and TIC-324002's process gain, within 4.5 and 1.1 % of the
plant correlation (V1: 49 and 55 % steep).

**Grounded on the licensor's own chart** (pointed to by the process engineer, session 33). Uhde's
Helwan operating manual, Fundamentals (UD-VT-G00-DC-0003 rev 00 page 1-44, Figure 15, "Three
phase equilibria of system Urea - Water"; `References/Sources/Urea Production Diagrams.pdf` PDF
page 19, a 300 dpi scan) draws P_H2O against temperature for urea-water strengths 90 to 99.7 wt%
— a Clausius-Clapeyron chart, log P against 1/T. Digitised on the scan's own ticks (log P at 798
px a decade; the temperature ticks linear in 1/T; the scan's 0.4° skew corrected), each line
fitted straight, log10 P[mmHg] = a + b/T, residuals under 0.006 in log10 P:

| wt% (urea-water) | a | b [K] | drawn from |
|---|---|---|---|
| 92.5 | 8.0042 | -2198.37 | 111 C |
| 95 | 7.8663 | -2214.98 | 130 C |
| 97 | 7.6819 | -2231.03 | 124 C |
| 98 | 7.4444 | -2212.24 | 136 C |
| 99 | 7.0530 | -2187.99 | 133 C |

(The 90 % trace has a 0.034 residual and the 99.7 % line is the chart's illustrative point D, 99.7
% at about 140 C and 26 mmHg — the classic prilling second stage at 0.03 bar a, the "99.7 %" the
process engineer asked about, in Helwan's own manual as a generic illustration; both are left
out.) On the chart's basis PFD 401 is 95.0 % and its water 0.314 bar a at 130 C, against the PFD
vapour's 0.319; 402 is 98.6 %, about 0.112 bar a at 140 C against 0.115. Over every line and
temperature drawn, the refit's water vapour pressure is within 13 % of the chart (mean 4 % low);
the published parameter is 27-35 % low everywhere. The chart's own slopes at the stages' vacuums:
+0.159 and +0.044 wt%/K (refit +0.175 and +0.045, within 10 and 3 %; V1 57 % steep), -0.153 and
-0.113 wt% per 0.01 bar (refit -0.173 and -0.119). Asserted in `tests/thermo/test_urea_melt.py`. The vacuum slopes are 14 and 17 % shallow: the binary
takes the whole vacuum as the water's pressure, where the PFD's vapour carries 3 and 12 % NH3,
CO2 and air (B-58's third point, unchanged).

**The ceiling** (the heel class: the water removed cannot exceed the water present).

$$ w_{eq} = \min\Big( w_{des} + [w_{UQ}(T,P) - w_{UQ}(T_{des},P_{des})],\ w_{max} \Big), \qquad
   w_{max} = \frac{w_{urea}}{w_{urea} + w_{biuret} + w_{HCHO}}\Big|_{feed} $$

(`strength_ceiling`, `equilibrium_urea_fraction(..., w_max=)`). PFD 402's ceiling is 99.13 %; on
the refit the anchored strength reaches it only at 0.02 bar a above 170 C (V1's model at 140 C
below 0.051 bar a). The soft sensor PY-324201 / AY-324701 infers from T and P alone and reads the
uncapped equilibrium past the ceiling, as the DCS would. The diagnostics' P-x residual is taken on
the stage's own parameter (+0.0630 bar at 402's design, the binary's 2.29 % water against the
PFD's 1.39 %).

**Both ways** (`test_urea_melt_equivalence.py`): the port on the published parameter `==` V1's

feed (ceiling 99.26 %; the refit there 98.90 %, under it).

## XLIX.4 The ejectors' maps (handoff B-57, the Typo Rule)

**The 1-D core**, V1's unwired `ejector_huang.py`, ported verbatim
(`units/evaporation/ejector_gas_dynamics.py`; `critical_backpressure` loses the temperatures and
areas V1 never read). **The data** (`data/unit_324.py` `EJECTOR_DUTIES`): Uhde's vacuum-unit
stream table, UD-AU-324-DZ-0009-005 PDF page 20, completed by Körting — 712 634 normal, 761
maximum kg/h at 0.12 bar a, 40 C; 714 1822 kg/h at 0.35 bar a, 90 C; 715 84 kg/h at 0.33 bar a,
41 C; 717 450 kg/h at 1.16 bar a; 721 1300 kg/h; 722 46.5 kg/h at 1.05 bar a; 759 400 kg/h; 927
1061 and 929 366 kg/h of motive steam at 4.1 bar a, 146 C, 2.13 kg/m3. Körting's operating data
(same document, BAL 211-12/100 E page 7 of 18, PDF page 8): the suction gas 27.4 air, 366 water,
155.3 NH3, 212.3 CO2 at 40 C and 122 mbar (21.61 kg/kmol); diffuser throats 106.5 and 30.8 mm,
motive nozzle orifices 24.7 and 14.5 mm; motive 3.1 bar g, 146 C. 324F002 (UD-AU-324-DZ-0007-006
p20): motive 650 kg/h at 4.1 bar a, 144.5 C; 94 kg/h of 24.1 kg/kmol gas at 0.2 bar a, 45 C;
discharge 1.0 bar a; no throat in the archive. 715's molar mass from its PFD row (27.79).

**The map** (`units/evaporation/ejector_map.py`), equations in the module docstring:

$$ A_t = \frac{\dot m_{p,duty}}{\dot m^*(P_{m,duty}, T_m; 1)}, \quad
   C = K\,\dot m^*_{gas}\big(P_s, T_s, M_s;\ A_3 - A_t\,\tfrac{A}{A^*}(M(P_m/P_s))\big), \quad
   P_c = P_{d,duty}\,\frac{P_{c,1D}(P_s, P_m)}{P_{c,1D}(duty)} $$

$$ \mathrm{pull} = C \cdot F(r), \quad r = r^*\frac{P_d}{P_c}, \quad
   F = \sqrt{\frac{r^{2/\gamma} - r^{(\gamma+1)/\gamma}}{r^{*2/\gamma} - r^{*(\gamma+1)/\gamma}}}
   \ (r < 1),\ 0\ (r \ge 1),\ 1\ (P_d \le P_c) $$

| ejector | effective nozzle | mixing throat | K | P_c scale | shut-off at 4.1 bar a |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 324F002 | 19.13 mm (from 650 kg/h) | 44.45 mm, fitted on the duty (K = 1) | 1 | 0.564 | 88.7 mbar |
| 324F004 | 24.46 mm, 98.10 % of 24.7 | 106.5 mm (drawing) | 1.3300 | 0.265 | 14.6 mbar |
| 324F005 | 14.37 mm, 98.19 % of 14.5 | 30.8 mm (drawing) | 0.8701 | 0.501 | 112.9 mbar |

The loss-free 1-D model under-states 324F004 by 33 % and over-states 324F005 by 13 %, and its
critical back pressures are 1.8 to 3.8 times what the ejectors are rated to discharge into: each
map is anchored on its own duty for capacity (K) and break (the P_c scale — the ejector taken as
critical at its rated discharge, the minimal-margin assumption; handoff B-61). The subsonic
closure above P_c is this module's own (the gas meeting the jet at a static pressure that rises
with the discharge pressure from its sonic r* P_s; continuous with its slope at P_c, zero at
P_c / r* = 1.85 P_c). Tabulated on 239 suction nodes (0.010-1.200 bar a by 0.005) x 121 motive
nodes (0-6.00 bar a by 0.05, the steam chests' 6 bar g), built lazily (0.18 s for three), read
bilinearly; every duty is a node, so 761 kg/h at 0.12 bar a and 0.35 bar a critical come off the
table to rounding; within 0.1 % of the 1-D points wherever the ejector pulls a tenth of its duty
(0.05-1.10 bar a suction, 2.5-5.0 motive). Declared: one gamma, 1.33, for both streams; the gas's
molar mass and temperature held at the duty's (no Körting molar-mass correction); the motive
temperature at the duty's.

**What it does** (324F004 against 0.3 bar a unless stated): 200 kg/h at 0.05 bar a, 761 at 0.12,
1377 at 0.2, 7717 at 1.0; at 0.131 and full motive, critical to 0.369 bar a, 573 kg/h at 0.60,
100 at 0.68, nothing from 0.69; the motive sagging, 910 kg/h at 2.5 bar a, 904 at 1.5, 708 at
1.0, 281 at 0.8, none without motive. In the critical mode more motive pulls slightly less (the
wider jet), which is Huang's model; the motive's lever is the break.

**Both ways** (`test_ejector_map_decided_equivalence.py`, V1's two lines transcribed on V1's
lifted constants):

| case | V1 324F004 | map 324F004 | V1 324F002 | map 324F002 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the PFD's vacuums, design motive | 584.0 | 844.98 | 72.0 | 214.06 |
| motive halved (HIC-329606 25 %; 195 kg/h; 2.05 bar a) | 292.0 | 924.04 | 36.0 | 264.36 |
| discharge 1.5 (324F004) / 2.5 (324F002) bar a | 584.0 | 0 | 72.0 | 0 |
| from atmosphere | 4517.08 | 7814.00 | 221.07 | 882.63 |

## XLIX.5 The vacuums the maps hold (handoff B-61)

At the PFD's design vacuums the vendor-anchored ejectors out-pull the PFD's loads: 324F004 845
kg/h at 0.131 bar a against 712's 584, 324F002 214 at 0.33 against 706's 72. Each vacuum is a
balance between the condenser's saturated vent (`condenser_node`, the vent rising steeply as the
shell pressure falls) and the ejector's pull, held by PIC-324202 / PIC-324203 admitting false air.
Measured on the ported condensers at the design temperatures and full motive:

| | the bleed to hold the PFD vacuum | the bleed valve wide open | settles, PFD bleed (21 kg/h) | settles, bleed wide open | melt there (refit) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 324F003 / 324E005 | 108.2 kg/h | PV-324203 26.7 kg/h | **0.1200 bar a**, vent 761.3 | 0.1207 | 97.84 % |
| 324F001 / 324E002 | 104.1 kg/h | PV-324202 67.4 kg/h | **0.2294 bar a**, vent 120.6 | 0.2871 | 96.02 / 95.05 % |

324F003 settles where Körting rated 324F004: at 0.120 bar a 324E005 vents exactly the 761 kg/h of
the vendor's maximum duty. The vendor documents describe a vacuum system sized with margin over the
PFD, and the PFD's 0.131 and 0.33 bar a are part-load points it holds only with more false air
than the bleed valves pass — or with the motive throttled into the break, which Flowserve's motive
valves were not sized for (HV-329606's normal case 1427 kg/h at 3.9 bar a, 81 %; HV-329605's
390 kg/h, the PFD's, at 3.8 bar a, 69 %, where Körting's 324F002 takes 650 kg/h at 4.1).

The plant's own trend (`References/DCS Trends/Book2.xlsx`, two months from 2023-07-07, 5280
samples): PT-324201 median -0.670 bar g (p10 -0.690, p90 -0.647), about 0.343 bar a, with
HIC-329605 at a median 60 % (p10 50, p90 80). The plant holds the PFD's stage-1 vacuum; the
duty-anchored map would hold 0.23-0.29 bar a. PT-324204 is not in the trend book.

**The vacuum valves**, read from Flowserve's calculation sheets (UD-MR-G00-DZ-0048-003, scanned)
and catalogued (`data/control_valves.py`): PV-324202 Pos. 55, DN25, Kvs 4, modified equal
percentage, 46 kg/h of air at 0.9 -> 0.3 bar a and 32 C, Kv 2.73 at 87 %; PV-324203 Pos. 56, Kvs
1.6, 23 kg/h at 0.9 -> 0.14 bar a, Kv 1.38 at 95 %, choked; HV-329605 Pos. 66, DN80, Kvs 40, LP
steam 4.1 -> 3.8 bar a at 146 C, 233 / 390 / 429 kg/h at 52 / 69 / 72 %; HV-329606 Pos. 67, DN80,
Kvs 125, 800 / 1427 / 1600 kg/h at 4.0 / 3.9 / 3.8 bar a out, 73 / 81 / 78 %. The PFD's 21 kg/h
sits at 61.1 % on PV-324202 and 92.0 % on PV-324203; the motive valves' normal cases at 69.1 and
80.8 %, the sheets' own 69 and 81.

Re-anchored on the PFD instead (option a of B-61), 324F004's K would be 0.919 — the loss-free
model within 8 % — and it would pull 526 kg/h at 0.12 bar a against Körting's 761; 324F002's
scale 0.336, 31.6 kg/h at 0.2 bar a against Körting's 94.

Decided 2026-10-01 (option a) and built in session 34: §L.1.

## XLIX.7 Stage 1 — 324E001 / 324F001 (`units/evaporation/first_evaporator.py`, `data/unit_324.py`)

V1's stage 1 (``main.py`` 9693-9890, the 323D002 -> 324E001 line and the stage) ported line for
line. The separator: a melt holdup with mass, energy and species balances; a vapour space whose
pressure is a molar balance between 324E002's anchored saturated vent and the ejector's pull.

$$ \dot m_{vap} = \mathrm{clamp}\Big(\dot m_{feed} - \frac{\dot m_{urea}}{w_{eq}(T, P)},\ 0,\
   \dot m_{feed}\Big), \qquad
   T' = T + \frac{P_{wr}\,\Delta t}{M c_p + k_{cap}\Delta t}, \qquad
   P' = P + \Delta t\, f(P') $$

$P_{wr} = \dot m_{feed} c_{p,feed}(T_{feed} - T) + UA(T_{sat}(P_{chest}) - T) - \dot m_{vap}\lambda$,
$k_{cap} = \dot m_{feed} c_{p,feed} + UA\,[Q > 0]$, $f(P) = (RT/V_v)(n_{vent}(P) - n_{pull}(P))$ on the
drawing's 70.5 m3 less the melt, 15.64 kg/kmol; T and P closed by Picard to 1e-12 in at most 20
iterations (V1's G7; 5 to 7 measured), the pressure stepped backward
(`core.node.backward_euler_pressure`, V1's ``_backward_euler_p``, ported verbatim), 324E002's
cold end held at the last full solve's (a tear, `t_vent_324e002_c`). The chest is V1's solved
law (`units/steam_chest.py`), the header lagged through the melt's 180 s; the melt drains through
the barometric leg, $\dot m_{401} = \dot m_{401,des}\sqrt{M/M_{des}}$; the species ride on V1's
anchored volatilities (`thermo.urea_liquor.vapour_y`, ``SOL_E001``: no biuret formed at design,
0.06 wt% urea in the vapour); LIC-329505 drains the chest's condensate (V1's active steam trap).

**The departures**, each a decided divergence and a switch in the transcription:

| switch | the port | V1 | measured both ways (`test_first_evaporator_decided_equivalence.py`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| B-58 (decided for this unit) | the melt on the -85.3 K refit, under the feed's ceiling | `evap_w_eq`, -211.96 K, no ceiling | LP header -10 %: the melt at 93.99 % after 5 min, V1's 93.89 % |
| chest (decision 20) | 3.7 bar a, the DDS (line 21, read from the page image); stroke 73.80 %, UA 969.7 kW/K | 3.96 bar a, 0.90 x a retired 4.4; UA 785.6 | LP header -10 %: the melt 0.31 K warmer after 10 min |
| gains (decisions 10, 21) | TIC-324001 1.50 x 6 bar / 160 K = 0.05625 bar/K, 320 s; PIC-329203 0.30 x 100 / 6 = 5.0 %/bar, 75 s; PIC-324202 2.00 x 100 / 1 bar = 200 %/bar, 200 s | 1.5 bar/K; 0.30 x its chest scale; 2.0 %/bar | TIC +2 K: 130.55 C after 10 min, V1 131.72 (27 times gentler, stable); PIC-324202 to 0.30: 0.3138 bar a, V1 0.3297 |
| valve (decision 23) | PV-324202 on Flowserve Pos. 55's trim from 61.07 % | linear from 50 % | PIC-324202 to 0.30: 15.38 kg/h of air after 10 min, V1 16.04 |

## L.1 The ejectors' capacity on the PFD's design loads (handoff B-61, option a)

the design vacuums were part-load points the bleed valves could not reach, where the plant's trend
holds PT-324201 at the PFD's 0.34 bar a. Decided: each map's capacity anchored on the PFD's design
flow at its design vacuum and the duty's motive pressure (`data/unit_324.py`
`EJECTOR_DESIGN_LOADS`; `units/evaporation/ejector_map.py` `ejector_map`), the vendor's map kept
as `vendor_map`:

$$ K_{des} = K_{duty}\,\frac{\dot m_{s,des}}{C_{duty,table}(P_{s,des},\ P_{m,duty})} $$

read off the vendor map's table as the plant reads it (0.131 bar a is not a node), so the decided
table gives the design load to rounding. The throats, the nozzles and the break are the vendor's.

## L.2 The held melt boils (handoff B-62, option a)

V1's boil-off is the feed's water alone, so a stage with no feed boiled nothing and its held melt
superheated to the chest (§XLIX.7). Decided: the separator's holdup boils past its own boiling
point at the live vacuum (`units/evaporation/holdup_boil.py`), the excess sensible heat paid as
latent heat:

$$ w_b(T, P) = \min\big(w_{u,des} + [w_{model}(T,P) - w_{model}(T_{des},P_{des})],\ w_{max,hold}\big) $$

$$ T' = T^* - \frac{x\,\lambda}{C}, \qquad w_u'(x) = \frac{w_u M - y_u x}{M - x}, \qquad
   w_b(T', P) = w_u'(x) $$

T* the stage's semi-implicit step, C its own denominator (M c_p + k_cap Δt), x the kilograms boiled
in the tick, solved by the Illinois regula falsi on (0, x_max] — x_max the volatiles above the
holdup's ceiling and at most the holdup above its floor. The holdup's equilibrium is the stage's
anchored melt equilibrium on the holdup's OWN design composition (PFD 401 reconciled, 94.301 %;
402, 97.701 %), so the design holdup sits exactly at its boiling point and the feed's term is V1's
untouched. The vapour is the stage's (the anchored volatilities); the species layer takes the feed's
and the holdup's boil-off together.

**Inside the implicit pressure step.** The holdup's boil-off answers the vacuum by thousands of
kg/h per mbar. Held at the fixed point's iterate, stage 2's Picard rang between boiling and not —
on a feed loss it ran to its 20-iteration cap unconverged; so each stage evaluates the boil-off at
the trial pressure inside `backward_euler_pressure` (the condenser's inlet recomputed there, its
back-pressure held at the iterate as V1 holds it), then boils the holdup at the solved pressure.
Stage 2 then converges in 5 or 6 iterations, stage 1 in at most 18 on its feed loss; where the
holdup does not boil, the step is V1's to the bit.

**At design** stage 1's held melt boils 1.6 kg/h: PFD 317 normalised carries 80.0016 % urea against
V1's 80 %, so the feed boils that much less, and the holdup makes it up — the melt holds 130 C to
3e-7 K over an hour. Stage 2 boils nothing at design.

**Both ways** (the stages' decided-equivalence tests), the feed lost:

| | V1 at 30 s | port at 30 s | V1 at the end | port at the end |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| stage 1 (323P003 stops) | 150.00 C, 94.30 %, nothing boils | 142.64 C, 96.07 %, 5175 kg/h boiling (11 182 at once) | 151.94 C, 94.30 % (the heel) | 151.94 C, 97.07 % |
| stage 2 (stage 1's leg stops) | 147.76 C, 97.70 % | 145.57 C, 97.94 %, 879 kg/h (1316 at once) | 175.11 C, 97.70 % | 174.92 C, 98.64 % |

The melt holds at its boiling point and climbs as it concentrates, until at the chest's saturation
its equilibrium at the vacuum is reached and it boils no more. In fed transients the holdup boils
where its temperature leads its composition: TIC-324001 to 132 C, 130.52 C after ten minutes against
130.55 without (the departures' re-measured values below).

(`second_evaporator.leg_urea_strength`) takes the leg's strength, anchored as a departure from the
design so the design and every fed steady state stay V1's:

    w_feed = w_401,des + ( w_leg,Urea - w_leg,Urea,des ),    clamped to [0, 1]

stage 1's reconciled holdup at design, 94.3011 % urea (``W_S401``), giving the 94.31 % anchor
(``R324_W_EV1``) exactly. The argument ``feed_w_urea`` is gone from `SecondEvaporator.step`; the
species layer already took the leg's composition. The decision's words ask that "the liquid
entering Stage 2 must have the exact thermodynamic state (composition and enthalpy) of the liquid
leaving Stage 1's separator leg": the composition and the temperature are the leg's (stage 1's
advanced holdup and solved temperature, as before); the urea basis carries the option's 0.009-point
design anchor, which keeps the design point exact.

Measured both ways (`test_second_evaporator_decided_equivalence.py`): the leg drains the design melt
at the design rate while stage 1 makes none (``w1_live`` 0, a 323P003 trip as stage 2 sees it). V1
takes the 75.9 t/h as urea-free and boils all of it: 114.3 C in 5 s, -9.3 C in 30 s, -103.5 C in a
minute. The port holds the design to the bit.

The trip through both stages (`test_second_evaporator.py`, stage 1 and stage 2 chained, design
cold ends): after 30 s the leg carries 71.5 t/h at 96.07 % (B-62 boiling stage 1's held melt);
stage 2 takes 68.72 t/h of urea in it, boils 1253 kg/h of the feed's water and 671 of its own

## LI.3 323F010's held liquor boils (handoff B-24; B-62's class)

V1 caps 323F010's evaporation at the design split of the feed, ``min(phi m_feed, duty branch)``
(``main.py`` 8551), so above design the surplus heated the liquor past its own bubble point and
the product never passed 80.00 % (§XXX.6). The decision: "if a bulk fluid in a chest-heated vessel
exceeds its boiling point, it boils". The port keeps V1's two branches and adds the held liquor's
own boil-off past the bubble point of its whole composition at the live PT-323204
(`holdup_boil.liquor_boil`):

    T'          = T* - x lambda / C
    w_k'(x)     = (w_k M - y_k x) / (M - x)
    T_bub(w'(x), P) = T'                    solved for x in (0, x_max] by Illinois regula falsi

T* the semi-implicit temperature step, C its denominator; y the overhead's composition, last
tick's vapour (the A-6 tear) with its entrainment; x_max = min(C (T* - T_bub(w)) / lambda, M - 1 kg,
the first species the overhead would exhaust) — the excess sensible heat paid as latent heat with
the bubble point held, which brackets the root because the bubble point climbs as the overhead
strips the volatiles. The bubble point is the stage's own (`liquor_stage.bubble_t`, V1's
``sol_bubble_t_dep``). It is evaluated at the trial pressure inside the stage's linearised backward
step — the boil-off joins the evaporation in the vapour moles and the swell — and at the pressure the
step ended on: the drain's heel cap is net of it, the holdup and the species lose it, LV-323505's
blow-through share counts it. The pressure step keeps the temperature step before the boil, the
vapour composition and the biuret extent see the temperature after it.

Because the boil reads the LIVE pressure, B-22's deeper-vacuum half is resolved with it: a liquor
standing above its live bubble point boils down to it. Its vacuum-loss half is unchanged — there
the liquor sits below its live bubble point and V1's design-rate evaporation goes on (handoff B-22).
V1's relaxation target stays on the design vacuum, so under a deeper vacuum the relaxation retains
heat that the boil then pays out as vapour: the books close either way.

Measured (`tests/units/recirc/test_pre_evaporator.py`, 1 s steps unless stated):

| case | V1 | port |
|---|---|---|

## LI.4 The vacuum train (`units/evaporation/vacuum_train.py`, `data/unit_324_train.py`)

    705 + 790 --703--> 324E002 --706--> 324F002 (+924) --708--> 323C005
    709 --> 324E005 --712--> 324F004 (+927) --714--> 324E006 --715--> 324F005 (+929) --717-->
            324E007 --722--> atmosphere;      719, 720, 721, 759 --> 328D003 I

V1's ``vacuum_train_324`` (``main.py`` 3987-4048), run each tick through ``core/vacuum.py``
``VacuumTrain324.solve``, ported verbatim and EXECUTED against: the first-stage inlets as the PFD
rows moved by the live vapour and false air (14799, 12040, 3342, 26840 kg/h, V1's literals, now
`PFD_705_KGH` ...), the second and third condensers on the upstream condenser's live vent species
and the ejector's motive as departures from their design rows (`cascade_inlet_kmolh`), each
condenser `condenser_node` at its shell. The ejectors are mixing nodes; what pulls each vacuum is its
stage's pressure balance on the ejector's map. Two of V1's run-time facts are ported as run:
``VacuumTrain324.solve`` passes no ``tv_prev`` (``main.py`` sets ``_vac_unit.tv_prev`` but the wrapper
never forwards it — and ``vacuum_train_324``'s sixth positional argument to
``vacuum_condenser_node`` would land on ``cw_in_c``), so every condenser solves with its
back-pressure bracket centred on its design cold end; and its ``cw_factors`` is empty, so the
cooling water is the design's (the port takes per-condenser overrides for the cooling-water
system). 703 - 705 - 790 is the PFD's own 1 kg/h of rounding at every state, as V1 publishes it.
324E006 and 324E007 sit at V1's 0.3 and 1.0 bar a (handoff B-66).

The stages' overheads reach the train as the stages book them: PFD 705 and 709 carry each stage's
feed boil-off and its held melt's (B-62), ``m_vap_kgh + m_boil_kgh``; 790 is what HV-323605 passed
(`PreEvaporatorResult.pull_kgh`, which includes 323F010's boil-off, B-24), with LV-323505's
blow-through share. The train hands back 324E002's and 324E005's cold ends (the stages' tears),
708 and 706's inerts (323C005), the four condensates (328D003) and 722.

The motive steam (decision 23's class, §5 rule 7; `motive_steam`). V1 strokes HV-329605 linear on
twice PFD 924 (``R324_HV9605_SPAN``) and HV-329606 linear on 927 and 929 from 50 %. The port runs
both on their Flowserve trims (Pos. 66, 67, modified equal percentage) from the strokes that pass
the design motive on their normal cases, 69.06 % (390 kg/h) and 80.16 % (1400 kg/h), HV-329606's
flow split as the PFD splits it (B-64). Ten points shut: V1 80 % of the motive, the trims 74 %
(289, 904, 133 kg/h); wide open V1 twice the design, the trims 2.53 times (HV-329605, sized for
429 kg/h at 72 %) and 1.81 times.

The tags. The decision named "324F006" and "324F007": the archive's TOC (UD-AM-G00-AB-0022), the
merged P&IDs and the PFD carry 324F001 to 324F005 only — 324F001 and 324F003 the separators, 324F002,
324F004 and 324F005 the ejectors — and ``References/Mapping of Evaporation Section.md`` draws the
series above. The train is the four condensers and three ejectors.

In the loop with both stages (`test_vacuum_train.py`, the cold ends fed back one tick late as V1
feeds them): five minutes at design hold every row within 0.04 kg/h of the PFD's (stage 1's held
melt boils 1.6 kg/h, PFD 317's 80.0016 % urea against V1's 80 %) and the cold ends within 1e-4 K.
HV-329606 ten points shut: after ten minutes stage 2 at 0.130125 bar a (324F004's map, still
critical, pulls a shade more on the lower motive, B-61), PIC-324203 bleeding 21.2 kg/h, 324E006
condensing 1478 kg/h where it condensed 1763, 722 at 23.7 kg/h.

## LI.5 Findings B-65 and B-66

**B-65.** The stages' vacuum balances read the train's cold ends one tick late, so within a tick the
condenser absorbs any vapour at the held cold end and the boil-off gets no answer from the vapour
load. The held melt's boil-off answers the vacuum steeply, and a 323P003 trip pulses it: 1266 kg/h,
nothing for three ticks, 6180 — 335 pulses in two minutes, 709 swinging 2.1-7.0 t/h; an HV-329606
cut, 59. Stage 1 does not pulse. Measured remedies: the cold end lagged on its condenser's
tube-side water residence, V/Q from the datasheet geometry (324E002 11.5 s, 324E005 7.7 s; 11.6 was a
rounding of 11.55 on a 995 kg/m3 density, corrected in §LII.1) — no
pulse, the trip's boil-off climbing 3 to 1251 kg/h over a minute; or the cold end solved inside
the implicit step — smooth, 16-52 ms a tick for the two stages.

**B-66.** V1 holds 324E006's shell at 0.3 bar a. As a live node (0.573 m3 free, 324F005 on its map
against the atmosphere, 324F004 discharging against it) it holds 0.3 at design, falls to 0.255 bar
a on an HV-329606 cut, rises to 0.360 on a fifth of its cooling water — stage 2 untouched in each —
and on a lost cooling water rises to 1.0 bar a in 5 s, 324F004 breaks and stage 2's vacuum climbs
to 0.259 bar a, its melt to 144.2 C; V1 holds 0.3 and lets 324F005 "pass" 1804 kg/h.

Both are the process engineer's (handoff B-65, B-66). Decided 2026-10-02 as recommended and built
(§LII): the lag (option a), and the live node on the name plate's 0.542 m3 where the scratch took the
0.573 m3 the datasheet's geometry gives.

# Part LII — The vacuum train as the plant runs it: the lagged cold ends, 324E006's shell; 324E007's ammonia vent

Session 36, 2026-10-02. The process engineer decided handoff B-65 (option a: "the tube-side water
residence time lag physically damps the system while remaining cheap, apply the lag") and B-66 (the
Typo Rule: "make 324E006 a live node ... we want the condenser to spike to 1 bar a when cooling is
lost; we want 324F004 to break; and we want Stage 2 vacuum to collapse"). Both live in
`units/evaporation/vacuum_train.py` `VacuumTrain`, the train with its state, which the scheduler
steps after the two stages; `vacuum_train`, called alone, stays V1's (row 172) and takes the shell
as an argument, `p_324e006_bara`, V1's 0.3 by default. The function was split, without changing a
floating-point operation, into `_first_condensers` (the rows, 324E002, 324E005) and
`_back_condensers` (324E006, 324E007, the books), so the node can step between them. Verifying the
trip found B-67 (§LII.4).

## LII.1 The cold ends lagged on their tubes' water (handoff B-65, option a)

V1 hands each stage's vacuum balance the cold end its condenser settled at in the last full solve,
one tick late (``s.tlag["324E002_T_VENT"]``, ``["324E005_T_VENT"]``). The port lags each cold end
a vacuum balance reads on its condenser's tube-side water residence — the water's thermal inertia,
which V1's algebraic exchanger leaves out:

    T_v,lag' = T_v,lag + dt / (tau + dt) (T_v - T_v,lag)          (backward Euler, `first_order_lag`)
    tau      = V_tubes rho_w / m_cw,des,      V_tubes = n pi d_i^2 L / 4

the tubes from the datasheets (`data.unit_324.VACUUM_CONDENSERS`: count, outside diameter less two
walls, length), the cooling water the PFD's, rho_w IAPWS's saturated liquid at the water's mean
temperature. The channels' water exchanges no heat and is left out (324E006's name plate gives
0.455 m3 tube side, channels included, against its tubes' 0.181 m3).

| condenser | tubes | bore [mm] | length [m] | V_tubes [m3] | water [t/h], mean T [C] | tau [s] | read by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 324E002 | 2329 | 21.8 | 5.9 | 5.129 | 1591, 35.0 | 11.536 | stage 1 (`cold_end_c("324E002")`) |
| 324E005 | 486 | 21.8 | 4.9 | 0.889 | 415, 32.0 | 7.672 | stage 2 (`cold_end_c("324E005")`) |
| 324E006 | 250 | 16.0 | 3.6 | 0.181 | 208, 32.5 | 3.116 | its shell (§LII.2) |
| 324E007 | 70 | 16.0 | 2.5 | 0.035 | 23, 32.5 | 5.479 | nothing: its shell is 1.0 bar a |

Session 35 quoted 324E002's residence as 11.6 s: the scratch's 11.55 s, on a 995 kg/m3 density,
rounded up. The datasheet geometry gives 11.54 s; the decision's "11.6 s / 7.7 s" are these two.
324E006's lag is the same class on the tear B-66 creates, applied under §5 rule 7.

Seeded on the design solves' cold ends, the lag leaves the design untouched. A 323P003 trip with
stage 1, stage 2 and the train in the loop (`test_vacuum_train_decided_equivalence.py`):

| two minutes from the trip | V1's tear, V1's train executed | the port |
|---|---|---|
| stage 2's held-melt boil-off | 1266 kg/h, 0, 0, 0, 6180 ... — 335 pulses | 110 kg/h at 2 s, 1110 at 30 s, 1251 at 60 s — no pulse |
| stage 2's vacuum, 324E006's shell, PFD 709, stage 1's boil-off | pulsing with it | no pulse |
| 722 to atmosphere, the first 70 s | up to 9840 kg/h on the bursts | at most 49.1 kg/h |
| stage 2's melt | above 138.3 C | never below 140 C |

The trip's other cases: an HV-329606 cut ten points gives one 843 kg/h flash of the holdup on the
tick the vacuum dips (the map pulls more on less motive, B-61) and settles in a second — a single
transient, not a ring. Cost: 6.4 ms a tick for the two stages and the train at design, 16 ms
through the trip — the condensate back-pressure's grid filling as the cold ends move, a cache that
warms.

## LII.2 324E006's shell, a vacuum node (handoff B-66, the Typo Rule)

324F004 discharges into 324E006's shell; 324E006 condenses what it can at its lagged cold end;
324F005 pulls the rest on its design-anchored map into 324E007. The stages' balance (`core.node`),
on the shell's own volume:

    dP_6/dt = (R T_6 / V_6) (n_vent(P_6) - n_pull(P_6))
    n_vent  = min( vent_PFD,715 . vent_model(P_6, T_v6, n_714) / vent_model,des , m_714 ) / M_vent
    n_pull  = suction_capacity("324F005", P_6, P_m,929, P_324E007) / M_vent

* V_6 = 0.542 m3, 324E006's shell side on Uhde's name plate (UD-AU-324-DZ-0005-008 rev. 01, Aguilar
  y Salas 12160-8; a scan, read visually: "Volume — shell side 0.542 m3, tube side 0.455 m3";
  `data.unit_324_train.E006_SHELL_VOL_M3`). The datasheet's 550 mm shell less its 250 tubes over
  3.6 m gives 0.573 m3 — the session-35 scratch's — but the name plate is the vendor's own (decision
  33's class). References carries no volume (``324-1b Equipment Descriprion and Datasheet 2.md``).
* T_6 the lagged cold end; n_714 324F004's discharge's species (`cascade_inlet_kmolh`, V1's); the
  vent's molar mass from its composition at the old pressure; P_m,929 the nozzle pressure HV-329606's
  share puts on 324F005; P_324E007 V1's 1.0 bar a.
* Stepped backward (`core.node.backward_euler_pressure`) between E006_P_MIN_BARA = 0.010 bar a, the
  deepest suction 324F005's map is tabulated on, and E006_P_MAX_BARA = 324E007's 1.0 bar a, where
  324F005's body passes what arrives: the train's streams carry 715 as 324E006's vent at the node's
  pressure, so the mass closes there too.

The order in `VacuumTrain.step`: the rows and the two stages' condensers at the stages' solved
vacuums; the shell stepped on what 324F004 now discharges; 324E006 and 324E007 solved at the new
shell; the three cold ends lagged toward the solves'. The stages read the shell (324F004's
discharge) and the cold ends as the train left them on the tick before.

At design the node holds 0.3 bar a to 1e-13 alone (324F005's map reads its design load as
41.00000000000001 kg/h); in the loop five minutes keep it within 3e-7 bar (stage 1's held melt
boiling 1.6 kg/h at design, B-62).

## LII.3 The cascade — 324E006's cooling water lost

`test_vacuum_train.py`, stage 1, stage 2 and `VacuumTrain` in the loop, the water cut at 0.5 s:

| time after the cut | 324E006's shell [bar a] | stage 2's vacuum [bar a] | melt [C] | PIC-324203's bleed | 712 / 722 [kg/h] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.300 | 0.131 | 140.00 | 92.0 %, 21.0 kg/h | 584 / 1982 |
| 1.5 s | 0.646 | 0.1317 | 140.00 | 92.0 % | 566 / 1964 |
| 2.4 s | 1.000 (324E007's) | | | | |
| 4.5 s | 1.000 | 0.1522 | 140.03 | 89.9 % | 157 / 1447 |
| 2 min | 1.000 | 0.2587 | 144.09 | 73.4 %, 12.0 kg/h | 17.3 / 1185 |

324F004 breaks against the shell: at stage 2's design vacuum its critical back pressure is 0.369 bar
a and it entrains nothing past 1.85 times that; as stage 2's vacuum is lost its critical back
pressure rises with the suction (0.540 bar a at 0.2587), and the vacuum settles where 324F004's 1.4 %
of critical capacity meets 324E005's vent — 324E005 still condenses stage 2's vapour, so the vacuum is
lost to 0.259 bar a, not to atmosphere. PIC-324203 closes its bleed against it. 324E007 takes what
324E006 no longer condenses and sends 1185 kg/h to atmosphere. No pulse in stage 2's vacuum or the
shell. V1, executed on the same loss: 324E006 condenses nothing and passes all 1804 kg/h, yet its
shell stays at 0.3 bar a and 324E005 is to the bit what it was — stage 2 never learns.

The other cases: a fifth of 324E006's water lifts the shell to 0.3603 bar a, 324F004 still critical,
stage 2 within 2e-8 bar; HV-329606 ten points shut, the shell falls to 0.255 bar a (324F005's map pulls
more on less motive) and after ten minutes stage 2 sits at 0.13012 bar a (with V1's tear and fixed shell, 0.130125).
The train alone, thirty seconds without the water and then the water back: the shell 1.0 bar a, its
cold end at the vapour's 104 C; 0.369 bar a twenty seconds after, 0.3001 in a minute, 0.3 within 1e-6
in two and a half.

## LII.4 Finding B-67 — 324E007's vent on a near-zero design ammonia back-pressure

`vacuum_condenser.vent_moles` (V1's, §XLVII) puts each condenser's NH3 and CO2 vent on the PFD vent's
partial pressure times the ratio of the condensate's Extended UNIQUAC back-pressure to its design
value, the condensate at the inlet's condensable composition. The design back-pressures against the
PFD's partial pressures:

| condenser | p*_NH3,des [Pa] | PFD p_NH3 [Pa] | p*_CO2,des [Pa] | PFD p_CO2 [Pa] |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 324E002 | 5468 | 5910 | 836 | 1257 |
| 324E005 | 3841 | 3385 | 2496 | 1780 |
| 324E006 | 2761 | 3489 | 5663 | 5166 |
| 324E007 | 24 | 1660 | 2.28e6 | 14330 |

324E007's design condensate holds more CO2 than its ammonia binds: its free ammonia's back-pressure
is 24 Pa, so the ratio multiplies any rise by 68. Late in a 323P003 trip its condensate loses its CO2
(0.027 kmol/h against 0.254), the free ammonia's back-pressure rises toward a dilute solution's, the
anchored partial pressure toward 0.7 bar, the vent's condensable fraction to its cap: 324E007 vents
its whole inlet, its cold end at the water's 30 C, 722 at 214 kg/h for two minutes where the PFD has
31. Measured remedy: the departures additive, p_k = Y_des s_k P_des + (p*_k - p*_k,des), floored at
zero — exact at design; 324E007 condenses 183-191 kg/h through the trip, 722 23.8-34.1 kg/h. The
process engineer's (handoff B-67).

## LIII.2 What V1 models

``steam_system.step_steam``, once a tick after the synthesis loop:

* **Four levels.** The 25 bar a battery limit held; 329D005 (``P_MP``, 19.7), 329D009 (``P_9``, 9.0)
  and 322D001A/B (``P_LP``, 5.01325 bar a — 4.0 bar g) as lumped saturated vapour capacitances,
  C = V_vap . d(rho_g,sat)/dP on the drums' as-built volumes (V1 read 322D001's 3470 mm, NLL 1050 mm
  and 62 m3, 329D005's 13.8 m3 and 329D009's 8 m3 from the vendor drawings), each stepped
  semi-implicitly on its valves' conductance.
* **The valves.** ISA-75.01 compressible steam flow anchored on each valve's design node pressures
  (``_valve_flow``): PV-329204 and PV-329205A seeded at 50 % on their design flows (902 on V1's
  39 400 kW / 1850 kJ/kg = 76.7 t/h, 903); PV-329205B, PV-329207C and HV-329602 on K = 2.0
  (kg/s)/sqrt(bar), PV-329207A on 3.0, HV-329601 on PV-329204's K — numbers no document gives;
  PV-329207B anchored at 50 % on 932's 16 707 kg/h to 3.9 bar a.
* **The controllers.** PIC-329204 PI about its seed (1.8 %/bar, 0.018 %/(bar s)); PIC-329205's split
  range, proportional only (40 %/bar, a 0.02 bar dead band); the PIC-329207A/B/C trio on a master set
  point (A at +0.1 bar, C at -0.1), retuned by V1 to 24 %/bar and 0.28 %/(bar s); the level loops
  LIC-329502/503/504 velocity PI (2.5, 90 s) on linear valves (no datasheet found), LV-329504 fed
  from a held 9 bar a boundary (329P001A/B are not modelled).
* **The users.** The stripper's MP draw is live (39 400 kW x its duty ratio / 1850); 322E002's LP
  raising is live; 324E003's 9-bar draw is live, the rest of 907 a constant; every other LP user is
  one constant, ``M_USERS_LP`` = the design raising less the turbine's export, set at boot.
* **The closures.** The 9 -> 4 letdown adds desuperheating water m_ld (h_g,9 - h_g,4) / (h_g,4 - 419);
  329D009's vapour gains a design-anchored 275 kg/h of "saturation water" in proportion to 903; the
  LP header is floored at 3.5 bar a (``P_LP_MIN_BARA``, "the site LP main tie-in"). The level loops
  do not write the pressures, and none of the waters above leaves a drum's liquid.

The plant reads three things from it: Tsat(P_MP) for 322E001's shell, Tsat(P_LP) for 322E002's
shell, and the headers lagged into 323E002, 323E010, 324E001 (LP) and 324E003 (9-bar) — the inputs
the ported units already take as arguments (`stripper_322e001(t_steam_c)`,
`carbamate_condenser_322e002(t_shell_c)`, the chests' ``p_lp_bara`` / ``p_mp_bara``).

# Part LIV — The condensers' vent departure (B-67) and the steam network ported (unit 329)

Session 37, 2026-10-02. The process engineer decided B-67 (option a, the additive departure), B-68
(every simulated user live on its header, the rest at their PFD rows), B-69 (the LP header at the
plant's 4.0 bar g) and B-70 (the strict mass-balance corrections: the drums' own water, the
blowdown, no floor), and authorised the steam system's port.

## LIV.1 B-67: the condensers' NH3 and CO2 vent on additive departures

`vacuum_condenser.vent_moles` now writes the condensate's back-pressure as a departure added to
the PFD vent's partial pressure, not multiplied into it:

    p_k = max(Y_des s_k P_des + (p*_k(w_cond, T_v) - p*_k(w_cond,des, T_v,des)), 0)    k = NH3, CO2
    rel_k = p_k / P = max(Y_des s_k (P_des / P) + (p*_k - p*_k,des) / (1e5 P), 0)

written in the second form so that at the design back-pressure the departure is a literal zero and
the relative partial pressure is V1's expression to the bit. Every condenser's anchored vent is its
PFD row at design on either law; the design solves' cold ends move in their last bits (324E007's by
3e-9 K, its model vent at design by 6e-7 kg/h), so the train's design rows hold to 1e-8 kg/h
(722 and 759 at 2.5e-9) where they held to 1e-9.

**Proof.** V1's own module runs with the switch: `tests/equivalence/b67_switch.py` loads a second,
private copy of V1's ``vacuum_condenser.py`` and replaces its ``vent_moles`` with V1's function
transcribed with that one change; V1's ``solve``, ``_q_balance`` and ``vent_kgh_at`` reach it through
their module globals, and V1's four specs are lifted from ``main.py`` on that copy. The condenser,
the condenser node, both stages ("B-67", a ninth switch on stage 1 and a tenth on stage 2) and
the train are ``==`` the switched V1 everywhere. Both ways (`test_vacuum_condenser_decided_equivalence.py`):

| | V1's ratio (executed) | the port |
|---|---|---|
| 324E007, inlet CO2 at a tenth (0.027 kmol/h, as two minutes into a 323P003 trip) | vents 210.64 of 210.82 kg/h, condenses nothing, cold end 30.0 C | vents 24.55 kg/h, condenses 186.25, 54.76 C |
| the train two minutes into the trip (stages at 0.306 / 0.080 bar a) | 722 = 217.0 kg/h, 324E007 at 30.0 C | 722 = 30.2 kg/h, 54.1 C |
| inlet CO2 one per cent below / above design | 30.76 / 31.25 kg/h | 23.81 / 37.51 kg/h |

**Re-pinned** (the port's numbers move where a condensate's back-pressure leaves its design): the
cascade of B-66 — 324E006's shell at 1.0 bar a in 2.2 s (2.4 before), 324E007 sending 1125 kg/h to
atmosphere (1185), stage 2 at 0.2587 bar a; HV-329606 ten points down — stage 2 at 0.13007 bar a,
324E006's shell 0.2534, 722 22.7 kg/h; the 323P003 trip — stage 2's boil-off 110 / 1121 / 1280 kg/h
at 2 s / 30 s / 60 s, 722 never above the PFD's 31.0 kg/h (49.1 under the ratio); B-65's V1 side,
with the switch, 342 pulses and 8.3 t/h to atmosphere.

**Found building it (handoff B-71).** The additive form has the ratio's hazard mirrored. At 324E007's
design the condensate, at the inlet's condensable composition, carries more CO2 than its ammonia
binds: its CO2 back-pressure is 22.8 bar against the PFD vent's 0.143 bar of CO2, so a departure in
it is 159 times the vent's own scale. One per cent of inlet CO2 either way swings the CO2 vent
between nothing (floored) and the whole inlet (table above); HIC-329606 ten points down takes 722 to
74.1 kg/h and 324E007's cold end to 36.8 C. A per-species slope min(1, p_k,des / p*_k,des) — the
ratio where the design back-pressure exceeds the PFD's partial pressure, the addition where it is
below — was measured in scratch: 324E007 30.74 / 31.27 kg/h at -1 / +1 % CO2; the trip 24.5-31.9
kg/h; HIC-329606 -10 23.6-32.8 kg/h. It is V1's ratio on 324E005 (both back-pressures above their
partial pressures) and the addition on 324E002. Not built.

## LIV.3 What the port runs

`ureasim/units/steam/` (`drums`, `steam_valves`, `header_control`, `steam_network`) on
`data/unit_329.py`, `data/unit_329_network.py` and `thermo/water_steam.py`. Each tick, in V1's order:

* **The vapour nodes**: C = V_vap d(rho_g,sat)/dP on V1's vapour spaces (329D005 6.9 m3, 3.388 kg/bar;
  329D009 4.0 m3, 1.969; 322D001A/B 91.3 m3, 45.92), each stepped semi-implicitly, P' = P + r dt /
  (C + g dt), g = -dr/dP over a 1e-3 bar perturbation (at least 0) — the three in turn, as V1 does,
  so the LP step's conductance reads 329D009's new pressure. No floor but zero (B-70).
* **The waters (B-70)**: 902's superheat boils 329D005's water; ds_9 comes out of 329D009's; 960's
  (9-bar saturated steam let down, h_g(P_9)) and 963's (h(312 C, 4.4 bar a)) boil 322D001's; 913
  flashes into the LP vapour, x = (h_f(P_9) - h_f(P_LP)) / h_fg(P_LP), 959 leaves 322D001's water.
  LV-329503 and LV-329504 run at the tick's starting pressures so 913's flash enters the LP balance on
  the tick it crosses (V1 runs them after the pressure step).
* **The drums (decisions 33, 11)**: each drum's water a mass over its vessel with 2:1 heads —
  horizontal V(h) = L [R^2 acos((R-h)/R) - (R-h) sqrt(h(2R-h))] + pi h^2 (3R-h)/6; vertical, two
  drums, heads of depth D/4 — the level read between its taps (329D005 +-750 mm about its axis,
  329D009 +-375 mm, both from their as-built GAs; 322D001 300 and 1800 mm above its bottom tangent
  line), its height by bisection to the last bit. A drum's outflows are scaled so it keeps a 1 kg
  heel; a full drum's excess is published as an overflow. V1 integrates each level on a constant
  mass per per cent and clamps it.
* **The valves**: the butterflies on V1's anchored ISA-75.01 law (`steam_valve_kgs` == V1
  ``_valve_flow``); PV-329205A / B and LV-329502 / 503 / 504 on Flowserve's trims (decision 23), the
  two letdowns handed their saturated condensate's pressure as its vapour pressure (decision 31), so
  LV-329502 passes 57 989 kg/h whether 329D009 is at 9 or 5 bar a.
* **The controllers**: PIC-329204 PI about its seed (4.5 %/bar, Ti 100 s, the table on PT-329204's 40
  bar span; integral authority +-50 %); trip 21.2 loads 10 bar g into its set point for 2 s; HV-329601
  forced open above 12 bar g with the trip active and shut for 3 s below it, the operator blocked
  while forced (Uhde's sheet 3); PIC-329205's split range about PV-329205A's 19.55 % (40 %/bar, V1's,
  no row); the PIC-329207 trio on its master, A at +0.1 bar (100 %/bar, Ti 150 s), B on it about its
  50 % bias (66.7 %/bar, 150 s), C at -0.1 (66.7 %/bar, 200 s); LIC-329502 (V1's 2.5 / 90 s, no row),
  LIC-329503 (2.00 / 200 s), LIC-329504 (2.50 / 500 s), velocity PI.
* **The safety valves (decision 32)**: SV32951, SV32952 and the four SV32978-81 as `GasReliefValve`s,
  their orifices back-solved from Sempell's certified capacities at the relieving pressure, the steam
  at the sheet's temperature on the saturated-vapour line (Z 0.871, 0.920, 0.944).

At design every node and every drum balances to 1e-10 kg/h and the headers stay at their design
pressures to the bit for an hour; 0.46 ms a tick.

## LIV.6 Measured and not built; found

* **PV-329207A's and C's 3 % cut-off** (sheet 5) — wired, PV-329207C chattered shut and open on
  alternate ticks (0 and 970 kg/h, +-0.0004 bar) as its controller settled near 3 %; not wired, the
  decided classes' "once measured stable" (handoff B-72).
* **Trip 21.2's forcing of HV-329601** — wired (decision 39: an interlock as Uhde draws it); near 12
  bar g it relays open for a tick and shut for three to six, 214 changes over 110 s, until PIC-329204
  has shut the supply (B-72). The port's valves stroke instantly; no actuator times are modelled.

  (79 t/h) and the PFD's 65.9 t/h; the header sees the PFD's basis, the model is V1's (B-74).

# Part LV — The vent's ratio where its design back-pressure is above (B-71), the steam users on their valves (B-73), and the scheduler (Phase 5)

Session 38, 2026-10-02. The process engineer decided B-71 (the blended vent law: V1's ratio where the
design back-pressure exceeds the PFD's partial pressure, B-67's addition where it is below), B-72
and B-74 (Phase 7 Calibration Deferrals: the instant valves' relays and 322E002's duty stay as
built), and B-73 (the Typo Rule: the motive steam, 328C004's stripping steam and XV-322915's flood on
physical valve equations governed by their headers' live pressures), and authorised Phase 5's
scheduler. The plant started at 100 % load is to hold its LP header at the operators' 4.0 bar g.

## LV.1 B-71: V1's ratio where the design back-pressure is above the PFD's partial pressure

`vacuum_condenser.vent_moles` now decides per species, at design, which form the condensate's
back-pressure takes:

    p_k = max(Y_des s_k P_des + (p*_k(w_cond, T_v) - p*_k,des), 0)    p*_k,des <= Y_des s_k P_des
    p_k = Y_des s_k P_des . p*_k(w_cond, T_v) / p*_k,des               p*_k,des >  Y_des s_k P_des

the second V1's own expression, operand for operand, so a species on the ratio is V1's to the bit.
Both forms are exact at design. The rule falls at the four condensers' designs as:

| condenser | NH3: p*_des / PFD partial pressure | form | CO2: p*_des / PFD partial pressure | form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 324E002 | 5468 / 5910 Pa (0.925) | addition | 836 / 1257 Pa (0.665) | addition |
| 324E005 | 3841 / 3385 Pa (1.13) | V1's ratio | 2496 / 1780 Pa (1.40) | V1's ratio |
| 324E006 | 2761 / 3489 Pa (0.791) | addition | 5663 / 5166 Pa (1.10) | V1's ratio |
| 324E007 | 24 / 1660 Pa (0.015) | addition | 2.28e6 / 1.43e4 Pa (159) | V1's ratio |

**Proof.** The switched V1 module (`tests/equivalence/b67_switch.py`) now transcribes V1's
``vent_moles`` with both decisions; every condenser, node, stage and train equivalence is ``==`` on
it. 324E005, both species on the ratio, is ``==`` V1's unswitched module on every inlet (NH3 and
CO2 at half to one and a half times design), the switch the identity on stage 2. Both ways
(`test_vacuum_condenser_decided_equivalence.py`, V1 unswitched):

| | V1's ratio | B-67's addition (session 37) | the port (B-71) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 324E007, inlet CO2 1 % below / above | 30.76 / 31.25 kg/h | 23.81 / 37.51 | 30.74 / 31.27 |
| 324E007, inlet CO2 at a tenth | 210.64 kg/h, nothing condensed, 30.0 C | 24.55, 54.76 C | 24.55, 186.25 condensed, 54.76 C |
| the train two minutes into a 323P003 trip (stages 0.306 / 0.084 bar a) | 722 = 135.9 kg/h, 324E007 at 32.1 C | — | 722 = 29.1 kg/h, 54.0 C |
| 324E002, inlet NH3 at half | 1113.7 kg/h | — | 210.5 kg/h |

## LV.2 B-73: the steam users on their valves, against their headers' live pressures

**The motive steam** (`vacuum_train.motive_ratio`, `motive_steam`). HV-329605 and HV-329606 keep their
Flowserve trims from the strokes that pass the PFD's motive (69.06 and 80.16 %), between the LP header
and the nozzles they feed; a choked nozzle passes a flow in proportion to its pressure, so the outlet
is where the valve's flow and the nozzle's agree:

    m = m_des . Phi(h, P_LP, P_n) / Phi(h_des, P_LP,des, P_n,des),    P_n = P_n,des . m / m_des
    Phi = f(h) P1 Y sqrt(x M / T1),  x = min(dP / P1, F_gamma xT),  T1 = T_sat(P_LP)

solved by bisection on [0, m_des P_LP / P_n,des] until the bracket stops shrinking (0.08 ms a call);
P_LP,des = 5.01325 bar a (B-69), P_n,des = 4.1 bar a (every ejector duty prints it), xT Flowserve's
on the normal cases (0.7828, 0.7028). At the design stroke on the design header the residual at the

## LV.3 The scheduler (``project.md`` §3.6, built)

**`engine/schedule.py`.** A `Schedule` is the units' `Step`s in order, the `DeclaredTear`s and the
tear writes. Each step's wiring names the source of every argument: ``Result(unit, field)`` an
earlier step's output this tick; ``State(unit, field)`` a unit's state as it stands when the reader
steps — an earlier unit's after its step, a later unit's as it left the tick before; ``Tear(name)``
a `TearState` field; ``Operator(tag)``; ``Boundary(name)``. A field is a dotted path through
attributes and mapping keys (`lookup`). `Schedule.validate` refuses: a unit scheduled twice; a
``Result`` of a step not yet run; a ``State`` of the reader itself or of an unscheduled unit; a later
unit's ``State`` or a ``Tear`` with no declared tear; a declared tear nothing reads; a tear read with
no writer, written by an unscheduled unit or written and never read. It then builds the flowsheet
from the wiring (`core.flowsheet`): every read an edge, every declared read a cut. The flowsheet must
order (`evaluation_order`, which refuses an uncut recycle), and every uncut edge must run forward in
the schedule — V1's order is proved a topological order of the plant's torn graph.

**`engine/scheduler.py`.** `Scheduler.tick` resolves each step's wiring at the moment the step runs,
runs it, counts it, and after the last step refuses a tick in which a unit did not step exactly once;
then writes the tears from the producers' results and advances the clock (`PlantState.end_tick`). A
tick of any step but 0.1 s is refused (A-14). `PlantState` now holds the units, their controllers,
the operator's positions and the boundary values beside the clock and the tears.

**`engine/plant/`.** The plant's schedule, one module per plant section, in V1's ``step_sim`` order:

| V1 section | step | reads from the tick before |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 329, the steam network | every user's draw on its PFD row (B-68), 328C003's 911 |
| 7, 9, 11, 13 | 323C003, 323F004, 323F010, 323D002 | 323F004, 323D001, 323E011, 323F010 and 324E002's pressures; LV-324501B's recycle |
| 14-20 | 323C005, 328D003, 328E007, 328C002, 328C003, 328C004, 328D001 | 702, 756, 708, 324E002's inerts, 322C001's temperature; 719 / 720 / 721 / 759, 741; 739 and 328C004's temperature; 748, 750 and their vapours, 775, the hydrolyser's and 328D001's pressures; 328C004's pressure; 718A, 323E011's pressure |
| 22 | 322E006, 322C001 | XV-322915 as I 22.1 left it |
| 23, 24 | 323E003, 323E011 | 718B, 323E011's pressure |
| 26, 29, 31 | HV-329605/6, 324E001, 324E003, the vacuum train | the lagged cold ends, 324E006's shell |
| (new) | the steam users' meter | — |
| 35 | the trips: I 22.1 | — |

22 steps, 39 declared one-tick reads each with its reason, 20 tear writes: V1's eight cross-unit
recycles and the other cross-tick flows `TearState` now names (unit 324's condensates and 324E002's
vent inerts, 328C004's 741, LV-324501B's recycle, the steam users' draws, 911), each seeded on its
design. The meter turns each user's live draw into the header's view (decision 47's class): the
chests' duty ratios on their PFD rows (918, 919, 926, 920), the motive steam, 931 and the flood as
they pass. The synthesis loop's outputs are boundary values at their design (`plant/boundary.py`):
322E001's bottoms (PFD 208 at 119 and 172 C), LV-322501 sealed, HV-322604's design purge, the
stripper's and the HPCC's steam on the network's closure, trip 21.2 clear.

**Proofs.** (1) The refusals, each on a toy schedule (`tests/engine/test_schedule.py`); the plant's
schedule validates, its 22 units once each, its uncut edges forward, and with its cuts removed its
flowsheet does not order — the recycles are real; 323F004 moved ahead of 323C003 is refused. (2) The
liquor train through the scheduler (`tests/equivalence/test_scheduler_equivalence.py`): 323C003 to
323D002 on their plant wiring, the chained test's other inputs as boundary values, ``==`` V1's stages
1 to 4 on every field of every tick for 500 ticks through a 15 % cut of the stripper's bottoms. (3)
On a toy schedule a ``Result`` arrives the same tick, a later unit's ``State`` and a ``Tear`` exactly
one tick late, the tear's seed on the first; on the plant every tear holds its producer's output at
each commit (`tests/engine/test_scheduler.py`). (4) The design over the assembled plant: started on
its design seed at 100 % load the plant holds its LP header at 5.01325 bar a within 2.4e-5 bar over a
minute, every user within 0.02 % of its PFD row; over an hour nothing runs away, the largest drifts
323F010's holdup +10.2 kg (0.16 %), 323C005's temperature -0.08 C, 328D003's compartment III -6 kg
of 212 784, every pressure within 7e-4 bar (the hydrolyser's, of 16.8 bar a, the largest). They are where the ported units' design points meet their
neighbours' to a few parts in 10^5: stage 1's held melt boils 1.6 kg/h (B-62), so 324E002's condensate
leaves at 26 767.5 kg/h on the first tick against 328D003's 26 768.

**A tick costs 10 ms** (unit 324's stage 1 and vacuum train two thirds of it): SLOW runs in real time
with a tenth of a core; FAST's 60 times needs 600 ticks a second and gets about 100 (handoff A-18).

**Closed: handoff A-10.** The schedule reads every recycle tear from the plant state — 702, 756, 708
into 323C005, 718A into 328D001, 718B into 323E003, 739 into 328E007, 748 and 750 into 328C002 — and the
assembled plant runs on it.

# Part LVI — The LP header downstream of 322D001A/B, and the synthesis loop scheduled (Phase 5)

Session 39, 2026-10-02. The process engineer noted that the 4 bar g LP steam network sits downstream
of 322D001A/B and asked that the dependency be explicit in the steam network's wiring and here, the
port corrected if the linkage had been abstracted or routed wrongly; added mid-session that
322D001A/B's water is boiled in 322E002's shell. The engineer authorised the synthesis loop's engine
glue — V1's ``step_sim`` sections 1 to 6, 34, 36 and 37's loop pressure — and asked that any
unphysical mass or energy sink in the loop-pressure integration be flagged immediately, with
attention to V1's recycle lags and to 322E003.

## LVI.1 The LP header downstream of 322D001A/B

**What the documents draw.** PFD 26 (UD-VT-329-FB-0001, the scanned flow diagram, read from the
image): 322D001A/B's water runs to 322E002's shell and returns as steam and water (the thermosyphon,
"39.63" MW on the drawing); the drums' tops leave as one line, "147 C; 4.5 BAR", which becomes
stream 917 and the LP header; 960, PV-329205B's letdown from the 9-bar header ("175 C, 9 BAR"),
joins that header downstream of the drums; 963 (PV-329207C) enters 322D001B, 915 / 914 (913's flash)
and 916 (LV-329504's make-up) enter 322D001A; 959 blows the drums down. P&ID 107/1
(UD-VT-329-FB-0006, read from the scan): each drum's top nozzle N3 (DN 500) joins the DN 700 header
700-STLS1-329353; PI-329206 sits on 322D001A's top, SV32978/79 and SV32980/81 on the two drums' tops;
PT-329207 (PI-329207, PY1-329207 to PIC-329207A/B/C) sits on the header itself; PV-329207A vents and
PV-329207B exports (FI-329407, to 320MT02) from the header. The 329-1 mapping agrees: "Steam
discharge to 4bar steam header with 2 pressure indicators PI-329206 and PI-329207".

**What the port had.** One vapour node for the drums and the header together: 322D001A/B's 91.3 m3
of steam space as the header's capacitance, the drums' certified safety valves, PIC-329207's trio
reading it, every LP user drawing on it; 322E002's raising out of 322D001's water into it, and its
shell boiling at its saturation. The lumping is the documents' own: the PFD prints 917 at 4.4 bar a,
PT-329207's loop summary its normal at 4.4 bar a, and no document gives the line's volume or a drop
between the drums and the header. Two things were abstracted: stream 917 was not published — the
header's users were subtracted from the drums' steam directly — and 960 was routed into the drums:
its superheat boiled 322D001's water (B-70's class, "a superheated steam inlet boiling its drum's own
water"), which no drawing supports, since 960 never reaches a drum.

**The patch** (`units/steam/steam_network.py`; the transcription's switch "917"). The drums' balance
is written on their discharge,

    m_917 = users_LP + PV-329207A + PV-329207B - m_960
    dP_LP/dt . C = raise + m_963 + ds_963 + m_915 - m_917,

so the header holds nothing of its own and the drums feed it; 960 joins the header past the drums and
its superheat leaves with the header's steam; 963's still boils the drums' water. ``SteamNetwork``
publishes ``flows_kgh["917"]`` and the drums' saturations ``t_hp_c`` / ``t_lp_c`` as properties: the
scheduler hands 322E002's shell 322D001A/B's saturation of the tick before, and 322E002's raising of
this tick enters the drums (`engine.plant.synthesis`, `engine.plant.steam`).

**Measured.** At design 917 = 68 929 kg/h, PFD 917's 68 928, and nothing else moves (960 is shut).
324E003 lost, PV-329205B letting 4658 kg/h down: B-70's build boils 70.4 kg/h of 322D001's water on
960's superheat, the header 5.13219 bar a and 322D001 at 50.1292 % after 30 s; the port boils none,
5.13168 bar a and 50.1311 %, the drums discharging 70 240 kg/h. Both ways in
`test_steam_network_decided_equivalence.py`.

## LVI.2 The synthesis loop's engine glue

**The boot pin** (`data/synthesis_pin.py`). Six of the loop's anchors are what V1's assembled loop
does at its own design seed, back-solved at start-up (``_pin_hpcc_ua``: 18 000 ticks in cascade, a
manual-seed capture, the recycle tear and the kinetics re-solved against the PFD's extents) and cached
in ``backend/.boot_pin_cache.json`` under a SHA-256 of V1's model sources. The cache's key is the hash
of V1's present source (V1's own file list, V1's own key function), so the cache is what V1 boots on;
the port carries its values verbatim (§4: values V1 itself back-solved): 322E002's UA (equal to the
import-time back-solve), its seed liquid make 189 257.547 kg/h, the melt's N/C 3.07858, the raising
29.5197 kg/s; 322R001's recycle tear (2107.45 kg/h at design, NH3 +129.1 kmol/h), its seed feed N/C
3.072961, the design per-pass conversion 0.541822, the kinetics re-solved on the live feed (A2
4.4195e12, +1.5 %; the biuret pre-exponential 3.6076e6, +14.6 %; the reference temperature
450.110 K, 2.7 K below the import-time one), the anchor's column state. The node profile and the
melt's c_p the pin restores are the import-time fixed point's, to the bit.

## LVI.4 The loop's flagged sinks (handoffs B-75 to B-78)

Ported as V1 writes them; flagged, measured on the assembled plant, and sent to the process engineer.

**B-75, the residual credit and the recycle tear.** The boundary PT-329201 integrates leaves a
constant +2024.9 kg/h at the seed (the motive's re-pin over PFD 116 has no exit); V1 subtracts it
again scaled by the loop-mass fraction. Its mirror is the boot pin's recycle tear, 2107.5 kg/h,
deleted from the reactor's feed in proportion to the CO2 load ratio. Without the credit PT-329201
climbs 1.07 bar in 2750 s (+1.35 bar an hour). At 80 % CO2 the tear falls to 0.8 and the credit does
not: 405 kg/h, 0.27 bar an hour; scaling the credit by the same ratio moves PT-329201 by 0.12 bar in
30 minutes — small beside what the turndown itself does (below).

**B-76, the backlog recondenses into no liquid.** 329P006A stopped five minutes: the uncondensed
backlog peaks at 1569 kg; in the 35 minutes after the water returns, 1583 kg recondense and reach no
inventory. 322E003's sump fell from 3837 to 2940 kg; the reactor's holdup ends 1090 kg low; PT-329201
is 0.39 bar above design at 40 minutes.

**B-77, one capacity counts the holdups twice.** HV-322605 to 45 %: in 20 minutes the reactor's
holdup gains 11 089 kg and PT-329201 rises 5.46 bar (8183 kg on 1500 kg/bar) — the starved stripper
drains less, and the same mass is liquid in 322R001 and pressure on the node.

**B-78, the inventories.** (1) 322E003's full sump: at 80 % CO2 the motive puts 322F001 near its stall
(B-12); its sump is full within ten minutes and loses 14.5 t of carbamate in 30 minutes (about 28 t/h)
while PT-329201 climbs 6 bar, on V1's lines and the port's alike. 321P002B stopped: not measured — a tick costs up to 26 s once
HV-322604's purge condenses (A-18). (2) The forward-carbamate
pulse: HV-322602 74 to 60 % adds 2500 kg to the reactor in 30 minutes that leaves no inventory. (3)
The overflow's mushy throttle deletes what it holds back below 65 C; not reached in any scenario
measured. (4) The production surge's 5 min recycle lag holds mass in no inventory.

**A lost motive stalls the tick (handoff A-18).** 321P002B stopped by hand: 322F001 entrains nothing,
322E003's vent turns ammonia-rich and HV-322604's purge condenses in its line (B-19). The condensing
letdown's dew search walks down from the inlet temperature, each step a Newton whose every evaluation
interpolates the Extended UNIQUAC speciation grid, tabulated node by node on first use at about 30 ms;
the purge's composition moves every tick, the letdown's cache misses, and the search walks into
untabulated nodes. Measured: 0.76 s for the tick of the stop, 1.5 s four ticks later, 26 s fifteen
ticks later (profile: 78 % in the letdown's speciation, 19 % in the vacuum train's). The grid holds
about 450 000 nodes. Nothing in the physics changes the answer; the remedies are A-18's.

Session 40, 2026-10-03. The process engineer decided the synthesis loop's flagged sinks — B-75 (b),
