against V1's 2024.91, 1e-4 bar an hour. The CO2 demand cut to 80 %: s settles at 0.8015, the credit
at 1623.0 kg/h; after two minutes PT-329201 reads 140.6989 bar a on V1's credit and 140.7072 on the
port's.

ends at 3634.21.

(V1 deletes it); a minute after XV-322903 reopens 226.25 kg are still held and the sump is still

## LVII.2 The motive-loss stall (handoff A-18)

**The cause, measured.** HV-322604's letdown arguments were captured through a 900 s motive loss
on the assembled plant and replayed through the flash. A lost motive turns 322E003's vent
CO2-rich and almost dry — 2 to 69 % CO2, 0.08 to 0.26 % water (session 39 wrote "ammonia-rich";
it is not). Such a gas needs a liquor holding its water at a_H2O near 0.1; its incipient liquor
leaves the model's range (1000 mol/kg water) before it gets there, and no isothermal flash
converges. The solve did not stop: four to fifteen failing Newtons at every temperature of the
bracket and of the regula falsi, 50 000 to 100 000 liquid-state evaluations a call — 0.5 to 1.3 s
with every node already tabulated — each new region tabulating hundreds of nodes at 20 ms, the
liquor's heats on V1's grid at three speciations a node, and the answers flagged non-converged (an
outlet up to 11 K over the single-phase answer on almost no liquor).

**The fix**, three parts, no converged answer moved:

1. *The flash stops at the first isothermal flash with no answer* (`condensing_letdown`, method
   step 4): the outlet is the single-phase answer flagged not converged, as it was when the walk
   bracketed no root. 42 cooling-loss cases — seven cooling fractions, six outlet pressures, every
   one converged — are unchanged to the bit; a call on the lost-motive vent costs 3000 to 6000
   evaluations, 30 to 50 ms.
2. *The liquor's heats of absorption on the liquid-state grid*
   (`ammonia_backpressure.liquor_heat_of_absorption_j_mol`): one speciation gives both grids'
   pressures at a node, so the heats are V1's to the bit, at a third of the cost.
3. *The node stores* (`thermo.node_store`; `ammonia_backpressure.build_state_store`,
   `build_back_store`; ``tools/build_liquid_state_store.py``): the liquid-state grid and V1's
   back-pressure grid tabulated ahead of time over the whole block a liquor up to 1000 mol/kg reads
   at 10 to 100 C — 460 460 nodes each (65 x 77 x 92), on every core (31 and 86 minutes on eighteen worker processes here) — and kept beside
   the module (`.liquid_state_grid.bin` 11.1 MB, `.back_pressure_grid.bin` 14.7 MB), each keyed on the SHA-256 of the property modules, its node function's
   source and the grid's spacing. A node is served from its store, the doubles the lazy path
   computes written and read back bit for bit; no node failed; a missing or stale store is never an
   error, only slow. The stores also serve V1's grid where the lost motive stalled it next:
   322C001's start-up calibration (5 s on the first tick) and the vacuum train's back condensers
   (2.4 s ticks at 896 s), whose condensates wander into untabulated nodes.

**Measured on the assembled plant**, 321P002B stopped by hand, 15 minutes:

| | mean tick | worst tick | ticks over 100 ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| session 39 | — | 0.76 s on the stop, 26 s fifteen ticks later, rising (the run was abandoned) | — |
| the letdown fixed, the liquid-state store | 23.6 ms | 5.0 s (tick 0), 2.4 s (896 s) | 87 |
| both stores | 20.4 ms | 1.03 s (tick 0, start-up), then 0.18 s | 11 — ten after start-up, at most 0.18 s |

Fifteen minutes of the lost motive run in 184 s of wall time, 4.9 times faster than the plant clock, measured with the full test suite running beside it on the same machine. The simulator pays the plant clock in passes of up to half a second (handoff A-14), so the ten ticks of 103 to 179 ms are caught up within their pass: the plant keeps real time throughout. The first tick costs 1.03 s once, at start-up — the two stores read and their keys hashed, 322C001's design-pin calibration — before any exercise begins. From the eighth minute the plant ticks in 9 to 10 ms, as at design.

## LVII.4 Exercise snapshots (`engine/snapshot.py`)

The whole `PlantState` written as JSON and restored so the restored plant replays bit for bit:
floats as their shortest round-tripping decimals (non-finite ones tagged), tuples, mapping proxies,
sets, deques (a transit line's queue, with its bound) and non-text-keyed mappings tagged; an object
of a ``ureasim`` class as its class and attributes, rebuilt without its constructor; an object
reached twice written once. Only ``ureasim`` classes are named or rebuilt. On load the plant's shape
— its units, controllers and every attribute both sides hold — is checked against a freshly built
plant and a snapshot from a different model is refused with the first difference. Saved 30 s into
a transient (HV-322605 at 45 %, 329P006A stopped), the restored plant runs the next 300 ticks equal
to the saved one in every published value, through the text and through a file, with the
letdown's cache cleared (`tests/engine/test_snapshot.py`). The rewrite's: V1 had no exercise save.

## LVIII.1 V1's section 6, scheduled (`units/synthesis/indicators.py`)

V1 relaxes ten published indications every physics step:

    y_k = y_(k-1) + dt / (tau + dt) . (x_k - y_(k-1)),       y_0 = x_0

on TT-322012 (322F001's discharge, tau 120 s), TT-322013 (322E001's top gas, 180 s), TT-323001
(downstream of LV-322501, 180 s), TT-322010 (322E002's product, 240 s), PI-322E002 (the bubble
point, 30 s, capped at the feeds' 144.2 bar a), TT-322002 (322E003's overflow, 180 s), TT-322011
either side of HV-322604 (120 s), TT-329125 (the tempered water's return, 25 s) and AT-322701 (the
reactor overflow's N/C on an atom basis, 40 s). TT-322004's lag is 322E001's sump's (§XXVIII). The
implicit-Euler weight is not additive over steps, so a lag advanced once per console publish — six
plant seconds at FAST — would not be V1's indicator: the lags are a scheduled step, ``322-DISPLAY``,
after HV-322604 (V1's section 6 after section 5), reading only this tick's results. Its store is in
the plant state, saved with an exercise. Proven: the ten lines transcribed beside V1's lifted
``_lag1``, ``react_nc_ratio``, time constants and cap, fed 3100 ticks of hold, step and ramp, every
indicator ``==`` on every tick, the cap binding through the step
(`tests/equivalence/test_indicators_equivalence.py`).

## LVIII.2 The console packet (`engine/packet/`)

V1's push task sends every browser its ``step_sim`` return value with a ``_health`` block stapled on;
the screens bind into it by dot-path, the trend window resolves its pens through the same paths, the
stream inspector reads its ``STREAMS``. `build_packet` publishes that dictionary from the port's
plant — results, unit objects, loops, the operator's positions and the recycle tears the tick read
(V1's ``m756_prev`` and its kin, ``Scheduler.tears_read``) — one module per V1 block: unit 321's flat
keys, ``pumpA`` / ``pumpB``, ``ratio`` and the SIC faceplates (`unit_321`); the synthesis loop
(`synthesis`); unit 323 (`recirculation`); units 328 and 322C001 (`desorption`); unit 324
(`evaporation`); unit 329 (`steam`, V1's lumped state mapped onto the network's streams, the map in
the module); the stream registry (`streams`); the flags and trips (`status`).

**The rule for a value.** Each key carries the port's equivalent of V1's expression with V1's
rounding; where the port decided a divergence the value is the port's (a level between its taps,
decision 33; TI-322015 where the P&ID draws it, decision 37; the stripper's steam on its PFD row,
decision 52; PT-329201's certified relief under V1's ``SV_32201`` keys, decision 32; FFIC-329401 as
a ratio station, decision 26). V1's display relations are ported with their constants
(`data/console_packet.py`): TT-321002 = TT-321001 - 0.8 (1 - level), PI-321003 = 7.3 phi_fwd, the
discharge header 7.5 + (164 - 7.5) phi_fwd. A few V1 diagnostics are evaluated as V1 evaluates them:
the overhead's free acid CO2 and its pressure-building push, HV-322604's capacity at the tick's
starting pressure, LV-324501's selector closure, PY-324201 / AY-324701 on the stage's refitted
equilibrium. A quantity the port does not model publishes None under V1's key — unit 335's UF85
cascade (its faceplates keep V1's four keys, each None), V1's unit-328 energy ledger.

**Proven against V1's source:** V1's packet is read statically out of ``main.py`` — every key path
to each leaf, a comprehension or a splat standing for the dictionary at its path — and equals the
port's packet's, less V1's five diagnostic blocks (handoff A-19), with no path V1 lacks; every PFD
row and literal the registry uses ``==`` V1's; each block's values tested against the port's results
(`tests/engine/packet/`). Of the 268 paths the screens' overlays bind, 264 resolve and the four
others are unit 335's. A packet costs 2.7 ms and 70 kB of JSON.

## LVIII.3 Faceplates

SIC-323902, 323P001B's standby speed controller, is V1's spare faceplate: MAN at 0 % and offering no
other mode, stepped on its own output each tick (V1's section 33, "stepped for liveness; off the
network"), so its PV shows what the operator sets. It is scheduled as step ``SIC-323902``. FFIC-329401
is a ratio station (decision 26), which the faceplate lookup did not find: ``r323_ctrl_set`` refused
it as "not on this model" where V1 accepted it; the lookup now finds ratio stations, and the station
enters MAN with the slave's set point by hand and AUTO on the ratio it makes.

## LVIII.4 The engine served (`net/engine_host.py`, `engine/session.py`)

V1 steps the plant in ``sim_task`` and pushes in ``push_task`` on one event loop. The host steps the
plant on its own physics thread so the server's event loop does nothing but the network: a pass every
0.1 s pays the wall clock (capped at V1's 0.5 s) to the session in slices of at most 10 ms of wall
time, and drains the command queue between slices, so a command waits at most a slice's steps. The
simulator's owed time is integer nanoseconds, so a pass paid in slices runs exactly the steps one call
runs — proven, 300 steps at FAST, the plants equal to the bit (`tests/net/test_engine_host.py`). Each
command is applied whole between two ticks and its ``(accepted, reason)`` travels back on the future
the server awaits; the ack and the audit event follow, in arrival order. The session publishes the
packet with V1's ``_health`` block (``ok``, ``heartbeat``, ``age_s``, the error and its traceback
while a fault holds, cleared by the next clean pass), the server sends a non-finite value as None,
and the status bar reads the engine's state (running at its pacing, frozen, or faulted). The
historian records the packet — V1's paths, 704 leaves once its composition tables are left out — and
answers ``history`` / ``history_paths`` requests from any role. Measured over a real socket: the
plant keeps real time at SLOW.

## LVIII.5 Arbitration (`data/tags.py`, handoff A-8)

The server enforces the role and the assignment before the engine sees a command; the engine
answers for the process. The resolver must read the field the engine acts on: ``r323_ctrl_set``
carried a fixed row, unit 323, while the engine moves the faceplate its ``id`` names on units 322,
323, 324, 328 and 329 — a trainee assigned 323 could move other sections' faceplates, and a trainee
assigned 328 could not move their own. It is now attributed by its ``id``; ``controller_set`` by
``id`` then ``tag``, the engine's precedence; PIC-329207A / B / C's leg commands carry rows (they
were unattributable, so an assigned station was refused them). A test pins every command type the
engine applies to the section of the instrument it moves. End to end over a socket, a trainee
assigned 323 is refused LIC-328505, FIC-329402 and HIC-322605 with the section named, an observer
everything, a trainee ``freeze``; the instructor is not restricted.

## LVIII.6 B-79 decided, and measured

Option (a): the dry outlet, flagged not converged, and HV-322604's deposition alarm, the solid's
dissociation constant a Phase 7 data gap (handoff Section C). With 321P002B stopped the flash has no
answer for 127 s of the first 142 s, the outlet falling to 1.3 C at 30 s and back to 26 C at 90 s,
the dry purge converging at 55.6 C from 180 s; the deposition alarm (V1's L3-7: below 20 C, or while
the line condenses) fires for 80 s, from the first second to 132 s. §LVII.2's handoff text gave the
threshold as the tracing's 60 C; it is 20 C. The not-converged flag is the flash's own and reaches no
console.

# Part LIX — The relief and overflow routings decided, the faceplates and the instructor's panel (Phase 6)

Session 42 (2026-10-03). The process engineer confirmed B-79 as built (the 20 C alarm and its 80 s
window accepted), decided A-19 (a) — V1's diagnostic blocks stay out of the packet — and A-15 and
A-16 as the strategy pasted in session 41 laid out, asked for the ejector design calculations in
`References\Datasheets` to be checked, and authorised the faceplates and the instructor's panel.

## LIX.1 The stripper's blow-through reaches 323C003, and SV32351 / SV32352 relieve it (handoff A-16)

**What V1 does.** When 322E001's bottom seal is lost, LV-322501 passes HP stripper gas with the
bottoms (`StripperSumpResult.blowthrough_kgh`, the D-20 seal law, §XIX). V1's section 23 hands that
gas to 323E003's gas envelope; 323C003's two-source pressure law (§XXVIII) never sees it, so the
column — whose safety valves are sized on exactly this case ("Failure of LV 322501", 60 t/h of
carbamate gas, Uhde UD-RL-323-EC-0001 / -0002) — cannot reach their 6.01 bar a.

**What the port does (decided 2026-10-03).** The gas enters the column's head space with the
letdown flash and loads the overhead line by its own volume at the head space's state:

$$ Q_{equiv} = Q_{301}\,r_{301} + Q_{302}\,r_{302} + \frac{\dot m_{blow}\,f}{\rho_{blow}(P, T)},
   \qquad \rho_{blow} = \frac{P\,M_{blow}}{R\,T} $$

$$ P_{target} = \sqrt{P_{d001}^2 + (Q_{equiv}/C)^2} $$

$M_{blow}$ the stripper top vapour's live molar mass (`StripperResult.top_mw`), $T$ the column's
temperature. The PFD's own volumes are ideal-gas volumes to 2 % (stream 305: 3.20 kg/m3 printed,
3.14 ideal at 4.1 bar a and 119 C), so the third term is on the law's basis. SV32351 and SV32352,
alike, read PT-323201 at the top of the tick and pop at their set pressure (`core.relief.SafetyValve`):

$$ M_{head} = \frac{\dot m_{305} + \dot m_{blow}}{\dot m_{305}/M_{305} + \dot m_{blow}/M_{blow}}, \qquad
   W = \min\big(2\,W_{API520}(A, P, T, M_{head}),\; \dot m_{305} + \dot m_{blow}\big) $$

each orifice back-solved from Sempell's certified 72 273.6 kg/h at 6.51 bar a (orifice T, gas of
molar mass 25.07, k 1.010, Z 1.00 at 125 C; UD-RL-G00-DZ-0002-001 page 3), $M_{305}$ = 24.92 (PFD
305). The law holds no gas inventory, so a lifted valve passes at most what the head space receives
on the tick; the law reads the gas left, $f = 1 - W/(\dot m_{305} + \dot m_{blow})$ on every source,
and what is left leaves overhead: 323E003 takes $\dot m_{305} f$, the two sources $\times f$ and the
blow-through $\times f$ (`engine/plant/recirc.py`). With no blow-through and the valves shut, $f$
is exactly 1.0 and the added term exactly 0.0: every V1 scenario below 6.01 bar a is V1's to the bit.

**Measured** (`tests/units/recirc/test_rectifying_column.py`): 30 t/h of molar mass 30 against the
design 3.2 bar a downstream settles the column at 5.4715 bar a — below its valves. At 6.05 bar a
with 323D001 at 4.3 bar a the valves lift for four ticks, relieve every kilogram the head space
receives, fall through 5.51 bar a and reseat; shut, the column climbs back in 2.1 s and they lift
again on the 26th tick — the saw-tooth of an oversized valve on half its sizing case.

On the assembled plant (5 s of design, then LIC-322501 in MAN at 100 %): the seal breaks at 115 s
and 29.6 t/h blows through; the column's target rises to 6.05-6.11 bar a and SV32351 / SV32352 lift
20 times between 117 and 175 s, a few ticks each at 48-53 t/h; 323D001 then settles from 4.3 to 3.9
bar a and the column rides at 5.6-5.8 bar a with the valves shut. On V1's routing the same failure
holds the column at 4.6-4.8 bar a and 323D001 at 4.1-4.3.

## LIX.2 The overflows routed (handoff A-15), and 323D011's envelope full

**328D001's overflow into 323E011** (decided 2026-10-03, the process engineer's direction of
2026-09-30). A full drum's overflow (`RefluxDrumResult.m_overflow_kgh`, §XLIII.4) enters 323E011's
shell up the vent line, the same tick (the drum steps in section 20, the condenser in 24). Like the
791 wash it is liquid, not gas load:

$$ \dot m_{in} \mathrel{+}= \dot m_{over}, \quad gen = g(\dot m_{in} - \dot m_{791} - \dot m_{over}),
   \quad \text{sens} \mathrel{+}= \dot m_{over}\,c_p\,(T_{d001} - T), \quad
   \dot m_{cond} = \max(\dot m_{in} - \dot m_{791} - \dot m_{over} - \dot m_{702} - W, 0) $$

With no overflow every term adds 0.0 and the condenser is V1's to the bit. 323E011 carries no species
(V1's), so the drum's liquor flashing at 1.13 bar a is not modelled.

**328C003's, 328C004's and 322C001's overflows** are boundary sinks (decided 2026-10-03):
`engine/plant/boundary.BOUNDARY_SINKS` names each vessel's overflow and temperature fields; no step
reads them (`tests/engine/test_schedule.py`), and the packet publishes them under the port's own
block ``BOUNDARY_SINKS`` (``{unit: {m_kgh, t_c}}``, one and two decimals) — not V1's, asserted both
ways (`tests/engine/packet/test_packet.py`). 322C001 flooded with LV-322502 shut sends 33.4 t/h at
43 C.

**323D011's envelope full** (decision 11's class, applied 2026-10-03). With 328D001 overflowing,
323D011 is fed beyond what LIC-323503 can draw, and V1's tank has no ceiling: before this session
LI-323503 reached 210 % in 50 minutes and the node's vapour space hit its 2 % floor at 2600 s, the
node jumping to 1.72 bar a. Now the envelope — condenser shell less bundle, plus the tank, 4.375 m3
(V1's) — is full at its volume times the condensate's density, 4204.5 kg, and the excess leaves as a
published overflow (`FlashCondenserResult.m_overflow_kgh`), taken from the tick's liquid balance
before the node steps.

**Measured** on the assembled plant (LIC-328501 in MAN at 0 from 2 s): LI-328501 reads 100 % at
800 s (its taps), the drum overflows from 1301 s at 30.3 t/h; LIC-323503 saturates, 718A rising to
25.7 t/h back to the drum; the envelope is full at 2630 s (LI-323503 177 % on V1's design-holdup
scale) and overflows 8.1-8.3 t/h. At full the node rings between 1.0 and 1.6 bar a on its 2 % vapour
floor, PV-323203 passing 1 to 1077 kg/h. The overflow's destination and the flooded node are open
(handoff A-20).

## LIX.4 The ejector design calculations read

The `References\Datasheets` design calculations were read, then the vendor archive for 322F001:

| document | content |
|---|---|
| `References\Datasheets\322F001 Design Calculations.pdf` (UD-AU-322-DZ-0013-003, Körting, 12-page scan) | AD 2000-Merkblatt B1 / B9 / B6 strength calculations only: the body's cylinders at 205 bar and 200 C — OD 164 x 60 (bore 44 mm), 174 x 45, 225 x 32.5, 102 x 16, 114 x 17 — and the heating jacket at 11 bar and 190 C (OD 242 and 160 x 4). No nozzle or mixing-throat dimension, no performance data |
| UD-AU-322-DZ-0013-002 (arrangement drawing 159000 633789 D, read from the A1 scan) | outer dimensions (N1 DN 120, N3 DN 160 outlet bore 160, N2 bore 90); the motive nozzle, needle and mixing throat drawn, not dimensioned |
| UD-AU-322-DZ-0013-005 (operation instructions, 68 pages) | §5: "The design points and operating data may be found in the design diagrams and the diagram system — see annexes": 14 diagrams in pairs — 1.x the pressure rise PD - PS against suction XMS with the free nozzle area as parameter, 2.x the motive pressure drop against XMS — at motive XMTR 40-100 % (actuator stroke 50 to 0 mm). The annex is not in the archive copy: its enclosures are the general drawing, Flowserve's Series 2000 actuator and Foxboro's SRI986 positioner |
| UD-AU-322-DZ-0013-006 (fabrication and inspection, 86 pages) | material certificates, NDE, hydraulic test, the function test of the control device, the name plate |
| UD-AU-322-EC-0013 (Uhde's technical specification) | remarks 1-8: the free area of the NH3 nozzle variable over 40-100 %; at design capacity and a 10 m L.C. suction head about 90 % free; at 60 % capacity 50 %; Körting to deliver H-Q curves at 100, 90, 80, 70 and 60 % capacity |
| `References\Datasheets\324F002 / 324F004 / 324F005 Design Calculations.pdf` | AD 2000 strength calculations (as §XLVIII.2 recorded) |

So no ejector curve and no throat dimension exists in either archive; Körting's 14 diagrams are named
but not enclosed (obtainable from Körting, order 2/131/4/04219). The geometry stays back-solved
(§XXI.4) and B-12's stall margin unvalidated. One discrepancy is recorded for Phase 7: the
specification's "about 90 %" free area at design capacity against the port's 84.4 % at HIC-322602's
74 % (V1's design opening on the DDS's linear map, §XXII).

## LIX.5 The faceplates (`hmi/faceplates/`, `data/faceplates.py`)

**Routing** — V1's ``overlays.js`` ``activate`` over every element of the ten screens (387): the pumps
the engine models (321P002A / B, 329P006A / B) open the pump faceplate and the 22 the overlays bind
to nothing stay inert; every block valve and its hand switch the block-valve faceplate (V1 toggled a
valve on its symbol; here the symbol opens the faceplate, as V1's hand switches did); HS-322915 its
keyswitch; LV-324501A / B the route; 22 hand stations; 82 loops; the two speed controllers from
eight elements; the MASTER SP from five; 139 indicators read-only; navigation, analysers, stream
hotspots and eleven unbound unit-335 instruments none (`tests/hmi/faceplates/test_router.py`).

**Each faceplate** renders the packet, refreshed on every packet while open, keeps the field the
operator is typing in, and sends one of the engine's commands; ENTER is SET and closes it; the answer
to its own command is shown with its reason. The loop faceplate reads the loop's block (``{pv, sp,
op, mode}``); MAN sends the output, AUTO the set point (bumpless from the PV), CAS the mode, and a
cascade slave names its master as the port wires it; a pressure is shown in bar g and sent in bar a
(the screens' convention, state_access). The speed faceplates offer MAN alone while the pump is
stopped and send, in CAS, the ratio master's set point (``ratio_set``). The pump faceplate has one
live button and an explicit run, its interlock line V1's words over the trips. The MASTER SP is
V1's ON / OFF cascade.

**Three V1 front-end defects corrected**, none a change of what an operator may do:

* HIC-329605, HIC-329606 and HIC-323605 send ``op``. V1's front end sent ``value``; its own
  ``handle_cmd`` reads ``op`` (``if "op" in cmd``), so those faceplates did nothing in V1
  (`tests/data/test_faceplates.py` asserts V1's field refused and the port's taken).
* A loop the packet carries no block for is not on this model: V1 kept a private mode, set point
  and output in the browser's ``localStorage`` (``ots_ctl_v1``) — console-owned state (§4a).
* FIC-328406 offers MAN, AUTO and CAS: decision B-50 (2026-09-30) made it LIC-328505's slave, but
  V1's faceplate whitelist (`data/operator_commands.FACEPLATE_MODES`) offered MAN alone, so no console
  could engage the decided cascade. A faceplate offers CAS where the overlay marks a slave (V1) or
  the loop's modes include it.

# Part LX — 323E011's overflow to 323C005, the history request and the trend window (Phase 6)

Session 43. The process engineer decided A-20 (b) — a full 323E011 / 323D011 envelope overflows
through PV-323203's vent line, its only outlet above the liquid, into 323C005, which is built to
scrub what is vented to it — asked that the node's oscillation be measured on it, and authorised the
console's history request and the trend window, plotting the engine historian over the protocol with
no samples kept by the console.

## LX.1 The envelope's overflow in 323C005 (`units/desorption/atmospheric_absorber.py`)

323C005 steps before 323E011 (V1's order), so the overflow and the condensate temperature it
leaves at are two new one-tick tears (`TearState.m_e011_over_kgh`, ``t_e011_over_c``, written from
`FlashCondenserResult.m_overflow_kgh` and ``t_c``; seeded 0 and 45 C). The overflow is liquid: it
is not part of the gas the vent law sees, it is not absorbed and carries no absorption heat, and it
falls to the sump with its sensible heat:

    M cp dT/dt = [V1's three inlets and absorption] + m_over cp (T_over - T)
    k_cap      = (m_756 + m_702 + m_708) cp / 3600 + m_over cp / 3600          [semi-implicit]
    sump in    = m_756 + m_abs + m_over                                         [N4 drains it]

The model carries no composition for 323E011's liquor, so none of it flashes at 1.0 bar a, and the
overflow passes whatever PV-323203's stroke (the decided routing names the line, not a liquid rating
of the valve). At zero overflow each added term is an exact zero and the column is V1's to the bit
(`test_no_overflow_is_the_column_without_one`; every V1 scenario in the equivalence file).

**Measured** on the assembled plant, LIC-328501 in MAN at 0 from 2 s: 328D001 overflows from about
1300 s at 30.3 t/h; the envelope fills at about 2650 s and overflows 7.4 to 9.4 t/h; 323C005 takes it
a tick later — its sump 8.3 to 10.7 kg (N4's head 49 to 56 mm), PFD 343 34.9 to 42.5 t/h to 328D003,
the liquor 52 to 54 C where it ran 62 C before (the overflow is cooler than the absorption heat
leaves the solvent). Alone, 8.2 t/h at 46 C on the design: the stack keeps 80 kg/h and the solvent
822, the bottoms 42 380 kg/h, the liquor 53.26 C, the mass balance closed on every tick.

## LX.2 The node's ring at its vapour floor — not reached by the routing

The routing does not resolve the ring A-20 measured: 323C005 is downstream at its 1.0 bar a and
does not act on the node. Measured, as before the routing: at full envelope the node swings 0.87 to
1.63 bar a (ten minutes from 2700 s). A tick-by-tick trace from a snapshot at 2700 s gives the
mechanism — a four-tick limit cycle:

    tick   p_E011   701 (323F004 reads p one tick late)   gen    702
    k      1.351    4265                                    207    177
    k+1    1.251    4035                                      0    207
    k+2    1.237    4002                                      0     28
    k+3    1.336    4232                                    211      8

The free volume is at its 2 % floor, 0.0875 m3 against 3.14 m3 at the design level, so each tick's
generation moves the node about 0.1 bar; 323F004, one tick late, answers a 0.11 bar swing with about
230 kg/h of flash vapour, which carries the gas load across the condenser's constant capacity
(gen 0 or about 210 kg/h). The loop gain at the floor, d p / d gen x d gen / d 701 x d 701 / d p, is
far above one. It is B-51's class — a full vessel's vapour-space integral at its floor, deferred by
the process engineer on 2026-09-30 to the solver review — and is filed there.

**A physical alternative, measured, not built** (a new mechanism, for the process engineer): the
module's docstring calls the drum, the line, the shell and the tank one gas space, but V1's node
volume leaves out 323F004's. With 323F004's vapour space added — 1.08 m3, its 1384 mm x 1800 mm
shell (`References/323F004 323E010 323F010.md` §3.1) above its 60 % level set point, heads left
out — the same snapshot runs without a ring: the node falls from 1.31 to 1.13 bar a over ten minutes,
each minute's band under 0.03 bar, PIC-323203 opening smoothly to about 21 %. It raises the node's
design capacitance by a third (3.14 to 4.22 m3), so the design transients would leave V1's.

## LX.3 The history request (`hmi/bridge.py`)

``request_history(paths, span_s, max_points, end_sim)`` sends the protocol's ``history`` (row 212)
and returns its id, 0 with the link down; ``request_history_paths`` likewise; the server's
``history_data`` is re-emitted as ``history_received(id, ok, reason, result)``. The bridge holds
nothing. On the engine host a ten-pen, one-hour query on full rings costs 4.4 ms of the physics
thread (0.7 ms for one minute, 3.9 ms for eight hours, 800 points a pen): one open trend window, at
one request a second, takes 0.4 % of it.

## LX.4 The trend window (`hmi/trend/`)

A separate top-level window, one per console (View > Trend window, Ctrl+T), as V1's popup:

* **Pens.** Ten. A tag trends what V1's trend map gives it (`series.trend_sources`): the path of its
  first bound indicator, valve opening or push button across the ten screens, a block valve's state
  or a pump's ``.on`` as a 0 / 1 pen; an absolute pressure trended gauge (BARG), as the indicators
  show it; 214 tags, 25 gauge, 9 digital. A pen is added from a trendable element's menu ("Trend"),
  or by dragging the element onto the plot (first free pen) or a row (that pen); refused unbound
  ("NOT BOUND") or past ten ("SLOTS FULL").
* **The plot.** Each pen on 0 - 100 % of its range, ``(v - lo) / (hi - lo) x 100``, mid-scale on a
  degenerate range; an analogue pen auto-scaled to its samples in view, padded 5 %, a flat trace
  given 0.5 either side; a digital pen on 0 - 1, stepped. The left axis reads the last marked pen's
  range, else per cent; the time axis the plant clock, and below it the desktop clock the engine
  stamped (interpolated between the answer's own samples). A marked pen is drawn 3.2 px on top, the
  others fade to a quarter.
* **The table.** Tag, live value (the packet's, as every indicator reads it), MIN / MAX / AVG over
  the view, the range (``A`` while auto), a value under each ruler (the last sample at or before it),
  the unit or STALE (newest sample over 30 s old), LOW / HIGH to fix the range (blank returns it to
  auto; an inverted or empty range refused, "BAD RANGE"), and x to empty the slot.
* **Rulers.** Ten, dropped by a click on the plot, dragged along it, removed from their chips; a
  ruler that leaves the view is dropped. **Spans** 1 m to 8 h and a typed one (5 s to 24 h). **Scroll**
  a quarter span back or forward, no further back than eight hours; forward past now is LIVE.
* **The source.** The window keeps no samples: live, it asks once a second for its whole window
  (one request in flight, a lost answer retried after 5 s) and repaints the answer; scrolled back, it
  asks once for the window it moved to. A newer request supersedes an older answer; a refusal, or the
  link lost, blanks every pen and says so ("HISTORY UNAVAILABLE — ..."). What the window keeps is its
  view — pens, span, ranges, marks — in the console's settings (V1's ``localStorage``).

**Departures from V1:** V1 appended every packet's value to its pens between backfills; the port
reads the historian alone. V1's SAVE composed a report image; the port saves the window's image,
which carries the same clocks, span, rulers and table. A click on a screen element now fires on
release without a drag, as V1's browser click did, so a drag can carry the tag to the trend window
(V1's HTML5 drag; its ``dragend`` screen-rectangle fallback is not needed in Qt).

# Part LXI — The display gaps decided, single-machine mode, the stream inspector and the data report (Phase 6)

Session 44. The process engineer decided B-51's 323E011 instance (323F004's vapour space in the
node, the "Typo Rule"), deferred A-2 and A-8 until the physical and UI port is complete — one machine,
one console with universal permissions, the instructor's panel paused — authorised the stream
inspector, and asked for the Phase 6 display gaps B-5, B-6 / B-7, B-9, B-11 and B-16 to be resolved,
as scheduled on 2026-09-29. B-9 was put to the process engineer and decided (one ceiling, 183 C); the
station login was asked and deferred with A-2. An archive report made by another tool was reviewed
against the open data gaps and every claim checked on the page (§LXI.9).

## LXI.1 323F004's vapour space in the 323E011 node (`units/recirc/flash_condenser.py`)

The drum, the vapour line, the condenser shell and the tank are one gas space; V1's node volume is the
envelope's alone. Decided 2026-10-07:

    V_v = max(V_env - M / rho, 0.02 V_env) + V_F004,     V_F004 = (pi/4) 1.384^2 . 1.800 . (1 - 0.60)
        = 1.083 m3                     [`References/323F004 323E010 323F010.md` §3.1; LIC-323505 60 %]

a constant (the drum's own level does not move it); the floor applies to the envelope alone, and
SV32357 relieves the same volume. The design capacitance rises by a third, 3.14 to 4.22 m3; at a steady
pressure nothing changes.

**Measured.** A full envelope (323F004 coupled one tick late, design inlets, 323P008's draw shut): on
the envelope alone the node rings 0.59-1.82 bar a in every minute of five; with the drum's vapour space
it holds 1.1300 bar a flat, PV-323203 on its 25 % stroke, the excess leaving as the overflow
(`test_a_full_envelope_holds_its_node_on_323f004s_vapour_space`, and the alternative). On the assembled
plant, from session 43's snapshot at 2700 s (LIC-328501 shut, the envelope full): the node falls from
1.41 to 1.13 bar a in ten minutes, every minute's band under 0.03 bar after the first, PIC-323203 about
21 %, where it rang 0.87-1.63. The transients slow: 701 up 10 % with PV-323203 held, 1.28 bar a in
4.4 s (V1's volume 1.31); the vent empties the node below 1.0 bar a in 5.6 s (5.0); SV32357 on a shut
vent lifts at 110.3 s and every 25.4 s, 12 times in 400 s (82.1 s, 17 times). Both ways: V1 verbatim
and the port are bit-exact while the node holds; on the first tick it moves, the port's step is
0.7435 of V1's, the ratio of the free volumes, to the last bits (`volume_decided` switch).

## LXI.2 322E001's one flood ceiling (`units/synthesis/stripper.py`, handoff B-9)

    dT_bot = max(dT_bot, dT_flood)                                     [V1: dT_bot + dT_flood]

Both rises are scaled on the 11 C gap to the 183 C reactor liquor and describe one end state; V1 adds
them. Both are exactly 0.0 at design and never negative, so the design point and every state below the
flooding limit (134 % of design load) are V1's to the bit. Past it, V1 against the port:

| bundle at | dT_bot (steam) | dT_flood | V1's TT-322004 | the port's |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.10 of the limit | 10.93 | 3.50 | 186.43 | 182.93 |
| 1.50 | 11.00 | 9.38 | 192.38 | 183.00 |
| 10.0 | 11.00 | 11.00 | 194.00 | 183.00 |

The flood rise itself is unchanged; its efficiency knockdown moves under 0.4 % through the carbamate
the cooler bottoms decompose. TT-322013 reads the attenuated dT_bot as before. V1's side runs through
`tests/equivalence/b9_switch.py`, V1's own function recompiled with the one statement switched.

## LXI.3 TT-322002 on 165 C (`data/unit_322e003.py`, handoff B-16)

``OVERFLOW_T_DES_C`` = 165.0 (PFD 206; the DCS reads 165.7 over 1921 samples) where V1 pins 178.8, its
ejector's suction pseudo-temperature. What V1 anchors on the pin follows it: UA_eff,des = 5329.5 /
(165 - 80) = 62.70 kW/K, eps = 0.17647, UA = 68.98 kW/K (V1's 58.505); the condensing temperature's
Clausius-Clapeyron anchor (slope 0.0709 K/bar, V1's 0.0754) and the thermal driving force's
denominator. The cooling water's 95.0 C return and the duty are unchanged; 322F001 keeps its own
178.8 (``unit_322f001.T_SUCTION_DES_C``), so its discharge balance does not move. The overflow sits
20 C under the 185 C ceiling where V1's sat 6.2 C under it: half the water, the purge below 24 %, a
35 % stronger spindle or +7 % throughput each took V1 to the ceiling; on 165 C they read 173.23,
171.24, 170.51 and 170.95 C, the purge shut 177.0; the rail is reached at +23.5 % throughput or 30 %
of the water. At the plant's normal-operation means TT-322002 reads 162.0 C (the plant 165.7; V1's
pin 175.7). XV-322903's vendor sizing case (carbamate at 165 C, §LXI.9) agrees with the pin. V1's
side seeds its ``SCRUB_OVERFLOW_T_C`` with 165 (`b16_switch`), so V1's own statements re-derive.

## LXI.7 Single-machine mode: the superuser (`net/protocol.py`, `net/server.py`, `run.py`)

*A-2 and A-8 closed 2026-10-16 (decisions 124, 125, §LXXII): the superuser stays the default console; the multi-station deployment is supported, on an optional station token, and the instructor's panel unpaused.*

A-2 and A-8 deferred by the process engineer until the port is complete. ``Role.SUPERUSER``: no command
type refused (``is_authorised``), the instructor's lists, roster and exercises (``runs_the_exercise``),
never narrowed by an assignment; granted only to a loopback peer (127.0.0.0/8, ::1, IPv4-mapped
loopback) — a remote station asking for it is refused at ``hello`` with the reason. `run.py` with no
mode serves on 127.0.0.1 and opens the console as the superuser; ``station`` still asks for an
operator. The engine's refusals (a latched trip, an interlock) reach the superuser as any role. The
main window shows the instructor's menu to the superuser.

## LXI.8 The stream inspector (`hmi/widgets/stream_hotspot.py`)

A ``strm`` hotspot or an ``ae`` analyser opens it (`faceplates.faceplate_for`) when the packet
publishes its stream; otherwise nothing opens, as in V1. ``stream_rows`` is V1's ``renderStream``:
route, phase, T, P, the mass flow in t/h and kg/h (both published fields), molar flow, MW, specific
enthalpy and its flow ("— (not modelled)" when absent), the H0 / H1 / H2 basis, density and volumetric
flow, then each of V1's nine components present on either basis, mol % and mass %; an analyser the
composition alone. Proved by executing V1's ``COMP_LBL`` / ``fStrm`` / ``renderStream`` in node on
every stream the design packet publishes, whole and composition only: the same strings. The inspector
is a faceplate on the console's theme (V1's #555 cell borders, monospace), the whole table in view;
it computes nothing. **Departure:** V1 filled its popup once at open; the inspector redraws from every
packet, and reads "NOT PUBLISHED" when the record goes.

An archive report from another tool (TOC pages per tag, uncited web values) was checked document by

were verified, refuted or left unopened as follows.

* **320K002's performance curves exist** — Nuovo Pignone's predicted curves, UD-AU-320-DZ-0001-165
  (73 scanned pages; overall and per-stage, per load case, surge lines; normal guaranteed point about

  map stands until the process engineer decides.
* **Isometrics for units 323 / 324 exist** (UD-RL-323-AB-0001 / -0002, line to drawing); A-11's run
  lengths can be measured; not done.
* **323D002's overflow**: nozzle N12 at EL +5452, line 200-US8-323262-EC07DB (UD-RL-100-MB-0146, as
  built), to seal pot Z2301Z near EL +2000, whose overflow ties in at EL +1620 (UD-RL-100-MB-0157 sheet
  B6); the pot's drain beyond is P&ID 105/1's system "30". **328D003's** trim isometric
  (UD-RL-100-MB-0301) has no overflow — the report's claim refuted.
* **HP angle valves**: HV-322605's CONVAL set (UD-MR-G00-DZ-0042-021) is the Kv table the port already
  runs; XV-322902 (-043) and XV-322903 (-054) are DN 120 on/off, Kvs 196 — on/off in V1 and the port.
* **FT-329409 0-500 m3/h and TT-329005 0-200 C** (UD-MR-329-EC-0001, F 329409 and T 329005), read from
  the right document (the report pointed at the ammonia plant's loop list): decision 10's class
  applied — FIC-329409 0.60 x 100 / 486 t/h = 0.1235 %/(t/h), Ti 250 s; TIC-329005 1.50 x 100 / 200 =
  0.75 %/K, Ti 300 s. Measured against V1's tunings: a 10 % FIC set-point cut settles in an hour
  (294.68 t/h at 300 s, 275.52 at 3600 s) where V1 settled it in two minutes; a 5 K TIC rise reaches
  84.46 C in an hour where V1 reached 85.00 in five minutes (closed-loop time constants about 400 s

* **FO-329458 / FO-329459**: 30 kg/h each of saturated LP steam, 9.0 to 1.0 bar a (F 329458 / 329459);
  with FO-322457, 90 kg/h into 322C001's vent line. Not modelled (a new mechanism).
* **Relief valves**: SV32353's, SV32357's and SV32253's specifications re-read — liquid cases only, no
  gas coefficient; the report's claim refuted, 0.917 stays assumed.
* **323P008**: its specification (UD-AU-323-EC-0017) and performance-test description (-DZ-0015-007)
  located, not read.
* **Henry constants on a urea melt, solid carbamate's dissociation constant**: the report gave no
  source; its dissociation pressures (85 Torr at 25 C, 1 atm near 59 C) are consistent with V1's
  160 kJ/mol but uncited — both gaps stay open.
* Not opened: 324F003's operating manual (a manual cannot hold the measured vacuum the gap asks for);

# Part LXII — 320K002 a boundary feed, the isometrics' run lengths, the trace steam, the DCS's tunings and the Phase 7 runner (Phases 6 and 7)

Sessions 45 and 46. The process engineer decided four items on 2026-10-07 — 320K002 onto its vendor's
curves, A-11's routes measured on the isometrics, 322C001's trace steam modelled, FIC-329409 and
TIC-329005 kept on the DCS table's rows — and authorised Phase 7, the transient runner first, with
B-51's ringing watched. Session 45 built the three physical changes and began the runner; it ended on
the usage limit with no document updated. On 2026-10-08 the process engineer revised the first
decision — 320K002 is outside the simulation's scope, a fully automated boundary feed — asked for the
interrupted documents, the runner finished and run, and the original DCS tuning constants found in the
plant's own table. This part records both sessions.

## LXII.1 320K002, the CO2 compressor, a boundary feed (`units/synthesis/co2_compressor.py`)

**What session 45 built, and withdrew.** Nuovo Pignone's predicted stage curves (UD-AU-320-DZ-0001-165,
scanned) were digitised — every speed line of the four stages, 21 points from surge to the line's end,
each drawn back over its scan — and the machine stacked from them stage by stage on its data sheet's
normal point (UD-AU-320-EC-0001: 6470 rpm, 26 230 / 6985 / 1560 / 290 m3/h, polytropic efficiencies
0.793 / 0.739 / 0.711 / 0.524), the real gas's Z on SRK. The stack reproduced the vendor's own overall
curve within 0.5-3 % of flow and the data sheet's 148.0 bar a within 0.06 bar. At 80 % load the
vendor's machine surged where V1's never did (no antisurge loop was modelled). The process engineer
withdrew it the next day; `control/machines.py`, `data/unit_320_k002.py` and their tests are deleted.

**Decided 2026-10-08.** "Since the CO2 compressor is outside the simulation scope, it must be modeled as
a fully automated boundary feed. Hardwire the speed governor and any necessary surge protections to
perfectly match the synthesis loop's demand without any operator intervention or faceplate exposure."

    delivery = max(demand, 0)                                  [kg/h, into the discharge line's node]

The demand is the battery-limit CO2 rate, PFD 101's 54 618 kg/h at design (operator entry
``320K002-CO2``). The discharge line is unchanged (`units/synthesis/co2_line.py`): its node, its
check valve, PV-322203 and PIC-322203; the node's floor is the PFD's 1.3 bar a suction (stream 105).
What the boundary removes: the curve, the speed and its governor's 8 s integral, the surge and
stonewall flags (V1's ``K002_SURGE`` / ``K002_STONEWALL`` are no longer published), and the operator's
command — ``co2_set`` is instructor-only (`net/protocol.py` ``INSTRUCTOR_ONLY_COMMANDS``), where V1's
screen 322-1 carried a COMPRESSOR SPEED hand station (`frontend/co2_compressor.js`). The machine is
still the plant's rate setter; the N/C ratio block divides by its delivery.

Measured both ways (`test_co2_line_equivalence.py`, V1's block transcribed with its machine an
argument):

| case | V1 (fitted map, 8 s governor) | the boundary |
|---|---|---|
| design | 54 618 kg/h into 144.2 bar a, the node still | the same, dP/dt a literal 0.0 |
| demand cut to 80 % | first tick 54 113 kg/h; ten minutes later 0.956 of its speed, 43 694 kg/h | 43 694 kg/h on the first tick |
| settled at 80 % | line 142.965 bar a | the same to 1e-6 |
| XV-322902 shut, PIC-322203 in AUTO | the line packs to PIC-322203's 168.01 bar a, the vent takes the feed | the same |
| XV-322902 shut, PIC-322203 held shut in MAN | 676 bar a at 1,000 s; surge at the 1.15 ceiling, 42.7 t/h still delivered; 1,114 bar a at 2,000 s | 676 and 1,209 bar a |

Neither side stops a blocked line: SV32064, the certified relief on 320R001 at the machine's discharge
(UD-RL-320-EC-0003, set 160 bar g), is modelled on neither (handoff B-83). The synthesis loop's pins
move in the fourth decimal (B-75's PT-329201 140.7011 / 140.7094 bar a against 140.6997 / 140.7079 on
the vendor curves); the CCW-loss scenario's PT-329201 141.1734 against 141.1733.

## LXII.2 322C001's trace steam (`units/absorption/vent_line.py`, `data/unit_329.py`)

Decided 2026-10-07: "Model it. 90 kg/h of steam alters the vent gas composition and temperature. Do not
ignore known mass inflows." Three DN15 restriction orifices on the 9-bar header (329D009), each rated
30 kg/h of saturated steam from 9.0 to 1.0 bar a at 175 C — Uhde's loop summaries F 322457
(UD-MR-322-EC-0001) and F 329458 / F 329459 (UD-MR-329-EC-0001 rev 1, PDF pages 33-34), tie-ins on P&ID
UD-VT-322-FB-0003 sheet 102:

* FO-329458 into the vent line between the column's top nozzle and PV-322201, and FO-322457 across
  XV-322915 downstream of it: 60 kg/h into the gas TI-322015 reads, mixed adiabatically;
* FO-329459 into SV32253's discharge, 30 kg/h, which TI-322015 does not see.

Each orifice is choked, its flow on the header's live pressure with the flood's law (§LIV):

    m_trace = 60 . Phi(P_9, P_atm) / Phi(9.0, P_atm)

The three draw on the 9-bar header and are taken out of PFD 910 ("steam tracing"), which carried them:
910's unmodelled share falls from 1094 to 1004 kg/h, so the header's design balance is unchanged.
**TI-322015 reads 53.7 C at design** where it read 46.0 C (the DCS reads 43.4 C); trip 22.1's 57 C is 3.3
K away (handoff B-84). The steam's water joins the vent gas to PV-322201.

## LXII.3 The product-line routes on the isometrics (`data/process_routes.py`, handoff A-11 closed)

Decided 2026-10-07: "A physics-based simulation cannot rely on layout estimates when the actual plant
geometry is available." Each route is read from its as-built isometric's bill of material (Uhde's
index UD-RL-323-AB-0001 / -0002 to UD-RL-100-MB-xxxx, scanned): the straight pipe of each size on the
flowing path, plus each long-radius elbow's centreline arc (ASME B16.9, R = 1.5 NPS), each size at its
own bore (DIN 2463 stainless DN 400 / 200 / 150; DIN 2462 HP 219.1 x 16.0 and 168.3 x 12.5):

    td = rho . V / m_dot,      V = sum_i pi/4 . D_i^2 . L_i

| route | lines (drawings) | volume [m3] | inventory [kg] | design td [s] | V1's estimate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 322E001 -> 323C003 | 200-US1-322302 (MB-0014): HP 120 3.4 m, 160 30.3 m | 0.8879 | 1021.1 | 28.2 | 25 m at 187.1 mm, 21.8 s |
| 323C003 -> 323F004 | 400-US14-323266 (MB-0148), 200-US4-323252 (MB-0138) | 0.8421 | 960.0 | 32.6 | 15 m, 16.0 s |
| 323F004 -> 323F010 | 150-US4-323253 (MB-0139) | 0.5677 | 650.0 | 23.1 | 15 m, 16.8 s |
| 323F010 -> 323D002 | 200-US6-323256 (MB-0142) | 0.6835 | 786.7 | 30.5 | 30 m, 36.9 s |

## LXII.4 The Phase 7 transient runner (`tests/phase7/`)

The validation harness A-14 asked for ("the Phase 7 driver runs V1 at the same step"): V1's own
``main.step_sim(0.1)`` and the rewrite's ``Scheduler`` through one operating procedure, each in its own
process (V1 keeps its plant in module globals), both at the fixed 0.1 s step. Commands reach V1
through ``handle_cmd`` and the rewrite through ``engine.command.apply_command``, between two ticks;
both packets on V1's key paths, so one path reads one quantity on both sides.

* `scenarios.py` — the procedures as data: the cold start (V1's ``test_transient_coldstart.py``: the
  loop empty and at 5.7 bar g, the feeds on, 16 000 s); trip 22.2 (``test_ccw_loss_chain.py`` phase 2:
  329P006A and B stopped at 60 s, run to ten minutes past the latch); the HPCC rupture
  (``run_hpcc_rupture.py``: water into 322E002's product in steps of 0 to 40 t/h, ten minutes each,
  321D003's level held); the vacuum break (HIC-329605 to 0 % for fifteen minutes, then back to each
  engine's own opening).
* `drivers.py` — one engine through one procedure: the commands due, the disturbance, the tick; every
  tick the watched pressures (328C004, 323E011, PT-329201) reduced to 10-s windows — reversals of the
  tick-to-tick change larger than 0.01 bar, and the window's peak-to-peak; a window with six reversals
  and 0.05 bar is ringing (B-51) — and the trips' first latch; the packet sampled on the scenario's
  interval. Smith's two-point FOPTD (tau = 1.5 (t63 - t28), t_d = t63 - tau) for the cold start.
* `compare.py` — per path the first, last and peak-to-peak on each side and the largest gap, paired by
  time; the trips' latch times; the ringing; the cold start's identification against the 3 June 2025
  start-up trend's band (tau 2884-4055 s, dead time at most 572 s, final 137.5-150.5 bar g). It
  measures; it does not judge.
* `run.py` — ``python -m tests.phase7.run <scenario>|all [--side both|v1|port] [--out DIR]
  [--duration S]``; the records and the report go outside the project tree.

Speed at the design point: V1 16 ms a tick, the rewrite 23 ms.

**A port defect the runner found.** The console's PT-329201 (``EJ_322F001.PI_329201``) and
322E003's ``P_overflow`` / ``P_offgas`` published the scrubber's design pins: 140.7 bar a whatever the
loop did. V1 overwrites both with the live loop pressure the tick read (`main.py` 8105-8106); the port
missed the overwrite, and no equivalence test moved the loop while reading the packet. Fixed in
`engine/plant/synthesis_loop._322e003` (register row 240); the four port runs were made again on it.

**A second port defect: a dry melt's "boil" condensed.** The port's first cold start crashed at
8 112 s, 324E003's temperature overflowing a polynomial after the evaporation train had run away from
6 873 s (324F001 to 1 635 C, 324F003 to -770 C). In the cold start 324F001 sits on its 1.5 kg floor
for 6 000 s with no feed and boils dry — 84.25 % urea, the rest biuret, no water. Fed again, its
vapour by relative volatility (`thermo.urea_liquor.vapour_y`) is pure urea, above the melt's 85.51 %
ceiling, and `holdup_boil`'s bound x_max = M (w_max - w_u) / (w_max - y_u) turned negative: the stage
"boiled" -85.7 kg a tick, condensing vapour it did not hold, and its latent heat drove the melt up
7.7 K a tick while the vacuum sat on its 0.05 bar a floor. Decision 45's boil (B-62) is the port's
own; V1 has no holdup boil and held 59.8-141.4 C through the same start. Fixed: a vapour at least as
rich in urea as the ceiling cannot concentrate the melt, which then does not boil. Run again, the
start crashed the same way at about 10 000 s through a second path: 324F003 at 0.17 bar a, its melt
90.97 % against the 91.01 % the melt model holds at its window's 99 C edge — below the window
`equilibrium_urea_fraction` holds the edge, so the strength no longer falls as the melt cools, and a
melt a hair weaker than it reads as superheated at any temperature; the stage boiled itself down
through 0 C. Fixed: below the window a held melt does not boil, and the latent heat it pays cannot
take it below the edge, x_max <= C (T* - 99) / lambda (`T_WINDOW_LO_C`). Replayed from a 6 500 s
snapshot, 324F001 recovers from 103 to 134 C and 324F003 holds at the window's edge, 99.0 C, where
its true boiling point is not known to the model (register row 242, `test_holdup_boil.py` on both
captured states; B-66's 4.5 s vacuum moves from 0.151936 to 0.151903 bar a, `test_vacuum_train.py`).
The other three scenarios' records stand: their stages never boiled dry and stayed above 118 C.

**Results** (both engines on the session's code; the records and reports outside the tree):

* **Cold start** (16 000 s; the loop empty at 5.7 bar g, the feeds on). PT-329201 rises on both,
  identified by Smith's two-point method against the 3 June 2025 start-up trend's band (tau

  | V1 | 3825 | 435 | 145.1 | all three |
  | the port | 3645 | 405 | 134.9 | tau and dead time; the final 2.6 bar under |

# Part LXIII — B-51's backward pressure step, SV32064 on the CO2 line, and B-87 traced (Phase 7)

Session 47. The process engineer re-sent the session 46 decisions, found built; then, on 2026-10-09,
decided two of the items Phase 7's comparison had raised: B-51 — the pressure step switched on its
own stability, chosen over a fixed free-volume threshold and over every node always — and B-83
option (a), SV32064 on the CO2 line node. Both were built; B-87's cause was traced on both engines.
An external tool's report of the same work, pasted with the request, claimed both built and B-87
traced; it had no access to the tree (it said so), nothing in it had been built, and its SV32064 set
(160.01 bar a) and its B-87 mechanism are not what the code and the measurements give.

## LXIII.1 The backward pressure step where the explicit one would ring (`core/node.py`, `units/desorption/second_desorber.py`, handoff B-51 closed)

**Decided** by the process engineer on 2026-10-09 (decision 78). A fixed free-volume threshold would
have been a number no document fixes; every node always would have moved every transient by the
step's truncation and re-baselined the bit-exact suite.

**The equation.** The node's pressure ODE is unchanged (`vessel_dpdt`, §XIV):

    f(P) = (R T / V_v)(n_gen - n_out(P)) + (P / T) dT/dt - (P / V_v) dV_v/dt

and each tick (`stable_pressure_step`):

    f0 = f(P),    G = dt . (f(P + h) - f0) / h,    h = 1e-7 bar       the explicit step's own gain
    G >= -1:   P' = P + f0 . dt                                        V1's step, to the bit
    G <  -1:   P' = P + dt . f(P'),   P' in [max(min(P, P + f0 dt), P_floor), max(P, P + f0 dt)]

Forward Euler multiplies a departure from the pressure the node heads for by 1 + G each tick: at
G = -1 the factor is zero, below it the departure changes sign every tick — the ringing B-51
measured — and below -2 it grows. -1 is the analytic edge of a monotone step, not a tuning
(`EXPLICIT_STEP_LIMIT`). Where the outflow rises with the pressure the root lies between the old
pressure and the explicit one, which bracket the backward step.

The backward step is `backward_euler_pressure` (V1's ``_backward_euler_p``, §XLIX.7): Newton from
the old pressure, iterated to the root inside the bracket, bisecting where a step would leave it.
**Not a single Newton correction**, as the question put to the process engineer described it: the
overhead line's compressible law has an unbounded slope at zero differential, the residual
P - P_old - dt f(P) is concave there, and one correction from the old pressure can overshoot below
the receiver; iterating inside the bracket lands on the root. On a backward tick 750 is
re-evaluated at the settled pressure, so the moles the head space lost are the moles 328C002
receives; the liquid's books (decision 24) do not read 750.

**Where it acts.** G scales as 1 / V_v times the overhead line's slope. (a) A head space closing
towards the roof: with LV-328505 shut from design, from 13 927 kg (1333.2 s; V_v 0.91 m3, 5.7 % of
the shell, against 14.43 m3 at design) at the 0.1 s step and
from 10 585 kg (976 s) at 0.5 s. (b) Where the overhead line's differential closes towards zero:
with the LP steam lost at the 0.5 s step, from the fourth tick. At design G = -0.063 at 0.1 s; the
nine scenarios of `test_second_desorber_equivalence.py` run on V1's explicit lines (``ON_BOOKS``,
B-51 out) agree with the port bit for bit.

**Measured.**

* 328C004 alone, LV-328505 shut from design, 0.1 s, 2,000 s: V1's explicit step rings from 1380 s —
  62 ringing windows, 750 alternating shut and open every tick, 2.09 to 4.76 bar a once full; the
  port takes the backward step from 1333.2 s and holds 3.6997 to 3.6998 bar a, no ringing window.
* The same at 0.5 s, 4,000 s: no ringing window; full at 1422.5 s, where the explicit step's
  ringing, biasing the bottoms' temperature and so the boil-up, had it full at 1427 s.
* The whole port, session 46's case (14 000 kg, LIC-328505 in MAN at 0 %, 30 minutes): 17 892 of
  18 000 ticks backward, no reversal in any 10-s window; the first window falls 3.70 to 3.28 bar a
  as the head space is cut to 0.83 m3 at once, the pressure then rises smoothly to 3.77 bar a at
  eight minutes and settles at 3.67 — where on the explicit step it rang from 50 s, up to 2.54 bar
  in 10 s, 2.4 to 4.7 bar a.
* The port's cold start, re-run on the new code (Phase 7 runner, against session 46's V1 record):
  328C004 still floods (B-87, LI-328505 to 513.9 %) but no 10-s window rings — none of 48 —, its
  worst 10-s span 0.40 bar where it was 3.64, the column at 2.95 to 4.18 bar a where it swung 1.83
  to 4.18, and it ends at 4.18 bar a where it ended mid-swing at 1.89. The other rows keep their
  ranges and their gaps to V1; their final values move a little, the ringing's absence carried
  round the recycle — the loop 135.8 bar a (135.7), AT-322701 3.169 (3.186), the conversion
  57.29 % (57.60), the stripper's bottoms 58.84 % urea (58.93).

V1's side of the decided tests moves where it runs with B-51 switched in: with the LP steam lost
and 749 at 130 C V1's lines hold 141.08 C at 3.494 bar a, discarding 419 kW (140.96 C, 3.482 bar a,
414 kW on V1's explicit step); LV-328505 shut, V1 holds 20.2 t at 2000 s (20.0 t). Decision 24's
books test keeps V1's explicit step: 750 at the settled pressure presupposes the liquid paying what
boils, so the transcription refuses B-51 without "vapour".

## LXIII.2 SV32064 on the CO2 discharge line (`units/synthesis/co2_line.py`, handoff B-83 closed)

**Decided** by the process engineer on 2026-10-09, option (a) (decision 79); option (b), PIC-322203's
set point from the DCS, was not taken: it stays V1's 168.01 bar a, above the valve's set.

**The datum.** Sempell's orifice selection, Uhde "Safety Relief Valves — Calculation of Orifice"
UD-RL-G00-DZ-0001-001 page 72 of 163 (scanned; read at 400 dpi): SV32064, AD 2000-A2; gas,
M 43.370, k 1.510, Z 0.74, 140 C, 67 000 kg/h required on 436.48 mm2 at alpha 0.588; orifice H,
615.75 mm2, lift-limited to 5.26 mm; actual capacity 74 444.40 kg/h at alpha_w 0.654 and 10 %
overpressure; set 160 bar g, blowdown 10 %; DN 40 PN 250 in, DN 80 PN 40 out; SC 250 H - 40 80.
Its set agrees with Uhde's specification UD-RL-320-EC-0003 (set 160 bar g, relieving 177.00 bar a).
`data/relief_devices.py` carries it in ``RELIEF_SIZING`` (seventeen valves), `data/unit_320.py` the
line's constants.

**The equations** (decision 32's law, §XLIV.3, `core/relief.py`):

    P_set = 160 + 1.013 = 161.013 bar a          (the sheet's atmosphere, decision 71)
    P_reseat = 161.013 - 0.10 . 160 = 145.013 bar a,    P_rel = 161.013 + 0.10 . 160 = 177.013
    A = 74 444.40 / W_API520(1 m2, 177.013 bar a, 413.15 K, 43.370, k 1.510, Z 0.74)
    W = min( A . W_API520(P, T_line, M_line, k 1.510, Z 1),  reseat_vent(P_free, 145.013) )
    P' = P_free + dt . vessel_dpdt(P, T_line, V_line, M_line, 0, W / M_line)

on the line's gas: M_line the feed's molar mass, T_line TI-322017's 120 C, V_line 21.566 m3. Lifted
at P >= P_set read at the top of the tick, shut at P <= P_reseat. Below the set the step is the
previous expression to the bit.

**Measured** on the line alone, XV-322902 shut at the design 54.618 t/h: SV32064 lifts 31.7 s after
the shut and stays lifted — its orifice passes the whole feed at 147.55 bar a, above its reseat,
where it would pass 53.7 t/h — and PIC-322203 never opens its vent. At 30 t/h it cycles between
reseat and set, 17 lifts in 2,000 s. With PIC-322203 in MAN, V1's block packs to 676 bar a at
1,000 s; the port holds 147.55. The relief leaves the plant: it is published in ``BOUNDARY_SINKS``
under 320K002 (its kg/h at 120 C) — V1's ``CO2_FEED`` has no key for it, and the port adds none to
V1's blocks.

**Trip 22.2 on the new code** (the Phase 7 runner, port side re-run against session 46's V1 record):
trip 22.2 latches at 14 767.4 s (14 769.2), no watched pressure rings, 322R001's peak 166.8 bar a
(172.7); the rest within a few tenths. Its record does not sample SV32064: on the whole plant from

# Part LXIV — B-86, B-87, B-88, B-39, A-7, B-13, B-82 and B-89 decided; the Phase 7 re-runs and the steady state at 1750 MTPD (Phase 7)

Session 48. The process engineer decided, in two pastes on 2026-10-09, the items Part LXIII's trace
and this part's measurements left open. First: B-87 as a mix of option (b), "the conservation rule" —
a condenser cannot pass more condensate than it receives as vapour — and option (c), "the topology
rule" — FIC-328402 on 735, as the plant meters it, which is B-39; B-86 option (c), "the extrapolation
rule" — below the melt model's window, V1's closure alone, no holdup boil; and B-88 option (c) — trip
22.2 takes the CO2 boundary's demand to zero, as the compressor's own trip would (decisions 80-83).
Second: A-7, zero overlay overlap; B-89, 323E011's creep accepted; B-13, 322E002's gate at 1.0; B-82,
the HPCC rupture rebuilt as process into the shell; A-18, targeted profiling and caching
(decisions 84-87). The Phase 7 cold start, trip 22.2 and HPCC rupture were re-run, the steady-state
comparison at 1750 MTPD was run on both engines over every packet leaf, and the overlay gate reaches
zero.

## LXIV.1 No holdup boil below the melt model's window (`units/evaporation/holdup_boil.py`, handoff B-86 closed)

**Decided** 2026-10-09, option (c) (decision 82). The melt equilibrium (`thermo.urea_melt`, B-58's
refit) is valid from 99 to 200 C and 0.02 to 1.00 bar a and holds the window's edge outside it.
Session 46 bounded decision 45's boil there — no boil at or below 99 C, and no more latent heat than
brings the melt to 99 C — so a melt weaker than the edge's strength boiled down to the edge on every
tick it was heated above it: 324F003 parked at 99.0 C through the cold start, and on the tick it first
reached the edge, its pressure at its 0.02 bar a floor, it boiled 1.35e6 kg/h (B-87's link 1).

**The rule.** After the existing test that the holdup is superheated, w_b(T*, P) > w_u,

    w_b(99 C, P) > w_u   =>   no holdup boil: x = 0, T' = T*          (V1's closure alone)

w_b the stage's anchored equilibrium (§L): the melt's boiling point at the live vacuum lies below the
window, where the model does not reach, so it is not known and the holdup does not boil; the stage
runs on V1's feed closure at whatever temperature its step gives. A melt whose boiling point is inside
the window boils as before, and there w_b(99, P) <= w_u <= w_u'(x) puts the root at T' >= 99, so
session 46's cap C (T* - 99) / lambda never binds; it stays as the bracket's end.

**Measured** (`test_holdup_boil.py`, 324F003's 4 471 kg at C 9 000 kJ/K): 90.97 % urea at 0.1735 bar
a, against the edge's 91.01 %, holds 99.5 C and 120.0 C (session 46's bound boiled both to 99.0 C);
the cold start's 89.49 % at 0.2879 bar a, where the edge's strength is 84.77 %, still boils, 462.18
kg/h, to 108.8969 C. A 50 % liquor at 0.33 bar a and 135 C — far below the window — no longer boils
(it boiled its half kilogram above the floor); the floor test now runs on a 90 % melt, 50 g above its
floor, which boils those 50 g.

## LXIV.2 A condenser's vent never negative (`units/evaporation/vacuum_condenser.py`, handoff B-87 option (b))

**Decided** 2026-10-09 (decision 80). **The defect.** `condenser_node.inlet_kmolh` scales the PFD row
on the inlet's air-free mass, r = (m_in - m_air) / (m_in,des - m_air,des), and carries the false air's
departure on the air's composition:

    n_k = n_k,des r + y_air,k (m_air - m_air,des) / M_air + y_air,k (m_air,des / M_air)(1 - r)

For an inert the terms leave (n_k,des - y_air,k m_air,des / M_air) r + y_air,k m_air / M_air: the
row's inert less the design false air's share of it, scaled by r. PFD 709's N2 is 0.5708 kmol/h,
the 21 kg/h false air's share 0.5755; at Phase 7's burst (709 = 1.352e6 kg/h, r 405, 0.084 kg/h of
false air) N2 = -1.889 kmol/h, O2 +1.327, the inerts' sum -0.562. `vent_moles` sizes the condensables
the vent carries as n_c = n_i y / (1 - y), y at its ceiling at 0.02 bar a: 324E005 vented -2.176e10
kg/h and booked the same as condensate. The node's mass closed only by booking the negative vent.

**The rule.**

    n_i = sum_k max(n_in,k, 0)                                   k inert
    n_vent,k = max( min(n_c split_k, n_in,k), 0 )                 k condensable
    n_vent,k = max(n_in,k, 0)                                     k inert

so the model vent, the anchored vent (§LII) and the shell's vent (B-66) are never negative and the
condensate inlet - vent never exceeds the inlet. `inlet_kmolh` is V1's and is not changed: the
row's N2 lies 0.0047 kmol/h below the false air's share of it, which matters only at a burst
hundreds of times the row.

**Measured** (`test_vacuum_condenser_decided_equivalence.py`, V1's own module beside the port; 324E005
is V1's on every other inlet, B-71): at the burst's inlet, 0.02 bar a, design water — V1 vents
-2.17594e10 kg/h, its cold end at the vapour's inlet; the port vents 1 322 366.44 kg/h of the 1.352e6
arriving and condenses 29 634, its cold end 133.1347 C, every vented species >= 0. Wherever no inlet
species is negative the floor is inert: every condenser, node, stage and train equivalence runs on
V1's ``vent_moles`` transcribed with the floor (`tests/equivalence/b67_switch.py`) and stays ``==``.

## LXIV.3 FIC-328402 meters 735; 744 is 322P002's delivery (`units/desorption/ammonia_water_tank.py`, handoffs B-39 and B-87 option (c) closed)

**Decided** 2026-10-09 (decision 81). Every plant source puts FT-328402 and FV-328402 on 328P003's
discharge, line 100-AW3-328062 (§XXXV.4, handoff B-39's evidence: Uhde's loop summary F 328402, the DCS
table's "328062,AW", the P&ID); Flowserve sizes FV-328402 for 31.4 m3/h at 56 C — 735's service.

**What the plant has instead of V1's law.** V1 draws 735 in proportion to compartment II's holdup,

    m_735 = 31 114 . M_II / M_II,des

a level-following draw. The plant has none: LT-328507 and LT-328508 are open-loop indicators (the
owner's mapping, `References/323D003 Datasheets.md`; `Mapping of Absorber unit.md`), so 328D003's level
is the operator's, on FIC-328402's set point. And 744 has no control valve: P&ID 102 draws 322P002 A / B
(line 80-AW3-322104) through 322E006 to 322C001 (80-AW3-322107) with FI-322402 alone — read from the
page image of `References/Merged_Searchable_PIDs.pdf` page 3, and page 7 for the tank and pumps.

**The equations.**

    m_735 = FIC-328402's flow loop (`FlowLoop`, §XXXV.4) on 735: design 31 114 kg/h at
            990.89 kg/m3 (31.4 m3/h, PFD), FV-328402's stroke on 735 58.40 % (58.79 on 744),
            the set point up to V1's 60 000 kg/h on 735's density, B-38's gain
    m_744 = 31 478 kg/h while 322P002 A or B runs, else 0;    both against the heel caps (§XXXV.5)

FT-328402 reads what 328P003 delivered when compartment II's heel caps the header (B-38's form),
with FT-323401, FT-323402 and FT-328405. B-38's other half — FT-328402 reading nothing while 322P002
is stopped — has no object left: 744 is on no loop. FFIC-329401 already ratioed 735 (§XLII.3). The
console keeps V1's key, ``LPCC_3232.E003.FIC_328402``, and its place on screen 328-1, now fed 735;
the indicator's note, written for 744, is the converter's decided edit (`DECIDED_EDITS`, the only line
of `screen_layout.py` that changed).

**Measured.** At design nothing moves (735, 744 and the levels hold to the bit). Both ways
(`test_ammonia_water_tank_fic328402_equivalence.py`, the transcription's ``b39`` switch off for V1's
structure): the condensates up 30 % for an hour — V1's 735 takes 1 133.2 kg/h of the surplus and the
tank stands at 51.8 %, the port's holds 31 114 and the tank takes it all, 51.94 %; the tank at 99.95 %
on the design inflows — V1's 735 is 1.999 times its design, 62 197 kg/h, B-87's link 4; the port's
31 114. On the port alone (`tests/units/desorption/test_ammonia_water_tank.py`): 322P002 stopped an hour
fills the tank to 56.48 % (V1 56.08), restarted it delivers the design 744 at once; 343 gone an hour
draws it to 42.97 % (V1 43.40); nothing arriving, 322P002 loses suction at 13.8 s and 328P003 at 14.6
s (V1 26.1 and 31.6); 741 at the whole design bottoms overflows the full tank from 25.5 s at 33 724
kg/h (V1: 333.5 s, 2 610 kg/h, its 735 doubled). FIC-328402's set point move to 25 m3/h is unchanged:
414.7 s within 1 % on the port, 198.5 s on V1's gain, both on 735.

## LXIV.4 Trip 22.2 trips the CO2 boundary (`engine/plant/synthesis.py`, `engine/command.py`, handoff B-88 closed)

**Decided** 2026-10-09, option (c) (decision 83), a change to decision 73's boundary: on the plant,
XV-322902 shutting against a running compressor brings the machine's own trips and antisurge; the
boundary reflects the machine tripping without modelling it. V1's own comment on trip 22.2 says it
"cuts CO2 + NH3 feed" (``main.py`` 4963).

**The rule.** On every tick trip 22.2 is latched, the 320K002 step shuts XV-322902 (V1's action) and
sets the boundary's demand, ``plant.operator["320K002-CO2"]`` (``co2_set``), to zero — on that tick's
line step too, so the trip acts on the tick after it latches, as V1's actions do. ``co2_set`` above
zero is refused while the trip is latched, naming it ("320K002 is tripped by trip 22.2, latched: reset
the trip before restoring the CO2 demand"), as an open of XV-322902 is; zero is accepted; once the
trip is reset the instructor restores the demand. Nothing restores it on its own: a tripped
compressor does not restart itself.

**Measured** (`test_synthesis_loop_decided_equivalence.py`, the synthesis harness's ``B-88`` switch
off for V1): the loop put at 155.5 bar a, trip 22.2 latching on its first tick — V1 keeps asking
54.618 t/h of the blocked line, which packs until SV32064 lifts on tick 316 (31.7 s) and still holds
159.70 bar a after a minute; the port's demand is zero from the same tick, its line holds 144.25 bar a
and SV32064 never lifts. With the switch on, the transcription is ``==`` the port on every tick of the
existing trip 22.2 test.

## LXIV.6 The steady-state comparison at 1750 MTPD (`tests/phase7`, scenario ``steady_state``)

**The procedure.** Both engines from their design seeds — 1750 MTPD at 100 % load, the PFD both are
anchored on — left alone for an hour at the 0.1 s step, one process each (`python -m tests.phase7.run
steady_state`). A scenario with an empty tag list samples every numeric and boolean leaf of the
packet every 60 s (`drivers._drive`, a leaf first seen late padded with None); `compare.steady_table`
pairs the two packets leaf by leaf at the hour: the gap, the gap over V1's value, and each engine's own
drift over the second half hour. A leaf agrees within 1 % of V1's value or 0.001 absolute. Nothing
here judges a difference (§LXII.4): a decided divergence that acts at design differs by design.

**Measured** (V1 14.8 ms a tick, the port 18.0): no trip, no watched pressure rings on either side
(328C004, 323E011 and PT-329201 hold every 10-s window flat). **3 084 of the 3 188 numeric leaves the
two packets share agree**; no flag differs. PT-329201 140.7 bar a, the reactor's conversion 54.17 %,
the stripper's bottoms 55.84 % urea, the product 97.7 % urea, LI-328505 and 328D003 at 50 % — the same
on both. The 104 that differ, by cause:

| leaves | V1 | port | cause |
|---|---|---|---|

| SIC-321950 / 321951 Kc, Ti (4) | 2.0, 8 s | 3.38, 35 s; 1.01, 50 s | the DCS table's rows (decision 77) |
| 14 chest leaves: 324E003's, 324E001's and 323C003's chests and 323F010's PIC-329208, with their TICs' outputs | 8.1, 3.96, 3.96, 1.76 bar | 5.9, 3.70, 3.90, 2.50 | the chests on their datasheets' pressures (decision 20) |
| TT-322002 (three leaves) | 178.8 C | 165.0 | B-16, TT-322002 on 165 C |
| TT-322015 | 43.0 C | 53.7 | the trace steam (decision 75; handoff B-84) |
| 322E001's steam, the MP supply | 76 676 kg/h, 76.7 t/h | 66 908, 58.0 | the PFD's basis with the licensor's duty (decisions 47, 52) |
| FIC-328402's mass | 31 478 kg/h (744) | 31 114 (735) | decision 81 |
| HV-322604's outlet (S0204, SCRUB_OFFGAS_LP) | 4.0 bar a | 3.9 | 322C001's live pressure (decision 29, A-17) |
| 323E011's vent 702 (16 leaves) and PIC-323203's output, 323C005's 341 (14) | 453.6 kg/h, 81.0, 25.1 % | 475.6, 82.6, 27.0 | not decided: both engines start at 440.7 kg/h and creep, V1 +13 kg/h in the hour, the port +35, its PIC-323203 opening 2 points where V1's moves 0.1 (handoff B-89, accepted 2026-10-09, §LXIV.10) |
| 324E007's vent 722, its CO2 and NH3 (9 leaves), 715's CO2 (2) | 6.92 kg/h CO2 | 6.67 | stage 2's vapour 3 kg/h apart (709 3 344.6 / 3 341.6 kg/h), amplified on 324E007's CO2 by V1's ratio (B-71) |

Drift over the second half hour beyond 1 %: on both, the clocks, the totaliser, 740's urea (0.38 ppm),

## LXIV.9 322E002's tube leak, process into the shell (`units/synthesis/tube_leak.py`, handoff B-82 closed)

**Decided** 2026-10-09 (decision 87): rebuild the HPCC rupture with the leak's real direction — the
140 bar a synthesis loop into the LP steam drum's 5 bar a — on the live differential, the loop's
inventory lost, the drum contaminated. V1's malfunction is a test script (``tests/run_hpcc_rupture.py``)
that injects water into 322E002's product, the shell's water entering the process against the
differential; neither engine had the malfunction in its plant.

**The equations** (module docstring; `data.unit_322e002` ``LEAK_DP_DES_BAR``, ``LEAK_VOLATILE``):

    W = W_sev . sqrt( max(PT-329201 - P_322D001, 0) / (140.7 - 5.01325) ),   W <= m_product
    f = W / m_product,   n_leak,k = f (n_gas,k + n_liq,k),   322R001 gets (1 - f) of each
    shell: NH3, CO2, N2, O2, H2, CH4 -> 322D001A/B's steam space (the LP header);
           H2O, urea, biuret -> 322D001A/B's water;
           Q = H0(gas, T_prod, v) + H0(liq, T_prod, l) - H0(volatiles, T_sh, v) - H0(rest, T_sh, l)
           boils Q / h_fg(T_sh) of the drums' water (condenses it, Q < 0)

both pressures the tick before's; W_sev the instructor's rate at the design differential. The split
in the shell is complete — the boiling water at 152 C and 5 bar a strips the ammonia and CO2 and
decomposes the carbamate, the process's own stripping principle — an assumption no plant document
measures. H0, the elements datum (§I), prices NH3 and CO2 dissolved in the leak's liquid, so their
desorption is paid out of the shell.

**Wired.** `CondenserHoldup.step` applies the leak after the condenser's evaluation, before the sump
and 322R001 read it (``leak_severity_kgh``, state; ``CondenserStepResult.leak``). PT-329201's boundary
takes it out (`LoopPressure.step(m_leak_kgh=)`). The steam network takes its four flows
(`SteamDraws.leak_*`): the volatiles and the boil into the LP node's balance — its implicit step's
residual too — the water and solids into 322D001's water, inside the drum's heel cap; the solids are a
state (``m_d001_solids_kg``) that the blowdown and any overflow take at the water's strength
(``d001_solids_ppm``). The instructor starts it with ``trigger_fault`` id ``322E002`` and ``value`` in
t/h (refused without one), stops it with ``clear_fault``. 322E002 reads 322D001A/B's pressure of the
tick before, a declared tear (the network steps after it). At zero every term is a literal zero added
at the end of its sum: every equivalence test runs unchanged.

**Measured.** At design (`test_tube_leak.py`), 10 t/h at the design differential: 3.99 % of the
250.6 t/h product; 9 310.98 kg/h of volatiles and inerts to the steam, 689.02 kg/h of water and solids
(1.031 kg/h of urea) to the drums; Q = -1 381.95 kW, condensing 2 360.0 kg/h of the drums' steam — the
desorption of the leaked liquid's ammonia and CO2 outweighs its 18 K of sensible heat. Half the
differential leaks 1 / sqrt(2) as much; the whole product at most. On the plant from design, 10 t/h
for twenty minutes: PT-329201 140.70 to 138.35 bar a, the leak easing 10.00 to 9.91 t/h with it;
LT-322E002 50 to 47.2 %; 322D001A/B's level 50.0 to 51.6 %, LV-329504 closing 48.3 to 37.4 %; the LP
header 5.02 bar a, 5.12 at a minute, back to 4.99; the drums' water at 11.4 ppm of solids.

**The Phase 7 HPCC rupture on it** (V1 re-run unchanged, the same 0 / 2.5 / 5 / 10 / 20 / 40 t/h
schedule, ten minutes each; the port's tube leak at those rates at design). V1's water and the port's
leak move the loop in opposite directions:

| at 3 600 s | V1 (water into the process) | port (process into the shell) |
|---|---|---|
| PT-329201 | 137.2 bar a | 134.8 |
| 322R001's level LT-322504 | 80 to 100 % | 80 to 35.7 % |
| the reactor's H/C | 0.398 to 1.099 | 0.398 to 0.365 |
| the reactor's conversion | 50.44 % (48.0-59.8) | 47.38 % (47.4-54.6) |
| 322E001's bottoms | 51.81 % urea | 56.78 |
| 323D002 | 74.77 % urea | 81.44 |
| trip 22.1 | not latched | latched at 3 378.9 s |

No watched pressure rings on either side. **Trip 22.1 latches on the port** during the 40 t/h step:
with the reactor drawn down to 36 % 322E003's off-gas turns ammonia-rich, 8.3 mol % NH3 at design
to 17.2 % at 3 000 s and 19.7 % at 3 360 s, 322C001 absorbs more and its vent warms from 55.1 to
56.4 C, and TT-322015 crosses V1's 57 C high-high at 3 378.9 s; XV-322915's flood then holds it at
128-131 C. The margin it crosses is B-84's: 3.3 K at design since the trace steam.
