## LXV.1 FFIC-321404A / B, the ratio controllers (`units/feed/station.py`, handoff B-85 closed)

**Decided** 2026-10-09 (decision 92): the plant's PI ratio controllers built as drawn, trimming the
speed controllers, on the DCS table's 1.00 / 100 s and 1.00 / 90 s; V1's open-loop demand does not
reflect the plant's control structure.

**Read.** Uhde's functional diagram UD-MR-321-FF-0002 (scanned, read from the page images): page 2
FFIC-321404A over SIC-321950, page 3 FFIC-321404B over SIC-321951, page 4 FY-321404. Each ratio
controller takes FY-321404 as its MV; its output, divided by 100 and multiplied by the SIC's maximum,
is the SIC's external set point (E1REF); its balance (BALIN / BALREF) is the SIC's working set point
over that maximum, so a SIC not on cascade carries its ratio controller with it. FY-321404 =
FT-321401 [t/h NH3] / FYM-322403 [t/h CO2] . 44 / 17, the total ammonia over the CO2 to synthesis,
the same measurement for both machines. The loop summaries UD-MR-321-EC-0001 rev 1, F 321404A / B
(PDF pages 8, 9): function FFIC, realised in the control system, alarms high and low, range
0-4 "Ratio" (line D07). SI-321950's maximum is 180 rpm (decided in session 46).

**The equations** (`FeedStation._ratio_loop`; `data.unit_321` ``FY_321404_SPAN``,
``FFIC_321404A/B_KC/TI_S``):

    e        = ((N/C)_sp - (N/C)_PV) / 4 . 100                    [% of FY-321404's span]
    dOUT     = Kc (de + dt / Ti . e)                              velocity PI, Kc 1.00, Ti 100 / 90 s
    open_cas = OUT . 180 / 152                                    the SIC's external set point [%]
    SIC not in CAS:  OUT = WSP_SIC . 152 / 180                    WSP its set point in AUTO, the
                                                                  machine's opening in MAN

The PV is the model's published N/C, V1's molar ratio (M_CO2 / M_NH3 = 2.584 where the DCS block
writes 44 / 17 = 2.588), the last good value held below 5 % of the design CO2; the controller's
output is held with it there, so it does not integrate an error that is not being measured. The
ratio set point is V1's one (``ratio_set``), shared by both controllers; entering CAS still puts it
on the live ratio (V1's bumpless rule). The table's 2 % deadband is not modelled (B-28, §LXV.4).
V1's ``cascade_opening_pct``, the open-loop demand, is deleted.

**Measured** (the station alone, both ways in `tests/equivalence/test_feed_equivalence.py`, the
transcription's switch ``b85``; every per-tick comparison ``==``):

| case | V1's open-loop demand | FFIC-321404B over SIC-321951 |
|---|---|---|
| CO2 stepped down 10 % | N/C jumps 0.2248, back within 0.005 at 375.3 s | jumps 0.2248, back at 539.8 s |
| N/C set point 2.20 | settles the 1.90 at 294 s; the 2.20 never reached in 50 s (2.093) | inside 0.02 of 2.20 at 398.7 s, no overshoot (2.1808 at most) |
| 321P002A started, both on cascade | each machine's opening halved at once, N/C to 2.310 | the machine must be run up in AUTO first: at 40 % it takes the N/C to 2.584 while FFIC-321404B takes 321P002B down; on cascade both integrate the same error, the N/C inside 0.02 of design 349.2 s later, the duty 37.23 / 46.35 % |

The loop closes with a time constant of about two minutes (the process gain 0.72 % of span per %
of output at design), stable and without overshoot; a CO2 rate change is now a ratio disturbance the
controller corrects over its integral, where V1's demand followed the CO2 at once. Two machines on
cascade share no fixed split: each holds where the error closed. The design seed is unchanged
(FFIC-321404B's output 70.56 %, 83.561 % of opening). On the plant the synthesis harness's final
pins moved by the controller's response (the tempered water lost, 141.3424 bar a for 141.3496;
every per-tick comparison of the glue unchanged), and again with B-81, B-77 (b) and A-12 (§LXV.8).

## LXV.2 The letdowns' two-phase lines (`data/process_routes.py`, handoff B-81 closed)

**Decided** 2026-10-09 (decision 91): the homogeneous two-phase density for the transit downstream
of the letdowns, the step up from a liquid plug that invents no slip correlation.

**The equations** (``TWO_PHASE_SEGMENTS``, ``homogeneous_density``, ``LETDOWN_FLASH``):

    td    = (rho_l . V_up + rho_m . V_down) / m_dot
    rho_m = 1 / ( x / rho_g + (1 - x) / rho_l )

each valve's design flash at its outlet:

| letdown | x | rho_g [kg/m3] | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| LV-322501 | 0.13145 | 3.39 | PFD 301 over PFD 208: 650.46 kmol/h x 26.39 (the table's mass cell reads 1716, a digit short), 4.1 bar a, 119 C |
| LV-323501 | 0.04179 | 0.68 | PFD 701 over PFD 314, V1's ``R323_PHI_V701`` |
| LV-323505 | 0.02780 | 0.29 | PFD 319's sensible heat above its bubble point at 323F010's 0.46 bar a on the rigorous surface (82.34 C), cp 2.679, the pre-evaporator's latent 2280 kJ/kg; PFD 790's density — the PFD has no row for the valve's flash alone |

**Where each valve sits**, read from the isometrics (scans, the bills of material): LV-322501 on
UD-RL-100-MB-0014 sheet 1, after the 3.4 m of 120 pipe from 322E001/N2 (item 25), the 30.3 m of 160
pipe to 323C003/N1 after it; LV-323501 after the 400 run from 323C003/N5, the 200 line of MB-0138 and
its DN 400 1.0 m after it; LV-323505 on MB-0139 sheet 2, 0.29 m into the sheet's 1.2 m of 150 pipe
(50 + 133 + 105 mm to its flange), the 0.91 m after it with the sheet's 90 and 45 degree elbows
rising 1.72 m centre-line to 323E010/N1.

| route | volume [m3] | after the valve [m3] | rho_m [kg/m3] | liquid plug [s] | two-phase [s] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 322E001 -> 323C003 | 0.8879 | 0.8331 | 25.30 | 28.17 | 2.32 |
| 323C003 -> 323F004 | 0.8421 | 0.4941 | 16.05 | 32.63 | 13.75 |
| 323F004 -> 323F010 | 0.5677 | 0.0292 | 10.34 | 23.06 | 21.88 |

The other two routes run liquid-full and are unchanged. The flash is the design's: a line's live
dead time is still its inventory over the live flow (the inventory now 13.75 s x 105.9 t/h = 405 kg
on the column's bottoms line, 960 as a plug), but a line whose liquor does not flash — a cold line
at start-up — transits as fast as the design's two-phase line; a live flash fraction would need the
receiving stage's flash of the tick before at each inlet, a refinement not built. The equivalence

## LXV.3 AI-329701 shows a tube leak; the malfunction's rate (handoff B-90 closed)

**Decided** 2026-10-09 (decision 89): the contamination routed to the steam system's conductivity
analyser, "AI-329701 or the equivalent modelled drum analyser"; the malfunction command takes a
``rate``, 10 t/h when the panel sends a bare trigger.

**Read** (UD-MR-329-EC-0001 rev 1, the index and the loops, scans): A 329701, "329D001 Steam
Condensate Tank", function AI, realised in the control system with AH and SAHH, conductivity
0-10 uS/cm (line D07), low-pressure condensate on line 0-CPL2-329D001, P&ID 107/2 (PDF pages 6-7);
A 329702, "CPL fr. 322E002 HP Carb. Cond.", function AE, realised LO — a local sample probe, AE 329702,
on 50-CPL1-329048, P&ID 107/1 (pages 8-9). Unit 322's loop summary lists no analyser on 322D001A/B
or their blowdown (A 322701 the N/C meter, A 322711-714 the HP vessels, A 322751-754 on process lines).
So the DCS instrument that sees process in the steam system is AI-329701, on the LP condensate the
users of the contaminated steam return to 329D001; the urea a leak leaves in the drums' water does
not conduct, and no transmitter reads it.

**The equations** (`units/steam/condensate_analyser.py`; `data.unit_329`):

    c     = min(n_NH3, n_CO2) . 1000 / Q_LP users          [mol/L, a dilute condensate's litre a kg]
    kappa = 0.055 + (73.5 + 44.5) . c . 1000                [uS/cm at 25 C]
    AI-329701 = min(kappa, 10);  over range when kappa > 10

the limiting ionic conductivities of NH4+ and HCO3- and pure water's conductivity from the CRC
Handbook of Chemistry and Physics; the leak's ammonia and CO2 taken whole into the condensate of the
LP users' draws (the step ``329-USERS``, which reads ``322E002.holdup.leak``), the CO2 — the lesser —
pairing as ammonium bicarbonate, the excess ammonia, a weak base suppressed by the ammonium,
neglected. The dilute law holds inside the transmitter's range (c below 1e-4 mol/L); past it the
transmitter reads its top. 329D001's holdup is not modelled, so the reading follows the leak on the
tick; its working volume is logged (Open data gaps). The alarms' set points are DCS database values.

**Measured.** At design 0.055 uS/cm. A bare ``trigger_fault 322E002`` leaks 10 t/h: 295.2 kmol/h of
NH3 and 95.9 of CO2 into 52.2 t/h of LP condensate, kappa 216 624 uS/cm — the analyser pinned at 10,
over range. 0.1 kg/h reads 2.22 uS/cm; about 0.45 kg/h of leak reaches the top of the scale.

**Published** in a port block, ``ANALYSERS`` (`engine/packet/steam.analysers`; V1's paths stay V1's):
``AI_329701``, ``AI_329701_over`` and ``D001_solids_ppm``, the drums' solids from the leak. No
screen binds them yet: V1's screen 329-1 has no element for AI-329701, and a new element is a
``DECIDED_EDITS`` decision (decision 40).

**The panel** (`data/faceplates.MALFUNCTIONS`, `hmi/instructor/panel.py`): the tube leak is a
malfunction with a rate box, t/h, 10.0 to start, its TRIGGER sending ``{"type": "trigger_fault",
"id": "322E002", "rate": r}``. The engine (`engine/command._tube_leak`) takes ``rate`` or ``value``
and 10 t/h when the command carries neither (``unit_322e002.LEAK_DEFAULT_TH``); session 48's refusal
of a bare trigger is gone. The panel stays paused (A-2); it renders and sends, nothing else.

## LXV.4 A-18, B-84, B-28 and B-25 closed as decided

* **A-18** (decision 88): FAST runs as fast as the machine allows. The engine already pays the owed
  plant time in whole 0.1 s steps (A-14), so on a machine that ticks in 10.4 ms FAST runs at about a
  sixth of its nominal sixty; the physics sets the CPU cost and no interpolation table or
  approximation is introduced for a pacing target. Nothing changed in code.
* **B-84** (decision 90): trip 22.1 keeps V1's 57 C high-high and 55 C clear on TI-322015 with the
  trace steam's heat (§LXII.2); the HPCC rupture's cascade — the reactor drawn down, the off-gas
  ammonia-rich, 322C001's vent over 57 C (§LXIV.9) — is the emergent behaviour the simulator should
  teach. The DCS database's own value stays an open data gap.
* **B-28** (decision 93): the DCS table's 2 % deadband (1 % on LIC-322501) is not modelled on any
  loop. In a noiseless model a deadband only stalls the integral and leaves a permanent offset; it
  exists on the plant to stop an integral hunting on measurement noise, which the model has none of.
  V1's one use, LIC-329505's ``Dz=2% EU``, is set to zero too (``data.unit_324``
  ``LIC_329505_DZ_PCT``; the first evaporator's harness switch "B-28"): a 1 % set-point step leaves
  the condensate level at 50.0 % on V1's band, 51.0003 % without it after ten minutes.
* **B-25** (decision 94): 323D002 stays V1's species blender with no reaction. The design formation
  is below the PFD's resolution, under 0.005 wt% (§XXXI.6); an anchored kinetic term would
  over-model it. A trainee can hold Compartment I at 80 % without a biuret consequence — a recorded
  omission.

## LXV.5 PT-329201 on the loop's vapour inventory (`units/synthesis/loop_pressure.py`, handoff B-77 closed)

**Decided** 2026-10-09 (decision 95), on session 49's measurement of the pure vapour node: the
physical gas space — the vendor's 241.7 m3 less the live liquid holdups — with a linearised
carbamate buffering coefficient anchored on the design point's solubility, not a derivative of the
Extended UNIQUAC surface every tick. It replaces V1's lumped 1500 kg/bar.

**Measured before the build** (scratch probes on the port's cold start, the node patched in):

| variant | capacity | cold start (tau / dead time / final) |
|---|---|---|
| V1's lumped node | 1500 kg/bar | 3600 s / 420 s / 134.65 bar g (§LXIV) |
| vapour only, 241.7 m3 less the liquid | 194 kg/bar empty, about 72 at design | 990 s / 1320 s / 151.95 bar g, swinging 73-158 bar a on the half-hour samples |

**The equations** (module docstring; `data.unit_322_loop`):

    (C_vap + C_buf) dP/dt = (m_in - m_out) - f_loop . s . R_des - m_relief - (dM_liq/dt - rho_g . dV_liq/dt)
    C_vap = (V_loop - V_liq) . MW / (Z_des . R . T)            V_loop 241.7 m3, T TT-322009
    rho_g = P . MW / (Z_des . R . T)                            Z_des 0.7627
    C_buf = b_207 . M_R001                                      b_207 0.015364 kg/(kg.bar)
    b_207 = 1 / (141.3 . dln P_bub / dm)                        PFD 207 at 183 C, the design off-gas

* **V_loop**: 322R001 185.4, 322E001 24.7, 322E002 21.6, 322E003 10.0 m3 (session 40's reading of the
  arrangement drawings).
* **V_liq, M_liq**: 322R001's holdup at PFD 207's 990 kg/m3; 322E003's sump with what the scrubber
  holds back (B-78) at PFD 206's 1133; LT-322E002's holdup — its level law's own mass, 100 % =
  HPCC_LIQ_DES_LIVE x TAU_FILL_MIN = 18 926 kg — at the PFD's 1139 for 322E002's liquor; LT-322501's
  sump between its taps, 7 894 kg over the span, at 1134.64. The stripper's falling film and the sump
  below the lower tap are in no model state and stay in the vapour space. At design 153 151 kg and
  152.45 m3: 89.25 m3 of vapour.
* **dM_liq / dt**: each unit's holdup's gain over its own step, published in its result (322R001's
  ``dm_liq_kgh``, the sumps' and LT-322E002's ``dm_kgh``) — so an initial condition written into a
  holdup between ticks (the Phase 7 cold start, an exercise loaded) is not taken for a flow. The
  volume the liquid gains compresses the vapour it displaces, rho_g . dV.
* **Z_des**: the reactor's off-gas on the PFD, 113.3 kg/m3 at 141.3 bar a and 183 C, on the ideal gas
  law with its design molar mass: 0.7627, held for the live gas.
* **b_207**: `liquor_buffering_per_bar`, a central difference of ln P_bub (`thermo.vle.bubble_p_bara`)
  on PFD 207's composition at 183 C, adding and removing 1e-3 kg/kg of the design off-gas's NH3, CO2
  and H2O (54.5 / 41.8 / 3.7 % by mass). The model puts PFD 207's bubble point at 40.36 bar a, outside
  the window its LP stages validate; its logarithmic slope, 0.4603 per kg/kg, is lifted onto the
  stream's 141.3 bar a — V1's anchoring. 0.015364 kg/(kg.bar): 2 088 kg/bar on the design holdup of
  135 904 kg, beside the vapour's 71.6 — 2 160 kg/bar in all, 1.44 times V1's 1500. An empty reactor
  buffers nothing: the cold loop starts on its vapour alone, 194 kg/bar.
* **The backlog** (V1's G_ph . m_vap,net, the uncondensed vapour's pseudo-mass) adds nothing: what
  322E003 fails to condense is mass its sump did not receive, which the liquid inventory already
  carries. V1's ``SYN_LOOP_C_KG_PER_BAR`` and ``SYN_P_PHASE_GAIN`` are deleted from the port's data;
  the console's ``dP_phase`` is the backlog's share of the node's rate on its live capacity.

**The alternatives, measured and not taken** (for the process engineer):

| buffering | b [kg/(kg.bar)] | on the design holdup [kg/bar] |
|---|---|---|
| Extended UNIQUAC's slope, ratio-anchored on 141.3 bar a (built) | 0.01536 | 2 088 |
| the same slope unanchored (dP_bub/dm at 40 bar a) | 0.0538 | 7 315 |
| PI-322E002's melt law (V1's calibrated K_N 0.18, K_W -0.25), at PFD 207's N/C and H/C | 0.0709 | 9 640 |

The temperature-scaled variant was measured and not built: the anchored slope moves from 0.414 at
170 C to 0.499 at 190 C, about 8 % either side, inside the anchoring's own uncertainty. 322E003's
liquor (s 0.953) returns a negative slope on the same model — adding the off-gas lowers its bubble
pressure — and is not buffered; neither are LT-322E002's and LT-322501's liquors, whose design
compositions are not in the data.

**The harness** (`test_synthesis_loop_equivalence.py`, switch "B-77"): the transcription calls the
port's pure functions (`loop_liquid`, `liquid_growth`, `vapour_capacity_kg_per_bar`) on its own
states, the liquids' gains taken over its own tick; with the switch on every state of the glue is
``==`` the port's on every tick of every scenario. On the whole plant (§LXV.7) the HPCC rupture holds
the loop's pressure, but the cold start does not pressurise and trip 22.2 is not reached (B-91).

**The HPCC rupture.** The leak drains 322E002's liquor, which the vapour inventory carries as
liquid, not as the loop's pressure: PT-329201 falls 1.7 bar over the hour where V1's lumped node,
on the session-48 port, fell 5.9. The reactor is drawn down the same (35.8 %), the off-gas turns
ammonia-rich and 322C001's vent climbs, but on the loop's higher pressure TT-322015 stops 0.7 K short
of V1's 57 C: B-84's margin, now crossed only by a larger or longer leak. AI-329701 reads the leak's
bicarbonate from its first step — 2.5 t/h is 54 000 uS/cm on the dilute law, the transmitter at its
10 uS/cm top with its over-range flag — the instrument the plant's DCS shows the rupture on (B-90).
The two-phase lines (B-81) shorten the LP train's dead times; no scenario rings on them.

**The cold start does not pressurise on the vapour inventory** (handoff B-91, raised). The feeds are
V1's (CO2 54.5 t/h, ammonia 42.7 t/h on both engines), but PT-329201 climbs about a bar every
1 000 s — 14.6 bar a at 1 350 s, 20.0 at 3 990, 30.4 at 15 870 — where V1's lumped node reaches 90
bar a by 3 990 s and 146 by the end. The boundary's inflow goes almost whole into liquid: the
condensing units are anchored on the design and condense their design fractions at any loop
pressure, and the reactor fills to a third. V1's node counted that liquid as pressure, which is how
1500 kg/bar was tuned to the start-up trend; the vapour inventory counts only the vapour, which the
units leave none of. On the plant no carbamate liquor forms at 20 bar a and 170 C — its bubble
pressure is the loop's — so the gas stays gas and the loop pressurises. The buffering term adds to it:
b_207 is linear at the design and makes a liquor at 20 bar a absorb, where it would flash. The
session's pure-vapour probe (no buffering, the HPCC's and the stripper's liquid on assumed volumes)
reached 152 bar a, ringing. The decision's own test — the pressurisation "better than V1's lumped
approximation" — is failed; the options are B-91's.

**Trip 22.2 is no longer reached** with the tempered water lost: the loop climbs 5.4 bar in the
first 80 minutes and settles near 147 bar a, HV-322604's purge rising with it, where V1's node, which
counts the uncondensed vapour's pseudo-mass on 1500 kg/bar, climbs to 155 bar a in 5.6 hours. The
vapour 322E003 cannot condense now weighs on 2 160 kg/bar and the boundary finds a balance below the
high-high; the scenario no longer teaches 22.2 (B-91).

Session 50. The process engineer's paste of 2026-10-10 decided five items: B-91 option (a), the
loop's condensation and buffering capped by the liquor's bubble pressure at the live loop pressure;
the five AC4 hand switches and AI-329701 on the overlay screens through the converter's decided
edits; B-18, HV-322604 re-anchored at 72 %; B-37, PFD 734 routed to 323E003; B-20, 323C003's urea
closed on the drain. Its next step was the Phase 7 cold start and trip 22.2 in the 137.5-150.5 bar g
band. A second paste on 2026-10-14 asked for the suite cleared on the new baselines, the reactor's
runaway fixed by a boiling cap or a semi-implicit node balance, the 51 bar a plateau broken, and the
documents finished. It came with four data reports and the process engineer's handwritten readback
of the plant DCS of 13 October 2026 (`Urea Simulation Docs/Data/DCS_Extract_2026-10-13.jpg`), which
was read from the photograph: 323P008's low-level trip 5 %; TT-322015 HH 110; 324F003's vacuum
-0.9 bar g; AI-329701's H1 15 and H2 18; LIC-323502's gain 1.2, TI 400 s, TD 0, TF 0, DZ 2.0 %.
Decisions 97 to 103.

## LXVI.1 The loop's liquor condenses no more than its bubble point allows (`units/synthesis/liquor_saturation.py`, handoff B-91 option (a))

**Decided divergence, 2026-10-10 (decision 97).** V1's condensing units are anchored on the design
and condense their design fractions at any loop pressure. The port caps them on the saturation
fraction of the melt:

    d = (P_bub - P_loop) - (P_bub,des - P_loop,des)          P_bub,des - P_loop,des = 3.5 bar
    f = 1                       d <= 0
    f = max(1 - b_207 . d, 0)   d > 0                         b_207 = 0.015364 per bar

P_bub is PI-322E002 of the tick before (`condenser_holdup.p_bub_prev_bara`, seeded at the outlet's
design 144.2 bar a), the model's own bubble law for the melt; P_loop is PT-329201. The design head is
`data.unit_322_loop.LIQUOR_DP_DES_BAR`, a subtraction of the two design pressures (A-13). b_207 is
decision 95's buffering slope of PFD 207's liquor, read here as the fraction a bar of deficit takes
off what the liquor can hold. Where f < 1:

* 322E002's melt holds f of each distributing species' liquid: phi_gas = 1 - f (1 - phi_gas)
  (`carbamate_condenser.step(sat_frac=)`);
* 322E003 condenses at most f of its demand: cool = min(rho_cond, f) (`engine/plant/synthesis_loop`,
  322E003's input read from ``Result("322E002", "holdup.sat_frac")``);
* the reactor's liquor buffers f of its b_207 (`loop_pressure.step(sat_frac=)`: C_buf . f).

At and above the bubble pressure f is exactly 1 and every relation is the session-49 one, bit for
bit: the design seed is unchanged.

**Measured** (the loop started at 130.7 bar a, two minutes; `test_synthesis_loop_decided_equivalence`):
on the first tick the melt's design bubble pressure stands 10.0 bar above the loop's head, f =
0.8464; PI-322E002 falls to 123.0 bar a and f returns to 1; the loop ends at 130.4372 bar a, V1's
transcription at 130.4017.

## LXVI.2 322R001's liquor at its bubble point; the residence on the liquid passing (`units/synthesis/reactor_boil.py`, `reactor_inventory.py`, handoff B-92)

**Decided divergence, 2026-10-14 (decision 102).** The paste reported a 597 C runaway on the port's
cold start. V1's node balance (`reactor_hydraulics.node_dtdt`) has no ceiling; V1's own model run on
its own cold start reaches 420 C at 1 500 s, so the runaway is V1's, made larger on the port by the
lower loop pressure. The engineer offered a semi-implicit node balance or a boiling cap on B-62 /
B-24's class; the cap was built, since a semi-implicit step stabilises the integration but not the
physics — a liquor above its bubble point is not a state a bubbling column can hold.

    1 / T_bub(P) = 1 / T_des - (R / dH_vap) . ln((PT-329201 + 0.6) / 141.3)
    E_n   = m cp . tau_n . (T_n - T_bub) / dt                 every node above T_bub      [kJ/h]
    H     = n_CO2 . 117 000 + max(n_NH3 - 2 n_CO2, 0) . 23 000 + n_H2O . 36 900              [kJ/h]
    x     = min(sum E_n / H, 1)       the share of the overflow's NH3, CO2 and H2O that flashes
    T_n   = min(T_n, T_bub)

T_des is the pinned top node, 183.00 C, under the off-gas line's 141.3 bar a (PFD 207), 0.6 bar over
PT-329201's design (a subtraction of the two design pressures); the slope, 0.532 K/bar at design, is
PI-322E002's Clausius-Clapeyron law at 23 kJ/mol. The flashed moles move from the overflow to the
off-gas; the off-gas partial pressures and the reactor's off-gas pressure are recomputed on them.
What the volatiles cannot pay is published as ``q_boil_unpaid_kjh`` and leaves as sensible heat
(non-zero only on the first ticks of a state started far above its ceiling).

**The residence.** On the cold start the ceiling alone left PT-329201 near 45 bar a: the reactor's
outflow is zero while it fills, so its residence volume flow sat on the 1e-6 floor, the kinetics ran
to equilibrium and biuret, and 1 000 to 1 400 kmol/h of urea held the loop's mass in the liquid. The
kinetics' throughput is now the larger of the liquid that left the column and the liquid that
entered its holdup on the tick before:

    V_dot = max( max(m_out, m_in,prev) / rho_melt , 1e-6 )        m_in,prev seeded at PFD's overflow

At the design seed both are the PFD's overflow: the seed is V1's.

**Measured** (130.7 bar a start, two minutes): the bubble point 177.55 C under nodes at their design
temperatures; the port flashes 127.5 t/h on the first tick and its nodes end at or below the bubble
point, the top at 176.78 C; V1's top node stands at 181.76 C, 4 K superheated; PT-329201 130.4372,
V1's transcription 130.4761. At the design seed the top node settles at 183.02 C, 0.02 K above its
pinned bubble point, and the reactor flashes about 35 kg/h (handoff B-94).

## LXVII.1 PFD 734 as its departure from the PFD's row (`units/recirc/lp_carbamate_condenser.py`, handoff B-94)

The PFD's 323E003 balance closes on 305 + 718B + 776 + 797 = 321 + 308 without 734 (§LXVI.4), so
734 enters as its departure from PFD 734's 1534 kg/h (`data.unit_323e003.E003_M734_DES_KGH`):

$$ \Delta\dot m_{734} = \dot m_{734} - \dot m_{734,des} $$

in the tank's mass, in the sensible term, $\Delta\dot m_{734}\,c_p\,(T_{734} - T)$, and in the
semi-implicit capacity. At design FIC-323401 delivers 1534.0 kg/h to the bit and the departure is a
literal zero: the unit is V1's on every tick (`test_pfd_734_decided_divergence`, 600 ticks ``==``).
At 2000 kg/h, after half an hour, 323P001 returns 37 292.4 kg/h against V1's 36 835.2; on the unit
alone, after four hours, 37 304.4 kg/h (469.2 over the design) with the level back on 50 %; FIC-323401
shut, 308 carries 1544.6 kg/h less. ``m_734_kgh`` None is V1's (no 734).

**The design seed** (the steady state, an hour from the seed, §LXVII.8): 3080 of 3188 shared leaves
within 1 %, where session 50 had 2858 and session 49 3083. 323P001 settles 18 kg/h below its design
(session 50: 1.54 t/h above), 323D001 on 50.00 %, PT-329201 0.0009 bar above design in 45 minutes.

**B-92 at the seed, measured.** The bubble law returns exactly 183.00000000000003 C at 140.7 bar a,
the pinned top node, so the ceiling is zero at the seed state itself. It is not zero from the first
tick: V1's pinned node profile is not stationary on the live node chain — on the first tick node 0
falls 8.3 uK and the top node rises 6.05 uK (node 2 stands 0.045 K above its stationary under the
seed's own heats) — and V1's own top node, uncapped, settles 0.0224 K above its pin within the hour.
The ceiling pays that surplus as latent heat: 29.9 kg/h flashed on the first tick, 31 to 37 kg/h
over the hour. Without the ceiling the top node runs to 183.024 C and 322E003's new saturation reads
the hotter liquor (0.99971); with it 322E003's stays 1. Nothing was changed: the residual is V1's
pin's, not the ceiling's (handoff B-92 note, B-94 closed on the measured agreement).

## LXVII.2 322E003 on its own liquor's bubble point and on a full sump (`units/synthesis/scrubber.py`, `scrubber_sump.py`, handoff B-91)

**Its own liquor** (option (a)). The sump's liquor, the overflow it receives, at TT-322002, on the
model's law for the loop's melt anchored on PFD 206:

$$ P_{bub,E003} = P_{206}\,e^{\frac{\Delta H}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_{206}} - \frac{1}{T}\right)}
   \max(1 + K_N(N/C - N/C_{206}), 0)\,\max(1 + K_W(H/C - H/C_{206}), 0) $$

$P_{206}$ = 140.7 bar a, $T_{206}$ = 165 C, $N/C_{206}$ = 2.550 and $H/C_{206}$ = 1.299 (PFD 206's
NH3/CO2 and H2O/CO2), $\Delta H$ 23 kJ/mol, $K_N$ 0.18, $K_W$ -0.25 (PI-322E002's, `data.unit_322e002`),
the ratios clamped to 0.5-2 times design. No document gives the scrubber liquor's own law, and the
Extended UNIQUAC model returns a negative slope on PFD 206 (Open data gaps). 74.61 bar a at 125 C,
30.78 at 80 C. The saturation fraction is decision 97's on 322E003's own design head, zero (PFD 206
leaves at the loop's pressure): $f_3 = \max(1 - b_{207}\,(P_{bub,E003} - P_{loop}), 0)$ above, 1
below; the bubble pressure is the last overflow's (`ScrubberSump.p_bub_bara`), read on the next tick
as 322E002's is. It replaces 322E002's fraction in 322E003's gate: $cool = \min(\rho_{cond}, f_3)$.

**A full sump.** The condensate is capped at the room the sump has on the tick, net of the wash,
the carryover and the backlog it takes in any case:

$$ \dot m_{cond} \le \dot m_{room} - \dot m_{wash} - \dot m_{carry},\qquad
   \dot m_{room} = \dot m_{suction} + \dot m_{pulse} - \dot m_{recond} + (M_{max} - M - M_{held})/\Delta t $$

what it cannot take stays in the vapour, as the cooling gate's shortfall does (``sump_frac``,
published). Below a full sump the room is the tick's whole volume and nothing binds. Room for half
the design condensate passes 47 238.2 kg/h (the 36 915 kg/h wash and half the rest) and hands
10 323.2 back; none passes the wash alone; mass closes on every call.

The decision text's "0.30 floor" is COND_CHOKE_MIN, which floors the flooded-surface derate of the
shell DUTY (the published temperatures), not the condensation; V1's condensation has no level term.
The full-sump cap is the condensation limit the decision asked for.

**The retained gas — not built, measured.** The decision asked that the gas HV-322604's seat ceiling
holds back (``m_retained = w_offered - w_passed - m_recond``) be added to PT-329201's node. The node
already holds it: it integrates $(\dot m_{in} - \dot m_{out}) - \dot M_{liq} - \dot m_{relief}$ on
the loop's boundary, $\dot m_{out}$ counts only what HV-322604 passes (capped at the offer less the
uncondensed part, `purge_valve.seat_ceiling_kgh`), and the uncondensed gas is taken out of 322E003's
overflow before the sump, so it is in neither $\dot m_{out}$ nor $\dot M_{liq}$ — it is in the
vapour term by construction (decision 95, §LXV). Adding it again would count each kilogram twice and
make mass. Trip 22.2's shortfall is the node's balance (§LXVII.8), not a missing term.

**Both ways** (`test_the_loop_condenses_no_more_than_its_bubble_point_decided_divergence`, switch
``B-91`` now carrying 322E003's own liquor and the room; `test_synthesis_loop_equivalence.py`'s
transcription runs the port's scrubber under the switch).

## LXVII.3 The cold start against the plant's start-up procedure (option (b))

The HFC SOP (`References/Sources/HFC_Stamicarbon_Urea_Plant_SOP_Formatted.docx`, section 4, written
on Uhde's operating manual UD-VT-G00-DC-0003) and the 3 June 2025 trend
(`References/3.6.2025 Synthesis startup.md`) against the Phase 7 cold start (V1's
``test_transient_coldstart.py``):

| | the plant | the scenario |
|---|---|---|
| synthesis temperature | preheated to 125-150 C with steam (TT-322005 158.9 C at 11:20) | the design node profile, 170-183 C |
| 322E003 | filled completely with flush water before the feeds; its tempered water at 125 C until TDY-329125 shows condensation | empty; TIC-329005 at its design set point |
| HV-322605 | shut until LI-322504 shows 20 %, then ~50 % level; the trend: HIC-322605 0 until 14:20, LT-322504 100 % at 14:21 | its design opening from the first tick |
| CO2 | 70 % of design (FY-322403 ~20 000 Nm3/h) | the design feed lineup |
| N/C | 3.0 until the reactor overflows, 2.0 after | the design ratio |
| HV-322604 | completely open | its design 72 % |
| PT-329201 | 5.7 bar g at 11:15; 100.1 at 12:15; 131.0 at 13:24; 141.9 at 14:21 | 5.7 bar g at 0 s |

So the scenario starts the reactor at 0 % liquid with its outlet open, where the plant holds
HV-322605 shut until the level reaches 20 % (and fills the scrubber first). **The mass accounting
of the two nodes during the fill** (the decision's ask): V1's lumped node (B-77 (a)) integrates the
whole boundary on one 1500 kg/bar, so every kilogram the loop's liquids gain is counted as pressure —
the loop's liquid inventory at design, 137.4 t in 322R001 alone (B-77's 137 396 kg) and 3.8 t in
322E003's sump, is worth $137\,396 / 1500 \approx 91.6$ bar on V1's node. The port's node (B-77 (b))
counts only the vapour: $C_{vap} + C_{buf}$ = 75 + 2111 kg/bar at design, and the liquid's growth
$\dot M_{liq}$ is taken out before the pressure integrates. On the cold start V1 therefore rises with
the fill, the port with the vapour the feeds leave; a held-shut HV-322605 changes the fill's timing,
not this accounting. Building the plant's procedure into the scenario is not decided (handoff B-91).

| | PV-329203 (item 27, PDF p. 28) | PV-329212 (item 32, PDF p. 33) |
|---|---|---|
| valve | DN 250 Neldisc, metal-seated, L-ANSI150, spring to open | DN 80 balanced Neldisc, S-L-ANSI150, spring to open |
| maximum Cv (= FpCv) | 4870 | 150 |

## LXVIII.3 Solid ammonium carbamate in a dry letdown (`thermo/condensing_letdown.py`, handoff B-79 (b))

Admitted (decided 2026-10-14): E. P. Egan Jr., J. E. Potts Jr. and G. D. Potts, "Dissociation
pressure of ammonium carbamate", Ind. Eng. Chem. 38 (1946) 454-456:

$$ \log_{10} P_{diss}\,[\text{bar}] = 8.2697 - \frac{2741.9}{T},\qquad
   K_p = p_{NH_3}^2\,p_{CO_2} = \tfrac{4}{27}P_{diss}^3 $$

(1.017 bar at 58.7 C, 89 Torr at 25 C). A gas the liquor leaves dry — no aqueous root in the
Extended UNIQUAC range (method step 4) or no dew down to the single-phase answer — whose outlet
stands above the solid's saturation lays the solid down (step 5):

$$ n\,h_{SRK}(y, T_{in}, P_{in}) = V\,h_{SRK}(y_v, T, P_{out}) + s\,h_{carb(s)}(T),\qquad
   \ln(p_{NH_3}^2 p_{CO_2}) = \ln K_p(T) $$

$2\,NH_3 + CO_2 \to NH_2COONH_4(s)$, $s$ the deposit, $h_{carb(s)}$ Voskov and Voronin's
($\Delta H_f$ -645.05 kJ/mol, `thermo.enthalpy`), ideal-gas partial pressures. Solved by bisection
in T between the dry answer, where the balance is short of the deposit's heat, and the temperature
the gas just saturates at, where nothing deposits; at each T the deposit that puts the gas on
$K_p(T)$, by bisection. ``LetdownFlash.solid_kmolh``. HV-322604 carries the solid on to 322C001
as the NH3 and CO2 it holds, in its liquor, where the beds' liquor takes it up (the deposit kept in a
physical destination, decision 60's class), and raises its deposition alarm while it lays it
(``carbamate_deposition``). The design purge (94.8 C) is far below saturation: nothing deposits.

**Measured.** Session 40's lost-motive vent (38 % CO2, 5.2 % NH3, 81.07 C, 140.67 to 3.79 bar a):
the dry answer 29.60 C stands at p_NH3^2 p_CO2 = 0.057 bar^3 against Kp 6.5e-4; the line lays 4.449
mmol of carbamate per mole of gas and the outlet holds at 51.01 C, the gas left on Kp to 1e-9; the
enthalpy closes to 0.05 J/mol. 321P002B stopped on today's plant (300 s, both ways):

| HV-322604's outlet | 30 s | 90 s | 180 s | 300 s | lowest | solid |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| without the solid | -8.7 C | -9.0 | -36.8 | -35.4 | -38.2 | — |
| with it | 24.1 | 21.2 | -32.2 | -11.9 | -34.1 | 1.02 kg in 300 s, at most 0.66 kmol/h |

The vent turns to 97 % CO2 and 0.2 % NH3 by 180 s, so the deposit's heat lifts the outlet little
there; the single-phase answers are SRK roots (Joule-Thomson 0.69-0.93 K/bar), not a bracket. The
alarm stands 299.7 s with the solid, 296.4 s without. Both ways at the vent of 30 s:
`test_the_solid_lifts_the_purge_off_its_dry_answer_decided_divergence` (-8.69 against 24.03 C,
7.41 mmol per mole).

## LXVIII.5 LV-329505 on Flowserve's trim (`units/evaporation/first_evaporator.py`)

plug PODP1GG (Valtek modified equal percentage), LP condensate 8.5 / 20.1 / 27.1 m3/h at 4.1 -> 1.2,
3.7 -> 1.8 and 3.7 -> 2.2 bar a, 143 / 140 / 140 C, 921 / 924 / 924 kg/m3, vapour pressure 3.93 /
3.61 / 3.61 bar a, FL 0.99 / 0.99 / 0.9281; the capacity printed on the maximum case only, Kv 46.57
at 74 %, flashing. By IEC 60534-2-1 (session 37's method),

$$ K_v = Q\sqrt{\frac{\rho/1000}{\Delta P_{eff}}},\quad
   \Delta P_{eff} = \min(\Delta P,\ F_L^2(P_1 - F_F P_v)),\quad F_F = 0.96 - 0.28\sqrt{P_v/P_c} $$

gives 11.969, 32.366 and 46.548 (0.05 % under the printed 46.57): calculated, not printed. The design
stroke, where the normal capacity passes PFD 919's 18 489 kg/h, is 62.19 % (V1 linear from 50 % on
its span). The trap passes

$$ \dot m = \dot m_{cond,des}\,\frac{\phi(h)}{\phi(h_{des})} $$

on the modified equal-percentage curve, anchored on the chest's design condensate; no pressure
term (V1's trap has none). ``FirstEvaporator.lv_329505`` None is V1's; the harnesses run it.

## LXIX.1 323E011 on its dew point; PV-323203 never vents backwards (`units/recirc/flash_condenser.py`, handoff B-30)

V1 condenses a constant 5589 kg/h and generates gas only above it (§XXXII.2-3). The port takes the
form of 323E003's condenser — V1's dew point, with the cap at the gas that arrives removed (B-34) —
anchored on V1's constant at the design node, 1.13 bar a and 45 C against the 35 C water mean:

$$ T_{dew} = 45 + T_{sat}(P) - T_{sat}(1.13),\qquad
   C(P) = 5589\,\frac{\max(T_{dew} - 35,\ 0)}{45 - 35},\qquad gen = G - C(P) $$

and the vent's differential floored at zero (option (c), decision 80's class):

$$ \dot m_{702} = 440\,\frac{h}{25}\sqrt{\frac{\max(P - 1.0,\ 0)}{0.13}} $$

At the design node both are V1's to the bit (``condensation_capacity_kgh(1.13) == 5589.0``). The
capacity rises 14 122 kg/h per bar about the design, against the vent's 1700 and 323F004's flash,
2800; it is zero where the dew point meets the water, 0.79 bar a. Below the gas that arrives the
condenser draws on the node's gas, so the node has an equilibrium on both sides. The capacity's
slope makes the node stiff: on a tick where the explicit step would ring (a full envelope's 1.17 m3,
a 1 s tick) the pressure takes the backward step, the vent and the condensation at the pressure it
settles on (`core.node.stable_pressure_step`, decision 78's class); at the 0.1 s step on the plant's
volumes it never does. The energy balance still condenses what the tank receives, G - m_702; the
two differ only by the node's own inventory change, a few kilograms per bar.
``FlashCondenser(**V1_CONDENSER)`` is V1's, which every harness runs.

**Measured** (the condenser alone; V1's constant in brackets):

|---|---|
| PV-323203 held at 10 % / 50 % | 1.14798 / 1.10530 bar a (1.8125 / 1.0325) |
| 701 up 10 %, vent at 25 % | 1.1584 bar a within 4.4 s, 486 kg/h vented (1.52, 883) |
| 701 down 10 %, vent at 25 % | 1.10244 bar a within 6 s, 390.6 kg/h vented, no floor (0.1 bar a at 248.8 s, venting 38.6 kg/h backwards) |
| the same in AUTO | 1.1046 at 60 s, PV-323203 to 16.0 % in ten minutes, 1.1212 at 30 min (shut, the node standing at 0.896) |
| PV-323203 shut | 1.1615 bar a within 10 s, the condenser taking the whole gas; SV32357 never lifts (7.1 bar a at 100 s, lifting at 110 s) |
| PIC-323203 set at 1.30 | the vent shuts and the node stands at the 1.1615 ceiling (1.30 on 16.46 %) |
| with 323F004: the column bottoms cut 10 % | 1.1211 bar a, PV-323203 at 8.6 % passing 147 kg/h (1.129, shut) |
| with 323F004: the vent shut | 1.1559 bar a, 4349 kg/h flashed (1.286) |
| the flash lost (1 s tick) | the vent shut at 66 s, the node at 0.8753 bar a (0.695); the tank at its heel at 1993 s |

## LXX.2 Each inlet at its producer's live temperature (handoff B-31, decision 118)

V1 charges the LP condensers', 323C005's, 328D003's and 328C002's inlets at design temperatures,
literals or constants, whatever their producers do (§XXXII.6, §XXXIII.4, §XXXIV.3, §XXXV.3,
§XXXVIII.4, §XLI.2). The port charges each as its departure from its producer's design:

$$ T_{in} = T_{in,des} + (T_{producer} - T_{producer,des}) $$

so wherever a producer stands at its design the inlet is V1's to the bit, and an off-design thermal
upset crosses into its consumer's energy balance. A producer that steps before its consumer is read
on this tick (its ``Result``), one that steps after on the tick before (a declared ``State`` read or
a ``Tear``):

| unit | inlet | V1's [C] | producer | its design [C] | read |

| | 786 | 61 | 328D001 ``t_c`` (the overflow's, A-15) | 61 | this tick |
| | 321 | 74 | 323E003 ``t_c`` | 74 | this tick |
| | 791 | 56 | 328D003 compartment II ``t_ii_c`` | 56 | this tick |
| 323E003 | 305 | 119 | 323C003 ``t_c`` | 135 | this tick |
| | 718B | 45 | 323E011 ``t_c`` | 45 | tick before (``State``) |
| | 776 | 61 | 328D001 ``t_c`` | 61 | this tick |
| | 797 | 46 | 322C001 ``t_c`` (PFD 797: its inerts, 46 C) | 43 | this tick |
| 323C005 | 756 | 43 | 322C001 ``t_c`` (the solvent the vent already reads) | 43 | tick before |
| | 702 | 45 | 323E011 ``t_c`` (the overflow's tear, A-20) | 45 | tick before |
| 328D003 | 343 | 56 | 323C005 ``t_c`` | 55 | this tick |
| | 719, 720, 721, 759 | 45, 40, 41, 55 | 324E002 / E005 / E006 / E007's cold ends, ``nodes[tag].hot_out_c`` | the PFD's 45, 40, 41, 55 | tick before (tears ``t_719_c`` ... ``t_759_c``) |
| 328C002 | 775 | 61 | 328D001 ``t_c`` | 61 | tick before |

| | 750 | 140 | 328C004 ``t_c`` | 143 | tick before |

The utilities stay at their design values, as the decision states: 323E011's cooling water at its
35 C mean, 741 at 40 C (it leaves 328E001, the recycle cooler, not modelled), 322C001's 954 at 46 C
and 328C003's 911 at its 2235 kJ/kg drop. **708 stays at 121 C**: no unit computes 324F002's
discharge temperature — V1's vacuum train carries only its mass, 706 + 924, and so does the port's
— so it has no live producer temperature to depart from; handoff B-97 (new) carries it.

Each unit carries ``live_inlets`` (True; False is V1's design temperatures), each producer's
temperature a keyword argument defaulting to its design, so every unit-level harness that does not

neither plant-level harness needs it — the scheduler's runs the liquor train alone and `run_both`
compares the synthesis loop, outside which B-31, like B-30 and B-22, stays live. The schedule gains
eight declared tears (69 to 77) and the state four (``t_719_c`` ... ``t_759_c``, seeded on the
PFD's cold ends).

seed is not an exact fixed point (B-94): 323C003 leaves its first tick 1.2e-5 K off 135 C, 322C001

45.0200 against 45.0204 C, PT-329201 the same to 2e-11 bar.

## LXX.3 A-13 closed by its audit (`tests/engine/test_check_valve_audit.py`, decision 119)

The rule (2026-09-30): a design differential fed to an anchored law is the subtraction of its two
design pressures, never a literal, so the law's live differential at design is the same float. The
audit reads the source with `ast`:

* every module-level ``*DP*`` name under ``ureasim/data`` and ``ureasim/units`` is audited or named
  as no differential — ten differentials, each written ``a - b`` and equal to the float its two
  pressures make: XV-322902's ``CO2_DP_HP_DES``, 322E001's ``DP_TO_LOOP_DES_BAR`` and
  ``LV_322501_DP_DES_BAR``, 322E002's ``LEAK_DP_DES_BAR``, the loop's and the scrubber's
  ``LIQUOR_DP_DES_BAR``, 328C002's and 328C004's ``*_DP_COL_BAR``, 322R001's ``BOIL_DP_DES_BAR``
  and the stripper's ``LV_322501_DP_ANCHOR_BAR``; four are no differential — PV-323203's two floors,
  328P006's rated head (LV-328503's design inlet is built on the same sum) and the steam network's
  numerical probe;
* `check_valve_kgh` has one call site, XV-322902's tie-in (`units/synthesis/co2_line.py`), and it
  passes ``CO2_DP_HP_DES`` by name;
* the assembled flowsheet's first tick passes the design flows ``==``: the tie-in 54 618.0 kg/h of
  CO2, LV-322501's letdown 130 482.0 kg/h.

The one literal the audit found, ``LV_322501_DP_DES_BAR = 139.8`` (the CONVAL sheet's operating
point, fed to no law), is now ``P_DES_BARA - P_DOWNSTREAM_BARA``, the same float. The rule stays a
standing rule; the audit fails on any new differential written as a literal or left out of it.

## LXXI.1 708 at 324F002's discharge temperature (handoff B-97, decision 121)

V1's train carries 708's mass only, ``s["708"] = s["706"] + s["924"]``, and V1's 323C005 charges it
at the PFD's literal 121 C (§XXXV.3). The port computes 324F002's discharge on the ejector's first
law — the jet's kinetic energy recovered in the diffuser, so the discharge leaves with its inlets'
enthalpy — and publishes it as its departure from the same mix at design:

$$ T_{708} = 121 + \big(T_{mix}(n_{706}, T_{706}, m_{924}, h_g(P_{LP})) - T_{mix,des}\big) $$

The mix (`thermo/steam_gas_mixing.py`, new): 706 at 324E002's solved cold end, its water saturated
vapour there and its NH3, CO2, N2 and O2 on the H0 vapour datum (`thermo.enthalpy`, CODATA / JANAF
heat capacities; the formation terms cancel); 924 at the LP header's saturated steam enthalpy at the
live header, HV-329605 throttling it at constant enthalpy — the PFD's 924, 146 C at 4.1 bar a, is
that throttle of the PFD's saturated 4.4 bar a header to 0.3 kJ/kg (2742.67 against 2742.37); both
mixed at 323C005's 1.00 bar a, each species at its partial pressure, the water on IAPWS-IF97:

$$ \sum_k n_k h_k(T_{706}) + M_w n_{w,706} h_{g,sat}(T_{706}) + m_{924} h_{924} = \sum_k n_k h_k(T) + M_w n_{w,v} h_v(T, p_{w,v}) + M_w (n_w - n_{w,v}) h_f(T) $$

the water all vapour while its partial pressure stays under saturation, otherwise
$n_{w,v} = n_g p_{sat}(T) / (P - p_{sat}(T))$ and the rest condensed. The enthalpy rises with T, so
the root is unique; Illinois regula falsi on IF97's liquid range, [0, 350] C, to 1e-9 K — 13
evaluations at design, 0.38 ms a call on an idle machine. Declared approximation: NH3 and CO2 stay in
the gas when water condenses.

$T_{mix,des}$ = 125.6215 C, on the design solve of 324E002 (706: 0.8743 kmol/h of water, 0.5328 NH3,
0.1133 CO2, 1.1637 N2, 0.2909 O2, 72.0 kg/h at 45.000 C), the design 390 kg/h and the header's
design 4.0 bar g (B-69); the PFD's 121 C is 4.6 K under it — heat lost, or the licensor's own
balance — and the departure carries it. Measured (`vacuum_train`, the design rows otherwise):

| case | 924 [kg/h] | T_708 [C] |
|---|---|---|
| design | 390.0 | 121.0, to the bit |
| HIC-329605's motive halved | 195.0 | 112.917 |
| a fifth more | 468.0 | 122.527 |
| shut: 706 alone, its water condensing at the mixing point | 0 | 63.040 |
| stage 1's shell at 0.36 bar a (4.7 kg/h less 706) | 390.0 | 121.767 |
| the header at the PFD's 4.4 bar a | 390.0 | 118.400 |

The wiring: `VacuumTrainResult.t_708_c`; the train reads the LP header as HV-329605 does,
``State("329", "p_lp_bara")``; ``TearState.t_708_c`` seeded on 121.0, written from the train
(``TEAR_WRITES``), read by 323C005 a tick late — 78 declared tears. 323C005 charges it under
``live_inlets`` (B-31's switch; False is V1's 121 C). The design's 462 kg/h at 63.04 C instead of
121 C cools 323C005's liquor to 54.218 C in ten minutes, the vent and the absorption unmoved. On the
assembled plant the first tick's 708 is 121.00039 C — the seed's own relaxation (B-94) reaching
324E002's vent — and 120.99686 C after five minutes.

## LXXI.2 UF85 (unit 335): the dosing live (decision 123)

V1 builds the whole dosing — ``step_uf85_cascade`` (FFIC-335406, the ratio master, over FIC-335405,
the metering pumps' flow loop, LV-324501B its permissive) and ``route_lv324501``, which joins the
delivered UF85 to the forward melt — and never runs it: ``step_sim`` calls the cascade with the
recycle permissive forced and the selector at ``uf_ratio=0.0`` ("UF85 deferred (granulation off)").
FIC-335405 sits at 0 %, FT-335405 reads nothing, FFIC-335406 is frozen, and the product is the raw
melt. Asked, the process engineer chose live dosing (2026-10-16): the cascade on the live route,
LV-324501B its only interlock, and the selector on what the pumps deliver.

`units/finishing/uf85_dosing.py` (new; `data/unit_335.py`): V1's equations, on `control.ratio`'s
`RatioMaster` and a `FlowLoop`:

    ratio_PV = 1000 . PV_405 / m_402                     (0 on route B or with no melt)
    SP_405   = max(OP_406 . m_402, 0) / 1000            [t/h], FIC-335405 in CAS
    m_uf     = 694 . OP_405 / 50                          [kg/h], FT-335405 lagged 5 s
    609      = 402G + m_uf,  uf_ratio = m_uf / m_402      (`second_evaporator.melt_route`)

`melt_route` gains V1's UF85 terms (``uf_ratio``, default 0, so stage 2's own call is V1's live one,
bit for bit); `MeltRoute.uf85_kgh`. The selector stream is (m w + m_uf w_697) / (m + m_uf) at
(m cp T + m_uf cp_697 40) / (m cp + m_uf cp_697), the PFD's 697 at 40 C, 60 % formaldehyde, 25 %
urea, 15 % water.

The design. The PFD's 402G, 697 and 609 rows are the granulation section's own case: 85 405 kg/h of
melt is 2 050 t/d, the granulator's 2 000 MTPD, not the urea plant's 1 750. V1's ratio is the PFD's,
694 / 85 405 = 0.0081260, and its base flow the plant's drain, 75 938.1 kg/h at design (V1's
reconciled 402), on which the ratio doses 617.07 kg/h — the operating manual's 625 kg/h (§2.6, its consumption figures).
V1 seeds FIC-335405 at 694 kg/h and 50 %, the granulation case; live, that seed is no fixed point
(it relaxes to the ratio over many minutes, V1's master being slow). The port seeds it at the ratio
on the design drain, 617.07 kg/h at 44.4577 %, so the design holds; ``fic_335405(694.0)`` is V1's
seed. The stroke law stays anchored on the PFD's 694 kg/h at V1's 50 %.

The schedule: step "335" (V1's section 30) between 324E003 and the train, reading stage 2's drain,
its route's fractions and temperature and LV-324501B's selection of the same tick; it publishes the
dosing and the 609 route. Stage 2's own route stays V1's (no UF85), so the recycle tear to 323D002 is
unchanged; UF85 joins downstream of 324F003, so nothing upstream reads it. The packet's selector, its
closure and the UF85 fields are the dosing step's: the design's 609 is 76.56 t/h at 138.62 C, the
selector closing to the bit, ``uf85_kgh`` 617.1, ``uf85_m3h`` 0.47, FFIC-335406 in AUTO on its ratio,
FIC-335405 in CAS at 0.617 t/h and 44.5 %. All 274 of the screens' bound paths now resolve (the
session 41 count of 268 predates decision 98's six). FIC-335405 joins `data.faceplates.CAS_MASTERS`
under FFIC-335406, V1's front-end table; its modes were already in ``FACEPLATE_MODES``.

Measured (`tests/units/finishing/test_uf85_dosing.py`, the design drain at 140 C):

| case | measured |
|---|---|
| an hour at design | 617.07 kg/h within 2e-13; FIC-335405 at 44.457653 % |
| the melt down 20 % at 10 s | the master's proportional kick on the jumped ratio takes the flow under the ratio's 493.66: 498.77 kg/h at 30 s, 485.72 at two minutes |
| LV-324501B for 30 s | no UF85 into the recycled melt; FT-335405 to 0.0016 t/h on its 5 s lag; FFIC-335406 frozen; back on route A, 489.12 kg/h a minute later |
| FIC-335405 in MAN at 60 % | 832.8 kg/h on the stroke; the master tracks the achieved ratio, 0.010967 |

V1's master, 0.5 on the ratio and 60 s, is slow; neither loop has a row in the plant DCS's table and
Uhde's functional diagrams for unit 335 (UD-MR-335-FF-0002, eleven sheets, read from the scans) draw
neither, so V1's tunings stay and the two join the DCS-rows data gap.

Both ways (`tests/equivalence/test_uf85_dosing_equivalence.py`): from V1's seeds, through a 20 %
ramp, 30 s on LV-324501B and FIC-335405's four mode changes, every field of the cascade, both loops'
histories and the selector ``==`` V1's two functions on every tick; V1's executed call, the
permissive forced, ``==`` the port on the same switch; live, the port doses 617.07 kg/h where V1
doses none.

## LXXII.1 A-8: unit assignment by plant section, signed off (decision 124)

Kept as built in sessions 3, 41 and 42 (§LVIII.5, §LIX.6). The instructor assigns a trainee station
a set of plant sections (`data/tags.SECTION_IDS`: 321, 322, 323, 324, 328, 329, 335); the server
resolves each command to the section of the instrument the engine moves (`tags.section_of_command`,
reading the field the engine acts on, in its precedence) and refuses one outside, naming the
instrument, before the engine sees it. The engine's 41 plant command types (`engine.command.
PLANT_COMMANDS`) are all accounted for: the 38 an operator may send are each pinned to their section
(`tests/data/test_tags.py` ``test_every_plant_command_is_attributed_to_the_section_it_moves``), and
the three the instructor alone sends — ``trigger_fault``, ``clear_fault`` and ``co2_set`` — are
never narrowed, as an instructor is not. ``None`` is unrestricted and ``[]`` is assigned nothing,
different states on the wire; an instructor and the loopback superuser are never narrowed; an
assignment is kept by station name across a reconnect; a command the resolver cannot attribute is
refused for an assigned station (fails closed). Per-tag locking — two trainees inside one section —
is not built: the sign-off makes the section the unit of assignment.

## LXXII.2 A-2: the station token (decision 125)

A station declared its role in ``hello`` and the server believed it — right on a closed classroom
network, not on a routable one. The port now takes an optional shared token:

* `run.py`: ``--token T``, or the ``UREASIM_TOKEN`` environment variable (which keeps the token out of
  the process list), handed to the engine in ``server`` mode, to the console in ``station`` mode, and
  to both in the default mode. An empty token is no token.
* `net/protocol.py`: ``hello(role, station, token=None)`` carries ``token`` only when the station has
  one, so a token-less ``hello`` is the message it always was.
* `net/server.py`: ``StationServer(token=...)``. With a token, a ``hello`` that presents none, or
  another, is refused before its role is read — the superuser on the engine's own machine included —
  with the reason ("this engine requires a station token, and the station presented none"; "the
  station token is not this engine's"; neither echoes a token), logged, and the station disconnected
  so it cannot guess again on the same connection. The comparison is `hmac.compare_digest` on the
  tokens' UTF-8 bytes, its time independent of how much of the token was right. An empty token is
  refused at construction: it would read as a login and admit anyone. With no token the server
  checks nothing and every existing behaviour stands.
* `hmi/bridge.py`: ``EngineBridge(..., token=None)`` presents its token in every ``hello``,
  reconnections included.

The token admits a station; it does not grant a role. Among the admitted stations each still
requests its role, and the superuser is still granted only to a loopback peer (§LXI.7). A key per
role, which A-2 also named, is not built. Layout persistence stays per machine, in ``QSettings``.

**A defect found by the measurement.** The bridge's handling of a refusal said "no retry: the reason
will not change", and retried: its ``abort()`` emits ``disconnected``, whose slot scheduled a
reconnect and overwrote the refusal with "DISCONNECTED — link lost". On a real socket a console with
a wrong token connected three times in 1.5 s, and would have gone on every 5 s. Fixed: a refusal sets
a flag before the abort; the disconnect and error slots then leave the refusal's reason on the bar
and schedule nothing, the console blanks its indicators, and ``connect_to`` clears the flag. The same
path served the protocol-version and remote-superuser refusals, which no longer retry either.

## LXXIII.2 Trip 21.2's hand switches typed; TRIP_84_8_FLAG1 traced

**The hand switches** (decision 39: as the loop summaries type them; read from the scans):

| switch | loop summary | instrument | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| HS-321634, "Override Motor NH3-Pump" | UD-MR-321-EC-0001, H 321634 (PDF page 24) | keyswitch (controlroom), TEA0003 | control room |
| HS-321603, "Emergency Cut Off" | UD-MR-321-EC-0001, H 321603 (page 20) | emergency shut off switch (controlroom), HZ 321603, TEA0002 | control room |
| HS-321604, "Emergency Cut Off" | UD-MR-321-EC-0001, H 321604 (page 21) | emergency shut off switch (local), HZ 321604, TEA0001 | local |
| HS-322606, "Override SOH XV322902" | UD-MR-322-EC-0001, H 322606 (page 52) | keyswitch (controlroom), TEA0003 | control room |
| HS-323604, "Override Motor Carb. Pump" | UD-MR-323-EC-0001, H 323604 (page 60) | keyswitch (controlroom), TEA0003 | control room |

Each is a binary input to the DCS. The three bypasses are what A-12 built: maintained control-room
keyswitches. HS-321603 and HS-321604 are emergency shut-off switches, one in the control room and
one local. An emergency stop holds until it is released, so the port's maintained switch — operated,
21.2's inputs 5 and 6 lost until released — is the behaviour, and no logic changes. Their console
notes said "a maintained control-room keyswitch"; the converter now writes "the control room's
emergency shut-off switch" and "the local emergency shut-off switch" (`tools/convert_overlays.py`
``_ESD_NOTE``; `screen_layout.py` regenerated, the two notes the only change).

**TRIP_84_8_FLAG1.** AC4 PC21.5.1 (page 20) reads it as "DAT1:6/SG1-AC4-R0:VALUE3-TRIP_84_8_FLAG1".
The Safeguard SG1 writes it: UD-MR-G00-FF-0006, PC15 "units 304, 305, 306, 308, 384", sheet 8 (PDF
page 51, "TRIP 84.8"). Unit 384 is the instrument and service air.

    TRIP_84_8_FLAG1 = [two of three: not PT-384207A / B / C < L2] and not DISCREPANCY_84_8
                      and (TRIP_84_8_FLAG1 or RS_TR_84_8)

It is sent to AC2, AC3 and AC4 (AC4's on DAT28:6, SG1-AC4-S0 VALUE3); DISCREPANCY_84_8 comes from
AC3; sheet 9 sends the three transmitters' median to the DCS as PT-384207. The loop summaries

and ZALL on the ESD, 4.5 bar g normal, range 0-16 bar g, no setting printed. Trip 21.2 therefore
trips on a loss of instrument air, and the flag holds until its reset is pressed with the pressure

  (`tools/export_slides.ps1`, 2x and downsampled, as V1's migration rendered them), were compared with

## LXXIV.3 The liquid-rated valves' gas coefficient (decision 130)

SV32353 (328D001, orifice K), SV32357 (323D011, F) and SV32253 (322C001, M) are sized by Sempell on
liquid alone; the model relieves vapour through them (decision 34), on a gas coefficient the archive
was thought not to give — 0.917, SV32351/52's orifice T in the later file UD-RL-G00-DZ-0002-001, was
assumed. Sempell's orifice selections UD-RL-G00-DZ-0001-001 (163 sheets, AD 2000-A2, VdTÜV type test,
the same file as SV32353's and SV32357's) print, for every valve in gas or steam service at full lift,
"57 coeff. of discharge" 0.830 and "60 using coeff. of discharge" 0.922, whatever the orifice — J, L, M,
P, Q, R, T alike; a lift-limited valve prints less (0.353-0.705), and so do the smallest orifices
(E 0.723 / 0.804). On the three orifices wanted:

| orifice | valve, service | page | 57 / 60 |
|---|---|---|---|
| F | SV38107, gas (k 1.320, Z 0.81) | 130 | 0.830 / 0.922 |
| K | SV30909, gas (k 1.320, Z 0.41) | 62 | 0.830 / 0.922 |
| M | SV30203, gas (M 28.9, k 1.410) | 10 | 0.830 / 0.922 |

"60" is the coefficient Sempell's own "actual capacity" uses (the "calculated capacity" uses "57"), so
it is the one the API 520 law in `core/relief.py` takes: `data.relief_devices.GAS_KD_FULL_LIFT = 0.922`,
on SV32353, SV32357 and SV32253; SV32351/52 keep their own certified 0.917. Each valve relieves 0.5 %
more at a given state (SV32357 at 6.61 bar a: 886.4 kg/h where it was 881.6); on its shut-vent test
SV32357 now lifts every 25.1-25.3 s where it lifted every 25.4, and vents 36.6 kg in 400 s where it
vented 36.4. The open data gap is closed.

Session 59, 2026-10-17. The process engineer decided the question session 58 left: HV-323605,

/ B left catalogued (TIC-323013 models the tempered water's supply temperature directly, decision

## LXXV.1 The three valves on their trims (decision 131)

Each runs Metso's printed capacities as its curve (`control.valve.cv_fraction`'s printed form,
decision 108's class), its design stroke where its normal case passes the design flow
(`data.control_valves.design_stroke_pct`), and V1's law on a switch the equivalence harness keeps:

| valve | unit, law | design flow | design stroke | V1 | switch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HV-323605 | 323F010's vapour to 324E002, IEC 60534 compressible, anchored (`pre_evaporator.vapour_outlet_kgh`) | 12 013.3 kg/h, the overhead V1's balance gives (PFD 790 prints 12 040) | 64.08 %, xT 0.38 (normal case) | linear from 50 %, the globe valve's xT | `PreEvaporator(vent=V1_VENT)` |
| PV-323203 | the LP flash gas node's vent to 323C005, square root on the differential (`flash_gas_node.vent_valve_kgh`) | PFD 702, 440 kg/h | 21.64 % | linear from 25 % | `FlashCondenser(pv_323203=None)`, in ``V1_CONDENSER`` |
| TV-328002 | 328E004's cooling water on TIC-328002, the duty and TT-329007 on the water passed (`reflux_drum`) | PFD 1028, 408 t/h | 55.04 % | linear from 50 % | `RefluxDrum(tv_328002=None)` |

The laws:

    HV-323605:  w   = w_des . Phi(h, P1, P2, T1, M) / Phi(h_des, ...)        on phi(h), xT 0.38
    PV-323203:  m   = 440 . (phi(h) / phi(h_des)) . sqrt( max(P - 1.0, 0) / 0.13 )
    TV-328002:  Q   = min(Q_des . phi(h) / phi(h_des),  the decision-28 cap)
                TT-329007 = 30 + 8 . phi(h_des) / phi(max(h, 1 %))

each V1's own form with the trim's capacity ratio in place of h / h_des; the hand and controller
seeds — HIC-323605, PIC-323203, TIC-328002 — at the design strokes. The quoted 64.2 % for HV-323605
(§LXXIV.4) was the stroke for PFD 790's printed 12 040 kg/h; the valve passes the 12 013.3 V1's
balance gives, at 64.08 %.

What each does, measured:

* **HV-323605.** Its design xT, 0.38, chokes the valve once the 324E002 shell falls below 0.298 bar
  a at the design separator: there it passes at most 1.016 times the design overhead, where V1's
  globe xT passed 1.149 at 0.25 bar a. Both ways (`test_hv_323605_on_its_vendor_trim_decided_
  divergence`): the seed's own relaxation (B-94) parts the two on the first tick by 3e-8 bar; the
  324E002 shell to 0.25 bar a, V1's valve pulls 13 638 kg/h at once and its separator to 0.4319 bar
  a and 97.76 C after five minutes, the Neldisc pulls 12 196 kg/h and holds it at 0.4562 bar a and
  98.83 C. The unit's own tests restate a pinched or opened valve as the same fraction of its design
  capacity V1's strokes were of its 50 %: at half (32.04 %) the separator holds 0.538 bar a after two
  hours (V1's trim 0.530); opened to 1.6 times (79.09 %) it boils 3288 kg/h of its own at 0.404 bar
  a (2936 at 0.410); at a fifth (12.82 %) the choked valve passes 5.30 t/h at the 1.0 bar a clamp
  (6.31 on V1's), the separator stays above its design vacuum and the leg drains it to its heel at
  about 5000 s, where V1's settles at 6.5 % — and there the explicit species step is not stable
  (handoff B-98, §LXXV.4).
* **PV-323203.** The valve is large for its duty: the design sits low on its curve and its gain per
  per cent of stroke there is 1.85 times V1's; wide open it passes 10.3 times PFD 702 against V1's
  4.0. Held at its design stroke the node does exactly what it did at V1's 25 %. Both ways
  (`test_pv_323203_on_its_vendor_trim_decided_divergence`, PIC-323203 on V1's 0.60 %/bar on both
  sides): PFD 701 up 10 %, bit-exact until PIC-323203 first moves the stroke at tick 11; an hour on
  V1 at 1.3380 bar a on 31.11 %, the Neldisc at 1.2784 on 26.66 %. On the decided gain, the unit's
  cut trims to 13.2 % in ten minutes where V1's trim reached 16 %, and a 10 % cut in the column
  bottoms settles the node at 1.122 bar a on 6.6 % (V1's trim 1.121 on 8.6 %).
* **TV-328002.** At its sheet's 21.2 % it passes 24.3 % of its design water (V1's law 42.4 %), at
  90.5 % 3.08 times (1.81). Both ways (`test_tv_328002_on_its_vendor_trim_decided_divergence`): the
  strokes differ at the seed and the duties do not, so the two part on TIC-328002's first output and
  nothing else; 737 cut a fifth, V1 closes 10.5 points to 39.50 % and its drum stands at 59.050 C,
  the Neldisc closes 9.3 points to 45.73 % and stands at 59.303 C.

The plant-level re-pins: the synthesis loop's decided harness shares the port's steam network, so
V1's side of three tests moved by 1-3e-4 bar or 0.03 kg (B-75 141.4894, B-76 3650.52 kg, A-12's CO2
case 139.5413 bar a).

## LXXV.2 The process-deviation scenarios: what is put to the plant

`D:\Work\Urea Simulation\References\scenarios` holds four notes: `Scenarios.md` (the reactor and the
concentration train), `Scenarios2.md` (the synthesis loop, the LP and the waste-water sections),
`Scenarios3.md` (the LP condensers, the tanks, the desorbers) and `Scenarios4.md` (valve steps and
lag times). They are generic — "a Stamicarbon plant", an atmospheric flash tank, a 99.7 % melt, a
steam-driven HP ejector — and the fourth is an analysis of V1's own source files (its works cited are
`reactor.py`, `main.py`, `main_backup.py`). So they are not plant data (CLAUDE.md §4): nothing is
calibrated on them. Each claim is an expectation, measured on the port.

`tests/phase7/deviations.py` puts every section of the four notes on Helwan's plant: 78 deviations
carrying 191 claimed responses, each on the console's own lever (`engine.command`: a faceplate's set
point or output, a hand valve, a steam valve), applied after a settling minute on the design seed,
run 10 to 30 minutes, and each claim read off the published packet as the deviation's departure from
an unperturbed control run at the same plant time — at the end, or at its extreme on the way. The
control absorbs the seed's own drift (B-94). A departure inside 1e-4 of the indicator's value reads
as none, and so does one below the indicator's display resolution: the comparison is what the
console shows. Where Helwan's plant differs from the note the deviation is put on the equipment the
section describes (323F004 at 1.13 bar a for the "atmospheric flash tank", 322J001's liquid-ammonia
spindle HIC-322602 for the "HP ejector", 323P001 for the "lean carbamate pump" that feeds the HP
scrubber), and a claim no indicator publishes — a crystallised line, corrosion, cavitation, biuret
per stage, carry-over to a vent — is listed with the deviation as unmodelled, not invented.

`python -m tests.phase7.run_deviations OUT_DIR --workers 16` runs the 79 plants (45 minutes on this
machine; a wide-open HV-322605 or a starved stripper costs the solver several times a design tick).

## LXXV.3 The results

**147 of the 191 claimed responses come out as claimed.** Every section has its main response as
claimed: the levels, the pressures, the concentrations and the slips move the way the notes say for
the levels raised and lowered (S1-5.4, S2-2.2, S2-4.2, S3-1.2, S3-2.2, S3-3.2, S3-4.3), the steam
moved (S1-3.1, S1-4.1, S1-5.1, S2-2.1, S2-5.2, S2-5.3), the drum pressures moved (S1-3.2, S1-4.2,
S3-1.3, S3-2.3), the valves stepped (S2-2.3, S2-4.3, S4's steam supply, letdown, off-gas, ejector and
chest), the condensers' water moved (S3-1.4, S3-1.5), and the losses of seal blow through (S1-2.2,
S2-2.2b, S2-4.2b). The 44 that differ:

| class | claims | what the model does, and why |
|---|---|---|
| **defect, raised** | 11 | **A-21**: HV-322605 wide open (S1-1.2, S2-3.1a) — the stripper sends 76 % of its doubled feed overhead, its bottoms vanish and read 100 % NH3, the CO2 cannot enter, PT-329201 reaches 155 bar a and every trip latches at 37 s; V1 verbatim holds 140.7 bar a (3 claims). **A-22**: a full 323F004 has no ceiling — LI-323505 reads 100 % while its holdup grows, nothing reaches 323E011 (S1-2.1, 2 claims). **B-99**: 322E003's condensation does not answer its tempered water — TIC-329005 to 75 C or FIC-329409 to 360 m3/h leaves its duty at 5327 kW, PT-329201, LT-329501 and the overflow unmoved (S2-1.4a / b, 6 claims) |
| **a controller holds it** | 7 | TIC-324001 holds 130 C, so a lost vacuum takes less steam, not more (S1-4.2a); TIC-323007 holds 135 C on a column pressure moved either way (S3-6.1); PIC-322201 holds 322C001 (S1-1.1); FFIC-329401's ratio raises 328C004's steam with its feed, so NH3 slips less (S2-5.1); TIC-328002 and PIC-328202 hold 328D001 (S3-2.4, S3-5.1b). The notes describe the open loop or an operator's compensation |
| **no lever moves it** | 3 | PIC-324203 moves PT-324203 by 0.001 bar either way (its bleed valve's authority, B-61's finding): S1-5.2a / b's vacuum loss and deepening are not reached on that lever; a motive-steam loss is what breaks it (the Phase 7 vacuum break) |
| **unmodelled mechanism** | 8 | an empty 324F003 leg admits no air (S1-5.4b); 328D001's uncondensed vapour is V1's law on 737 and 328E004's duty, not on the absorbent 718A (S3-2.4); 323E011 condenses on its dew point (B-30), not on its wash 791 (S3-3.1b, 2); TT-328008 publishes 328C002's own top, the reflux's effect is on TIC-328008's inferential, which moves as claimed (S3-5.1, 2); the starved stripper's film does not dry out (S2-3.1b); inerts do not suppress the reactor's conversion (S4-offgas-close) |
| **below the display** | 3 | PT-329201's 0.1 bar resolution hides a transient under it (S2-2.1a, S2-3.1b peaks); TT-329125 falls 0.09 K where a slow rise is claimed (S2-1.2) |
| **the note against the model's physics** | 12 | S1-1.1: the reactor spills its 183 C melt into the off-gas line when full, which warms 322E003's gas (TT-322002 +1.7 K) where the note has it cooled, and the loop pressure falls 0.9 bar rather than spiking; S2-1.1: TT-322012 rises 3.1 K as claimed, then falls below the control as the scrubber drains; S2-1.3: more recycle carbamate brings more NH3 and CO2 than its water absorbs — PT-329201 +0.2 bar, TT-322012 +4 K; S2-1.4b: more tempered water cools 322E003 (the note's tempering-cooler bottleneck is not on the model; B-99); S2-2.1: 322E002 raises 0.7 % LESS LP steam when the stripper strips more, and 0.1 % more when it strips less — measured, not explained, for the process engineer; S2-2.2a: a filling stripper holds its drain back, so 323C003 boils less until the level settles; S2-4.1a: 323C003's boil-up is capped at its design split (V1), so more steam raises its temperature, not its vapour; S4-offgas-open: the note's Joule-Thomson cooling below 20 C is V1's artefact — the port's HV-322604 letdown condenses its gas onto the liquor (decision 38) and its outlet warms 9 K; S4-offgas-close: the conversion rises 0.2 points with the loop pressure; S4-ejector-close: closing the spindle drives the suction (V1's law, and Scenarios2 §1.1's own physics), which drains 322E003 — Scenarios4 claims the opposite of Scenarios2 |

Two runs that agree hide a defect: S2-3.1a (HV-322605 to 100 %) is A-21's collapse, and its claims
agree only because the reactor drains as the plant trips. S4-chest-close's melt cools to 58 C as the
vacuum deepens over a 324F001 that no longer boils — below where an 80 % urea solution crystallises,
which the model does not represent (no flag is raised, unlike the stripper's and the scrubber's).

The note's lag times (Scenarios4: the steam header 1-3 s dead time and 30-90 s time constant, the
ejector's vacuum under 1 s and 10-45 s, the stripper's level 5-10 s and 60-120 s, the reactor's
thermal profile 30-60 s and 8-360 minutes) are its own deductions from first principles, not plant
measurements; they are not pinned, and the port's are not identified here (the cold start's FOPTD on
PT-329201 is Phase 7's measured one, §LXII.4).

## LXXV.4 The species step at a heel (handoff B-98)

Restating LXXV.1's nearly shut HV-323605 exposed it: on the Neldisc at a fifth of its design capacity
the choked valve holds 323F010 above its design vacuum and the barometric leg drains it to its 1 kg
heel at about 5000 s. There some 80 t/h passes a 1 kg holdup, a residence of 0.045 s against the 1 s
tick, and the explicit species step (`liquor_stage.advance_species`, V1's ``sol_advance``) takes the
drained composition at the old holdup's: water and urea floor at zero and the liquor reads 0.000 %
urea and a 372 C bubble point until the level recovers (73.0 % again by 10 800 s). V1's linear trim
never reaches the heel in that case (it settles at 6.5 %). The backward step on the drained
composition,

    (M w)_new = [M_pre w + (m_in w_in - m_vap y + nu xi) dt / 3600] / (1 + m_liq dt / (3600 M_new))

measured in scratch, holds the heel at 74.5 % urea and is the explicit step's to 0.001 % away from
it; taken only where the explicit step would overshoot (m_liq dt / 3600 > M_new), decision 78's
class, it would leave every other state V1's to the bit. Raised, not built. (Corrected in §LXXVI.2:
the 74.5 % was the even-tick phase of a ring the explicit vapour draw leaves at the heel.)

## LXXV.5 Tests

`tests/phase7/test_deviations.py` (new): every deviation well formed, every path resolving in the
port's packet, the engine accepting every command at the seed (78), the verdict on a constructed
record, and one deviation end to end (LV-322501 to 90 %, two minutes: the stripper's level falls).
The three valves: each unit's tests restated or re-pinned to the vendor trims (§LXXV.1) and a new
test each (`test_pv_323203_on_its_vendor_trim`, `test_hv_323605_on_its_vendor_trim`,
`test_tv_328002_on_its_vendor_trim`); each equivalence harness on V1's law through its switch,
``==`` V1 tick by tick, and one both-ways test each.

`python -m pytest` — **7 507 collected** (88 new: 82 in `tests/phase7/test_deviations.py`, three vendor-trim tests and three both-ways tests for the valves), thirteen parallel parts, every part green on its first run. Re-pinned to the vendor trims: 27 unit tests of 323F010, 323E011 / 323D011, the gas node and 328D001 (restated where they held a valve at V1's stroke), the equivalence harnesses put on V1's laws through their switches, and three synthesis-loop tests whose V1 side shares the port's steam network (1-3e-4 bar). pyflakes clean; the headless grep prints nothing.

## LXXV.6 Not done

A-21, A-22, B-98 and B-99 raised with options, not built: A-21 and B-99 move decided or V1 physics,
A-22's destination is a routing choice, B-98 a new numerical mechanism. The notes' claims the model
answers differently on its own physics (§LXXV.3) are recorded for the process engineer; none is
built on, the notes not being plant data. PV-323202A / B stay catalogued (decision 131).
