# Part XCIX — The intro on the GPU (A-26) and a frozen engine's packet (A-27) (decision 169)

Session 87 (2026-11-04) took the process engineer's directive closing A-26 and A-27, the two items session 85 left
open. The advisor (Opus) was consulted on the plan before any edit and on the result before the close. No relation
of the plant changed: A-26 is the intro's drawing and A-27 is what the engine publishes while a plant is held. Both
were built so that nothing the plant computes moves (a test and a four-process run hold that for A-27).

## XCIX.1 A-26: the intro's frame rate, windowed and fullscreen (decision 169)

**What was asked.** 60 fps or better, 16.6 ms a frame and 10 ms as the target, windowed and fullscreen at 125 %
display scaling, with everything below `painter.py` Qt-free, the offscreen test platform unchanged, and the wire
raster attacked by a GPU canvas, a fixed-stage layer, or both, whichever profiling favoured.

**How it was measured.** The real `IntroSplash` under its own 16 ms timer, the hold phase after a 2 s settle, 6 s a
run, three runs a cell with the two renderers alternating inside the cell so the machine's drift reaches both alike,
on the development machine (i7-12700H, 20 logical processors, Intel Iris Xe, on AC power, 125 % scaling, display
60 Hz). Load is *k* busy-loop processes. The metric is the `paintEvent` time on the main thread (median, 95th
percentile, worst), the 95th percentile of the interval between frames, and the frames in three runs that came more
than 25 ms after the one before. The figures of session 85 (15.0 ms, 17.5 ms and 52 fps fullscreen) were taken on a
machine in another state: the same code measured 10.0 and 12.6 ms hours later, so no closure is claimed from an idle
figure and every cell below is an A/B in one sitting. The raster delivered rate is 62.7 fps because it is paced by
the 16 ms timer; the GPU canvas is paced by the display's vertical sync, 60.2 fps.

**What was tried, in order, and why the GPU canvas stands.**

| candidate | measured | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| fixed-stage wire layer: the wires at 1366 x 720, pixel ratio 1, composited scaled onto the device-resolution window | windowed 125 %: wires direct 3.94 ms, layer 2.70 + scaled composite 1.66 = 4.36 ms; fullscreen: 5.81 against 3.76 + 2.55 = 6.31 ms; 100 %: 2.90 against 2.83 + 0.38; edge energy 1.77 to 1.13 (-36 %) and 1.50 to 1.00 (-33 %) at 125 % | rejected: slower, and softer |
| a cache per quantised orbit azimuth | one device-resolution frame is 6.1 MB (9.2 MB fullscreen), 360 steps 2.2 GB, and 360 steps in the 32 s orbit is 11 poses a second, which stutters at 60 fps; the bob and the flow dots have other periods | rejected on arithmetic |
| worker threads for the wire raster | `QPainter.drawLines` holds the GIL: two threads 0.96 times one, four threads 0.99 times | rejected |
| a cosmetic pen for the thin batches | 2.39 ms against the hairline rule's 2.17 ms for the 12 batches at 125 %, ink +0.3 % | rejected: no gain |
| a GPU canvas, a multisampled `QOpenGLWidget` painted through the same `IntroPainter` | below | adopted, with the CPU rasterizer as the fallback |

The unthrottled cost of a frame is the same on both: the GPU canvas is bound by the GPU and the compositor at 13.5 ms
windowed (74 fps) and 15.6 ms fullscreen (64 fps), the rasterizer by the CPU at 12.3 ms (81 fps) and 15.1 ms (66 fps).
What the canvas changes is where the cost falls. The main thread's share becomes about the same at any window size,
and the machine's CPU stays free for the rest of the application. The baked paper still pays on the GPU (7.2 to 7.8
ms a frame against 8.3 to 9.0 without it), so the painter is unchanged.

**The result** (median of three runs, hold phase; paint = `paintEvent` on the main thread; "late" = frames more
than 25 ms after the one before, summed over the three runs):

| window | load k | renderer | fps | paint median | p95 | worst | interval p95 | late |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| windowed | 0 | CPU | 62.7 | 11.5 | 13.3 | 18.9 | 16.6 | 0 |
| windowed | 0 | GPU | 60.2 | 7.5 | 8.5 | 10.2 | 17.2 | 0 |
| fullscreen | 0 | CPU | 62.1 | 14.2 | 16.3 | 21.5 | 17.5 | 0 |
| fullscreen | 0 | GPU | 60.2 | 8.2 | 9.5 | 13.1 | 16.9 | 0 |
| windowed | 2 | CPU | 62.7 | 12.3 | 14.9 | 22.2 | 16.6 | 0 |
| windowed | 2 | GPU | 60.2 | 7.7 | 9.0 | 13.1 | 17.0 | 0 |
| fullscreen | 2 | CPU | 60.8 | 14.8 | 17.9 | 23.3 | 19.1 | 0 |
| fullscreen | 2 | GPU | 60.2 | 8.7 | 10.1 | 14.5 | 16.9 | 0 |
| windowed | 4 | CPU | 61.7 | 13.2 | 18.1 | 28.7 | 19.3 | 5 |
| windowed | 4 | GPU | 60.2 | 7.6 | 10.1 | 21.8 | 17.2 | 1 |
| fullscreen | 4 | CPU | 58.1 | 15.3 | 19.3 | 26.0 | 20.8 | 4 |
| fullscreen | 4 | GPU | 60.2 | 8.6 | 11.1 | 21.5 | 16.9 | 0 |
| windowed | 8 | CPU | 51.0 | 18.2 | 24.2 | 29.1 | 25.5 | 64 |
| windowed | 8 | GPU | 50.8 | 16.0 | 19.9 | 24.6 | 24.7 | 41 |
| fullscreen | 8 | CPU | 42.4 | 21.6 | 27.5 | 32.4 | 29.7 | 250 |
| fullscreen | 8 | GPU | 60.1 | 14.5 | 18.9 | 23.5 | 20.4 | 1 |

**What is claimed, and what is not.**

* The target of 10 ms holds for the main thread's paint time: 7.5 ms windowed and 8.2 ms fullscreen at idle on the
  GPU canvas (95th percentile 8.5 and 9.5 ms). It does not hold for the whole frame, which is bound by the GPU and
  the compositor at 13.5 and 15.6 ms unthrottled (above); at 60 Hz that leaves 1 ms of margin fullscreen on this
  integrated GPU.
* 60 fps is held through *k* = 4 of the 20 logical processors in both window modes on the GPU canvas (interval 95th
  percentile 17.2 ms at worst, one late frame in 3 runs), where the CPU rasterizer drops to 58.1 fps fullscreen and
  has 5 late frames windowed and 4 fullscreen. At *k* = 8 the windowed intro holds 60 fps on neither renderer (51.0 and 50.8 fps), and the
  fullscreen one holds it on the GPU canvas alone (60.1 against 42.4 fps). So the claim is 60 fps to *k* = 4 in
  both modes, and fullscreen to *k* = 8 on a GPU; it is not an unconditional 60 fps.
* A GPU that something else is using was not tested.

**First seconds** (frames from the first paint to 3.7 s, the scan phase, two runs): GPU windowed 60.4 and 60.5 fps with
no frame late; GPU fullscreen 61.2 and 57.9 fps with none and two late frames; CPU 62.8 fps in every run and none late.
The first frame is painted 58 to 65 ms after `play()` on the GPU canvas (78 to 96 ms on the CPU), with the first two
intervals 31 to 43 ms windowed from shader compilation, and one interval of 154 ms about 0.15 s into the first
fullscreen run (the scene is still the faint backdrop then). They are one-off.

**Where it is used.** `ureasim/hmi/intro/canvas.py` holds the canvas and the probe. `opengl_available()` is decided
once: false on the Qt platforms with no OpenGL (`offscreen`, `minimal`, `vnc`, `linuxfb`), false when the environment
variable `UREASIM_INTRO_RENDERER` is `raster` (the kill switch, in the README), and otherwise the answer of an
off-screen context: version 2.0 or later and a renderer that is not a software one (GDI Generic, the Microsoft Basic
Render Driver, llvmpipe, softpipe, swrast, a software rasterizer), which on a driver-less machine, a virtual machine
or a remote session would be slower than the CPU. The probe takes about 165 ms. `IntroSplash` creates the canvas as a
child that fills it, takes no mouse events and calls back into the splash's own paint routine, so the painter, the
scene and the data are the raster path's. If the canvas has no valid context 1 s after the window shows (`RENDER.
settle_s`) the splash deletes it and draws itself. The constants are `RENDER` in `data/intro.py`. Layering is as it
was: the scene, the flyby, the camera, the sequencer and the data import no Qt (`test_intro_layering.py`, which now
lists `canvas.py` with the Qt modules); `painter.py`, `canvas.py`, `splash.py` and `__main__.py` are the four that do.

**Three behaviours the move changed, each checked.**

* `repaint()` on a `QOpenGLWidget` paints nothing at once (the widget renders when its window's update request is
  delivered), and the start-up controller paints its status line with `repaint()` before a step blocks the event loop.
  The splash now asks the canvas to update and delivers the update request itself. Checked on the screen: with the
  GUI thread blocked, 2,990 footer pixels changed after `set_status` and `repaint()` on the canvas, 3,141 on the
  rasterizer.
* The exit fade is `setWindowOpacity` on a frameless window now hosting a GL child. Checked on the screen: the patch
  of paper reads 247 at full opacity and 103 at 0.3 and returns to 247 (rasterizer 231, 99, 231, on another frame).
* The picture. At the hold frame at 125 % the canvas reads edge energy 5.08 against the rasterizer's 5.06, ink 110.9
  million against 111.2, a mean difference of 1.11 in 255 and 1.3 % of the pixels differing by more than 32 (text
  and the finest edges); without multisampling the edge energy is 5.75 (aliased), at 8 samples 5.00. A test holds
  the canvas to 3 in 255, 5 % of the edge energy and 2 % of the ink.

**The real start-up path under the canvas** (`run._run_with_intro` driven by script, a screen grab from a plain thread
every 0.6 s): press, "Building screens", "Starting engine", "Connecting to the engine", "Starting the plant", the
console shown with a live packet (heartbeat 12) and the intro finished, no bridge blank during the start-up; the grabs
show the status line and the busy button on screen while the console builds. The same script on the CPU rasterizer
gives the same sequence (heartbeat 13).

**One finding that shaped the tests.** With about 60 shown GL splash windows alive in one test process, a later
`splash.grab()` crashed the interpreter (a Windows access violation). A script with seven live GL windows and a grab
ran clean. One splash exists in service, but the existing splash tests, which build a window each and never close
it, now draw on the rasterizer (`IntroSplash(opengl=False)`), so no test depends on the machine's GPU; the canvas has
its own tests (`test_intro_canvas.py`): the renderer names, each reason for no canvas, the probe made once and its
failure logged, the fallback when a canvas has no context, and, where a GPU exists and skipped elsewhere, the
canvas's frame against the rasterizer's, its mouse transparency and `repaint()` against `update()`.

**Retracted.** An early figure given in conversation, 13.4 ms for the GPU path against 8.8 ms for the rasterizer,
came from a harness that overrode `paintEvent` on the `QOpenGLWidget`, which is not how one is painted (`paintGL`), so
it did not draw the scene. Nothing from that harness is in this part.

## XCIX.2 A-27: a reset or a restored exercise while the engine is frozen (decision 169)

**The fault.** `EngineSession._install` (`reset_sim`, `snapshot_load`) builds a new `Scheduler` whose `results` are
empty, and `packet()` returned `{}` until the next tick. A running plant steps within a tenth of a second, but a
frozen one never does, so the engine published nothing for as long as it was held. The console's bridge, once it
has had a packet, is on the strict 5 s watchdog (`STALE_MS`) and blanks every indicator on silence, which is right
for a dead link and wrong for a live engine held by its instructor. Session 85 had seen this on the engine only.

**The decision (process engineer, 2026-11-04, session 87).** The engine publishes a packet for the plant it has
been given and does not step the plant to do it. The directive named the held start at launch as well; asked, the
process engineer kept decision 166 and A-25 point 2 for it, so the plant behind the start-up intro still publishes
nothing until 100% LOAD releases it (the start-up controller reads the first packet as the plant running), and the
thermo memo is still not warmed there. Reset and restore are the cases.

**The mechanism (`ureasim/engine/rehearsal.py`, `ureasim/engine/session.py`).**

* A packet is built from the results of a tick, so the plant's first tick is *rehearsed*: its state is copied the
  way an exercise save and restore copy it (`snapshot.encode_state` and `decode_state`), the scheduler ticks the
  copy once, and the copy's clock is put back to the plant's. The plant itself is never ticked: its clock, tears,
  controllers and historian are as they were (a test holds the plant's encoded state equal before and after).
* The packet carries the plant's own time, `t_sim` 0.0 after a reset and the exercise's own time after a restore;
  `server.publish` already sent `t_plant` with it, so the two clocks agree.
* The rehearsal is made lazily, where the packet is built, and only for a plant installed since the engine started.
  Made at install time it would be missed when a `reset_sim` and a `freeze` are drained in one gap, the plant
  frozen before a packet is asked for; a test drains them in that order.
* It is kept until the plant changes under it: an accepted plant command (a set point, a valve) drops it and the next
  packet rehearses the plant as it now stands, so a held console shows what the command did; a refused command
  changes nothing and does not. The first real tick drops it for good.
* A plant that cannot be rehearsed publishes nothing, as before, logs the fault once, and is not retried every pass.

**What it costs and what it leaves.**

| | measured |
|---|---|
| rehearsal after `reset_sim`, thermo memo warm | 16.7 ms (the copy 2.7 ms, the tick 11.2 ms, the packet 2.7 ms) |
| rehearsal after `snapshot_load` of an off-design state, memo warm | 56 to 82 ms |
| the same packet rebuilt each pass while held | 1.9 ms |
| first rehearsal in a fresh process, memo cold | 1.4 to 1.5 s, the cost the first real tick pays (a plant is not reset cold in service: the memo is warm by then) |

*No trace.* Four fresh processes, each running the plant 60 ticks after the install, with and without the rehearsal:
the plant's encoded state and the packet hash are equal to the last digit for `reset_sim` (state 8f923f70198c3ff9,
packet 1079badf752a2c87) and for `snapshot_load` of a 20 s off-design exercise (state c62f5ed1b55d9aa2, packet
a9a01a36b5e040c1). The twin computes the same first tick the plant is about to, so the thermo memo holds what the
plant's own tick would have put there. *Equality.* The packet shown for a held plant equals the packet its first real
tick publishes, but for `t_sim`, at the seed and 5 ticks in (`tests/engine/test_rehearsal.py`,
`tests/engine/test_session.py`). What the console shows is therefore the plant's first tick, one step (0.1 s) ahead of
its state and labelled with the plant's time: below any instrument's resolution at the design seed, and one step of
its dynamics for a restored exercise.

**Through the console (`tests/hmi/test_console_while_frozen.py`).** The engine (`EngineSession`, `EngineHost`,
`StationServer`) on its own thread and loop, a real `EngineBridge` and `MainWindow` on loopback TCP, at the real
`STALE_MS` of 5000 ms, with the strict window in force before any wait (the engine is started running, since a console
that has never had a packet is on the 30 s allowance and would pass for the wrong reason):

* freeze, `snapshot_save` at a known plant time, run on, freeze, `reset_sim`: the reset plant's packet (`t_sim` 0.0)
  is on the console 135 ms after the command was sent, and over the next six seconds, past the watchdog, the console
  has more than 30 packets, no DISCONNECTED, the engine label FROZEN, a bound readout other than `--`, and the plant
  not one tick on;
* `snapshot_load` of the saved exercise: its own `t_sim` on the console 98 ms after the command, and the same six
  seconds;
* released, the plant steps on from where it was put and the label reads RUNNING;
* with the link up and the engine's thread stopped, the console blanks 5.0 to 6.5 s later with "no data from the
  engine", every readout `--`;
* a closed link blanks it at once with the socket's reason, not after the watchdog.

The three scenarios take about 13 s, 5 s and under a second. `tests/net/test_engine_host.py` holds the host's side:
about ten packets a second after a freeze and a reset and after a restore, `t_sim` where the plant was put, the
plant not stepped. Eight deliberate breaks of the fix (no preview, the launch plant previewed, install keeping an old
rehearsal, a command leaving it stale, a refused command rebuilding it, a failing rehearsal retried every call, the
copy keeping its own clock, the plant itself ticked) were each caught by a test, the refused command's only after the
counting test was strengthened; a ninth, dropping the rehearsal on the first tick, changes memory only and no
behaviour.

**Found on the way: a silent engine looks live between blanks (handoff A-28, not changed).** After the watchdog
fires, the bridge reconnects, and `StationServer` replays its last published packet to any console that connects.
With the engine's thread stopped and the server up, the console's state followed: blank at 5.1 s, live with the dead
engine's last packet at 6.1 s, blank at 11.2 s, live again at 12.2 s, so it shows stale values as live for about five
seconds in six, which the bridge's own rule (a console that keeps the last values looks live and is not) forbids. The
watchdog test above passes because it asserts at the first blank. The replay is meant for a console that joins a
running engine, where the packet is a tenth of a second old; it carries no age. Raised as A-28 for the process
engineer's decision.

## C.3 The licensor's load procedure

Uhde's Operating Manual Part III (UD-VT-G00-DC-0003 rev. 00, ten scanned files mapped by the archive's TOC,
UD-AM-G00-AB-0022 pages 18-19) was rendered at 200 dpi and read with Windows OCR, sections 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8:

* page 4-16 (4.1.5.2): the synthesis is started on 70 % of the design CO2, a fill step before the reactor
  overflows;
* pages 4-18 to 4-20 (4.1.5.4-5): TIC-329005 to about 80 C once the scrubber condenses; PI-329201 to about 136 bar by
  the LP drums' master; 329D005 at about 17.0 bar before the overflow; LI-322504 about 50 % on HIC-322605; the stripper
  outlet 168-173 C; feed N/C 2.0, reactor N/C 2.9-3.1;
* page 4-28 (4.1.5.9): the load raised in 10 % steps, the reactor N/C 2.9-3.1, PI-329201 near 141 bar on PIC-329207,
  PIC-329204 for 7.9 wt% NH3 and 168-173 C at the stripper outlet, HV-322604 against inert accumulation and 322C001's
  overload, the scrubber run for its largest water rise (about 15 C at 245 m3/h), 322E003's level on the spindle;
* page 6-3 (6.1.2): a planned stop first cuts the load to 70 %, the feed N/C at 2.0, in the reverse of 4.1.5;
* page 1-82: PIC-329204 between 17.0 and 20.0 bar, dependent on the plant capacity; page 1-58: the ejector "also
  self-regulating to a certain extent"; page 1-24: biuret rises below design capacity;
* pages 7-51 to 7-56 (7.2.4): the analysis-based conversion urea / (urea + 1.365 CO2) in wt%, worked to 58.8 % at the
  reactor outlet with N/C 2.89, and the stripping efficiency urea / (urea + 1.765 NH3), 0.80 in the example.

Both 70 % statements are transitional, on the way to the overflow or to the stop. No minimum load is stated, and
no set point for 75-95 % or above 100 %. The open literature (CRU Nitrogen+Syngas,
UreaKnowHow round table "Problem No. 24: Why is the minimum urea plant load 60%?", 2014) puts the usual floor near
60 %, consistent with Book2's 60.7 % hold; it enters no cell.

## CI.1 Neldisc: Valmet's S-Disc table reproduces the five balanced valves (data gap 7)

Valmet bulletin 2SL120EN (4/2022, public) is the Neldisc with the flow-balancing trim, the "S-Disc"; its Table 2 gives
Cv / Cv max at 10-100 % opening for ASME 150, 300 and 600. The Metso sizing sheets (`UD-MR-G00-DZ-0031-009`, PDF pages
29-33, read from the page images) print "BALANCED NELDISC, valve serie S-L-ANSI150" on PV-329207A, PV-329207B,
PV-329208 and PV-329212, and "S-L-ANSI300" on PV-329204. Their printed points against Table 2 (the class's column):

| Valve | Column | Deviation at the three printed points |
|---|---|---|
| PV-329212 | ASME 150 | +0.7, +0.6, +0.4 % |
| PV-329207A | ASME 150 | -0.2, -0.2, -0.1 % |
| PV-329208 | ASME 150 | +1.0, +0.2, -0.1 % |
| PV-329207B | ASME 150 | +1.2, -0.8, -1.2 % on the catalogue Cv 2580 (+6.7, +4.6, +4.2 % on its FpCv 2447.16) |
| PV-329204 | ASME 300 | +0.4, -0.2, -1.3 % on the catalogue Cv 1640 (+2.6, +2.0, +0.9 % on its FpCv 1604.25) |

* The module's linear chord (decision 108, kept by decision 153) departs from Table 2 above each valve's last printed
  travel by -2.9 to +4.6 % of rated Cv (PV-329207B +4.6 % at 70 %, PV-329212 -2.9 % at 90 %). Every design stroke lies
  below the last printed point, so the design point does not depend on it.
* **Correction to §LXXXVI.4.** Session 71's "the sheets print up to 30 % less than the bulletin" compared FV-329401's
  0.228 at 52.9 % with 0.326. 0.326 is Table 2's ASME 150 value at 52.9 %, the S-Disc's, and FV-329401 is a
  conventional (unbalanced) Neldisc. Against FV-329401, PV-329202 and PV-329203 the S-Disc table is 28-36 % high;
  the finding was a family mismatch, not a disagreement between the sheets and the vendor's curve.
* Bulletin 2LW22EN (1/2024, public), the conventional Neldisc, says "nearly equal percentage" and prints full-open Cv
  by size, with no Cv-against-opening table. The nine conventional valves still have no table. Indicative only, not a
  datum: a pooled ln-quadratic fit through their 15 printed points, anchored at 100 % = 1.0 (rms residual 5 %), puts the
  chord 13-22 % above the curve at 70-80 % travel for FV-329401, PV-329202 and PV-329203.
* Adopted as decision 170 (CI.5), superseding decision 153 for these five valves, with both sides measured (CLAUDE.md §5.6). The
  route stated here, normalising on the catalogue Cv with Fp kept separate, was replaced by anchoring on the printed points.

## CI.5 The build: decision 170, both sides measured

Approved by the process engineer ("Adopt, measure both") and built 2026-11-06. One change to the route CI.1 stated:
the trim is not normalised on the catalogue Cv. It is anchored on the sheet's printed points, which keeps every printed
capacity and the rated FpCv (so PV-329204's and PV-329207B's full-open capacity does not rise 2.2 and 5.4 %) and
makes the Fp question moot.

* **The trim.** `control_valves_metso._s_disc(rated, cases, ansi_class)`, ``S_DISC_RELATIVE_CV`` (the 150 and 300 columns).
  With T(h) Table 2, linear between its nodes and zero at h = 0 (an assumption: the table starts at 10 %), and the anchors
  shut, the printed points and wide open, each segment is y(h) = y_a + (T(h) - T(h_a)).(y_b - y_a) / (T(h_b) - T(h_a)).
  Every printed point is reproduced to the bit, the table's 10 % nodes are added between them (a node on a printed
  point, as PV-329207B's 10.0 %, is the printed point), travel and capacity are strictly rising (the inverse divides by
  both steps). The five valves: PV-329204 on ASME 300, the others on ASME 150 (the sheets' valve series); the nine
  conventional Neldiscs keep `_neldisc`, the chord.
* **The curves**, capacity as a fraction of rated at 20, 30, 50, 70 and 90 % travel, chord then S-Disc:
  PV-329204 0.1440 0.2275 0.4192 0.6701 0.8954 then 0.1289 0.2063 0.4118 0.6736 0.9018;
  PV-329207A 0.0888 0.1446 0.3280 0.5459 0.8486 then 0.0858 0.1397 0.2947 0.5377 0.8719;
  PV-329207B 0.1166 0.1905 0.3383 0.5627 0.8542 then 0.0907 0.1471 0.3089 0.5537 0.8763;
  PV-329208 0.0894 0.1467 0.3130 0.5568 0.8523 then 0.0864 0.1402 0.2949 0.5378 0.8720;
  PV-329212 0.0984 0.1476 0.3067 0.5413 0.8466 then 0.0866 0.1410 0.2969 0.5401 0.8726.
  The largest departure on a 5 % grid is 0.046 of rated (PV-329207B at 40 %: 0.264 on the chord, 0.218 now).
* **The design strokes**, where the normal case passes the PFD flow: PV-329207B 54.9630 to 55.9717 % (its design flow lies

# Part CII — The start-up intro's LOAD button: the plant started from a saved exercise (decision 171, session 90)

Session 90 (2026-11-06) was a side session started by session 88 on the process engineer's request of 2026-11-05: a
"load" button on the start-up intro that loads the saved exercise files. Session 88 had written steady states into
the repository's `scenarios` folder (each held 15 minutes with every transmitter within 1 % and no trip), in the
product's own exercise format (`engine/snapshot.py`, "ureasim-exercise" version 1). The session ran in the main
checkout beside session 88 and session 89, the parallel "Open gaps" session, which took decision 170, Part CI and
A-29 meanwhile; this is decision 171, Part CII and A-30. The advisor (Opus) was consulted on the plan before any edit
and on the result before the documents. No relation changed; in the engine only `EngineSession`'s exercise folders
changed.

## CII.1 What was asked, and what the process engineer decided

The brief: a second pill, "LOAD", beside "100% LOAD", with a start key of its own; after it the console asks the
engine for its exercises, the operator chooses one over the intro, the engine restores it, and only then is the held
plant released; the hand-over ends on the first packet after the release, because a plant restored while held
publishes its rehearsed first tick (decision 169); the start-up wait does not run while the chooser is open; the
repository's `scenarios` folder is offered by default; 100% LOAD behaves as before. Three points went to the process
engineer, who answered them twice on 2026-11-06, differently here and in session 88; asked which answers stood, the
process engineer settled them in this session:

* **Cancel, or no saved exercise:** the intro goes back to its two buttons with the reason on its status line, and
  nothing starts until the operator presses one.
* **A refused exercise** (a file the present model will not take): the chooser opens again with the engine's reason,
  the plant still held. The brief had the hand-over end with the reason, which would show a console whose plant is
  held and publishes nothing, blank within 30 s and reconnecting until the instructor pressed RUN.
* **SAVE writes the instructor's folder**, outside the repository (CLAUDE.md section 6's clean tree), and LOAD lists
  the shipped `scenarios` beside it.

## CII.2 The intro's last frame

`data/intro.py` gives each pill its own `StartOption` (key, label, width, label and icon offsets, glyph, and whether it
restores an exercise); `ButtonLayout` keeps what the pills share and gains the gap. `START_OPTIONS` orders them left
to right.

| Pill | Key | Width x height | Glyph | x (design px) | Restores an exercise |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100% LOAD | `load_100` | 250 x 56 (unchanged) | play triangle, icon_dx -81 | 113 to 363 | no |
| LOAD | `load_exercise` | 160 x 56 | folder, icon_dx -46 | 387 to 547 | yes |

The row is centred on the text column (cx 330, 434 units wide, gap 24). Each breathing ring reaches ring_gap + 2 = 7
units from its pill at the top of its breath, plus half its 2-unit stroke, so neighbouring rings stay 8 units apart.
Both pills, rings included, lie inside the flyby's "text column" clear zone (x 56 to 604, y 56 to 566), where the
wireframe is at its floor, and left of the stage's centre. The labels, measured with the painter's own font, sit clear
of their glyphs and 12 units inside their pills.

`scene.button_at(x, y)` names the pill under a design-space point (None between and beside them); `button_rect(key)`
is a pill's hit area, the 100% LOAD pill's by default; `build_frame(button=...)` takes one `ButtonState` for every
pill or one per key. The splash lights the pill under the pointer, takes one press at a time (the sequencer's gate)
and announces the pressed pill's key on its `START` event; both pills are drawn working once one is pressed. Enter and
Space press 100% LOAD only, so "PRESS ENTER TO START" and the keyboard start are as before; LOAD has no key. A press
the application withdraws (`splash.rearm(status)`, the sequencer's `cancel_start`, allowed only while starting and
before the console is ready) puts the buttons back, live, with the status line given.

## CII.3 The hand-over after LOAD (`hmi/startup.py`)

```
press LOAD -> build the console (hidden) -> wait for the engine -> connect the bridge
   -> LIST:    ask for the exercises (exercise_list)                    the wait for the engine runs
   -> CHOOSE:  the chooser over the intro                               nothing sent; the wait stopped
   -> RESTORE: snapshot_load {name}                                     the wait restarted, whole
   -> RELEASE: freeze, on false (decision 166's release), once the restore is accepted
   -> RUNNING: the release accepted; the next non-empty packet ends the hand-over
   Cancel, or no exercise -> IDLE: the intro's buttons back, nothing sent, the wait stopped;
                             the next press goes on from the console and link already up
```

* **The release waits for the restore.** It goes out only on the restore's acceptance, so a plant is never released
  from the design seed while an exercise is on its way.
* **The end waits for the release's acceptance.** A restored plant publishes its rehearsed first tick while held
  (decision 169); the server can send a pass's packet before that pass's ack, and rehearsed packets keep coming until
  the first real tick. Gating on the acceptance makes all of them harmless. The rehearsal is the packet the first real
  tick publishes, so a rehearsed packet that follows the acceptance shows the released plant.
* **The wait.** `STARTUP.packet_timeout_s` (45 s) runs over the list step, stops when the chooser opens or the buttons
  come back, and starts again, whole, at the choice or the next press, so the operator's time is never charged to the
  engine.
* **Reconnects.** The held engine publishes nothing, so a link the chooser or the waiting buttons keep open is dropped
  and reconnected by the bridge's first-packet watchdog (`FIRST_PACKET_STALE_MS`, 30 s), every 30 s. Each step's
  message goes out once per link and again on the next: the list asked again, the chosen exercise restored again (a
  second restore of the same file leaves the held plant where the first did), the release sent again; IDLE sends
  nothing. `QTcpSocket.abort()` on a connected socket emits `disconnected` at once (measured), so the controller sees
  every drop.
* **A refused exercise** opens the chooser again over the intro with `STARTUP.refused` ("The engine refused exercise
  {name}: {reason}") as its note and on the status line; a refused `snapshot_load` installs nothing, so the plant is
  held and untouched; the wait stops again. A refused release still ends the wait with the engine's reason.
* **Cancel, or no saved exercise** (an empty list, or one the server refused), calls `splash.rearm` with
  `STARTUP.no_choice` ("No exercise chosen") or `STARTUP.no_exercises` ("No saved exercise to load", with the server's
  reason when it gave one). The plant is still the launch plant, held and silent. The console is not built again: the
  next press, 100% LOAD or LOAD, sends its first message on the link that is up, or on the next one.
* **100% LOAD** keeps its steps: the release once per link, the first non-empty packet the end, a refusal or a silent
  engine the console shown with the reason. Only its send moved into a helper; its tests are unchanged and pass.

## CII.4 The chooser (`hmi/exercise_chooser.py`)

A `QDialog` opened with `open()`, not `exec()`, over the intro: a nested event loop would run the bridge's slots inside
it. It lists the names the engine sent, in the engine's order, the first selected; LOAD, Enter and a double-click
choose the selected name, CANCEL, Escape and closing the window choose none, and the answer is given once. A note (the
refusal) stands above the list with `CHOOSER.retry`, "Choose another exercise, or CANCEL to go back to the start
buttons." It is dumb in CLAUDE.md section 4a's sense: it opens no file dialog and reads no folder (a test reads its
imports); the engine restores by name. The controller takes the chooser as a callable, as the instructor's panel takes
its `confirm`, so the tests hand in their own. Full screen on the GPU canvas (decision 169) the chooser is the active
modal window and the topmost at its centre: `WindowFromPoint` at its centre returned its own window, and a desktop grab
shows it over the intro.

## CII.5 The exercise folders (`engine/session.py`, `run.py`)

`EngineSession(exercise_dir, shipped_dir)`: `exercise_dir` is the instructor's folder as before (`UREASIM_EXERCISES`,
else `~/ureasim-exercises`); `shipped_dir`, when given, is a folder of exercises shipped with the simulator, read and
never written. `exercises()` lists every valid name of both, each once; `snapshot_load` restores a shipped name from
the shipped folder, any other from the instructor's; `snapshot_save` refuses a shipped name ("... is an exercise
shipped with the simulator: save under another name") and writes the instructor's folder. A shipped name therefore
always means the verified file: no save shadows it, and a copy put in the instructor's folder by hand is listed once
and not restored. Without `shipped_dir` the session behaves exactly as before. `run.py` passes `SCENARIO_DIR`, the
repository's `scenarios`, on both of its paths (the intro and `--no-intro`), so the intro's LOAD and the instructor's
RESTORE list the same exercises and SAVE never writes the repository. On this machine `UREASIM_EXERCISES` is set
nowhere (user, machine, process), `launch.bat` sets none, and `~/ureasim-exercises` does not exist. Every file in
`scenarios/` loads on the present model with `snapshot.load(path, build_plant()[1])`, pinned by a test that reads no
file's contents and skips when the folder is empty; `scenarios/` is to be committed with this work, or that test and
the real-link scenario tests skip.

## CII.6 Measured on the real path

The real `run.py` intro path, scripted on this machine, windowed (times from the script's start):

| Event | t [s] |
|---|---|
| LOAD pressed | 2.31 |
| the chooser shown, five names | 2.57 |
| load105_steam chosen | 3.08 |
| the restore accepted (audit "snapshot_load") | 3.54 |
| the release accepted (audit "freeze") | 4.46 |
| ENGINE RUNNING | 4.50 |
| the console shown | 4.64 |

Three seconds later the console's clock read 25 863.8 s against the file's 25 860.2 s: the plant ran on from the
exercise, not from the design seed's 0. A second scripted run took CANCEL in the chooser (six names by then): both
buttons came back live with "NO EXERCISE CHOSEN" and "PRESS ENTER TO START", one console built; Enter then released the
design seed on that console (its clock 2.4 s 1.5 s after it showed). Once the chooser closes on CANCEL the splash is
the active window and holds the keyboard focus, windowed and full screen alike, so the operator's own Enter reaches it
(the scripted Enter is delivered to the widget either way). Over the real link
(`tests/hmi/test_start_from_exercise.py`) a hand-over takes about 2 s; with the bridge's first-packet watchdog cut to
1 s and the chooser open 2.5 s the link was dropped and reconnected while the operator decided, and the hand-over
still reached the running console from the scenario.

A-30 was found writing those tests' teardown: `EngineBridge.close()` schedules a reconnect through the abort's
`disconnected`; a probe's bridge was connected again 1.5 s after `close()` (handoff A-30, not changed).

(`D:\Work\reports\Open gaps resolution routes.md`) was not re-derived; this session searched what it had left

## CIII.1 A-28: a silent engine's last packet is not replayed (decision 172)

`StationServer` (`ureasim/net/server.py`) replayed `_latest`, the last packet published, to every console that said
`hello`, with no age. A console whose engine stopped publishing was therefore blanked by the bridge's 5 s watchdog,
reconnected 0.5 s later, and was handed the dead engine's last values as live (session 87: blank 5.1 s, live 6.1 s,
blank 11.2 s, live 12.2 s). Built on option (a), with session 89's two additions:

* `publish` stamps the packet on a monotonic wall clock (`clock=time.monotonic`, injectable; never the plant time,
  which a frozen plant holds); `snapshot_age_s()` is the packet's age, None before the first publish.
* The `hello` handler replays the packet and the stored status only when the packet is at most
  `data.engine.SNAPSHOT_REPLAY_MAX_AGE_S` (1.0 s, ten publish passes of `DT_S`) old. Older, it sends the status
  "ENGINE SILENT — no packet for N s" (fault) and an empty snapshot, and marks the connection silenced.
* The engine's next publish sends a silenced connection the stored status again, then the packet: the engine host
  sends a status only when it changes, so without it the silence would stay on a live console's status bar.
* An engine that has never published (the plant held behind the start-up intro, decision 166) is answered as before:
  its stored status and an empty snapshot, under the bridge's 30 s first-packet watchdog. A running or frozen engine
  publishes every pass (decision 169's rehearsal included), so its packet is at most a pass old.

Measured on the real loopback link (`tests/hmi/test_console_while_frozen.py`): with the engine's thread stopped, the
first blank comes at the watchdog as before, and through two more reconnect cycles no packet with content reaches the
console, each reconnect showing ENGINE SILENT.

## CIII.2 A-30: a closed bridge does not reconnect (decision 173)

`EngineBridge.close()` stopped its timers and aborted the socket; the abort emits `disconnected` at once and
`_on_disconnected` scheduled a retry, so a closed bridge was connected again 1.5 s later. `close()` now sets
`_closed` before the abort, `_schedule_retry` declines while it is set, and `connect_to` clears it, the pattern
`_refused` already follows. The console's own shutdown was never affected (the application exits after it). The LOAD
tests' own stop of `_retry` after `close()` (§CII.6) is now redundant, and kept.

## CIII.3 Trip 22.2 named as the simulator's own (decision 174); data gap 6 closed

The archive draws no synthesis high-high pressure trip: AC4's PC22 has no 22.2 and XV-322902 is commanded from the
Safeguard SG1, whose PC20 trips on 320K002's own causes (§LXXIII.7); the Operating Manual III prints no interlock
limit (Part C). The process engineer decided to keep V1's trip, its logic and its 155.0 / 148.0 bar a unchanged, as
the simulator's own protection, and to name it so. `data.unit_322_loop.TRIP_LABELS` maps the packet key "22_2" to
"22.2 (simulator)", and `trip_label` is read by the pump faceplate's interlock line ("TRIP 21.2, 22.2 (simulator)
ACTIVE") and by the engine's refusals and acknowledgements ("320K002 is tripped by trip 22.2 (simulator), latched",
"reset trip 22.2 (simulator)"). The packet's keys, the instructor's trip list and every other trip's wording are
unchanged. Register row 348. The data gap's row is deleted.

## CIII.7 B-120 option (b): V1's stripper slip gain against Book2's bands (decision 176)

Decided by the process engineer on 2026-11-06: option (b), the gain measured against Book2's bands before any change,
70-80 % load in scope. The gain is `unit_322e001.SLIP_GAIN` (V1's STRIP_SLIP_GAIN, 4.0), the volatile breakthrough
`f + SLIP_GAIN * slip * (1 - f)` on NH3 and CO2 with `slip = max(1 - g_nc, 0) + max(1 - g_hc, 0)`, exactly 0 at the
design (`units/synthesis/stripper.py`), so the design point does not depend on it. Each load ran the same trims at
4.0 and at 0, through session 86's runner (`opt_run84.py`, the gain set on the stripper's module before the run and
read back from the plant's stripper in each log), from the design seed: the ramp at 0.5 %/min, a 3 h settle, a 3 h
hold. The arms: 100 %, PIC-329204 on TT-322004 at 168 C and HIC-322605 on LT-322504 (B-120's own trigger); 92.3 %,
session 86's trims on Book2's medians, on the committed engine and on S2's prototype; 111 %, session 86's retuned
trims (C1t), on the committed engine and with C1's capacity margin; 70 %, the design handles with HIC-322605,
HIC-322602 and the levels trimmed (B-118 evidence, not B-120's test). Scratch scripts: `s91/mk91.py`, `an91.py`.

Means over the 3 h hold (spans in brackets); Book2's 10-90 % bands: 92.3 % TT-322004 166.20-167.43, TT-322005
182.14-183.01, PT-329201 137.42-139.68, AT-322701 3.234-3.262; 111 % 171.92-172.59, 182.27-183.13, 142.48-143.66,
3.242-3.259.

* **The gain drives the mode.** At 92.3 % on S2, gain 4 swings AT-322701 by 1.62 with peaks 1.5 h apart, TT-322005
  by 8.7 K and the conversion by 26.7 points; gain 0 holds AT-322701 within 0.02 and TT-322004, AT-322701 and
  FT-329403 (54.9 t/h) in Book2's band, TT-322005 5 K cold and PT-329201 0.8 bar high, as session 86 found before
  decision 170. At 111 % gain 4 swings TT-322004 by 5.6-5.8 K (irregular AT peaks) and gain 0 by 0.8-0.9 K, the
  means within 1.3 K of each other and neither in band.
* **At 100 % this arm did not test the gain:** TT-322004 reached only 169.4 C, short of B-120's 168 C trigger;
  both gains held steady and agree within 0.02 on every mean. Session 78 measured the 168 C case itself, gain 0
  holding it steady (§XCI.3).
* **On the committed engine at 92.3 %** neither gain oscillates, PIC-329204 (17.22 bar a), MASTER-329207 (5.62)
  and HIC-322604 (66.5 %) on their bounds in both, but gain 0 runs the reactor 12.4 K colder (TT-322005 171.1 C
  against 183.5, conversion 40.7 % against 59.8): gain 0 alone puts the as-built engine on B-118's cold branch.
* **At 70 %** both gains trip 22.1 on the ramp within two minutes of each other (322E003's sump full, TT-322015
  171-175 C, TT-322005 162 C, conversion 29-30 %): B-118's collapse is not the slip term.

No relation changed: the gain stays at V1's 4.0. The options (handoff B-120): (a) keep it; (b1) gain 0 as a decided
divergence now; (b2) gain 0 built with B-118's stripper change once that is decided. (b2) is recommended, because
on the committed engine gain 0 alone trades a mode that does not appear there for a 12.4 K colder reactor.

## CIII.11 Decision 179: the dynamic audit applies decision 163 on 323F010

`tests/engine/test_dynamic_audit.py::test_a_fast_shutdown_with_lv_322501_wide_open_stays_stable` failed on 323F010:
three successive reversals of its step where the audit allows two. Measured: at tick 805 PT-323204 parks on 0.50585
bar a — the thermo memo's pressure-bin edge, its quantum 1e-4 bar — and alternates by 1.5-3.3e-7 bar
(0.00015-0.0003 mbar), steps of 3e-6 bar/tick flattening into the turn; the solver converges to 1e-10 bar, so it is not
the solver's. It is decision 163's chatter (accepted up to +/-0.012 mbar in a quiet boil, period-two +/-0.22 mbar under a
surge), 50 times smaller. The process engineer chose to apply decision 163 in the audit: on 323F010 only a reversal is
counted above 0.012 mbar (`MEMO_CHATTER_BAR`), and any third successive reversal at the general floor
(`REVERSAL_FLOOR_BAR`, 1e-7 bar) must stay below it (here at most 0.0034 mbar); every other node keeps the 1e-7 floor
and the limit of two. Two-reversal alternations of up to 0.29 mbar under the blow-through are within the existing
limit, as before.

  4.380), so the master goes to 5.411 bar a. The engine's design is 5.013 bar a (4.0 bar g, `P_LP_BARA`), and

  the B-120 arms of §CIII.7), in place of session 91's time ramp to 40 %. Book2's 11.4 % at the dwell (the two runs

2. **322R001's off-gas grows about 4.5-fold**, from 22-23 t/h to 100-107 t/h at the ramp's end. 322E002's duty falls
   from 62 MW to 44-48 MW at the ramp's end (36.5-45.5 MW at its lowest), its saturation fraction at 0.69-0.99.
3. **322E003's condensate grows with the off-gas**, from 57-58 t/h to 127-135 t/h. The spindle solve holds LT-329501
   near 50 % until HIC-322602 reaches its 10 % floor, where 322F001 entrains most: 78-106 t/h at the ramp's
   motive. From there the sump floods (LT-329501 100 %), the full sump condenses no more than drains from it, and
   TT-322015 runs past H2. That is trip 22.1, at 3 720-4 200 s.
4. **Only M, as built trips on the vent.** Its liquor follows the tempered water (no S2 ceiling). Its saturation
   fraction falls to 0.77, 8.4 t/h stays uncondensed, and TT-322015 passes H2 at 1 980 s. The margin was small:
   TT-322015 read 109.3 C a minute earlier, against H2's 110 C. A, as built (HIC-322604 raw) and MO, as built also
   vented, 5.5 and 7.3 t/h at 1 740-1 920 s, with TT-322015 peaking at 95.4 C, and recovered.

## CIV.3 The plant's own descent into the dwells

Book2's samples (16.8 min apart) through both cuts:

* **2023-07-25.** The load falls from 109.9 % (05:49:50) through 106.1 % (06:06:38) and 90.4 % (06:23:26) to
  72.3 % (06:40:14), about 1 %/min between samples. TT-322005 reads 182.82, 182.74, 182.60, 181.67, then 180.83 C
  at 70.7 % and 180.96 C at 70.5 %.
  - PT-329207 rose first: 3.90 to 4.03 and 4.38 bar g at the cut's start.
  - TIC-329005 rose during the cut: 80.2, 85.5, 95.5, 99.8 C.
  - HV-322602 and PIC-329204 fell with the load: 75 to 39.3 %, and 20.0 to 17.2 bar g.
  - HVGT-322605 lagged the load: 41.7 % at 72.3 %, 37.9 % an hour later.
* **2023-08-19.** The load falls from 100.2 % (06:59:26) through 97.9 % and 81.5 % to 70.1 % (07:49:50), 0.7-1.0 %/min.
  TT-322005 reads 182.81, 182.78, 182.81, 181.93, then 181.09 C at 68.7 %.
  - PT-329207 rose before the load moved: 4.06 bar g at 06:42, 4.25 at 06:59, 4.34 at 07:16.
  - TIC-329005 rose 86.5 to 94.1 C, HV-322602 fell 63 to 36 %, and PIC-329204 fell 19.0 to 16.5 bar g.

The plant cut load faster than the arms' 0.5 %/min, and its reactor top fell about 2 K, to 180.8-181.1 C. The
engine's TT-322005 falls more than 20 K on the slower ramp. So the ramp's rate does not explain the collapse. The
rates are means between samples, so the plant's peak rate was at least as high. This partly answers §CIII.12's open
point, the plant's path to its dwell, at Book2's sample spacing: the operators raised the LP header first, before
or at the cut's start, and moved the tempered water, the spindle and the HP steam with the load. The arms moved
MASTER-329207 linearly over the hour.

## CIV.4 Reading

* **Correction 2 changes the route, and only for a time.** On the spindle solve the sump holds on the ramp in every
  arm until HIC-322602 reaches its 10 % floor. Session 91's flood at 2 040-2 100 s, with the spindle ramped open loop
  to 55 %, is gone. On 322F001's back-solved geometry (data gap 1) the 10 % floor entrains 78-106 t/h against
  127-135 t/h of condensate, the make growing with 322R001's off-gas.
* **Correction 1 sets the right end value, not a usable path.**
  - The anchored ramp backs 322R001 up to its band's top within 20-28 minutes.

    anchored 43.27 %.
  - The engine's discharge stays near its design 225 t/h until the reactor cools, so a time-linear path closes
    HV-322605 too early. No opening settled.
* **Correction 3 and the HIC-322604 offset do not keep the reactor hot.**
  - With S2 and gain 0, A, M and MO give the same result: trip at 3 720 s, TT-322005 157-160 C.
  - As built, the offset arm did not trip on the vent, but the vent margin in M was 0.7 K of TT-322015. The offset
    is not credited with removing it.

  trip comes at 3 720-4 200 s, at or just after the design-handle arms' 3 420-3 540 s (§CIII.7). Session 91's earlier
  trip was the boundary: the raw HIC-322605 ramp and the open-loop spindle.

# Part CV — Session 93: the plant's 5 November 2026 turndown (`Data/Trends 511.2026`) against the open data gaps and B-118 (decided 2026-11-08, decision 180)

Session 93 (2026-11-07/08) took up the process engineer's pasted request to resolve or narrow the open data gaps
from the plant DCS trends in `D:\Work\Urea Simulation Docs\Data\Trends 511.2026`, using the vendor-trimmed control
valves as in-situ meters, and to cross-check decision 178 and B-118. It is measurement only: nothing under
`ureasim/` changed, no decision was taken, and every script, export and run is in the session scratchpad
(`t511/`, `b118/`). The advisor (Opus) was consulted on the plan after the folder was inventoried.

## CV.1 The folder, and how it was read

The folder holds no numeric export. It holds 75 photographs (JPEG, 4 000 x 2 252) of one ABB 800xA trend display,
"UREA-LOAD : Trend Display", taken on 7 November 2026 between 21:13 and 22:08. Every window shown is on 5 November
2026. The display carries ten pens per group and a table under the plot.

| E, steam and water valves | 29 | 07:43-09:43 every 7.5 min (15 min), 09:06-16:06 every 30 min (1 h) | 15 min / 1 h | UREA-LOAD, FV-329401, FV-329409, PV-329202, PV-329203, PV-323203, HV-323605, TV-323013A, TV-323013B, PV-323202 |

Three properties of the table decide what the photographs can give:

* **"Current Value" is not 5 November data.** It is the live value at the photograph's clock (7 November, 21:13-22:08):
  UREA-LOAD reads 101.0-102.5 % in every photograph against window means of 69.2-102.0 %. It is used as a separate
  dataset, the plant's own ~101.5 % state on 7 November.
* **"MV" is the measured value** (ABB usage): every MV row carries its PV's engineering unit (FIC-329409 m3/h,
  TIC-329005 C, SIC-321951 rpm, LIC-324501 %, PIC-324202 bar g). No controller set point or output is logged; the only
  outputs are the VALUE rows of valve and hand-station tags.
* **"Mean Value" is the window mean** of each pen and "Ruler Value" the value at the ruler's time where a ruler was
  placed (group C at 13:08:14, group D at 14:36:12, outside its windows, group E at 10:05:41).

Method (scratchpad `t511/`):
1. Windows OCR of every photograph (`ocr.ps1`, word level `ocrw.ps1`) located the tables and labels. Its word boxes sit
   about one table row (~40 px) above the image's own pixels, so OCR positions were used only to locate, never to
   measure.
2. Every table was read visually from deskewed crops (`crop_tables.py`) and transcribed (`transcribed.py`): window
   centre, span, low and high range, current, ruler and mean value of every pen.
3. The traces were digitized (`geom2.py`, `digitize.py`). Time is anchored on the labelled dashed gridlines,
   interpolated between neighbours at each pixel's height (keystone). The high and low range lines (the dashed
   lines at the plot's top and just above the solid time axis) are found by RANSAC on white-pixel runs, as a
   quadratic in x (lens bend). Pen colours come from the table's colour column (one cell per pen, found on the image),
   refined on the trace pixels by four damped Lloyd steps; a trace pixel is one brighter than its local background
   (31 px median) and not white. Two photographs (214332, 220713, both cropped at a plot edge) were not digitized.
4. QA: every digitized pen-window is compared with the display's own window mean. 391 of 560 scored pen-windows agree
   within max(1 % of span, the unit's tolerance: 0.5 C, 0.4 K, 0.4 t/h, 1.5 rpm, 1 %, 1.5 m3/h, capped at 5 % of span);
   per pen below. The QA-passing windows hold 84 369 points in group A, 27 899 in B, 23 374 in C, 31 808 in D and
   138 438 in E. A point is a
   4-pixel column: 4.5 s on a 1 h window, 1.05-1.08 s on a 15 min window. That is the photograph's pitch, not the DCS
   history's own step, which the deadband-stepped traces do not reveal.
   Pens lying on a range line (PV-324202/203, PV-323202, HIC-335602 at 0 %) are hidden by the line and not scored.

## CV.3 Data gap 1 and B-118: 322F001 and 322E003 through the plant's turndown

**The entrainment ratio from the engine's own heat balance.** The discharge balance of `units/synthesis/ejector.py`
(`T_d (1 + mu) cp_D = cp_N T_mot + mu cp_C T_s`, cp 4.74 / 3.10 / 3.50, T_s the 178.8 C pseudo-temperature) inverted
for mu, every temperature in departure form from the plant's own full-load windows of the same day (14:10-15:40,
101.95 %): T_d = 107.566 + (TT-322012 - 113.25), T_mot = 28.934 + (TT-321001 - 18.30), T_s = 178.8 + (TT-322002 -
167.85). At the reference this returns the PFD's mu, 57 561.3 / 42 762 = 1.3461, by construction; the absolute mu is
not read, only its ratio. The sensitivity is 0.046 in mu per K of TT-322012, -0.024 per K of TT-322002 and -0.027 per
K of TT-321001, so a window's ratio carries about +/- 0.05. The motive is the PFD's 42 762 kg/h times FY-321401 on its
reference (FY-321401 is a fixed-density compute tag, `unit_321`; it tracks SIC-321951 at 0.338 t/h per rpm within
0.4 % in every window).

* **The plant's ejector keeps its entrainment ratio through the turndown**: mu / mu_ref 1.031 +/- 0.044 (n 15,
  0.97-1.12), so its suction follows the load, m_suc / m_suc,ref = 1.037 L / L_ref (RMSE 0.038, R2 0.86).
* **The operator closes the spindle with the load**: HV-322602 = 65.4 % (L / 101.95 %)^1.60 (R2 0.92, RMSE 2.3 %
  stroke, n 15): 65.4 % at full load, 55 % at 90.5 %, 40 % at 74.6 %, 35 % at 69.9 %. Book2 reads 76 / 63 / 40 % at
  111 / 92.3 / 69.3 %; the 5 November plant runs about 8 % of stroke more closed at 90 %.
* **The engine's closure stalls on the plant's own operating line.** At the plant's motive and stroke (absolute on
  the DDS map, level factor 1, the engine's fixed 4.2 bar lift), `ejector_322f001` reports stalled in every window at
  69.9-80.7 % load, and between 86.6 and 94.2 % it passes 44-93 % of the plant's suction; at full load it passes
  1.28-1.31 times it. Holding the plant's 100 % offset to the engine's 74 % anchor instead stalls it below about 87 %. The momentum closure puts the design point within 10 % of shutoff (motive fraction
  0.907, data gap 1's B-12 margin); the plant runs at a motive fraction of 0.69 with the nozzle at 72 % of its design
  area and entrains its full-load ratio. The engine holds the lift fixed at every load
  (`loop_hydraulics.ejector_pressures_bara`: both ends ride PT-329201 on their design offsets).
* **What lift the plant implies** (`lift_fit.py`): if the 4.2 bar lift is split into a static part and a friction
  part scaling on the discharge flow squared, the closure passes the plant's suction in every window only if the
  friction part is at least 2.41 bar (57 % of the lift); the 90 % windows alone need 0.6-1.0 bar, the 70-75 % windows
  2.3-2.4 bar. No hydraulic datum in either archive splits the lift, so this is a fit, not a datum. The fit scales the
  friction on the discharge flow squared; the prototype (CV.4) scales it on the motive ratio squared, which at the
  plant's constant mu differs by about 0.03 bar at 70 %.

## CV.4 The 322F001 friction prototype, both sides measured

**The prototype** (`b118/ej_proto.py`, scratch only): the part `lf` of the design 4.2 bar lift that is line and
distributor friction, scaling on the square of the motive ratio taken on the motive the engine delivers on its first
call (the design seed):

    p_disch,eff = p_disch - lf . (1 - r^2),   r = m_motive / m_motive,seed,   lf = 2.41 bar (CV.3's fit)

as-built multiplier reads 1.00002 there and the ramp moves EJ_322F001.suction_kgh by 1.3 kg/h on the first tick.

# Part CVI — Session 94: B-118's term audit of 322R001's turndown cooling (decided 2026-11-09, decision 181)

Session 94 (2026-11-08/09) took up the process engineer's second request of 2026-11-08: a term-by-term audit of
322R001's energy balance on the turndown ramp, with decision 180's workspace (S2's stripper terms, decision 177's
slip gain 0, the 322F001 lift prototype of 2.41 bar) beside the as-built baseline, then isolated prototypes of the
responsible terms, both sides measured. It is measurement only. Nothing under `ureasim/` changed (CLAUDE.md 5.6). The
scripts ran in the session scratchpad and are archived at `D:\Work\reports\B118_term_audit_scripts` (outside the
tree); the report is `D:\Work\reports\B-118 322R001 term audit.md`. The advisor (Opus) was consulted on the harness
before any run and on the reading before this record.

## CVI.1 The harness and the column identity

Four read-only recorders (`terms94.py`) wrap `reactor_inventory.reactor_322r001`, `reactor_inventory.node_boil`,
`ReactorInventory.step` and `CondenserHoldup.step`; each returns what it wrapped. With them attached the design seed
is identical on every packet leaf (3 268 leaves, 7 samples over 600 ticks). Read off `reactor_inventory.step` and
`reactor_hydraulics.node_dtdt`, the four nodes' temperature steps sum, exactly on every tick, to

    TT-322005(t-1) - TT-322010 = sum dT_rxn - sum loss_K - sum storage_K - sum cap_K
    dT_rxn,n  = q_n / mcp_live = carb_K,n - dehyd_K,n,   q_n = xi_carb,n 117 000 - xi_dehyd,n 15 500   [kJ/h]
    loss_K,n  = tau_n (1 - clamp(co2_scale)) (T_n - 40) / 21 600
    storage_K = tau_n (T_n,new - T_n,old) / dt,   cap_K = tau_n (T_n,pre-cap - T_n,new) / dt

with xi_carb = gas CO2 from 322E002 - off-gas CO2 (the anchored split plus the conversion-deficit slip, clamped at
zero) spread over the nodes by liquid volume. The residual is below 3e-10 K on every sample of every arm.

**The seed's budget.** Rise 13.00 K = carbamate 31.82 K - dehydration 18.82 K; the carbamate term is itself a
difference, gas CO2 489.4 kmol/h (53.40 K) less off-gas CO2 197.7 kmol/h (21.57 K). Wall loss 0 (gate 0), the boil
cap 0.045 K against storage -0.045 K. 322E002: shell 151.94 C, feed mix 155.20 C, adiabatic pseudo-temperature
600.48 C, exp(-NTU) = 0.0403 (NTU 3.212), CO2 gas fraction 0.2036.

## CVI.4 The four terms the request named

1. **TT-322010 and 322E002's quench.** On the ramp to L 0.80 TT-322010 moves only -0.8 to -2.7 K: the NTU term
   (-2.1 to -6.4 K) is offset by MASTER-329207's shell (+1.0 to +1.7 K) and the exotherm spike. It collapses (-10.9
   to -14.5 K) only after the reactor has, as 322E002's feed falls with the loop. At the plant's own steady bands,
   with Book2's shell moves and the flow in proportion to load, the constant-UA quench gives TT-322010 -11.22,
   -8.44, -3.54 and +4.87 K at 69.5, 80.4, 92.2 and 111 % against the plant's -1.18, -0.44, -0.42 and +0.10 K. A
   conductance on the tube-side flow, UA = UA_pin (m / m_ref)^n, reproduces the plant at n = 0.816, 0.847, 0.722 and
   0.709 (mean 0.77). The sensible inlet is not the term that matters: through the flash it is. At the seed,
   `hpcc_flash_split`'s CO2 gas fraction is 0.204; it is 0.100 at TT-322010 - 1 K, 0.051 at - 2 K and 0.335 at + 1 K,
   0.291 at PT-329201 - 3 bar and 0.130 at + 3 bar, and it does not move with the feed N/C between -0.1 and +0.4.
   With gas CO2 worth 53.4 K at the seed, 1 K of TT-322010 is about 27 K of the reactor's carbamate source.
2. **The carbamate heat supply.** The responsible term. It falls from 31.8 K to 18.6-20.6 K at L 0.90 and to zero
   by L 0.85 in both arms, the gas CO2 322E002 passes falling first (-9.6 to -10.6 K at L 0.90, its CO2 fraction
   0.170-0.171 against 0.204), then the off-gas taking more CO2 as the conversion falls: the split, re-solved at the
   live pressure on the design temperature, takes a fixed share of a growing unconverted CO2 (-13.7 to -16.0 K at
   L 0.85, -35.6 to -39.1 K at L 0.80), and V1's conversion-deficit slip adds to it (-4.7 to -5.8, then -16.2 to
   -18.7 K). Cooler, the reactor converts less, its off-gas takes more CO2, and the source falls further: a positive
   loop with no counterpart in the plant's constant rise.
3. **The dehydration sink.** It falls as the column cools (18.8 to 15.6-17.5 K by L 0.80-0.85): a stabiliser. The
   longer residence raises the conversion by +0.016 to +0.034 (about +0.5 to +1.2 K of sink) up to L 0.80; the feed
   composition moves it -0.02 to +0.05; the node temperatures take it down by up to -0.23 (all at constant inputs
   otherwise, `urea_extent_pfr` re-evaluated against the seed).
4. **The gated wall loss.** It subtracts 0.28-0.29, 1.0, 1.8, 2.6, 3.4-3.6 and 4.5-4.6 K at L 0.95, 0.90, 0.85,
   0.80, 0.75 and 0.693 on the ramp, 5.4 K at the 69.3 % end and 1.2-1.3 K at 92.3 %; quasi-steady it is
   (1 - L)/L (T - 40) 2 340 s / 21 600 s, about 6.5 K at 69.3 %. The gate is V1's stand-in for a stagnant reactor;
   Book2's load-invariant rise bounds a real running loss at about 0.7 K at design (the bands' 0.3 K spread over
   1/L - 1 = 0.44 at 69.5 %).

**A confound in the arms' handles.** The engine's seed runs HIC-322602 at 74.0 % and reads AT-322701 3.0. Session
93's handle laws put the plant's absolute values on it: HIC-322602 on 65.4 % (L / 1.0195)^1.6 (63.4 % at L = 1) and
AY-322701 trimmed to 3.19 (69.3 %) or 3.25 (92.3 %), so two handles step at t = 0. In the first five minutes the
suction runs to 69.4 t/h (design 57.6 t/h), LT-329501 drains from 50 to 35 %, the melt N/C to 322E002 swings from
2.88 to 3.42 and the flash's CO2 target from 0.315 to 0.065. The onset of term 2 on the ramp therefore carries this
step as well as the turndown; it is not attributed to the turndown alone.

# Part CVII — Session 95: B-118's candidate bundle verified on the five holds (2026-11-10/11)

Session 95 took up the process engineer's request of 2026-11-09 under decision 181: `ureasim/` kept as built,
the session's scratch verification of B-118's candidate bundle — P1 (322E002's UA on the load to the power 0.77),
P4 (322R001's wall loss on a stagnant reactor only) and decision 180's 322F001 lift (2.41 bar of the 4.2 bar
friction share on the motive ratio squared) — on the as-built stripper (slip gain 4.0, no S2 terms), on the five
acceptance holds, with and without P6 (322R001's conversion-deficit slip gain 0). Measurement only: no file under
`ureasim/` changed and no relation changed. The scripts and runs are archived in
`D:\Work\reports\B118_bundle_verification_s95` (outside the tree); the report is
`D:\Work\reports\B-118 bundle verification s95.md`.

## CVII.1 The seed: P1's drift found and removed

* **Where session 94's P1 drifted.** The first live call of `carbamate_condenser_322e002` carries exactly the feed
  of the module's synthetic design call (250 638.9350 kg/h both), so P1 had no offset at its anchor. Its drift was
  the basis itself: 322E002's feed mass wanders 4e-5 of itself over 600 ticks (about seven condenser calls a
  tick), and 322R001's `co2_scale`, the basis CVI.5 proposed, wanders 3.3e-6 by 60 s. **CVI.5's statement that
  `co2_scale` "keeps the seed identical through its own drift" is wrong**: it moves the seed as the feed mass does,
  only less.
* **The basis that keeps the seed identical** is the battery-limit CO2 demand over its design,
  `320K002-CO2 / 54.618 t/h`, the instructor's boundary condition and the load the Book2 fit was made on: 1.0 by
  construction at the design seed. P1 on that ratio (`proto95.py`, `ua_basis "demand"`) leaves every leaf of the
  packet identical to the plain seed over 600 ticks (0 leaves differ).
* **The 322F001 lift is not bit-identical**: its relation is on the live motive ratio, and the seed's own motive
  wanders, so TT-322010 departs 3.9e-5 K by 60 s, about 3 % of the plain seed's own 1.15e-3 K wander. It is kept on
  the motive, its physics being the friction of the motive flow squared.
* **The null ramp.** The full session-95 policy with bundle A at L = 1.0 for 1 800 s against the plain seed: every
  handle stays at the engine's seed (HIC-322602 74.0 -> 73.98 % on its level trim, every other handle exact), every
  PV within the seed's own wander, no trip. Session 94's t = 0 handle step is gone.

## CVII.4 The new failure: 322E002's condensation collapses from L 0.76

* **Onset.** On every 74.4, 69.3 and 68.9 % arm, A and B alike, 322E002's saturation fraction (`sat_frac`,
  decisions 97 and 135) first falls below 0.6 at L 0.757-0.763 on the ramp, independent of the hold's target.
  In the collapse the duty falls from about 40 MW to 2.8-3.9 MW, the equilibrium CO2 condensed fraction to about
  0, the condenser's bubble pressure rises to 185-208 bar against the loop's 138 bar, the product temperature
  falls to the shell's (151-154 C) and nearly all the feed's CO2 (1 960-2 080 of 2 470 kmol/h) leaves as gas.
  The collapse alternates with recoveries (duty back to 33-45 MW) every few minutes.
* **Before the onset** the condenser drifts toward it: from L 0.80 to 0.77 its feed CO2 rises 2 082 -> 2 258
  kmol/h as the load falls (the scrubber's recycle grows), the gas CO2 it passes 702 -> 883 kmol/h, TT-322010
  170.4 -> 172.6 C, and the saturation fraction rises to 0.99, the bubble pressure falling to the loop's.
* **The consequence.** 322R001's off-gas swings 15-112 t/h (26 t/h at L 0.95), 322E003 condenses all of it
  (uncondensed 0 from L 0.80), and its sump make swings 60-136 t/h. Over the settle the loop pressure climbs from
  138.4-139.3 bar a at the end of the ramp to 155 bar a, and the latch comes where PT-329201 crosses trip 22.2's
  155.0 bar a (the simulator's own protection, V1's assumed set point; A693 154.98 bar a at 4 980 s, 155.16 at
  5 040 s). At 60 s sampling the trips that latch with it (21.2, 21.8, 21.10, 22.1) cannot be ranked; the record is
  consistent with 22.2 first. TT-322005 rises to 189.5-190.3 C with the pressure before the latch.
* **P6 changes nothing that matters**: arm B agrees with arm A to four or five digits until the collapse, and the
  collapse's onset, the trips and their times move by at most 120 s.
* **Session 94's arms never collapsed**: on its absolute handles and P1 on the feed-mass basis, e_sat stayed at or
  above 0.83 down to each arm's latch (L 0.689-0.792), most of them with the reactor already cold (`D:\Work\reports\B118_term_audit_scripts\s94\runs`).
* **The discriminators** (ramp 1.0 -> 0.744, 1 200 s settle, arm A unless named):

  | arm | 322E002 collapse | trip | TT-322005 below L 0.80, C | at L 0.80: TT-322010 C, gas CO2 to 322R001 kmol/h, 322E002 feed t/h |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | A, sampled every 2 s | from L 0.763 | none by 4 320 s (PT-329201 143.5 bar a) | 181.4-184.5 | 170.1, 677, 229 |
  | A, PIC-329204 and MASTER-329207 at their seed | from L 0.749 | none by 4 320 s | 181.3-182.1 | 170.1, 649, 230 |
  | A, HIC-322604 at its seed | from L 0.754 | none by 4 320 s (143.2 bar a) | 181.3-184.2 | 170.2, 689, 230 |
  | A with P1 on session 94's feed-mass basis | none (e_sat >= 0.87) | none by 4 320 s | 163.6-178.9 | 168.7, 374, 224 |
  | A without P1 (P4 + lift) | none (e_sat >= 0.87) | latched at 3 960 s | 161.2-171.0 | 168.7, 444, 248 |
  | as built, no bundle | censored: latched at 2 820 s (L 0.769), before the onset window | latched | 166.5-169.3 | 168.4, 381, 239 |

  The no-bundle arm latched above the onset window and is no evidence either way; the arm without P1 passed
  L 0.76 (to 0.744) before its latch. **The collapse comes with P1 on the demand basis and with nothing else
  measured**, and the same term is what holds
  the reactor: with P1 on the load ratio 322E002 passes 650-690 kmol/h of gas CO2 to 322R001 at L 0.80, against
  370-440 kmol/h without it or on the feed-mass basis, and only those arms keep TT-322005 in Book2's band. The
  handles' departures (PIC-329204, MASTER-329207, HIC-322604) move the onset by at most 0.014 in L, and the onset's
  independence of the hold's target already excludes TIC-329005 (its departure at L 0.76 differs about twofold
  between the 74.4 and 68.9 % arms). The Book2 fit took 322E002's feed mass in proportion to the load, so that its
  NTU rises as L^(n - 1); in the engine the feed falls more slowly than the load (229 t/h at L 0.80, 0.92 of the
  seed's 250.6, the scrubber's recycle growing), so on the load ratio the NTU falls instead (0.84 / 0.92 = 0.92 of
  the seed's at L 0.80), a stronger cut than the fit implies, and on the feed-mass basis the cut is too weak to
  hold the reactor. Book2's TT-322010 departure at its 80.4 % band is -0.44 K; the arms give +0.1 K on the load
  ratio and -1.3 K on the feed mass.

  **At 2 s sampling** the onset is a smooth drift over about 50 s (L 0.767 -> 0.763): the saturation fraction
  0.986 -> 0.857, the equilibrium CO2 condensed fraction 0.50 -> 0.10, the bubble pressure 142 -> 150 bar a, the
  duty 38.8 -> 32.1 MW, the gas CO2 895 -> 1 124 kmol/h. Past it the condenser's state jumps between a condensing
  and a non-condensing solution from one 2 s sample to the next (saturation fraction 0.32, 0.78, 0.61, 0.53, 0.57,
  1.00, 0.45 ...; 94 large reversals in 859 samples), while the published TT-322010 moves smoothly. The drift onto
  the edge is the condenser's equilibrium at the live state; whether the switching past it is a physical
  relaxation or a stiff step ringing at tick scale (decision 78's class, decision 135's coupled solve) is not
  resolved at 2 s and needs a tick-resolution probe.

## CVII.5 322E003's sump balance (the request's L 0.85-0.69)

dm = make + recondensed backlog - suction - pulse; make = feed - vent; feed = off-gas in + LP wash (PFD 308) +
carry-over. The suction factor is the sump level of the tick before over 50 %, clamped to [0, 1.25]. Arm A at
69.3 % (kg/h; the 68.9 % arm agrees within the collapse's scatter):

| L | off-gas in | condensed off-gas | uncondensed | LP wash m308 | make | suction | 322F001 capacity at factor 1 | factor | level % | HIC-322602 % (bias) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.95 | 26 195 | 23 448 | 1 093 | 36 248 | 59 775 | 57 608 | 63 139 | 0.92 | 45.6 | 69.9 (+1.7) |
| 0.90 | 33 558 | 29 960 | 2 060 | 33 116 | 63 149 | 58 441 | 60 556 | 0.96 | 48.3 | 64.8 (+2.2) |
| 0.85 | 36 563 | 33 156 | 1 986 | 29 190 | 62 410 | 58 614 | 58 597 | 1.00 | 50.0 | 58.9 (+1.7) |
| 0.80 | 40 643 | 39 333 | 0 | 30 109 | 69 507 | 62 585 | 58 693 | 1.06 | 53.3 | 52.1 (+0.2) |
| 0.75 | 111 764 | 110 562 | 0 | 25 582 | 136 202 | 89 736 | 71 789 | 1.25 | 67.2 | 39.6 (-7.3) |
| 0.71 | 65 769 | 64 683 | 0 | 18 283 | 83 006 | 81 417 | 71 946 | 1.06 | 56.6 | 33.0 (-9.6) |
| 0.693 (hold start) | 95 354 | 94 257 | 0 | 17 044 | 111 339 | 91 943 | 78 998 | 1.13 | 58.2 | 30.2 (-11.0) |

* **The sump-head factor does not throttle the suction below 50 %.** The level never falls below 45 %; the factor
  is 0.92-1.00 to L 0.85 and 1.06-1.25 below, at its 1.25 ceiling through the collapse's surges. Only in the surges
  does the make exceed what the ejector draws at the ceiling.
* **323P001 / LIC-323502 is not pumping near-100 % wash.** m308 falls with the load, to 0.50 of the seed's
  36 834 kg/h by L 0.71 and 0.46 at the hold; LIC-323502 holds 46-48 %. Session 94's 0.89-0.97 of seed came under
  the absolute handles.
* **The sump fills to 100 % only after the latch**, when the trips stop 321P002A/B, the motive goes to zero and
  322F001 stalls (EJECTOR_STALL with the trips). Before it the level peaks at 68-74 %; HIC-322602's bias trim
  reaches -11 % at the hold's start and its -15 % limit after the latch.
* The sump's own balance closes to 1.3e-7 kg/h (the residual's largest value on any arm).

## CVII.6 Options (for the process engineer; no decision taken)

* **(a) Keep `ureasim/` as built (recommended).** B-118 continues on 322E002's low-load collapse under P1: a

  135) to tell a physical relaxation from a stiff-step ring, and the scrubber recycle that raises 322E002's feed
  against the load (322E003's make 59.8 -> 69.5 t/h from L 0.95 to 0.80). P1's basis stays open: the load ratio
  holds the reactor and folds the condenser, the feed mass keeps the condenser and loses the reactor, and Book2's

## CVIII.3 322E002's collapse in session 95's runs, read again (B-118)

Session 95's `D_tick` (bundle A at 74.4 %, sampled every 2 s) and five other archived arms, no new run.

| t s | L | melt N/C | P_bub bar a | sat. fraction | TT-322010 C | feed CO2 kmol/h | gas CO2 kmol/h | 322F001 suction t/h |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 800 | 0.852 | 3.526 | 152.3 | 0.852 | 169.5 | 2 067 | 609 | 57.6 |
| 2 400 | 0.803 | 3.293 | 147.6 | 0.910 | 170.5 | 2 096 | 666 | 61.9 |
| 2 760 | 0.774 | 3.082 | 143.3 | 0.970 | 172.1 | 2 202 | 817 | 68.8 |
| 2 880 | 0.764 | 2.811 | 145.4 | 0.935 | 170.7 | 2 332 | 1 004 | 73.6 |
| 3 000 | 0.754 | 2.425 | 174.8 | 0.496 | 154.0 | 2 572 | 1 664 | 87.7 |
| 3 120 | 0.744 | 2.418 | 178.8 | 0.447 | 156.6 | 2 575 | 1 662 | 95.3 |
| 3 600 | 0.744 | 3.042 | 141.0 | 1.000 | 172.2 | 2 151 | 866 | 70.9 |
| 4 080 | 0.744 | 2.451 | 177.9 | 0.464 | 160.7 | 2 488 | 1 529 | 90.7 |

* **The collapse is the melt crossing N/C 3.0 downward**, onto the low-N/C branch of `bubble_p_322e002`
  (`carbamate_condenser.py:304-308`, decisions 142 and 147). The bubble pressure's minimum, 143.3 bar a at
  2 760 s, is the branch point. After the onset the 336 samples with a fraction below 0.6 all hold a melt N/C
  of 2.23 to 2.58; the 177 samples at or above 0.9 hold 2.76 to 3.35.
* **It is a recycle, with a period of 14 to 21 minutes.** The CO2 322E002 does not condense passes 322R001
  as off-gas, 322E003 condenses it and 322F001 returns it: the feed's CO2 rises 25 % and the suction from
  57.6 to 95.3 t/h while the load falls 13 %, which lowers the feed's N/C further. Collapse at 2 900 s,
  recovery by 3 360 to 3 600 s, collapse at 3 840 s, recovery at 4 200 s, collapse at 4 320 s.
* **The recycle's gain [I].** The branch rises 9.38 bar at N/C 2.8 and 38.04 bar at 2.6 (`low_nc_rise`'s own
  figures), -47 and -143 bar per unit of N/C; through b_207 (0.0154 per bar) the fraction falls 0.72 and 2.2
  per unit; the feed's N/C moves about +1.2 per unit of fraction in `D_tick`. The product is 0.87 between 3.0
  and 2.8 and 2.6 below: a critical melt N/C near 2.8. The arms that do not collapse (`D_noP1`, `D_mfeed`,
  `D_plain`) dip to 2.86 to 2.92 and recover; the arm that collapses passes 2.81.
* **Why P1 on the load ratio brings it on [I for the cause].** Measured: with the reactor held, conversion
  rises to 61 to 64 %, the stripper's top gas carries 40 % less NH3 (3 971 to 2 402 kmol/h) while the fresh
  ammonia falls 19 %, and the loop goes ammonia-lean. Without P1 or on the feed mass the reactor is cold and
  its off-gas returns ammonia with the CO2.
* **The ratio could not act.** FFIC-321404's set point sat on its 2.0 floor from 960 to 1 680 s with
  AT-322701 at 3.30 to 3.42, and moved 2.7 % in the whole run while the melt N/C moved from 3.65 to 2.42
  (B-128).
* **A correction to CVII.4.** `e_phieq_co2` is the flash's equilibrium GAS fraction of CO2 (0.178 at L 0.85,
  0.000 at 154 C), not a condensed fraction: in the collapse the K-value flash asks to condense all the CO2
  and the saturation fraction forbids it. `hpcc_flash_split` back-solves its design K-values on the live
  feed (`carbamate_condenser.py:172-180`), so it does not see composition; the saturation law does.
* Not settled: the reversals between 2 s samples inside the collapsed phase.

## CVIII.4 The saturation law against Book2 (B-125)

`saturation_fraction` (`liquor_saturation.py:98-121`) is f = max(1 - b_207 d, 0) with
d = (P_bub - P_loop) - 3.5 bar. The 3.5 bar is the whole design head, so d = 0 at the design: the design point
is on the law's edge, and each bar above it removes 1.54 % of all condensation. Above the branch
`BUB_KN` 0.18 raises P_bub 26 bar per unit of melt N/C.

| Band | TT-322010 C | melt N/C [I] | P_loop bar a | P_bub as built | d bar | f as built | f with K_N 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| design | 170.0 | 3.079 | 140.7 | 144.2 | 0.0 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| Book2 92.3 % | 168.76 | 3.45 | 138.4 | 151.2 | +9.3 | 0.857 | 1.000 |
| Book2 69.3 % | 168.8 | 3.39 | 133.1 | 149.7 | +13.1 | 0.798 | 0.920 |

The melt N/C is AY-322701 plus 0.2, the offset the archived runs show between the two; the plant does not log
it. On the law as built the plant's own steady bands lose 14 and 20 % of their condensation, which the plant
does not. In every session 95 arm the fraction reads 0.85 to 0.93 from L 0.92 to L 0.80 (A923: 0.851 at
960 s), the reactor's off-gas 30.8 t/h at 92.3 % against the design 22.4, and 322E002's feed 229 t/h at
L 0.80, 0.92 of the seed. That is why P1's load-ratio and feed-mass bases differ: the feed does not follow
the load.

`T_prod` itself is an NTU quench (`carbamate_condenser.py:461-492`): T_adb 508 C, exp(-NTU) 0.030 to 0.043,
so dT_prod / d ln UA is about -59 K, on one specific heat (`CP_GAS` 2.0) and one heat of reaction
(`DH_CARB_KJMOL` 160); the equilibrium does not enter the outlet temperature.

## CVIII.5 322R001's holdup has no composition (B-126)

`reactor_inventory.py:328-329` sends on the tick's reaction product scaled to the hydraulic outflow; the
holdup is one mass (135 904 kg at the seed, 36 minutes of residence). Measured 305 s after a 20 % cut of the
CO2 demand: the reaction step makes 150.9 t/h of overflow, the vessel sends 226.2 t/h, drawing 49.3 t/h from
its holdup and boiling 15.3 t/h, and the overflow carries 2 933 kmol/h more N and 576 kmol/h more C than the
step produced, at the present composition. At a steady 92.3 % (arm A923) the melt N/C runs 3.65, 2.95, 3.21,
3.04 over about 48 minutes with the stripper's slip gain at 4.0; Book2 holds AY-322701 at 3.19 to 3.25.
Whether the missing inventory is the cause of B-120's mode is an inference [I].

## CVIII.6 The loop's design boundary and the reactor's tear (B-127)

`data/unit_322_loop.py:116-118`: in 134 215.2 kg/h, out 132 190.3 kg/h, residual +2 024.9 kg/h.
`reactor.py:323-326` subtracts `REACT_TEAR_DES_KMOLH` (`data/synthesis_pin.py:85-93`) from the feed, scaled
by the CO2 load ratio: 2 107.45 kg/h at the seed, NH3 129.1 kmol/h of it. Measured between the reactor's feed
and its products at the seed: N -121.45, C -1.25, H -359.07, O -1.84 kmol/h. That is 5.1 % of the fresh
ammonia (2 510.9 kmol/h) and more than its stoichiometric excess (about 103 kmol/h). Every other synthesis
unit closes on N, C, H and O to rounding: 322E001, 322E002, 322E003 and the reactor from its corrected feed.
`loop_pressure.py:268` credits the residual back. V1's reconciliation, flagged once as B-75; exact at the
design. Off the design the sink follows the CO2 demand; PFD 308 fell to 0.50 of its seed at L 0.71 (CVII.5).
The bias this leaves at turndown is of the order of 129 (s - r_308), at most about 27 kmol/h [I].

## CIX.1 The licensor's figures on the melt's bubble pressure (B-125, B-118)

`References\Sources\Urea Production Diagrams.pdf`, Uhde's Fundamentals UD-VT-G00-DC-0003 rev 00, read from the
page images. Figure 1 (page 1-30), liquid-gas equilibria of CO2-NH3 at constant pressure: the bubble-point
and dew-point curves meet at a maximum temperature T_AZ at one composition X_AZ, and the bubble temperature
falls on both sides of it; at constant temperature that is a pressure minimum, the pressure rising on both
sides. Figure 2 (page 1-31), CO2-NH3-H2O: a liquid top-ridge line that moves with the water. Neither carries
a scale. They support the rising branch below the ridge (decisions 142, 147) and do not support a flat law
above it. CVIII.4's reading of Book2 (a slope of about zero above N/C 3.0) is therefore restated: Book2 runs
AY-322701 3.19 to 3.25 at a lower loop pressure than the design's 3.00, which puts the plant's ridge above
N/C 3.0. B-125's fit moves the ridge's location (`BUB_AZEOTROPE_NC`) and adds a margin, both branches rising.
Open literature (search results only, no paper opened): a pressure minimum near N/C 3 and a design ratio of
2.95; the quantitative top-ridge data are Lemkowitz's and were not reachable.

## CIX.2 322R001's compartments (B-126)

`data/unit_322r001.py:5` records eleven sieve trays. The vendor archive's table of contents (pages 887 and
888) lists the reactor's file: the Technical Specification UD-AU-322-EC-0006, the Reactor Assembly
UD-AU-322-DZ-0006-004 rev 07, Trays Detail -008 rev 04, Trays Holes Layout -009 and Calculations for Internal
Trays -023; the first three located in `Soft copy\12\`. The specification is a scan and was not re-read, so
the count stands on the data module's own source. Open literature (search results only): 7 to 12 trays, often
10 or 11, a tray column modelled as mixed compartments in series. Step E3's holdup is twelve compartments,
the count to be confirmed on drawing -008 before it is used.

## CX.1 Wave 1, A-34: the loop's atoms closed tick by tick
